title: Samsung is beefing up Bixby with ChatGPT-style AI smarts - Android Police
mainText: Samsung is planning to enhance Bixby, its voice assistant, with generative AI technology, making it more intelligent and conversational for users. Although generative AI capabilities are currently available on Bixby, they are only for Samsung's smart home appliances. The revamp of Bixby is aimed at staying competitive in the AI market, following indications of generative AI upgrades at Galaxy Unpacked in July of the previous year. Bixby has been a feature on popular Samsung phones for some time now, but while Samsung has been updating its apps and services with Galaxy AI features, its voice assistant hasn't received much attention in the generative AI department. However, this could change soon as Samsung is reportedly considering giving Bixby a generative AI makeover. In an interview with CNBC, Won-joon Choi, Samsung's executive vice president of its mobile business, confirmed that the company is working hard to bring generative AI capabilities to Bixby. This means the voice assistant will become much smarter in the future, thanks to generative AI and large language models (LLMs). Samsung first launched Bixby in 2017 alongside the Galaxy S8 series. Since then, it has been extending Bixby to various devices like smart TVs and even home appliances. Now, with the rise of generative AI and LLMs, Choi believes it's time to redefine Bixby's strategy, so it can incorporate generative AI in the future and enhance its intelligence. The Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra introduced some new features for Bixby, such as taking calls and sending messages using text-to-speech. Currently, users use Bixby to activate Samsung's Galaxy AI hands-free. But with generative AI, it could significantly improve its performance, becoming more conversational and handling a lot more tasks. Bixby is about to get a brain boost thanks to generative AI. Generative AI in Bixby is already available on Samsung's smart home appliances, although it's not as robust as ChatGPT. But a Bixby powered by generative AI could be a game-changer, especially on your phone or smartwatch. For example, you may receive live feedback at the gym on your lifting technique. Plus, imagine asking your phone for battery-saving tips or how to enhance a photo when you're in a pinch. Samsung hinted at AI upgrades for Bixby during the Galaxy Unpacked event back in July 2023. According to TechRadar, Junho Park, Samsung's VP and director of global product planning, revealed during a chat after the event that generative AI is coming to Bixby. ChatGPT sparked a complete revolution, leaving everyone scrambling to figure out how to incorporate generative AI into their products. Samsung may be taking its time, but it appears that generative AI will make its way to its digital assistant sooner or later.

author: Divyanshi Sharma
title: Sony might grant PS5 Pro label to certain games, here is what it could mean - India Today
mainText: Sony is reportedly planning to introduce a PS5 Pro Enhanced label, which will serve as a mark of distinction for games that are optimized to utilize the console's enhanced capabilities. This label, internally referred to as Trinity Enhanced, is expected to indicate games that offer a PS5 Pro graphics mode, featuring enhancements like PSSR for 4K upscaling, a consistent 60 frames-per-second frame rate, and improved ray-tracing capabilities. Similar to the PS4 Pro Enhanced label of the previous generation, the Trinity Enhanced label will inform players when a game has been specifically optimized for the PS5 Pro hardware. This includes improvements in graphics performance and resolution, providing gamers with a superior visual experience. The PS5 Pro is expected to be launched in the Indian market later this year. The PlayStation 5 has been available since 2021, and for the first two years, there was a significant shortage of the console. Shortly after the PS5 shortage was officially over, rumors of the Pro model began to surface. Some early rumors suggested that the PS5 Pro would come with liquid cooling, posing a strong competition to high-end PCs. Rumors also suggested that the PS5 Pro would receive a major performance upgrade. Now, according to recent reports, Sony might start granting labels to certain games. The PS5 Pro is anticipated to have significant performance upgrades. With reports hinting at a potential launch towards the end of 2024, gamers can anticipate enhancements such as a 10-percent-higher-clocked CPU, 28 percent faster memory, and up to a 45 percent rendering performance improvement. These improvements are expected to result in smoother gameplay, faster load times, and enhanced graphical fidelity.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Samsung could launch a second 'Ultra' flagship phone this year - - Android Authority
mainText: Samsung is reportedly considering launching a second 'Ultra' flagship phone this year. The company's flagship foldable phone, the Galaxy Z Fold 6, might be getting a more premium variant. This information comes from a report suggesting that Samsung could launch an ‘Ultra’ branded Galaxy Z Fold 6 this year. The so-called Galaxy Z Fold 6 Ultra might have limited availability and could be more expensive than the standard model. The model number for the Galaxy Z Fold 6 Ultra is believed to be SM-F958, which matches the model number for the Galaxy S24 Ultra, SM-S928. The eight at the end of the model numbers is what denotes an Ultra model. For reference, the Galaxy Z Fold 5’s model number is SM-F946, and the regular Z Fold 6 is expected to come with model number SM-F956. The release of the Galaxy Z Fold 6 Ultra could be limited to South Korea. For now, SM-F958 appears to be in development only for Samsung’s home country. Its existence cannot be confirmed for the US, Europe, or any other market. While it’s logical to presume that the newly uncovered model number for the Galaxy Z Fold 6 points to a more premium variant of the phone, this alone is not proof enough of the device’s existence. We’ll have to wait for more evidence or other leaks to confirm that the Galaxy Z Fold 6 Ultra is indeed a thing. A new report suggests that the Galaxy Z Fold 6 Ultra could launch this year as Samsung's most premium flagship foldable phone.

author: PTI
title: ECI Taking Enough Steps To Inform Voters About NOTA Option On EVMs, Says HC Dismissing PIL - NDTV Profit
mainText: The Aurangabad bench of the Bombay High Court has stated that the Election Commission of India and the Maharashtra State Election Commission have taken sufficient measures to inform voters about the NOTA option on electronic voting machines. The Election Commission of India and the Maharashtra State Election Commission have taken enough steps to create awareness about the 'None of the Above' option on electronic voting machines, the Aurangabad bench of the Bombay High Court has said. A division bench of Justices Ravindra Ghuge and R M Joshi made the observation on March 22 while dismissing a public interest litigation seeking direction to the ECI to create awareness about the NOTA option. A copy of the judgment was made available on Monday. The petition filed by Suhas Wankhede, a student, stated that the ECI ought to appoint a brand ambassador to create more awareness among people about the NOTA option while they cast their votes. Taking note of a voters' guide pamphlet issued by the ECI, the court said the instructions about NOTA were published in bold letters in the document. "The long form of NOTA is conspicuously mentioned in bold letters and catches the attention of the voter immediately. The instructions are also set out in bold letters that NOTA is available as the last option on the electronic voting machine," the court said. The pamphlet was a pictorial guide to voters to make them aware of their rights and duties, it said. The court noted that both the ECI and the state election commission have taken steps to make people aware of their voting rights and the option of NOTA, and hence, no further directions are required to be passed. The court further said it was refraining from imposing a fine on the petitioner as he was a student.

author: HT Tech
title: Paint Your Own Starry Night Even in the Darkest of Hours with the New Galaxy A55 5G and Galaxy A35 5G - HT Tech
mainText: Samsung has introduced the Galaxy A55 5G and Galaxy A35 5G with advanced Nightography capabilities. This feature allows users to take stunning photos even in low light conditions. The Galaxy A series has made Nightography accessible to everyone, as these new models are affordable. One of the key features of Nightography is its ability to illuminate even the darkest photo settings and produce high-quality images with vibrant and true-to-life colors. This means you can get blur-free photos and videos even in the darkest surroundings without the need to use the camera flash. Samsung has been a pioneer in smartphone camera technology and has invested heavily in developing innovative solutions to improve low-light photography. The 50 MP main camera on both the latest A series models captures the finest details in every shot in high resolution during the day. At night, the larger-sized pixels absorb more light when the lighting is not enough and the 4X multi-readout feature generates bright and vibrant shots minus the noise. The Nightography feature combines a range of innovative technologies which work in tandem to deliver impressive results by optimizing the camera settings. Both the new Awesome A series models – Galaxy A55 5G and Galaxy A35 5G – also come with a Night Portrait Mode which brings the power of AI to Nightography so that you can capture the best version of yourself, every night, with the most breathtaking portraits. The AI-powered algorithms run a quick analysis of the scene and intelligently adjust parameters such as exposure, speed, etc to ensure that more light is absorbed and the noise is reduced every time you click a photo. In addition, an upgraded AI-powered ISP in the Galaxy A55 5G utilizes extra multi-frame synthesis processing to filter out the noise from data and churn out portraits in low lighting that will truly make you pause and say wow!

author: IANS
title: boAt introduces India's first headphones with head-tracking 3D audio - Telangana Today
mainText: boAt, a homegrown audio and wearable company, launched India’s first headphones with head-tracking 3D audio and spatial sound features on Monday. The headphones, named 'Nirvana Eutopia', were designed in India and are available for Rs 3,999 in black and white colours. The headphones feature spatial audio technology and integrate state-of-the-art 3D accelerometers and gyroscopes. As the user moves their head, the audio dynamically adapts, preserving the direction and alignment of the sound origins, creating the sensation of being fully immersed within the depicted scene. The headphones are equipped with calibrated 40mm dynamic drivers for an immersive 3D spatial sound. The device offers a 20-hour battery life (15 hours in head-tracked spatial mode), offering hours of uninterrupted bliss. With ASAP Charge and the Type-C port, just a quick 10-minute charge provides 90 minutes of uninterrupted enjoyment. The boAt ‘Nirvana Eutopia’ is designed around the Bluetooth v5.2 technology, offering seamless audio experiences, faster pairing times, and more dependable connections.

author: Livemint
title: Motorola Edge 50 Pro leak: Expected price, camera specs and all we know so far - Mint
mainText: The upcoming flagship from Motorola, the Edge 50 Pro, is generating a lot of buzz with its AI-centric features and advanced camera system. The smartphone is rumored to have a 6.7-inch pOLED display and a Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 processor. It is also expected to support fast charging. The Motorola Edge 50 Pro will feature a triple camera setup at the rear. The leaks suggest that the Motorola Edge 50 Pro will have a 50MP primary sensor, a 13MP ultra-wide-angle lens, and a 4,500mAh battery with fast charging support. The smartphone is set to launch on April 3 with an IP68 rating. The Motorola Edge 50 Pro is also expected to debut in India with a 6.7 inch 1.5K pOLED curved display, a Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 processor, and a triple camera setup. It is expected to feature 125W wired charging, 50W wireless charging, and come with Android 14 OS.

author: Editorji News Desk
title: Nothing Phone (3) price and chipset leaked: Snapdragon 8s Gen 3 processor expected - Editorji
mainText: The Nothing Phone (3) is creating a lot of excitement in the tech world with its leaked price and chipset details. The phone is expected to be powered by the Snapdragon 8s Gen 3 processor. This processor is known for its high performance and is commonly used in premium smartphones. The Nothing Phone (3) is expected to be priced competitively, making it a potential choice for consumers looking for a high-performance device at a reasonable price. More details about the phone, including its full specifications and launch date, are yet to be revealed. However, the leak has certainly piqued the interest of tech enthusiasts and potential buyers.

author: Editorji News Desk
title: WhatsApp working on new privacy feature to lock chats in linked devices, disable link preview and more - Editorji
mainText: WhatsApp is reportedly working on several new privacy features to enhance user control and security. These upcoming features aim to provide users with more options to safeguard their chats and improve overall privacy. Here are the key features currently in development: 1. Chat Lock for Linked Devices: With this feature, users will be able to lock their chats on linked devices. This means that even if someone gains access to a device linked to your WhatsApp account, they won’t be able to read your messages without unlocking them first. It adds an extra layer of security to prevent unauthorized access. 2. Disable Link Previews: Currently, when you receive a link in a chat, WhatsApp generates a preview with a thumbnail image and a brief description. The new feature will allow users to disable link previews, ensuring that no information about the link is revealed until it’s explicitly clicked. This can be useful for maintaining privacy and avoiding potential phishing attacks. 3. Third-Party Chats Section: WhatsApp plans to create a designated section for messages from other apps. These “third-party chats” will be kept separate from regular WhatsApp conversations. By doing so, WhatsApp aims to maintain its high privacy standards while allowing users to interact with messages from other platforms. These features are expected to roll out in future updates, enhancing user privacy and control over their WhatsApp experience. Stay tuned for further announcements and details as WhatsApp continues to refine and implement these changes.

author: Yordan
title: Realme GT Neo6 SE appears on TENAA as launch is confirmed for next week - GSMArena.com news - GSMArena.com
mainText: Realme is set to launch the GT Neo6 SE smartphone next week, as announced by the brand's chief marketing officer. The phone has cleared one of the final steps before launching in the Chinese market – obtaining certification by TENAA. The TENAA listing revealed photos from all angles and a specs sheet, confirming once again that the Realme GT Neo6 SE will be the company's first phone with a Snapdragon 7+ Gen 3 chipset. The phone will feature a 6.78” AMOLED screen, likely a BOE 8T LTPO panel with a resolution between Full HD+ and QHD+. The display is touted to be extremely bright, with the manufacturer promising up to 6,000 nits peak brightness. The smartphone, certified with model number RMX3850, will offer up to 16 GB RAM and 1 TB storage, a 5,500 mAh battery with 100W charging, and a 50 MP main camera with OIS. The phone is expected to launch with Android 14 and Realme UI 5. There are reports suggesting that the GT Neo6 SE will launch globally under a different name — Realme GT 6, but this information has not been independently verified yet.

author: Ankur Mishra
title: Google Podcast App To Shut Down From April 2; Heres How To Transfer Your Subcription To YouTube Music - Zee News
mainText: Google has officially announced that the Google Podcasts app, which has been downloaded over 500 million times on the Google Play Store, will be discontinued on April 2. Users are being informed about this change via email and are being given the option to export their subscriptions. Those who have podcast subscriptions will need to transition to YouTube Music. The Google Podcasts app is still available on the App Store and Play Store, and current users can switch to the new app before April 2nd. However, they will not be able to access content after that date. Google has been alerting users about the app's closure through in-app notifications. Now, they're showing warnings on the app's start page, encouraging users to move their data to YouTube Music or another podcast service. Here's how to transfer your subscriptions to YouTube Music: Open the Google Podcasts app on your Android or iOS device. Click on the Home tab to access your podcast subscriptions. Look for the Google notification regarding the shutting down of the Podcasts app. Click on the notification to open the Export Subscriptions option. Under Export Subscriptions, select 'Export to YouTube Music.' You will be redirected to the YouTube Music app. Choose a Gmail account to link with YouTube Music. Your podcast subscriptions will be added to YouTube Music, which may take a few minutes to complete.

author: Liam Croft
title: Rumour: PS5 Pro's 'Enhanced' Label Covers Resolution, Frame Rate, Ray Tracing Upgrades - Push Square
mainText: Sony is reportedly planning to introduce an 'Enhanced' label for games that take full advantage of the capabilities of its upgraded machine, the PS5 Pro, according to a new report from Insider Gaming. To earn this 'Enhanced' label, a game must feature at least one of the following upgrades: a higher 'target resolution' on the PS5 Pro compared to the 'fixed resolution' on the standard PS5 model, an improved 'target maximum resolution' on the PS5 Pro over a 'variable resolution' on the base PS5 system, a higher frame rate target on the PS5 Pro than the 'fixed frame rate' on the original PS5, or the use of the PS5 Pro's ray tracing features. If a game includes any one of these enhancements, it will be eligible for the 'Enhanced' label. Sony is encouraging both internal and third-party development teams to offer a graphical mode exclusive to the PS5 Pro that combines an upscaled 4K resolution with a 'constant' 60 frames-per-second, using its DLSS-like PlayStation Spectral Resolution system. Ray tracing effects would then be added or enhanced on top of this. The PS5 Pro, which is rumored to have a GPU up to three times faster than the base model and faster RAM, is reportedly targeting a Holiday 2024 launch. PlayStation Studios developers have reportedly had access to a PS5 Pro devkit since September 2023, and third-party developers received theirs in January.

author: Sankunni K
title: From April Fool hoax to passport of internet: The 20 years of Gmail - Republic World
mainText: Gmail, Google's revolutionary email service, is celebrating its 20th anniversary. Launched on April 1st, 2004, Gmail was initially thought to be an April Fools' Day prank due to its unprecedented offering of 1GB of storage, a figure that was astronomical compared to the 2-4MB offered by competitors like Hotmail and Yahoo Mail at the time. The brainchild of developer Paul Buchheit, Gmail was developed during Google's '20% time' policy, which allowed employees to dedicate a portion of their workweek to personal projects. The project, initially known as 'Caribou', was kept under wraps for years as Buchheit worked on creating its innovative, searchable web-based interface. Despite skepticism within Google about the feasibility of offering massive, free (ad-supported) email storage, Gmail was finally launched on April Fools' Day, further fueling the perception that it was a prank. Google opted for a limited, invite-only beta release in 2004, creating a sense of exclusivity and generating significant buzz. Gmail's impact was transformative, replacing clunky, desktop-bound email software with a fluid, web-based experience accessible from any device. Its search-powered organization eliminated the need for endless folders and manual filing, and its threaded conversations made email threads more manageable. Today, Gmail has over 1.8 billion active users and has fundamentally changed how we communicate. However, its journey has not been without controversy, with privacy concerns raised over Google's ad-based business model and mixed reception to features like Smart Compose and automatic categorization.

author: Divya Bhati
title: YouTube now allows desktop users to download music offline - India Today
mainText: YouTube Music has expanded its functionality to include offline downloads for its web app, a feature previously exclusive to mobile devices. This enhancement improves user convenience and accessibility, especially for those who primarily use the service on desktops or laptops. According to a report by 9to5Google, Google has been testing offline downloads for its music streaming service on the web app. While the feature has been in testing for some time, a wider rollout has been observed recently. Users are now beginning to see a message next to the Library tab, indicating the new capability to download music for offline listening. Although the feature may not be visible to everyone yet, some users have reportedly been greeted with a message beside their Library tab that reads: "New! Download music to listen offline." To save music offline using YouTube Music's web app, users can follow a simple step-by-step process: Navigate to an album or single's page. Look for the download button located between the "Save to library" and three-dot overflow menu options. Click on the download option to save the album or single. Similar to the mobile app, downloaded content on the web will have its own "Downloads" tab within the user's library. Convenient filters allow users to sort their downloads by playlists, podcasts, songs, or albums. However, there are some important points to consider: Download Limit: Offline downloads on the web app will count towards YouTube Music's 10-device download limit. Expiration: Similar to the mobile app, downloaded content will expire if the device is not connected to the internet at least once every 30 days. This new update brings long-awaited offline download functionality to the YouTube Music web app, particularly benefiting users who primarily access the service on desktops or laptops. It eliminates the need to rely solely on the mobile app for offline listening, enhancing convenience and accessibility. However, some key points to consider exist. While YouTube Premium subscribers likely enjoy offline downloads for both music and podcasts, it remains unclear if this feature extends to non-subscribers for podcasts specifically.

author: Livemint
title: Instagram Reels may come with a new ‘blend’ feature: Here's how it will work | Mint - Mint
mainText: Instagram is reportedly working on a new feature for its Reels platform, dubbed 'Blend'. This feature aims to provide users with a personalized and private feed based on shared reels. Users have the option to leave the blend at any time. Currently, the feature is in the internal prototype stage and has not been tested externally. The 'Blend' feature, if implemented, could offer a unique way for users to interact with content on Instagram Reels, potentially enhancing user engagement and personalization on the platform. However, it's important to note that since the feature is still in the prototype stage, there's no guarantee that it will be released to the public. Instagram has yet to make an official announcement regarding the 'Blend' feature.

author: Namit Singh Sengar
title: 'People Hate Me, Working 80 To 100 Hours A Week', Says Sachin Bansal As He Scales Up Navi - News18
mainText: Sachin Bansal, the founder of Flipkart, has now turned his attention to his fintech startup, Navi. Despite leaving Flipkart, which is now owned by Walmart, Bansal is fully dedicated to leading Navi. With assets under management (AUM) exceeding Rs 7,500 crore, Navi is gradually establishing its presence in the financial sector. In an interview with Moneycontrol, Bansal disclosed his complete commitment to the financial services company, stating that he spends 80 to 100 hours per week, including weekends, on its operations. Navi, like many other companies, adopted remote work policies during the pandemic. However, Bansal stresses that this was a temporary measure. The IIT-Delhi graduate is fully involved in managing Navi, to the point where he has stopped his activities as an angel investor. Instead, he devotes all his energy and time to his latest venture. According to Bansal, remote work is no longer allowed at the startup. While recognizing that some team members may dislike his position and the long hours he works each week, Bansal clarifies that he does not expect his colleagues to match his workload, despite the requirement for everyone to work from the office.

author: Karen Friar
title: Stock market today: US futures drift lower as faith in rate cuts fades - Yahoo Finance
mainText: On Wednesday, April 3, 2024, US stock futures indicated a potential for more losses. Investors were keenly awaiting a speech by Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, looking for hints about the future of interest rates. Futures for the S&P 500 slipped by 0.2%, while those for the Dow Jones Industrial Average were just below the flatline. The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 futures were leading the decline, down by almost 0.4%. This comes after the major indices closed in the red. The strong start to the year for stocks has been dampened by solid economic data, which has reduced hopes for three Fed rate cuts. Investors have adjusted their expectations to the point where they anticipate a smaller and later easing than what the policymakers have projected. The spotlight is now on Powell, whose speech on the economic outlook will be scrutinized for signs of a policy shift at the Fed's June meeting. Remarks by Michael Barr and other Fed officials will also be closely watched. The results of a shareholder vote due later Wednesday will reveal the winner of the intense proxy battle between Disney and activist investor Nelson Peltz. Indications are that Disney has garnered enough support to resist the board shake-up proposed by Peltz's Trian, according to sources cited by Reuters. In individual stock news, Intel shares dropped around 5% in premarket trading following the chipmaker's report of increased operating losses at its foundry business. Meanwhile, its competitor TSMC had to stop some chip production due to a massive earthquake in Taiwan, raising concerns about the supplier to Apple and Nvidia. Its US-listed shares saw a slight dip.

author: Sean Williams
title: 1 "Magnificent Seven" Stock to Buy Hand Over Fist in April, and 1 to Avoid Like the Plague - The Motley Fool
mainText: The 'Magnificent Seven' are seven of the largest and most influential public companies. They are Microsoft, Apple, Nvidia, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta Platforms, and Tesla. These stocks have been the major contributors to the recent record-closing highs of all three major stock indexes - the Dow Jones Industrial Average, the S&P 500, and the Nasdaq Composite. Over the past decade, Nvidia's stock has increased by more than 20,000%, Tesla's shares have gained over 1,100%, and both Amazon and Microsoft are close to 1,000% gains. In contrast, the S&P 500 has increased by a comparatively modest 183%. The 'Magnificent Seven' have undeniable competitive advantages. For instance, Microsoft has become a leader in the cloud, with Azure accounting for a quarter of cloud infrastructure service spending during the September-ended quarter. Among these seven businesses, there's an industry leader still trading at a historically cheap valuation, as well as a highflier that has mounting red flags. The article suggests that investors should consider buying one of these stocks and avoid another.

author: Reuben Gregg Brewer, The Motley Fool
title: 3 Utility Stocks to Buy Hand Over Fist in April - Yahoo Finance
mainText: Utility stocks are currently out of favor, providing long-term dividend investors with an opportunity to acquire attractive income stocks. When interest rates rise, dividend stocks can sometimes fall as investors switch to lower-risk income options, such as CDs. This is particularly true for utilities, as these capital-intensive businesses rely heavily on debt financing. Therefore, rising costs present a second challenge for the sector. However, over the long term, regulated utilities should be able to adjust and continue to provide reliable income streams to shareholders. If you're a long-term thinker, you might want to consider adding NextEra Energy, Black Hills Corporation, and Dominion Energy to your portfolio in April. NextEra Energy offers a modest dividend yield compared to the other two utilities on this list. In fact, its yield is only slightly above the average of the broader utility sector. But the yield is near a 10-year high for NextEra Energy, suggesting that the stock is currently undervalued. The real selling point, however, is the company's average annualized dividend growth of around 10% over the past decade, which is extremely high for a utility. Management expects to raise the dividend by that much again in 2024.

author: HT Trending Desk
title: Kamath brothers, Bansals India's youngest billionaires, according to Forbes - Hindustan Times
mainText: Zerodha founders Nithin and Nikhil Kamath, along with Flipkart founders Sachin and Binny Bansal, have secured their positions as India’s youngest billionaires, as per the recently published Forbes Billionaires List for 2024. These successful entrepreneurs are all in their 40s, and their remarkable achievements have catapulted them into the elite billionaire club. Nikhil Kamath, at the age of 37, stands out as India’s youngest billionaire, boasting a net worth of $3.1 billion. His assets and business ventures have propelled him to this prestigious position. Meanwhile, his elder brother, Nithin Kamath, aged 44, commands a net worth of $4.6 billion, further solidifying their family’s financial success story. The Bansal duo, Sachin and Binny, co-founders of Flipkart, have also made significant strides. Their contributions to e-commerce and technology have resulted in a combined net worth that places them among India’s wealthiest individuals. Sachin Bansal and Binny Bansal’s entrepreneurial journey began with the establishment of Flipkart in 2007, and their vision and hard work have paid off handsomely. These four trailblazers exemplify the spirit of innovation, determination, and business acumen, inspiring countless others to dream big and achieve greatness. As India continues to thrive in the global business landscape, the Kamath brothers and the Bansals serve as shining examples of what can be accomplished with vision, resilience, and unwavering commitment.

author: Vidya Sreedhar
title: Shareholders approve Vodafone Idea’s Rs 20,000 crore fundraising plan - The Economic Times
mainText: Vodafone Idea Ltd has received the approval of its shareholders for a proposal to raise Rs 20,000 crore through a combination of equity and equity-linked securities. The company's board had given its nod to this fundraising plan on February 27. With the approval of the shareholders now in place, the company is expecting to complete the equity fund raise in the current quarter. The promoters have also committed to participate in the proposed equity raise. Vodafone Idea is actively engaged with its lenders to secure debt funding, which will follow the equity fundraising. The company plans to raise around Rs 45,000 crore through a combination of equity and debt. The bank debt of the company currently stands at less than Rs 4,500 crore. As of the end of December, Vodafone Idea’s gross debt was Rs 2.15 lakh crore, which includes deferred spectrum payment obligations of Rs 1.38 lakh crore, AGR liability of Rs 69,020 crore due to the government, optionally convertible debentures amounting to Rs 1,660 crore, and dues towards banks and financial institutions. The company has been able to grow its 4G subscriber base and average revenue per user (ARPU) for the last 10 consecutive quarters. This improvement in operating metrics has prompted the company to tap the market for raising funds. The 4G subscriber base of Vodafone Idea has increased to 125.6 million from 121.6 million a year ago. The company has managed to reduce its consolidated net loss to Rs 6,986 crore in the quarter ended December, from Rs 7,990 crore a year ago, and Rs 8,738 crore a quarter ago. The approval of the shareholders boosted sentiment and saw shares of Vodafone Idea trading 2.3% higher on the BSE at Rs 13.74.

author: Shivendra Kumar
title: Shipping stocks surge up to 12% led by multibagger Mazagon Dock - The Economic Times
mainText: On Wednesday, shipping company stocks saw a significant surge of nearly 12%, with Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders leading the pack as it hit the day's high of Rs 2,225.25 on the NSE. Other top gainers included Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers, Cochin Shipyard, Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), and the Great Eastern Shipping Company, which saw gains between 10% and 3%. Cochin Shipyard also reached its 52-week high of Rs 1,062 on the NSE, gaining 8% in intraday trade. Over the past three trading sessions, Garden Reach Shipbuilders has remained unbeaten, extending its gains to 18%. This surge in Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers comes on the back of a 33% year-on-year (YoY) increase in its turnover for the financial year ended March 31, 2023. The company reported its highest-ever annual turnover of Rs 3,400 crore. The company attributed this robust financial performance to effective resource management and improved internal efficiencies. The company also declared an interim dividend @ 79% of Paid-up Share Capital, which is an increase from 55% of the previous year. In the shipping sector, Cochin Shipyard and Mazagon Dock have been standout performers. Cochin Shipyard has delivered a staggering one-year return of 337%, while Mazagon Dock has yielded 234% in the same period. However, Mazagon has lost 4% in 2024 due to profit booking, while Cochin Shipyard’s 2024 returns stand at 54%. One-year returns by Garden Reach are to the tune of 96% while those of SCI and Great Eastern Shipping Company are at 152.39 and 59%, respectively.

author: Irina Slav
title: Oil Prices Climb Toward $90 on Geopolitical Risk and a U.S. Stock Draw - OilPrice.com
mainText: Brent crude oil prices are inching closer to the $90 per barrel mark, following a report from the American Petroleum Institute that indicated a larger than anticipated reduction in U.S. inventories, coupled with ongoing geopolitical tensions. The report revealed a decrease in crude oil by 2.3 million barrels, gasoline stocks by 1.4 million barrels, and middle distillate inventories by 2.5 million barrels. Geopolitical events contributing to the tension include a Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian refinery and Iran's promise to retaliate against an Israeli strike on the Iranian consulate in Damascus, which resulted in five casualties. These events raise concerns about potential disruptions to oil supply from one of the world's top three exporters and the possibility of escalating conflict in the Middle East threatening oil supply security. In other news, Mexico's Pemex announced plans to cut crude oil exports by over 400,000 barrels per day as it redirects barrels to local processing capacity. This move is reportedly in response to Pemex cancelling several delivery contracts with clients in the U.S., Europe, and Asia in order to supply more oil to the new Dos Bocas refinery, with the aim of increasing domestic fuel production ahead of the presidential election in June. The focus now shifts to the OPEC+ meeting, where members are expected to maintain limited oil production until at least the end of June. This could result in a continued tight supply, potentially driving prices even higher. Despite these factors, some analysts predict lower prices due to expected disappointing growth in China's oil demand. However, recent manufacturing data from Beijing indicates a resurgence in activity for the first time in six months.

author: Aditya Nadkarni
title: 2024 Kia Sonet launched; prices in India start at Rs. 7.99 lakh - CarWale
mainText: Kia India has launched the 2024 Sonet in the country, with prices starting at Rs. 7.99 lakh (ex-showroom). The company has introduced four new versions of the Sonet, now available in the HTE  and HTK  guise, offered across the 1.2-litre petrol and 1.5-litre diesel engines. The HTE  variant gets a sunroof in addition to the features on the HTE variant, while the HTK  receives additional features in the form of LED connected taillights, automatic climate control, and a rear defogger. author: Sai Aravindh
title: Why NSE Revised Lot Size Of Nifty 50 Contracts | Profit Explains - NDTV Profit
mainText: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) has made revisions to the market lot of derivative contracts on select indices, including the benchmark Nifty 50, as part of its periodic review. The lot for the Nifty 50 has been reduced from 50 to 25. For Nifty Financial Services, the lot size has been reduced from 40 to 25, and for the Nifty Midcap Select, it has been reduced from 75 to 50. The market lot of the Nifty Bank remains unchanged at 15. These changes are part of a periodic review of lot sizes in derivatives contracts and will come into effect from April 26. All new contracts generated from the end of the day of April 25 and available for trading from April 26 will be with the revised market lot size. The exchanges are required to review the lot size once every six months based on the necessary adjustments. According to the Securities and Exchange Board of India's rules, the lot size for derivatives contracts should be fixed within Rs 5–10 lakh. Currently, the notional value of the Nifty 50 is approximately over Rs 11 lakh as the index has seen a significant increase recently. This change will be a major boost to retail participants as it becomes an attractive size to enter trades in the derivatives segment. Apart from leading to increased liquidity, this will also help traders to manage risks more effectively. The aspect to watch out for is how the brokerages will react to the move. Currently, on an average, a contract in options is Rs 20 per lot size. If the brokers do not reduce their brokerage overall, instead of paying Rs 20 for 50 lot size contracts, investors must still pay Rs 20 for 25-lot-size contracts.

author: Reuters
title: Intel discloses $7 billion operating loss for chip-making unit - Reuters
mainText: Intel Corporation has revealed the financial results for its foundry business. The company reported an operating loss of $7 billion for 2023, which is a deeper loss than the $5.2 billion in operating losses reported the previous year. The foundry business generated revenue of $18.9 billion for 2023, a decrease of 31% from $27.49 billion the previous year. Intel shares fell by 4.3% following the disclosure of these figures in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). During an investor presentation, Intel's CEO, Pat Gelsinger, stated that 2024 would be the year of peak operating losses for the company's chip-making business. He also projected that the business would break even on an operating basis by around 2027. Gelsinger attributed the foundry business's struggles to poor decisions made in the past, including a decision made a year ago not to use extreme ultraviolet (EUV) machines from Dutch firm ASML. Despite their high cost, these machines are more cost-effective than previous chip-making tools. As a result of these missteps, Intel has outsourced approximately 30% of its total wafer production to external contract manufacturers such as TSMC. The company plans to reduce this figure to roughly 20%. Intel has now transitioned to using EUV tools, which will increasingly meet its production needs as older machines are phased out. Gelsinger stated that in the post-EUV era, Intel is now very competitive in terms of price and performance and is returning to a leadership position. In contrast, in the pre-EUV era, the company carried a lot of costs and was uncompetitive. Intel plans to invest $100 billion in building or expanding chip factories in four U.S. states. The success of the company's business turnaround plan depends on its ability to convince other companies to use its manufacturing services. As part of this plan, Intel has begun reporting the results of its manufacturing operations as a standalone unit.

author: TOI Business Desk
title: Strong show by Indian economy! IMF ups India GDP forecast; good news for Pakistan too - The Times of India
mainText: The World Bank has revised its GDP growth forecast for India to 7.5% for 2024, up by 1.2% from its previous forecast. This upward revision is part of a positive outlook for South Asia, which is expected to grow at 6.0% in 2024, largely driven by India's strong growth and recoveries in Pakistan and Sri Lanka. The World Bank's South Asia Development Update states that South Asia is poised to maintain its status as the fastest-growing region globally for the next two years, with a projected growth of 6.1% in 2025. India's economic performance in Q4 of 2023 exceeded expectations, with a growth rate of 8.4%. The World Bank has highlighted that India will be a major contributor to the region's economy and it is expected to see output growth of 7.5% in FY 2023-24, followed by a moderate decrease to 6.6% in the medium term. According to the World Bank, activity in services and industry is expected to remain robust. The report also mentions positive signs in Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, with expected growth rates of 5.7% and 2.5% respectively. Martin Raiser, Vice President for South Asia at the World Bank, has expressed optimism about the region's growth prospects in the short term but has cautioned about challenges such as fiscal vulnerabilities and climate risks. Franziska Ohnsorge, Chief Economist for South Asia at the World Bank, emphasized the need for policies to enhance private investment and employment growth to leverage the demographic dividend. India's economic performance in Q4 of 2023 exceeded expectations, with a growth rate of 8.4% driven by investments and government spending. The country's composite Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) stood at 60.6 in February, well above the global average, indicating a strong expansion. Inflation in India has been within the Reserve Bank's target range, supported by stable policy rates since February 2023. Financial conditions in India have remained favorable, with domestic credit issuance growing by 14% year-on-year in December 2023. The nonperforming-loan ratio has decreased to 3.2%, and regulatory capital adequacy has surpassed requirements.

title: Delhi High Court declares Haldiram as a well-known mark - Bar & Bench - Indian Legal News
mainText: The Delhi High Court has declared 'HALDIRAM' as well as the red oval-shaped mark of the brand as a well-known trademark in respect of food items, restaurants, and eateries. This decision was made in the case of Haldiram India Pvt Ltd v. Berachah Sales Corporation & Ors. The Court opined that the concept of a 'well-known' trademark is ‘dynamic’. This declaration is significant as it provides Haldiram with stronger protection against infringement and misuse. A 'well-known' trademark is one that has gained substantial public recognition and indicates a connection between the goods or services and the trademark owner. This recognition can be as a result of extensive use, promotion, or registration of the trademark, either in India or internationally. The declaration of a trademark as 'well-known' is made by the Registrar of Trademarks or by any court in India. The declaration is based on several factors, including the duration and geographical extent of use of the trademark, the promotion of the trademark, the duration and geographical extent of any registration of the trademark, and the record of successful enforcement of the trademark. The declaration of 'HALDIRAM' as a well-known trademark is a testament to the brand's popularity and reputation in the market[1].

title: Bitcoin Back Down to $66K as Rising Treasury Yields Catch Investor Interest - CoinDesk
mainText: Bitcoin (BTC) has experienced a drop in value, currently trading around $66,000. This comes as traders are reacting to the resurgence of Treasury yields and the potential delay in rate cuts by the Federal Reserve until later this year. The CoinDesk 20 (CD20) was down 0.6% to 2,532. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note reached a two-week high of 4.40% overnight due to persistent inflation and unexpectedly strong manufacturing activity. An increase in the so-called risk-free rate typically leads to an outflow of money from risk assets and zero-yielding investments like gold. However, gold remained resilient amid the weak tone in bitcoin and Wall Street's tech-heavy index, Nasdaq. "Bitcoin retraced down to $65,000, mostly attributed to the recent macro outlook on interest rates and rising Treasury yields," said Semir Gabeljic, director of capital formation at Pythagoras Investments. "Higher interest rate environments typically tend to reduce investor appetite to risk." On Polymarket, bettors have ruled out a rate cut by May and are split 50-50 on whether one will happen in June. Most of the certain money is on it happening in the fall. The CME Fed Watch tool has a 97% chance of rates staying the same after May's meeting. Coinglass data shows that over $245 million in long positions have been liquidated in the last 24 hours, with $60 million in BTC positions getting rekt. "Perpetual futures funding rates for most crypto assets are back to 1bps, and global futures open interest decreased by 10 percent overnight, indicating some leveraged long positions are closed," added Jun-Young Heo, a Derivatives Trader at Singapore-based Presto. "As recent Bitcoin ETF inflows are stagnating and BTC and ETH market prices came below the 20-day moving average, some trend followers would have regarded yesterday's downturn as the end of a two-month-long rally."

title: Air India launches “Reimagined” Flying Returns programme: Rewards cheaper; Status earning easier; Turns Revenue based - Live From A Lounge
mainText: Air India has transitioned its 30-year-old loyalty programme, Flying Returns, into a new era. The loyalty programme, which was introduced in 1994 and last updated in 2012 when the airline joined Star Alliance, has now become a truly modern airline loyalty programme. Air India has transitioned to a revenue-based programme. Previously, the earning of FR Points was linked to a formula where the distance flown and the class of ticket booked determined how many points you would earn. Now, airlines have moved to “revenue-based” rewards programmes, where the number of points earned is directly correlated to the money paid. Club Vistara was the first revenue-based programme in India, and now Air India follows. Under the new programme, you earn a minimum of 6 FR Points/INR 100 spent for the base tier, with appropriate bonuses for the higher tiers of the airline. The status tiers have been renamed to red (base tier), silver, gold, and platinum, which are more in line with global status tiers. On each of these tiers, you earn bonuses over and above the 6 FR points/INR 100 spent on Air India. Earning status has been made much easier. You will earn 6 FR Tier Points for every INR 100 spent. The Tier Qualification Requirements have also been cut. On a rolling 365 days basis, now you need to earn the following FR Tier Points to qualify every year[1].

author: Lauryn Overhultz
title: Could Diddy’s multimillion-dollar real estate portfolio ‘be seized’ after raids? Legal expert weighs in - Fox Business
mainText: Sean 'Diddy' Combs' luxurious real estate portfolio has come under scrutiny after his properties were raided by Homeland Security as part of a human trafficking investigation on March 25. The future of his four homes now depends on the outcome of the legal proceedings. According to legal experts, Combs would need to be charged with a crime for any action to be taken against his homes. If charged, the properties could be included or referenced in the indictment as a means that served the ends of those alleged crimes, and they could be seized, says Priya Sopori, Partner at Greenberg Glusker and a member of the firm’s litigation group. If the properties were used to introduce victims of sex trafficking to potential abusers and sex offenders, and if Combs were found guilty of those alleged crimes, then the properties themselves could be seized by the government. Sopori also noted that Homeland Security could conduct additional searches on Diddy's wall safes, guest houses, or garages if they weren't included in the original search warrant. However, former federal prosecutor Neama Rahmani pointed out that it might be difficult to prove that Diddy's homes were connected to criminal activity. While RICO does allow for the forfeiture of properties that are the proceeds of criminal activity, proving this in Diddy's case could be challenging given his legitimate businesses in music, clothing, alcohol, and perfume. Rahmani added that as long as the businesses are legitimate, they are unlikely to be affected.

mainText: The NFL news cycle recently took another turn when the Buffalo Bills and Houston Texans agreed to a trade. This trade could potentially shift the balance of the AFC power structure, reshape at least two teams’ attacks, and bring all eyes to a receiver who has delivered loud messages on and off the field. Less than 24 hours after former NFL quarterback Robert Griffin III argued Diggs was essential to Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen's success, Diggs was Houston-bound. Now, as a star receiver moves halfway across the country and conference, who stands to gain and lose the most? Stefon Diggs and C.J. Stroud are among the winners. It’s too soon to know for sure how bright, young offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik will employ Diggs and what form the connection with reigning Offensive Rookie of the Year C.J. Stroud will take. But Diggs’ trajectory in Buffalo last season was concerning. After posting 85.5 receiving yards per game and a touchdown in 59% of regular-season contests through three years, Diggs maintained that pace through the Bills’ first 10 games with 86.8 yards per game and seven total scores. But after offensive coordinator Ken Dorsey was fired in November, Diggs’ production dropped under Joe Brady, who will keep his post in 2024. Diggs averaged 45 yards per game the rest of the year (43.1 including playoffs) and scored just once in seven regular-season games and zero times in two playoff contests. The Bills won six of their last seven compared to five of their first 10. While the attention he commanded undoubtedly helped his teammates, a player with Diggs’ vocal passion isn’t meant to stick with a team whose winning trends inversely to his production. C.J. Stroud, the second overall pick of the 2023 NFL Draft, has created the favorable situation from which he now reaps the benefits. His 23 touchdowns to five interceptions last year enabled the Texans to triple their win total year-over-year. Even so, what quarterback wouldn’t be thrilled to go through reads with Diggs, Nico Collins, Tank Dell, and Dalton Schultz as options?

title: It’s not just clouds, there’s a new weather threat for eclipse viewers to worry about - CNN
mainText: The upcoming total solar eclipse on Monday, April 8, has been a topic of discussion among weather enthusiasts and astronomers alike. The weather forecast for the eclipse is still uncertain, with some details beginning to emerge. There are indications that parts of the southern and central U.S. may experience clouds and rain, while the East Coast might enjoy some of the best weather in the country. The eclipse will begin when the moon starts to obstruct part of the sun, a process that will last from about 1 hour and 40 minutes in the Pacific Northwest to about 2 hours and 40 minutes near the Rio Grande Valley in Texas. This is the first total solar eclipse visible over the mainland U.S. since August 21, 2017. A 115-mile-wide strip covering parts of 15 states from Texas to northern Maine, known as the path of totality, is where the total eclipse can be seen. The moon will completely cover the sun for about three to four minutes during the peak of the event. The rest of the Lower 48 states, as well as Canada, Mexico, Central America, Cuba, Hispaniola, and Bermuda, will be able to see a partial eclipse. Rain and snow are forecasted in parts of the Southern Plains and lower Mississippi Valley, including central and eastern Texas into southern Arkansas, Louisiana, and parts of Mississippi. Some light rain or showers are possible in parts of the Midwest. Snow showers may dot parts of the northern and central Rockies, while a few showers are possible in Southern California. Despite the potential for wet weather, there's still a chance that the couple of hours on Monday will offer at least glimpses, if not full views, of the eclipse. So, even if the forecast looks wetter, don't be too discouraged, especially if the forecast mentions 'showers'.

title: As the world ages, cancer cases are projected to rise, hitting some countries like ‘a tidal wave’ - CNN
mainText: The American Cancer Society (ACS) has released its Global Cancer Statistics for 2024. The report reveals that an estimated 20 million new cancer cases were diagnosed in 2022, and 9.7 million people died from the disease worldwide. By 2050, the number of cancer cases is predicted to reach 35 million. This increase is attributed to the aging and growth of the population, assuming current incidence rates remain unchanged. Major risk factors such as unhealthy diet, physical inactivity, heavy alcohol consumption, and cigarette smoking are increasing in many parts of the world and will likely exacerbate the future burden of cancer. Lung cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer globally, as well as the leading cause of cancer death overall and in men. After lung cancer, men most often develop prostate and colon cancers and die from liver and colon cancers. In women, breast cancer is the most commonly diagnosed cancer and the leading cause of cancer death, followed by lung, colon and cervical cancers. Only 15% of eligible girls worldwide have received the vaccine for human papillomavirus (HPV), which causes virtually all cervical cancers. Every day in 2022, approximately 1,800 women were diagnosed with cervical cancer and nearly 1,000 women died from the disease worldwide. Cervical cancer continues to be the leading cause of cancer death in women in 37 countries in sub-Saharan Africa and in Latin America.

The problem extends beyond harassment, with a culture of masculinity and chauvinism prevalent in the fields of Antarctic science and exploration. The first Antarctic expedition to include women was the Ronne Antarctic Research Expedition in 1947–1948. However, the inclusion of women was seen by many in the polar community as contributing to tensions among the men. Despite the groundbreaking nature of their inclusion, the women on the expedition faced significant challenges. Jennie Darlington, one of the women on the expedition, asserted that 'women do not belong in the Antarctic' due to the harsh conditions and the potential need for rescue. She also spoke of the emotional burden she undertook, feeling that she had to suppress her feminine instincts and not act like a woman in a man's world. The practice of excluding women and singling them out as outsiders has resulted in behavior explicitly hostile to women becoming commonplace in Antarctica.

author: Sina Petri
title: Eating avocados can maintain blood sugar levels and promote balanced nutrition - VOGUE India
mainText: Avocados, the creamy green fruit, are gaining popularity due to their high nutritional value and potential health benefits, especially for people with diabetes. Unlike most fruits, avocados are low in carbohydrates and high in healthy fats, which means they have little effect on blood sugar levels and are beneficial for people trying to manage or prevent type 2 diabetes. Avocados are packed with monounsaturated fats, fiber, vitamins C, E, K, and B-6, and nutrients like riboflavin, niacin, folate, pantothenic acid, magnesium, and potassium. They're also a great source of lutein, beta-carotene, and omega-3 fatty acids. The high fiber content of avocados is particularly beneficial as it can help control blood sugar levels. A study published in Nutrition Journal found that adding half an avocado to the standard lunch of healthy, overweight people did not significantly impact blood sugar levels. Moreover, research suggests that avocados could help keep blood sugar levels in check. One study found that avocado consumption was linked to lower fasting glucose and insulin and lower rates of incident type 2 diabetes. Another study found an association between avocado intake and better glucose and insulin management, especially for people with type 2 diabetes. Avocados are also beneficial for heart health, which is crucial for people with diabetes as they are at a higher risk of heart disease. Diets rich in unsaturated fat and fiber, like that of avocados, are associated with fewer heart disease risk factors, like high cholesterol. A study on people with obesity or overweight and insulin resistance found that eating avocados in place of carbohydrates was linked to better blood sugar and cholesterol numbers. Despite their numerous benefits, avocados are high in calories and may cause weight gain if consumed in large amounts. Therefore, they should be eaten in moderation and preferably as a substitute for other high-calorie foods.

CMP reminds customers to stay away from downed lines, turn off or unplug major appliances and sensitive electronics, and never use ranges or outdoor stoves to heat their homes. Those in need of shelter or food are advised to reach out to 211 for available resources. Lingering rain and snow from the storm is expected to last through Saturday.

author: Axios
title: NATO plans for surviving a potential Trump second term - Axios
mainText: Top diplomats from NATO's member states, gathering Thursday on the alliance's 75th birthday, will be talking about the threat posed by Moscow — and from the potential next occupant of the White House. NATO has two new members and a resurgent sense of mission after Russia's invasion of Ukraine. But with Donald Trump waiting in the wings, the alliance could be on course for another existential crisis at a much more dangerous time for Europe. At this week's gathering in Brussels, NATO foreign ministers are expected to discuss a plan to Trump-proof military aid to Ukraine. The proposal would put a U.S.-led organization overseeing weapons shipments to Ukraine under NATO control to ensure continuity if Trump takes office in January. There are also ongoing discussions within the alliance about ways to ensure European militaries can match some responsibilities that would currently fall on the U.S., says Ivo Daalder, a former U.S. ambassador to NATO. Such deliberations tend to take place without mentioning the elephant not in the room, Daalder says. "Talking about Trump coming in is, in fact, talking about Biden losing. So it's more about, 'Europe needs to do more.'" The other side: Trump riffed in February that he'd "encourage" Russia "to do whatever the hell they want" to a NATO ally if the country wasn't spending enough on defense — the latest and arguably most inflammatory in his long history of alliance-shaking rhetoric. He said last month that he'd stay in the alliance if other members pay their "fair share," but also said the U.S. would be fine outside NATO because "we have an ocean in between [us and] some problems." Between the lines: While NATO members don't actually owe "dues," as Trump often phrases it, the U.S. accounts for two-thirds of all defense spending among member states, lending credence to his claim members are freeloading off American military might.

author: Michael Dorgan
title: Vaccinating migrants like US children would have prevented disease outbreaks at Chicago shelters: experts - Fox News
mainText: Medical experts have stated that the recent outbreak of measles and tuberculosis in Chicago’s migrant shelters could have been avoided if the migrants had been vaccinated at the border and if they weren’t living in cramped conditions. Chicago health officials reported a small number of TB cases at some migrant facilities, following reports of dozens of measles cases at these facilities. There are growing concerns that these cases will multiply and spread to the general population in Chicago. There are also fears that similar outbreaks could occur in other sanctuary cities such as New York, Boston, and Denver. Unlike most U.S.-born children who have to follow strict vaccination schedules, migrant students were not required to be vaccinated in order to attend school in Chicago under an exemption for children living in unstable housing. In New York City, migrant students were also given waivers at the start of the 2023-2024 school year. At least two students who tested positive for measles were living at Chicago's Pilsen migrant shelter, although it is unclear at the time of this publication if they had been vaccinated. Amid the outbreak, Chicago moved to vaccinate all migrants at its shelters. Nearly 40,000 migrants have arrived in Chicago since August 2022. Migrants who are stopped at the border and then released into the general population are rarely medically screened or given vaccines. Legal migrants, like Green Card holders, are required to be vaccinated for a range of inoculations as part of their approval process.

author: Ridhi Kale
title: How a forever-glowing you is possible - India Today
mainText: The aspiration for glowing skin is universal, transcending skin types. Previously, the only way to achieve this was through layers of foundation, but the trend has shifted towards more natural methods. The stress of modern life can take a toll on our health, which is often reflected in our skin. A healthy, glowing complexion not only regulates body temperature but also combats the effects of pollution and harmful ultraviolet radiation. Dr Garima Tyagi, a dermatologist at SENS Clinic, emphasizes the importance of a balanced diet and active lifestyle in maintaining skin health. Foods rich in antioxidants, such as cocoa, beans, green vegetables, beetroot, carrot, red cabbage, blueberries, raspberries, strawberries, cherries, and coffee, are beneficial for the skin. On the other hand, alcohol, sugary foods, fried and spicy edibles, as well as frozen and transfat-laden meals should be avoided. As we age, our skin loses collagen and elastin, leading to fine lines, wrinkles, discoloration, sagging skin, and even rough texture. Anti-ageing products containing peptides, retinol, and hyaluronic acid can combat these issues and slow down ageing by improving skin elasticity. Vitamin E and green tea extracts in these products also help significantly. Sunscreen is essential for preventing conditions such as premature ageing, tanning, sunburn, and even skin cancer. Drinking 8-10 glasses of water a day not only flushes out toxins but also hydrates the skin, making it supple and adding a lasting glow.

author: Steven Petrow
title: Five tips for aging better and healthier - The Washington Post
mainText: Steven Petrow, a contributing columnist for The Washington Post, shares his insights on how to age better and healthier. He reflects on his own experiences and observations of his parents' aging process, and how he vowed to avoid their mistakes. He highlights the importance of acknowledging physical and mental changes that come with age, and the dangers of denial. He shares a personal anecdote about his father's refusal to use a cane or walker, leading to frequent falls and eventually a fatal fall. Petrow admits that despite witnessing his father's stubbornness, he too found himself ignoring his own advice as he aged. He shares an instance where he attempted to reach a book from a high shelf without using a stepladder, realizing in that moment that he was repeating his father's mistakes. He concludes that aging smarter is not as easy as it seems, and despite our best efforts, we often end up repeating our parents' patterns. However, he emphasizes that aging does not have to be associated with illness, loneliness, and disability. He cites Deborah Carr, a sociologist who wrote in her 2023 book, 'Aging in America', that older adults in 2050 will lead very different lives than those who are retirement-age today. Petrow ends with a list of practical tips for aging better: ask for help when something is out of reach, use a cane or walker if balance becomes an issue, don't let denial lead to unwise choices, and fall-proof your home.

author: City Air News
title: International Sports Day and World Health Day celebrated - Cityairnews
mainText: The International Day of Sport for Development and Peace (IDSDP) and World Health Day were celebrated globally, emphasizing the significant role of sports in fostering unity among diverse communities and promoting health and well-being. The United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) established IDSDP, which is celebrated annually on April 6, to highlight the importance of sports in promoting peace and development worldwide. On the other hand, World Health Day, marked by the International Olympic Committee (IOC), underscores how sports and the Olympic Games can foster healthier lifestyles. The IOC President, Thomas Bach, stated that sports participation is a low-cost, high-impact tool to foster active and healthy lives throughout the year. The IOC and the World Health Organization (WHO) launched a joint program in November 2022 aiming to strengthen the role of sports in achieving the global target of a 15% reduction in physical inactivity by 2030. This initiative forms part of the IOC’s Olympism365 strategy, which aims to strengthen the role of sports in achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

author: Bloomberg
title: Covid 'radically altered' the top death causes for the first time in 30 years, Lancet says - Hindustan Times
mainText: The Lancet study, believed to be the first to compare deaths from Covid to deaths from other causes, reveals that Covid-19 became the second leading cause of death globally in the year after it was declared a pandemic. Heart disease remained the top killer, but Covid “radically altered” the main five causes of death for the first time in 30 years, displacing stroke. In 2021, 94 in every 100,000 people died from Covid, on an age-standardized basis. Since 1990, global life expectancy increased by 6.2 years, mainly due to reductions in death from diarrhoea and lower respiratory infections and better outcomes for people suffering from a stroke or ischemic heart disease. However, the Covid-19 pandemic has set us back significantly. From 2019 to 2021, progress was made in preventing deaths for most other top causes of death except for Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias and malaria. The study tracked 288 causes of death in 204 countries and territories and 811 subnational locations.

author: Parmita Uniyal
title: World Health Day 2024: 10 lifestyle tweaks to reduce cancer risk, boost longevity - Hindustan Times
mainText: An inactive lifestyle and junk food consumption is putting us at risk of cancer more than ever before. However, these lifestyle changes can help. World Health Day 2024: With each passing year, people across the globe belonging to all age groups, are finding themselves at an increased rate of cancer. The deadly disease can develop in any part of the body where cells undergo uncontrolled growth and division, leading to the formation of malignant tumours. Around 20 million cases of cancer were diagnosed worldwide in 2022, compared to 18 million in 2020 as per WHO. The number is expected to rise by a staggering 77 per cent to 35 million by 2050. (Also read: Viral fever spreading fast; expert tips to keep seasonal infections at bay) World Health Day 2024: Healthy eating patterns, weight management and physical activity can help reduce risk of cancer. Coronavirus pandemic may also be one of the many reasons cancer cases are on upswing. Lockdown led to disruption in healthcare services and delayed screenings and diagnoses. Increase in stress levels, and lifestyle factors such as decreased physical activity and altered dietary habits also may have contributed to this spike in undetected or untreated cancer cases. Ageing population across the globe, tobacco, alcohol and obesity are the key factors behind the increasing incidence of cancer, apart from pollution, as per World Health Organization. Healthy eating patterns, weight management and physical activity can help reduce risk of cancer. On the occasion of World Health Day on Sunday, April 7, 2024, we look at the lifestyle measures that can safeguard us from the deadly disease. LIFESTYLE CHANGES TO PREVENT CANCER Dr. Juhi Shah, Paediatric Medical Oncologist at Sunrise Oncology Centre recommends 10 lifestyle choices that research has shown to help lower the risk of developing cancer: 1. Avoid tobacco: Tobacco use is a leading cause of cancer and cancer deaths. Avoid smoking and exposure to second hand smoke to reduce risk of lung, throat, mouth and pancreatic cancer. 2. Eat clean: Emphasise on fruits, vegetables, millets, lean proteins and high fibre diet. Limit red/processed meats, sugary, fried/high-fat foods, to reduce the risk of breast and gastro-intestinal cancers. Plant based diets are rich in nutrients and antioxidants which reduce inflammation and protect normal cells. 3. Maintain a healthy weight and be physically active: Obesity is linked to breast, colon, endometrium and kidney cancers. Aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise weekly, with strength training exercises. 4. Avoid alcohol consumption: Alcohol is linked to an increased risk of liver, breast and colorectal cancers.

author: PTI
title: Indian-origin neurologist's UK study to revolutionise dementia diagnosis - The Week
mainText: An Indian-origin neurologist is part of a world-class research team in the UK that has been awarded a major grant this week to build on recent breakthroughs in potential dementia blood tests and generate the evidence needed for them to be used more widely in the next five years. Dr Ashvini Keshavan, Senior Clinical Research and Honorary Consultant Neurologist Fellow at University College London (UCL), is part of the team that will focus on the most promising biomarker for Alzheimer's disease called p-tau217. A second team made up of researchers from the Universities of Oxford and Cambridge will test various proteins to detect a variety of dementia-causing diseases. Both teams will recruit participants from sites spread across the UK with the hope of its cost-effective rollout on the National Health Service (NHS) over time. Proteins that underpin various dementia-causing diseases, and particularly Alzheimer's disease, which is the commonest cause of dementia worldwide, are now detectable in blood, said Dr Keshavan. The two studies that have been awarded funding by the Blood Biomarker Challenge grant are both seeking to implement blood tests in real world settings in the UK, to see if blood tests will prove useful in confirming the presence or absence of these diseases in people who have early dementia or mild but progressive cognitive problems. We want to ensure that our research will reflect the UK's ethnic and socioeconomic diversity and are aiming to broaden access to these tests, as the current gold standard tests to confirm the presence of these diseases are currently not accessible to most UK patients because they are either expensive or invasive, she explains. The Blood Biomarker Challenge is a multi-million-pound award given by Alzheimer's Society, Alzheimer's Research UK, the UK's National Institute for Health and Research and Gates Ventures and includes funds raised by players of People's Postcode Lottery. The UCL-led study is called ADAPT and will focus on plasma p-tau217 a blood marker of Alzheimer's disease and will answer the question of whether knowledge of this test result can improve rates of Alzheimer's diagnosis in conjunction with standard memory clinic assessments. The second study is called READ-OUT, which aims to test various proteins, including novel or less well-established ones, to detect a variety of dementia-causing diseases. If our research shows that these tests are clinically useful, and cost-effective, we would be able to contribute to the case for them becoming a part of the standard of care offered in the UK. This would have the potential for individuals to receive earlier diagnoses of their specific dementia-causing disease, said Dr Keshavan.

author: Alyce Collins
title: Oatmeal as Ozempic? What Dietitians Say About 'Oatzempic' Trend - Newsweek
mainText: The 'oatzempic' trend is a recent phenomenon on social media, particularly TikTok, where it has been touted as a quick weight loss solution. The drink, which consists of half a cup of rolled oats, one cup of water, lime juice, and a sprinkle of cinnamon, does not contain any Ozempic, a medication known for causing rapid weight loss. Despite this, the oat drink is claimed to help individuals lose up to 40 pounds in two months, and the hashtag has already amassed over 1,700 tags. However, Dr. Eldad Einav, a weight loss doctor, cautions against falling for the hype, labeling it as just another crash diet. He believes that the 'oatzempic' trend is another 'magic potion diet' that promises quick weight loss without addressing the root causes of weight gain. With over 25 years of clinical experience, Dr. Einav has witnessed numerous fad diets come and go, many of which people try without considering the potential risks. Therefore, before you start preparing your oats for this trend, it's important to consult with dietitians to understand the implications of this latest weight loss hack. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), healthy weight loss should be gradual, aiming for 1 to 2 pounds per week. In contrast, 'oatzempic' claims to help people lose up to 5 pounds a week, which is why registered dietitian and nutritionist Maya Feller labels it as 'another dangerous and restrictive fad diet.' While oats are a good source of fiber, Feller suggests that 'oatzempic' does not provide sufficient vitamins, minerals, protein, or fats to be an adequate meal replacement. Long-term adherence to this trend could lead to nutrient deficiencies and loss of lean body mass, which could slow metabolism and lead to dehydration. If the research shows that these tests are clinically useful and cost-effective, they could become part of the standard care offered in the UK, potentially allowing individuals to receive earlier diagnoses of their specific dementia-causing disease, said Dr. Keshavan.

author: sahas, Buzz Staff
title: Research Reveals Alarming Link Between Hand Sanitisers And Brain Health - News18
mainText: A recent study conducted by molecular biologists has revealed that the chemicals present in disinfectants, which linger on furniture and clothes, can damage the supporting cells in the brain. This damage is more pronounced during the critical stages of organ development. The study was carried out at Case Western Reserve University, Ohio, where molecular biologist Erin Cohn and her research team studied samples and found 1823 substances of unknown toxicity. They identified two types of harmful chemicals that halt the mutation of oligodendrocyte cells and, in severe cases, kill these cells. These cells are responsible for supporting the nerves in the body by forming an insulating sheath called the myelin sheath around the nerves. This sheath helps transmit brain signals to different organs and limbs of the body. Therefore, excessive exposure to these chemicals can affect our nervous system and interfere with brain and organ functions. The first chemical compound is used in wipes, hand sanitisers, disinfectant sprays, toothpaste, and mouthwash to kill bacteria and viruses. Although these chemicals do not severely harm the body when they enter the digestive system, the other harmful chemical belongs to the organophosphate class and is used as a flame retardant. These chemicals are commonly found in furniture, electronic items, clothing, and glue. The fat-soluble organophosphate is absorbed through the skin and reaches the brain, where it can harm the oligodendrocytes, which are highly vulnerable to flame retardants.

title: Beauty lessons to take from Shoaib Malik’s third wife Sana Javed - The Times of India
mainText: Sana Javed, a Pakistani actress who predominantly works in Urdu television and debuted in 2012, recently tied the knot with Pakistani cricketer Shoaib Malik and has since been in the limelight.
