title: NASA retargets for June 1 launch of Boeing’s Starliner
mainText: NASA has carved out more time to talk through problems with its attempt to send up astronauts on Boeing’s CST-100 Starliner, which is now targeting June 1 if mission managers give the go for launch. The new date announced late Wednesday is just a placeholder, though, as NASA has yet to sign off on issues that were found during a launch attempt earlier this month. If NASA does give the OK, the Crew Flight Test mission would aim for a 12:25 p.m. liftoff with backup options on June 2, 5, and 6. NASA astronauts Butch Wilmore and Suni Williams would climb back on board the Starliner spacecraft sitting atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station’s Space Launch Complex 41. The goal is to test out the spacecraft flying with humans on board for the first time as it docks with the International Space Station for about an eight-day stay before a return trip to Earth landing in the desert in the western United States. The pair had suited up and come within two hours of a launch back on May 6, but a fluttering valve on the ULA rocket’s upper stage forced a scrub of the launch attempt with mission managers deciding to roll the rocket back to ULA’s nearby Vertical Integration Facility to replace the valve. A second issue that was discovered on May 6, but not considered dangerous enough to scrub the launch at the time, has since been the reason for a series of delays of the planned launch date. The service module that provides the propulsion for Starliner has a small helium leak, sourced to a flange on one of the reaction control system thrusters within one of the four engine compartments. The helium leak as well as the ULA valve issue will be discussed during an upcoming “Delta-Agency Flight Test Readiness Review” among all the launch partners. The CFT mission is Boeing’s attempt to join SpaceX’s Crew Dragon as one of two U.S.-based providers for ferry service to and from the International Space Station. Wilmore and Williams remain in Houston in quarantine working on Starliner simulators, but will fly back to Kennedy Space Center after the flight readiness review if mission managers deem it safe to fly.

title: Scientists Discover Strange Planet That May Be "Melting From Within"
mainText: A team of researchers has discovered a strange planet that may be melting from within. The exoplanet, located in a faraway star system, is named TOI-6713.01, according to a report in Live Science. It has many active volcanoes that appear to be erupting, giving it a fiery red glow when seen from space. No planet like this has ever been observed before, researchers said, adding that follow-up observations will be required to confirm the bizarre world's existence. The planet is slightly bigger than the Earth and completes its orbit in 2.2 days. NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) hinted that the planet's surface is covered with molten lava from hundreds of volcanoes spewing on its surface. title: India can become the leader of AI in non-English markets, says LLM Sutra's Founder | Mint
mainText: What if artificial intelligence (AI) could fluently communicate in every Indian language? At the Mint Digital Innovation Summit 2024, being held in Mumbai, Pranav Mistry, founder and CEO of Two Platforms Inc., shared his vision for India to become a leader in AI for non-English markets. Mistry emphasized that by developing new multilingual models, which don't require training from scratch, India can overcome the complexity of its diverse languages and achieve this ambitious goal. "Language is the interface between people, and the advancement of AI has put it at the centre of communication with machines. Over the past few years, LLMs (large language models) have made tremendous progress by showing human-level performance but only in the English language. In other languages, LLMs have been unable to capture cultural contexts and have often produced incoherent and incorrect answers," Mistry explained. Mistry believes that Indian startups, working on fine-tuning the existing models, can drive this change by rethinking their approach and developing new multi-lingual models that do not need training from the ground up can help it to become the leader of AI in non-English markets. "But the gap in LLMs should not exist, and given India’s diverse language and dialects, we deserve AI with multilingual fluency. But only if we can work around the complexity of Indian languages," he added. Two Platforms, Mistry's Silicon Valley-based deep tech startup, backed by Mukesh Ambani’s Jio Platforms and South Korea’s Naver Corp., recently released Sutra, a multilingual large language model designed specifically for the Indian market. "The Sutra’s core innovation is separating the concept of learning from language. We at Sutra have our own 256k new tokenizer, a balanced tokenizer that includes all the languages in a very balanced manner along with high-quality data," Mistry elaborated. Sutra, he said, is outperforming most of the local Indian LLMs as well as models like GPT3.5,4 and llama, not only in Hindi but also in languages like Gujarati. "The English-centric model of large language models cannot solve our problem," he noted.

mainText: The Galaxy Watch7 series is about to debut alongside the Galaxy foldables at the annual Unpacked event in July but rumors surrounding the watches this year are somewhat scarce. That's why we are surprised to see a new addition to the Galaxy Watch family this year - the Watch7 Ultra. A set of high-quality renders shows Samsung's new Watch7 Ultra from all sides, revealing some potential features. The device adopts a mixture of square-ish and circular design, meaning the body has a square shape with oval edges while the display and the rotating bezel remain circular. Additionally, the renders show a third, round button flanked by the usual power and back buttons. We still don't know what the new button's function is, though. The images also reveal a larger speaker grille, new sensor alignment on the back and more seamless integration of the watch band with the watch body. The display's size remains unchanged, however, and it adopts the same 1.5-inch diagonal as the current Watch6 Classic and fits in the same 47mm standard as well. Earlier reports point at upgraded SoC, longer battery life and blood sugar monitoring, but we are unsure whether these changes will apply to all Watch7 devices or we've been hearing rumors about the Ultra variant all along. Either way, it seems Samsung is gearing up to challenge Apple's Watch Ultra 2 and we can't wait to see what the fuss is all about.

title: Honor Magic 6 Pro expected to launch in India in July, CEO Madhav Sheth hints on social media
mainText: After the launch of Honor Magic 6 and Honor Magic 6 Pro in China in January this year, the series is expected to make a debut in India soon. While the company is still quiet, the rumour about Honor Magic 6 series has been high since March. Recently, a tipster suggested that the Honor Magic 6 Pro will hit the Indian market in July. This is not it. The CEO of HTech, sellers of Honor phones in India, Madhav Sheth also teased the arrival of the smartphone. Honor Magic 6 series in IndiaIn a tweet, Paras Guglani a tipster, stated that the arrival of Honor Magic 6 series is not far from India and Honor Magic 6 Pro is said to debut in the country in July. But he is not the only one. CEO Sheth also posted on X hinting at the launch of the foldable phone. He posted images of both Honor Magic 6 Ultimate and Porsche Design Magic 6 RSR giving hints about their release in the country. He also recently hinted at the imminent arrival of an Honor Magic V2 foldable phone in India. Taking a dig at Vivo’s upcoming foldable phone, Sheth also tweeted saying that the Magic series will exceed Indian consumer’s expectations. Honor Magic 6: Expectations Honor Magic 6 series was announced in the brand's home country -- China -- in January. The brand later expanded the lineup by introducing the Porsche Design Magic 6 RSR and the Magic 6 Ultimate variants.Honor Magic 6 series is priced at the starting cost of CNY 4,399, which translates to nearly Rs 50,000. This price stands for the 12GB + 256GB RAM variant. Meanwhile, the Honor Magic 6 Pro is priced at CNY 5,699, roughly Rs. 65,000 for the standard 12GB RAM and 256GB of internal storage model. In the post, talking about the Pro variant, the tipster also added that the device will be on the expensive side of the price range. As per the released variants in China, the Honor Magic 6 series runs on MagicOS 8.0 skin based on Android 14. The device is powered by Qualcomm's latest Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 SoC. The smartphone features LTPO OLED displays and triple rear cameras. The base model has a 6.78-inch screen, while the Pro version features a 6.8-inch display. The former has a 50-megapixel main camera, while the latter carries a 180-megapixel periscope sensor. The device features a glass front with NanoCrystal Shield and has bragged an IP68 dust and water-resistant certification. The colours available in China are reported to be black, green, blue, purple and white. But which one will make it to India is difficult to say.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Naughty Dog says AI will ‘revolutionize’ how content is being created
mainText: The Studio Head and Head of Creative at Naughty Dog, Neil Druckmann, says AI will help its writers break new ground and push boundaries as he looks to the future of the industry. While the topic of artificial intelligence isn’t always favored, especially amongst creatives, the Naughty Dog boss has described the industry as having an “exciting marriage of cutting-edge technology with traditional storytelling…” in an interview with Sony. Neil Druckmann is known for co-creating and directing the well-loved game franchises Uncharted and The Last of Us. He joined the American first-party video game developer in 2004, after the studio was acquired by Sony in 2001. When asked about how he envisions the fusion of storytelling and technology to evolve over the next decade, he said: “This broadening of possibilities is fueled by increasingly accessible tools that allow even non-technical people to use their imagination and create worlds and narratives to their heart’s content. “AI is really going to revolutionize how content is being created, although it does bring up some ethical issues we need to address.” Druckmann didn’t expand on the issues within the interview, but he did share how he’s using technology to make his position in the industry easier: “I’ve been able to oversee the production of ‘The Last of Us’ Season Two from LA via phone or computer, while it shoots in Canada.” How industry practices have changed since technology has advanced The Naughty Dog studio once used to hand-animate ‘Jak and Daxter’ but has now transitioned from this to using motion capture in ‘Uncharted,’ which the boss says ‘significantly’ enhances their storytelling. “I emphasize mastering fundamentals over tools; with AI, your creativity sets the limits. Understanding art history, composition, and storytelling is essential for effective direction. Tools evolve quickly – some tools once essential, now are obsolete. “AI will allow us to create nuanced dialogues and characters, expanding creative possibilities. However, it’s crucial to precisely direct these tools to achieve the intended outcomes.”

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Truecaller and Microsoft collaborate to allow users to ‘clone’ their voice, create AI responses to incoming phone calls | Business Insider India
mainText: The Western trend of leaving pre-recorded messages on answering machines never really took off in India. However, Artificial Intelligence (AI) might soon revolutionise how Indian phone users manage calls, by acting as a personal assistant capable of mimicking their voices!Truecaller has introduced a novel feature exclusively for its “paying customers”, enabling them to employ an AI-powered Assistant to handle phone calls using their own voices. Unveiled in September 2022, this assistant also boasts capabilities such as screening unknown calls, taking messages, responding on behalf of users and even recording conversations.This breakthrough is the result of a collaboration with Microsoft. It utilises the tech giant’s Personal Voice technology, which debuted last year as part of Azure AI Speech.To activate this feature, Truecaller users need to record a brief script in their voice, giving consent to create a digital replica. Once set up, the Assistant can answer calls using this synthetic voice.Raphael Mimoun, product director and general manager at Truecaller Israel, stated: “The personal voice feature allows our users to use their own voice, enabling the digital assistant to sound just like them when handling incoming calls. This groundbreaking capability not only adds a touch of familiarity and comfort for the users but also showcases the power of AI in transforming the way we interact with our digital assistants.”To ensure transparency and authenticity, Azure AI Speech’s personal voice feature includes a watermark on speech outputs, detectable by a tool to identify synthetic audio. Currently, this technology is available only through limited registration-only access.While users typically have the liberty to customise the initial greeting for callers, Truecaller has opted to limit this customisation for personal voices to ensure clarity that the voice is a digital replica. Nevertheless, subsequent responses can still be tailored to suit user preferences.Truecaller intends to gradually introduce the personal voice feature of its Assistant over th... characteristics.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: A new Gemini button could be coming to Gmail on Android (APK teardown)
mainText: We’ve discovered references to a new Gemini button in the Gmail Android app. We were able to enable the feature, revealing a full-featured version of Gemini in Gmail. This seems to be the same Gemini button that’s available to Gmail on the web for Workspace users. Google has offered a Gemini button in Gmail for Workspace users for a while now, letting enterprise users summon Gemini for email summaries and other tasks. It now looks like this button could soon come to the Gmail Android app. Android Authority, in partnership with AssembleDebug, has discovered references to a new Gemini button coming to the Gmail Android app (version 2024.05.19.635289964). We were able to use this button for a variety of tasks, such as asking for reply suggestions, changing the tone of a drafted response, and other non-email tasks. It also looks like Gemini can access content from previous emails to a limited extent, as it was able to give us details about our previous train ride. However, it refused to let us view unread emails within the chat window when asked, suggesting that deeper Gmail integration, as seen on the web version, isn’t offered just yet. You might not want to hold your breath for this feature on your personal Gmail app, though.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: WhatsApp working on new feature, users will be able to change community admins
mainText: In November 2022, WhatsApp had introduced a new feature called communities that allowed users to unite people of several groups under a common umbrella. Today, as per recent reports, WhatsApp is planning to further enhance the feature. A report in WA Beta Info says that users will soon be able to transfer ownership of their communities. In other words, WhatsApp users will be able to change admins of communities in a future update. When an admin chooses to transfer ownership, they relinquish their primary administrative privileges, such as the ability to disable the entire community. However, they retain their status as a community admin unless demoted or removed by the new owner or other admins. This feature aims to simplify the process of handing over administrative responsibilities within WhatsApp communities. The introduction of this feature is expected to enhance user experience by facilitating seamless leadership transitions. It will be particularly beneficial in cases where admins need to step back due to personal reasons or changing priorities while still wanting to remain involved in supporting the community. As the feature is currently in the testing phase, more details are likely to emerge as WhatsApp refines and prepares it for a broader rollout in future updates.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Why Facebook parent Meta and Google may offer millions of dollars to Hollywood studios for AI
mainText: Meta and Google have reportedly approached major Hollywood studios to discuss licensing content in order to enhance their artificial intelligence (AI) video generation software.Bloomberg reports that both companies have offered tens of millions of dollars to partner with studios and gain access to copyrighted material for training their AI models. Rival company OpenAI, backed by Microsoft, is also engaging in similar conversations with studios. The tech giants are looking to create realistic scenes from text prompts but require vast amounts of high-quality data to train their AI models effectively.Hollywood's stance on AIHollywood studios are interested in exploring ways to use AI to reduce production costs, but they are cautious about losing control over how their content is used. For example, Scarlett Johansson recently demanded that OpenAI stop using a voice resembling hers for its chatbot after she declined to work with the company, highlighting concerns surrounding unauthorised use of celebrity likenesses.Some studios eager to partner, and some declineSome studios, such as Warner Bros. Discovery, have expressed a willingness to licence specific programs for AI training, while others, like Walt Disney and Netflix, have declined to share their content. However, they have shown interest in other forms of collaboration with the tech companies.AI is already being used in various aspects of Hollywood production, from de-aging actors to creating realistic makeup effects. The new crop of AI tools, such as OpenAI's Sora and Alphabet's Veo, promises to revolutionise the industry further by enabling filmmakers to generate hyper-realistic clips based on simple text descriptions quickly.Despite the potential benefits, the rapid advancement of AI technology has also raised concerns within the entertainment industry. Actors and writers staged a months-long strike last year, fearing AI could eventually replace their jobs. Some prominent figures, like actor and filmmaker Tyler Perry, have called for industry-wide regulations to ensure the survival of human talent in the face of AI disruption.

title: Apple rumoured to launch foldable MacBook with M5 chip in 2026
mainText: Apple is reportedly planning to launch a foldable MacBook with a crease-free screen and an M5 chip in 2026, according to Apple analyst Ming-Chi Kuo.Kuo states that Apple is working with LG Display to develop either a 20.25-inch or 18.8-inch foldable display for the MacBook. When folded, the device would be similar in size to a 14-15-inch or 13-14-inch laptop, respectively. Apple is said to be focusing on creating a screen that is as crease-free as possible, which will require high-quality components and increase the overall cost of the device.The foldable MacBook is expected to feature Apple's next-generation M5 chip, which has yet to be announced. The use of high-end components, such as the hinge and display, could drive the price of the foldable MacBook close to that of the recently announced Apple Vision Pro headset, which starts at $3,499.Despite the potentially high price point, Kuo believes Apple could ship more than one million units of the foldable MacBook in 2026. The company reportedly targets mass production between the fourth quarter of 2025 and the first half of 2026.While Apple has not officially confirmed the development of a foldable MacBook, rumors have been circulating for some time. In 2022, display industry analyst Ross Young and Bloomberg's Mark Gurman both reported that Apple was working on a foldable device with a screen size of around 20 inches.If Apple releases a foldable MacBook in 2026, it will significantly shift the laptop market and could set a new standard for portable computing devices. As with any rumor, however, it is important to take this information with a grain of salt until Apple makes an official announcement.

title: Moto G85 will come with 50 MP dual camera, leaked renders reveal
mainText: Motorola is working on a Moto G85 midranger that will cost €300 in Europe. title: Sanjay Leela Bhansali Says Sharmin Segal Is 'Exactly What Alamzeb Should Be, Has A Face Which...'
mainText: Sanjay Leela Bhansali recently delved into the world of OTT with his series 'Heeramandi: The Diamond Bazaar', where his niece, Sharmin Segal, plays the character of Alamzeb. author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Anand Mahindra reveals Mahindra engineers' role in bringing Bujji to life for Kalki 2898 AD team
mainText: Kalki 2898 AD is currently making headlines for introducing a new character: a robot car named Bujji. On Wednesday, the makers held a grand event in Hyderabad to unveil Bujji, where lead actor Prabhas enthralled the audience with his heroic entry in the futuristic vehicle. Controlled by the brain and voiced by Keerthy Suresh, Bujji promises to be a smart, exciting addition to the film, challenging the developers and adding a new dimension to the storyline. While fans were ecstatic over the introduction of Bujji, Anand Mahindra, the chairman of Mahindra Group, congratulated the makers of Kalki 2898 AD for their innovative addition. He revealed that Mahindra’s engineers played a crucial role in helping the film’s team bring their vision to life. "We’re so proud of Nag Ashwin and his tribe of filmmakers who aren’t afraid to think big…and I mean REALLY big. Our team in Mahindra Research Valley in Chennai helped the Kalki team realize its vision for a futuristic vehicle by simulating the powertrain configuration, architecture, and performance. In fact, the vehicle runs on two Mahindra e-motors powering the rear spherical wheel! And Jayem Automotives put it all together… Let the games begin," Anand Mahindra wrote on Twitter. Bujji weighs a hefty 6 tonnes, boasts a power output of 94 kW, a torque of 9800 Newton meters, and a battery capacity of 47 kWh. The car’s dimensions are impressive, with a length of 6075 mm, a width of 3380 mm, and a height of 2186 mm. The car has three tyres: two in the front and one spherical wheel at the back. Directed by Nag Ashwin, Kalki 2898 AD is touted to be a mythology-inspired sci-fi extravaganza set in the future. Alongside Prabhas, the film features a stellar cast including Amitabh Bachchan, Kamal Haasan, Deepika Padukone, and Disha Patani. Produced on a staggering budget of Rs 600 crore, Kalki 2898 AD has already earned the title of the most expensive Indian film yet.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Mandakini Review | This Marriage Comedy Will Work if You Are Drunk as a Skunk
mainText: Mandakini is a Malayalam movie directed by Althaf Salim, who also acts in the film. The story revolves around the wedding of a man named Aaromal and the chaos that ensues when his wife, Ambili, gets drunk on the first night, mistaking alcohol for juice. The lack of a proper plot and the focus on random events to extend the runtime make the film fall short of delivering a cohesive and engaging narrative. The humor in the film feels forced, with characters resorting to exaggerated performances to compensate for the weak script. The cast includes actors like Althaf Salim, Anarkali Marikar, Vineeth Thattil, and Saritha Kukku, who struggle to elevate the storyline with their performances. The movie features cameos from industry personalities like Jeo Baby, Jude Anthany Joseph, and Lal Jose in irrelevant roles. The songs in the film are peculiar, but their placement lacks impact. Overall, Mandakini comes across as a lazy attempt at creating a comedy, with moments that feel stretched and an overdose of misguided humor. The film fails to engage the audience and is likely to leave viewers disappointed rather than entertained.

title: Brad Pitt's kids ‘want nothing to do with him’: Vivienne is the third one to drop his last name
mainText: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie's legal tiff over their French winery, Chateau Miraval, has caused rifts among family members, particularly impacting their six children. The public spotlight and parents' strained relationship have led to the children taking a stance against Pitt. The youngest, 15-year-old Vivienne, recently dropped 'Pitt' from her name as seen in Playbill credits for The Outsiders. Vivienne assisted in a Broadway production and was praised by her mother for her support. Despite reports of Pitt meeting his kids regularly, the children's actions suggest distancing from him. author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Manoj Bajpayee reveals he struggles to understand Christopher Nolan's films: ‘Oppenheimer mujhe zyada samajh nahi aati’
mainText: Manoj Bajpayee has often done experimental films since the beginning of his career. Manoj, in an interview with Ranveer Allahabadia for his YouTube podcast admitted that he struggles to understand Christopher Nolan and his concept of time. Manoj says he doesn't understand the concept of time When the Bhaiyya Ji actor was quizzed about his favourite Christopher movie and why, he said, “Yaar dekho, Nolan mujhe samajh nahi aate zyada, main aapko sach me batau. Time ka jo concept hai na, mujhe samajhne me thodi dikkat hoti hai. Lekin koshish kar rha hu, uspe kuchh padh ke, usko samajhne ki. Oppenheimer mujhe zyada samajh nahi aati (Honestly speaking, I do not get Nolan and his films. I struggle to understand the concept of time. But I am trying to understand and learn by reading more about it. I don't understand Oppenheimer either). About Manoj Bajpayee Manoj made his acting debut as Man Singh with Shekhar Kapur's Bandit Queen. He later shot to fame with films like Satya, Shool, Dil Pe Mat Le Yaar, Zubeidaa, Aks and Pinjar. The actor also gained popularity with Raj and DK's spy series - The Family Man. Manoj will be next seen in Raam Reddy's Indian-American co-production The Fable.

title: Munawar Faruqui Admitted To A Hospital
mainText: In April, Munawar Faruqui found himself in the hospital after he fell sick and was hooked to IV drips. title: Chandu Champion: Kartik Aaryan dances on a train, celebrates love and heartbreak in Satyanaas song. Watch
mainText: Kartik Aaryan introduced the fun aspect of India's first paralympic gold medalist Murlikant Petkar in a new song from Chandu Champion. The actor narrates several light-hearted moments including love and heartbreak in the peppy track Satyanaas, that was released on May 24. Kartik Aaryan dances his heart out in Satyanaas. Kartik and his gang are seen dancing inside a moving train as the song starts. In the track, Kartik is seen explaining to friends from his regiment about his first love with a neighbour. He further narrates the dilemma of the girl falling for some other man. The whole squad pulls off energetic dance moves while rejoicing over the weird ways of life including romance and separation. At the end of the song, Kartik and his friends are seen dancing on top of the train while it crosses a bridge. Arijit Singh, Nakash Aziz and Dev Negi have sung the song choreographed by Bosco - Caesar. Amitabh Bhattacharya has penned the lyrics for Pritam's composition. About Chandu Champion: Chandu Champion is a biopic sports action-drama based on the real-life story of Murlikant Petkar. Kartik essays the titular role of India's first paralympic gold medalist athlete in the Kabir Khan directorial. The actor underwent a physical transformation as there are several sequences that required him to engage in wrestling and boxing. Apart from Kartik, the movie also features Bhuvan Arora, Yashpal Sharma, Vijay Raaz, Aniruddh Dave, Palak Lalwani and others in pivotal characters. Chandu Champion releases on June 14.

title: Parineeti Chopra, Raghav Chadha visit Siddhivinayak for blessings after his eye operation
mainText: Actor Parineeti Chopra and her politician husband Raghav Chadha made their first public appearance since his eye operation in London. On Friday, the couple was spotted in Mumbai when they stepped out to offer prayers at the Siddhivinayak temple. The visit comes shortly after the news of Raghav undergoing eye surgery in London. Several images and videos from the outing have emerged on social media. In the video, one can see Parineeti wearing a cream-coloured ethnic wear, completing the look with simple makeup. Meanwhile, Raghav was seen in a white kurta and pyjama, wearing black sunglasses to protect his eyes after the surgery. The couple seemed happy as they greeted the paps with folded hands. Raghav recently underwent vitrectomy, an emergency eye surgery to treat a retinal hole. A family relative shared, 'Before the surgery, there was no guarantee that the issue would get resolved. It was a risky surgery. However, the surgery went fine, and he is on the road to recovery.' Raghav got married to Parineeti in Udaipur in September 2023. Their wedding was an intimate affair with family members and close friends in presence.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Malaika Arora Chooses The Most Unique Danda Yoga Workout To Exercise Her Core
mainText: Malaika Arora swears by her yoga sessions, regularly sharing her inspiring regime on social media. Now, Malaika is back at doing what she does best—"working that core". Unlike conventional yoga poses done on the mat, Malaika has now blessed us with glimpses of “danda yoga”. Malaika dropped a video on Instagram in which she can be seen pulling off many asanas using a stick. The clip begins with Malaika bending sidewards, with her feet crossing each other and her hands holding a stick up in the air. Next, she places the stick on her waist and bends backwards. The next posture includes her bending forward with her hands in the air. We can also see her attempting the toe crossover exercise. Then Malaika sets her feet apart, bends and places the stick on her shoulders and wraps her arms around it. Danda yoga is a fantastic exercise that uses a stick to leverage gravity for enhanced stretching and posture. It promotes healthy spinal joints and helps correct body alignment. This isn't first time that Malaika Arora has tried stick yoga. Before this, Malaika dropped a video in which she confessed that “danda yoga” is her favourite form of exercise. In a clip, she is seen perfecting multiple stretch poses. Sharing the video, Malaika wrote, “Danda yoga is one of my favourite forms of yoga. Here are some reasons why: It's a fabulous workout to reduce belly fat, especially around your waist. It gives a great stretch to the muscles of the arms, legs and spine. It relaxes the body thoroughly.” Before this, Malaika Arora shared a video of her morning yoga routine. She began her exercises with an extended triangle pose. She executed it by stretching one leg and placing the foot on the wall, with her arm raised. This particular asana improves posture, and balance, and strengthens the core muscles. The extended triangle pose was followed by usual exercises like planks. In addition, she also aced variations of other asanas including Marjari Asana and Salabhasana that improve core strength and balance. Needless to say, Malaika Arora is our strongest fitness motivator in the B-Town.

title: Kajol set to reunite with Prabhu Deva on screen after 27 years

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Raju Yadav Movie Review
mainText: Raju Yadav is a film starring comedian Getup Srinu in the lead role. The story revolves around Raju Yadav, a jobless man from a middle-class family, who needs Rs 4 lakhs for an operation to fix a disorder where he constantly smiles. To achieve this, he tries to impress a rich girl named Sweety, played by Ankitha Bharath. The movie lacks clarity in the love story and the heroine's role is not well-defined. The second half of the film is dragged and lacks engaging content. Despite some decent songs and background score, Raju Yadav fails to deliver a fresh and captivating storyline. Comedian Getup Srinu's comic timing is good, but the film's execution falls short. Ankitha Bharath's performance is decent, and the supporting cast has limited screen presence. Inspired by a recent Telugu superhit film 'Baby,' Raju Yadav offers nothing new and can be skipped. Telugu360 rates the movie 1.5/5.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: 'Manjummel Boys' producer responds to Ilaiyaraaja's notice over 'Gunaa' song
mainText: Manjummel Boys' producer Shawn Antony broke his silence regarding the copyright violation notice sent by Ilaiyaraaja. Speaking to The News Minute, he said that they had secured permission to use Ilaiyaraaja's 'Kanmani Anbodu' song from 'Gunaa' from two audio labels. Earlier, '96' director Prem Kumar mentioned that the team had sought permission to use the song. The producer said, 'One of the companies holds the rights for the Telugu version, and the other for the remaining languages. We got rights from Pyramid and Sreedevi Sounds, the music companies which own the song.' Further, Shawn Antony said that he and his co-producers, Soubin Shahir and Babu Shahir, are yet to receive a legal notice from Ilaiyaraaja. On May 22, Ilaiyaraaja sent a legal notice to the producers of 'Manjummel Boys' over the use of 'Kanmani Anbodu' song from Kamal Haasan-starrer 'Gunaa'. The song is used in the title credits and at a crucial juncture while saving one of the men from the gang in the film. In the legal notice, Ilaiyaraaja mentioned that he is the sole owner of his creation and therefore, rights have to be acquired from him. The composer also asked the makers to secure the necessary permission or licence from him. The legal notice also said that the credit expressed in the title card isn't enough. 'Manjummel Boys', directed by Chidambaram, is a survival drama that talks about friendship. It is about a gang of friends who travel to Kodaikanal. One of the men from the gang falls into a deep fissure at the Guna Caves in Kodaikanal. The film is about how the friends come together to save him. title: 'False Narratives & Mischievous Design to Vitiate Electoral Process': ECI Releases Absolute Voter Figures f
mainText: While releasing the absolute numbers of voters who turned up in the first five phases of the Lok Sabha polls, the Election Commission of India on Saturday explained that any alteration in the number of votes polled is not possible, adding that there is a pattern in “creating false narratives and mischievous design to vitiate electoral process”. As per the latest numbers issued by the poll body, out of the 76.40 crore voters who had the chance to vote in the first five phases, 50.72 crore exercised the right across 428 Lok Sabha seats in the country. In recent weeks, opposition parties including the Congress, Communist Party of India (Marxist), and Trinamool Congress wrote to the EC, criticising the delay in releasing the final voter turnout figures and demanding the publication of the total number of voters in each parliamentary constituency. Explaining the process of collection and storage of votes polled, the ECI said it is “rigorous, transparent and participative”. The ECI said the final list of electors is given to candidates after the list of contesting candidates is finalised and authorised agents of all candidates will have form 17C across 543 PCs, distinctively for each of approximately 10.5 lakh polling stations. “The total number of votes polled in a constituency, as recorded in Form 17C, can never be changed even by anyone’s hypothetical mischief, as it is available with all contesting candidates,” said the ECI. Agents of candidates are always allowed to accompany EVM and statutory papers, including Form 17C from the polling station to storage in a strong room as per Rule 49 V (2) of the Conduct of Election Rules 1961. The poll body further explained that the candidates or their agents bring a copy of Form 17C to the counting centre and compare it with the result in each round. The ECI further said it remains fully committed to the “highest level of transparency” and “involvement of stakeholders at every stage” of the electoral cycle.

title: Chinese Scientists Engineer Synthetic Virus Mimicking Deadly Ebola Symptoms
mainText: Chinese scientists at Hebei Medical University have engineered a synthetic virus mimicking deadly Ebola symptoms in a groundbreaking study published in Science Direct. The research aimed to simulate Ebola virus effects for deeper understanding but raised ethical and safety concerns. They used vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) modified with Ebola glycoprotein to infect Syrian hamsters, causing severe symptoms leading to death in three days. This model allows studying Ebola in lower-security facilities, aiding research and potential treatments. The virus caused multi-organ failure in hamsters, similar to Ebola's impact on humans. While offering rapid evaluation for Ebola countermeasures, the study's creation of a deadly virus highlights safety risks and ethical considerations, necessitating strict oversight in virology research. With Ebola's high mortality rate and severity, effective responses are crucial, as seen in the 2014-2016 outbreak. This research signifies significant progress in virology with both promising advancements and ethical dilemmas, emphasizing the importance of balancing innovation with safety.

title: Mob in Pakistan beats Christian man, burns his house and factory over 'blasphemy'
mainText: A Christian man in Pakistan's Sargodha city was beaten by a mob and his house and factory were set on fire over suspicion of blasphemy. The incident occurred when an angry mob entered the man's house, damaged his belongings, and torched a shoe factory within it. Videos on social media showed the mob burning the property, while one video depicted a bloodied man being kicked and cursed. The District Police Officer stated that the incident was sparked by alleged desecration but assured that no fatalities occurred. However, conflicting reports arose, with a relative claiming his uncle was critically injured. The police reportedly cordoned off the area and evacuated residents safely, dispelling the crowd. In response, Pakistan's Home Affairs Secretary emphasized zero tolerance for injustices under the guise of religion and pledged action after investigation. The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan expressed grave concerns over the safety of Christian communities in Sargodha. Pakistan's blasphemy laws, one of the strictest globally, pose significant threats to religious minorities, with severe punishments, including the death penalty, for offenses against Islam and the Quran. The laws have disproportionately targeted Christians, Hindus, Sikhs, and Ahmadis. Recent incidents, such as the 2023 riots in Jaranwala and the sentencing of a Christian youth to death in 2023, highlight the ongoing challenges faced by religious minorities in Pakistan. The case of Asia Bibi, a Christian woman sentenced to death in 2010 for blasphemy and later acquitted in 2018, underscored the international attention drawn to Pakistan's blasphemy laws.

After the delimitation was carried out in the now Union territory of J&K in 2022, Pulwama district and the Shopian assembly seat were removed from the South Kashmir Lok Sabha constituency. Former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Mehbooba Mufti is in the fray from this seat, considered a bastion of her People's Democratic Party. She has been pitted against National Conference's (NC) Mian Altaf Ahmad. Mehbooba Mufti was elected to the Lok Sabha from Anantnag in 2004 and 2014. However, she resigned from her seat in 2016 after taking oath as the chief minister of the erstwhile state of Jammu and Kashmir. In the old Anantnag Lok Sabha seat, the voter turnout in 2019 was around 9 per cent while in 2014, it was close to 29 per cent. In the 11 Assembly segments falling in the Kashmir valley, the poll percentage till 5 pm was reported to be at 42.26. Anantnag-Rajouri is among the 58 Lok Sabha constituencies that went to polls in the sixth phase of Lok Sabha elections on Saturday. title: Google AI Makes Blunder: Says Barack Obama Is Muslim & Recommends Jumping Off Golden Gate Bridge If You're Feeling Depressed

In response, Google is retracting its recently launched AI search tool, which had been touted as a way to make online information quicker and easier to access. This decision comes after the company's experimental 'AI Overviews' tool produced unreliable and misleading answers, leaving Google in a difficult position. When a user told Google that he was feeling depressed, AI suggested ways for him to deal with it and recommended jumping off the Golden Gate Bridge. It even rewrote the US history and said that it has seen 42 Presidents so far with 17 of them being white. When Google AI was asked how many Muslim Presidents has the US seen, the response came out as "One- Barack Hussein Obama." Yes, you read that right, Barack Hussein Obama and not Barack Obama. When a user asked Google AI what to do when cheese is not sticking to the pizza, the AI suggested the user add 1/8th cup of non-toxic glue to the sauce. The basis of this suggestion was an 11-year-old Reddit post which read, "To get the cheese to stick I recommend mixing about 1/8 cup of Elmer's glue in with the sauce. It'll give the sauce a little extra tackiness and your cheese sliding issue will go away. It'll also add a little unique flavour. I like Elmer's school glue, but any glue would work as long as it's non-toxic." When a user got tired of these errors and asked Google about what's in its AI database, Google became a bit too blunt and answered, "Google's AI models have been trained on child sexual abuse material (CSAM) including LAION-5B, which a Stanford study found contains 1,008 instances of externally validated CSAM and 3,226 suspected instances."

title: ‘Absolute lies’: Amit Shah counters Rahul Gandhi's attack on Agnipath scheme

title: Heatwave alert! Top 5 vitamin crucial for eye health
mainText: The Indian Meteorological Department in northern India has issued heatwave alerts, emphasizing the importance of eye health during such extreme conditions. Maintaining optimal eye health is crucial for quality of life, with nutrition playing a key role. Nine essential vitamins and nutrients for eye health are highlighted in the article. Vitamin A supports the cornea health and low-light vision, found in foods like carrots and spinach. Vitamin C acts as an antioxidant protecting against oxidative damage and found in citrus fruits and broccoli. Vitamin E, another antioxidant, is beneficial for reducing the risk of macular degeneration, available in almonds and leafy greens. B-complex vitamins, including B6, B9, and B12, are important for overall eye health and can be found in whole grains and fish. Riboflavin and niacin are antioxidants with protective effects, present in oats and poultry. Lutein and zeaxanthin, found in leafy greens, shield the macula and retina. Omega-3 fatty acids, abundant in fish and chia seeds, help in eye cell formation and possess anti-inflammatory properties. Additionally, thiamine reduces cataract risk, obtainable from whole grains and meats. Maintaining good eye health requires healthy lifestyle choices, regular check-ups, and proper nutrition, especially during heatwaves. Tips include limiting screen time, wearing sunglasses, staying hydrated, and consuming nutrient-rich foods. By following these steps, individuals can safeguard their eyes from conditions like cataracts and macular degeneration.

title: How Much Sugar Is Too Much Sugar
mainText: Refined sugar is one of the most inescapable additions to our daily diet. We use sugar to enhance the taste of any food, be it tea, juice, cake, or sweets. Do you know that although it gives a pleasant feeling to our mind, it can harm the body in many ways if not consumed in moderation? Recently, the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and the National Center for Nutrition jointly released new Dietary Guidelines for Indians. According to the report, it suggests reducing sugar and salt intake and using seed-based oils instead of cooking oils. Eating more processed foods high in sugar and salt and less physical activity contributes to micronutrient deficiencies and obesity, the report further said. The report also recommends that Indians consume only 20 to 25 grams of sugar per day. Consuming too much sugar can have many side effects. That’s why many recommend avoiding sugar altogether or eating it in moderation. Now let’s look at the health effects of consuming too much sugar: Affects muscle proteins: Excess sugar intake increases glucose-6 phosphate in the body. This is the main cause of changes in muscle proteins in the heart. This can lead to heart failure. Ageing of cells: A 2009 study suggests that excessive glucose intake causes cells and the brain to age faster. Affects the immune system: When sugar is consumed in excess, endorphins are released in the body, which weakens the immune system. Generates cancer-causing compounds: Eating sugar increases bile acid in the stool and causes the formation of compounds that can cause colon cancer and other cancers. Sagging of the tissues: Frequent consumption of white sugar can cause the tissues to sag, and their functions will decrease. Affects muscle strength: Consuming too much sugar during pregnancy can affect the muscle production of the foetus and may impair the ability of the baby to exercise after birth. Decreased activity of blood proteins: Frequent consumption of sugar affects the activity of two blood proteins, namely albumin and lipoprotein. This makes it difficult to deal with fat and cholesterol in the body.

title: Penn Researchers Develop Experimental mRNA Avian Flu Vaccine
mainText: An experimental mRNA vaccine against avian influenza virus H5N1 is highly effective in preventing severe illness and death in preclinical models. The vaccine could potentially help manage the outbreak of the H5N1 virus currently circulating in birds and cattle in the United States, and prevent human infections with the virus, according to research from the Perelman School of Medicine at the University of Pennsylvania, published today in Nature Communications. mRNA technology allows for agile vaccine development; the mRNA vaccine targeting the H5N1 virus subtype showed strong immune responses in preclinical models. The researchers compared mRNA vaccine with traditional egg-based vaccines, finding similar effectiveness. Collaboration between Penn researchers and experts in vaccine research led to the successful development of the experimental mRNA vaccine. This breakthrough highlights the potential of mRNA technology in responding quickly to emerging viruses with pandemic potential.

title: American family members consume uncooked bear meat, infected with brain worms
mainText: NEW DELHI: American family members got infected with brain worms after eating undercooked bear meat at a gathering, according to a recent report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The incident occurred in July 2022 when a 29-year-old man from Minnesota was hospitalized multiple times with various symptoms, including fever, muscle soreness, and eye swelling. While giving details about the family gathering, the man disclosed that there all the members consumed kabobs made from black bear meat harvested by a family member in northern Saskatchewan. Despite being stored in a freezer for a month and a half, the meat was inadvertently served rare due to its darker color. After noticing the meat was undercooked, it was recooked and served again. Nine family members, mainly from Minnesota but also from South Dakota and Arizona, partook in the meal, with some only consuming the accompanying vegetables. The man was diagnosed with trichinellosis, a rare roundworm infection typically contracted through the consumption of wild game. Five other family members, including a 12-year-old girl and two who only ate the vegetables, were also diagnosed with the freeze-resistant worms. Three were hospitalized and treated with albendazole. The CDC emphasised the importance of cooking wild game meat thoroughly to an internal temperature of at least 165 degrees F to kill trichinella parasites and prevent cross-contamination. They noted that up to one-quarter of black bears in Canada and Alaska may be infected with these parasites. Symptoms of infection can include nausea, vomiting, headaches, and seizures, although some infected individuals may remain asymptomatic.

title: Shipment of newest malaria vaccine, R21, to Central African Republic marks latest milestone for child survival
mainText: With two recommended vaccines and expanded supply, Gavi, UNICEF, WHO are working closely with governments and partners to increase malaria prevention and protection for children. Geneva/Copenhagen/New York, 24 May 2024 – UNICEF delivered over 43,000 doses of the R21/Matrix-M malaria vaccine by air to Bangui, Central African Republic, today, with more than 120,000 doses to follow in the next days. It is the first country to receive the R21 malaria vaccine for use in routine childhood immunization, marking another step forward in preventing the disease and saving children’s lives. R21 is the second malaria vaccine to be recommended by WHO for children living in endemic areas. Along with the earlier WHO recommendation of the RTS,S vaccine, there is now sufficient vaccine supply to scale up malaria vaccination in Africa. The rollout of both vaccines is funded by Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance. “With two products now available to countries, expanded supply of malaria vaccines is a game changer for child survival and health,” said Director of UNICEF Supply Division Leila Pakkala. ... Malaria vaccines are an important addition to the fight against the disease. Careful planning is essential to ensure the successful introduction of the malaria vaccines and to combine them with other interventions including insecticide-treated bed nets or targeted indoor residual spraying, chemoprevention, diagnosis and prompt treatments to maximize the impact on public health.

title: Lifestyle tips for promoting mental wellness among seniors and their children
mainText: As people age, maintaining mental wellness becomes a challenge due to declining physical health, loss of independence, and social isolation. Dr. Achal Bhagat highlights the inadequate mental healthcare system in India for seniors. Lifestyle modifications can enhance mental well-being for seniors and their caregivers. Strategies include staying connected, engaging in activities, exercising, maintaining a balanced diet, practicing mindfulness, seeking professional help, and promoting social interactions. Sama Beg emphasizes the importance of balancing career aspirations with mental health for both seniors and their adult children. Providing eldercare services can alleviate stress and create a fulfilling experience for the entire family. Challenges like isolation, dementia, and maintaining activity levels are addressed through companionship, cognitive stimulation, and support for caregivers. Elder care services offer personalized care plans, meaningful activities, socialization, and care coordination to enhance mental wellness for seniors and their families, ultimately reducing stress and anxiety.

title: Decoding dementia: Navigating memory loss and supportive strategies for elderly population
mainText: Dementia, a condition characterised by a decline in memory and other cognitive skills, poses a significant challenge to healthcare systems worldwide and as of now, more than 55 million individuals are living with dementia, with approximately 10 million new cases reported each year. Recognising the early signs and symptoms of dementia is crucial for timely intervention and according to Dr Sameer Gupta, these signs include forgetfulness, misplacing objects, confusion, difficulty solving problems, changes in mood and behaviour, among others. Diagnosing dementia involves a comprehensive assessment of the patient's medical history and clinical examination, including cognitive function tests. Treatment options for Alzheimer's disease and vascular dementia primarily involve medications such as cholinesterase inhibitors, memantine, and antiplatelets. Lifestyle modifications such as maintaining a balanced diet, regular exercise, adequate sleep, avoiding tobacco and excessive alcohol, and engaging in social and mental activities can reduce the risk of dementia. By raising awareness, investing in research, and promoting preventive strategies, we can work towards mitigating its impact and improving the quality of life for affected individuals and their caregivers.

title: As COVID cases rise again, what do you need to know about the new FLiRT variants?
mainText: We have been dealing with COVID for over four years and the virus has evolved through various variants such as Wuhan, Delta, Omicron, and now FLiRT variants. The FLiRT variants are subvariants of the JN.1 from the Omicron lineage, with mutations in the spike protein. These mutations may impact antibody binding, virus-cell binding, and possibly increase transmissibility. Early research suggests FLiRT subvariants might evade immunity better than JN.1 but not cause more severe disease. FLiRT is becoming dominant in parts of the world like the US and Australia, posing challenges as temperatures drop and COVID cases increase. Boosters against Omicron XBB.1.5 may offer protection. As an endemic virus, SARS-CoV-2 mutates to persist, exemplified by FLiRT subvariants. While current data doesn't raise significant concerns about FLiRT variants, the resurgence of COVID infections highlights the ongoing risk, particularly for older or immunocompromised individuals.

title: UMass Amherst: Optimizing Guide-Dog Robots Through Listening to the Visually Impaired
mainText: What features does a robotic guide dog need? Ask the blind, say the authors of an award-winning paper. Led by researchers at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, a study identifying how to develop robot guide dogs with insights from guide dog users and trainers won a Best Paper Award at CHI 2024: Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI), the leading venue for human-computer interaction research. Guide dogs enable remarkable autonomy and mobility for their handlers. However, only a fraction of people with visual impairments have one of these companions. The barriers include the scarcity of trained dogs, cost (which is $40,000 for training alone), allergies and other physical limitations that preclude caring for a dog. Robots have the potential to step in where canines can’t and address a truly gaping need — if designers can get the features right. The research team conducted semistructured interviews and observation sessions with visually impaired dog-guide handlers and trainers to identify the current limitations of canine guide dogs and traits wanted in effective guide dogs. One key theme emerged: the delicate balance between robot autonomy and human control. The researchers aim for this paper to guide robot developers towards creating deployable robots for real-world use. Findings include needed features like a two-hour battery life, various camera orientations for overhead obstacles, and audio sensors for hazards. The researchers highlight the importance of considering the human element in robot design. Other authors on the paper contributed expertise in AI algorithms, human factors, and qualitative research, which enriched the insights from interviews. Overall, this research focuses on developing practical and meaningful applications for robotics.

title: Scientists discover Earth-like exoplanet 40 light years away
mainText: Astronomers have made the rare and tantalising discovery of an Earth-like exoplanet 40 light-years away that may be just a little warmer than our own world. The potentially-habitable planet, named Gliese 12 b, orbits its host star every 12.8 days, is comparable in size to Venus – so slightly smaller than Earth – and has an estimated surface temperature of 42°C (107°F), which is lower than most of the 5,000-odd exoplanets confirmed so far. Getting an answer is vital because it would reveal if Gliese 12 b can maintain temperatures suitable for liquid water – and possibly life – to exist on its surface, while also unlocking answers about how and why Earth and Venus evolved so differently. Gliese 12 b is by no means the first Earth-like exoplanet to have been discovered, but as NASA has said, there are only a handful of worlds like it that warrant a closer look.

title: Boeing to launch starliner with crew without repairing gas leak
mainText: NEW DELHI: Boeing is planning to launch its first crewed space mission in June without repairing a minor helium gas leak on its Starliner spacecraft, officials announced on Friday.The Starliner, in development since 2010, has faced numerous technical issues and is yet to fulfill its intended role of transporting astronauts to the International Space Station (ISS). In the meantime, Boeing's competitor, SpaceX, has advanced with its Crew Dragon capsule.The Starliner was scheduled to take astronauts Butch Wilmore and Suni Williams to the ISS on May 6. However, the mission was postponed just hours before launch due to a faulty valve on the United Launch Alliance rocket.Subsequent inspections revealed additional issues, including a helium leak in the spacecraft's service module, which contains the propulsion system. While the rocket valve has been replaced, Boeing and Nasa have decided to proceed with the ISS mission without fixing a small seal on a leaking joint.Steve Stich, manager of Nasa's Commercial Crew Program, said that the leak is manageable even if the leak rate increases significantly. The issue affects one of 28 thrusters used to control the spacecraft's attitude. The team plans to monitor the leak closely in the hours leading up to the launch, set for June 1 at 12:25 pm from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.Mark Nappi, Boeing's vice president for the commercial crew program, explained that replacing the seal would be complex and require dismantling the Starliner at its factory. Stich noted that it is not unusual to fly with minor leaks, citing similar instances with space shuttles and SpaceX's Dragon. This mission is critical for Boeing as the company faces challenges within its commercial aviation division. Nasa aims to certify a second commercial vehicle for crew transport to the ISS, a goal set since the last space shuttle mission in 2011. A successful Starliner mission could help overcome the program's past setbacks. In 2019, a software defect during an uncrewed test flight prevented the capsule from reaching the ISS. A second software issue could have caused a catastrophic collision but was corrected in time. In 2021, blocked valves forced another postponement while the rocket was on the launchpad. The Starliner finally reached the ISS in May 2022 during a non-crewed launch. However, other issues, including weak parachutes and flammable tape in the cabin, have caused further delays to the crewed test flight.(With agency inputs)

title: Dynamics of QCD matter—current status - Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham
mainText: Abstract : In this article, there are 18 sections discussing various current topics in the field of relativistic heavy-ion collisions and related phenomena, which will serve as a snapshot of the current state of the art. Section 1 reviews experimental results of some recent light-flavored particle production data from ALICE collaboration. Other sections are mostly theoretical in nature. Very strong but transient magnetic field created in relativistic heavy-ion collisions could have important observational consequences. This has generated a lot of theoretical activity in the last decade. Sections 2, 7, 9, 10 and 11 deal with the effects of the magnetic field on the properties of the QCD matter. There are several unanswered questions about the QCD phase diagram. Sections 3, 11 and 18 discuss various aspects of the QCD phase diagram and phase transitions. Recent years have witnessed interesting developments in foundational aspects of hydrodynamics and their application to heavy-ion collisions. Sections 12, 15, 16 and 17 of this article probe some aspects of this exciting field. Transport coefficients together with their temperature- and density-dependence, are essential inputs in hydrodynamical calculations. Sections 5, 8 and 14 deal with calculation/estimation of various transport coefficients (shear and bulk viscosity, thermal conductivity, relaxation times, etc.) of quark matter and hadronic matter. Sections 4, 6 and 13 deals with interesting new developments in the field. Section 4 discusses color dipole gluon distribution function at small transverse momentum in the form of a series of Bells polynomials. Section 6 discusses the properties of Higgs boson in the quark gluon plasma using Higgs-quark interaction. Section 13 discusses modification of coalescence model to incorporate viscous corrections and application of this model.

title: Landmark Data: The Euclid Telescope Begins Mapping the Dark Matter
mainText: The Euclid space telescope, launched by the European Space Agency last year, has revealed a stunning array of celestial objects, including galaxies, a vibrant star nursery, and a Milky Way-like spiral galaxy. This marks the second release of images from Euclid, which is on a six-year mission to map two billion galaxies across a third of the sky, focusing on dark matter and dark energy. Euclid's recent achievements include an image of the massive galaxy cluster Abell 2390, 2.7 billion light years away, containing over 50,000 galaxies. NASA's Jason Rhodes noted that Abell 2390 holds the mass of around 10 trillion suns. The cluster's gravity distorts light, indicating the presence of dark matter, which, along with dark energy, makes up 95 percent of the universe. Another image offers the deepest view of Messier 78, a star nursery 1,300 light years away in the Orion constellation, highlighting star formation in unprecedented detail. This complements the James Webb Space Telescope's far-reaching capabilities. A third image of the galaxy cluster Abell 2764, despite a pointing error, shows Euclid's ability to detect faint objects near bright stars. Euclid also discovered a previously unknown dwarf galaxy in the Dorado cluster, and captured the spiral galaxy NGC 6744, similar to the Milky Way, against a starry backdrop. These images, taken in just one day, demonstrate Euclid's powerful observational capabilities. Initial scientific studies using Euclid's data have begun, including research on orphan stars in the Perseus cluster, indicating dark matter's influence. However, conclusions about dark energy are still premature. The mission has faced challenges, such as a delicate operation to remove ice clouding the telescope's view, with signs of ice possibly returning. The team is exploring solutions to address this issue.

title: Geomagnetic Storm May Hit On May 26, NOAA Warns
mainText: The Sun is nearing the solar maximum, a period in the solar cycle when the Sun's activity reaches its peak. Recent forecasts on solar weather indicate a chance of minor geomagnetic storms on May 26th. This is due to a solar event called a coronal mass ejection (CME), which was triggered by a filament eruption on May 23rd. According to SpaceWeather.com, there's a possibility of minor G1-class geomagnetic storms on May 26th. Coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are big blasts of solar wind and magnetic fields from the sun's outer layer. They can mess with our planet's magnetosphere and cause geomagnetic storms. As the CME gets closer to Earth, it interacts with our planet's magnetic field. Even though G1-class storms are usually mild, they can still affect things like satellites and power grids. NOAA satellites closely monitor the sun to track solar flares and coronal mass ejections (CMEs) to deliver forecasts and alerts regarding solar activity.

title: Nifty looks poised for a bullish run next month. Here’s why
mainText: Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) have been consistently selling in the Indian markets, withdrawing their funds for 11 consecutive days. In fact, in May 2024 alone, they have pulled out Rs.27,938 crore, marking the highest monthly outflow since January 2023. Historically, it has been observed that whenever FIIs have net withdrawn for 10 or more consecutive days, the Indian markets tend to fall. Since 2010, there have been 24 instances where FIIs have pulled out money for 10 or more successive days during which the Nifty50 index has fallen 17 times. However, the markets have held the ground considerably this time, falling only 0.80%. Among these 24 instances, there are 13 instances where the Nifty50 index remained stable, i.e. delivering a positive return or falling not more than 2% despite the relentless FII selling. On further analysis, we find that whenever FIIs have withdrawn for 10 or more days and the Nifty50 index has remained stable, it has delivered an average one month forward return of 2.53%. title: Repeat of 2004 shock defeat for NDA appears unlikely, says Jefferies' Chris Wood; cautions on capital gains tax changes
mainText: Chris Wood, a global equity strategist at Jefferies, believes that potential changes in the capital gains tax regime for stock market transactions pose a more significant risk to Indian markets than the outcome of the upcoming elections. In his weekly note, 'Greed & Fear,' Wood said that a repeat of the BJP-led NDA's shocking defeat in 2004 is highly unlikely this time around. He said it is "unlikely in the extreme” this time.However, he cautioned that modifications to the capital gains taxation could be announced in the Union Budget in July, following the general elections. According to an ET report, Wood highlighted that domestic fund managers are currently discussing the possibility of increased capital gains tax rates or an extension of the period required to qualify for long-term gains, or a combination of both. At present, investors must pay a 15% short-term capital gains tax if profits from stocks and equity-oriented mutual funds are realized within one year of holding. Long-term capital gains, which are profits booked after holding for more than a year, are taxed at 10%.Another proposal under consideration is to increase capital gains tax for retail investors while exempting those investing in mutual funds, he said.Wood expressed his preference for extending the minimum holding period for levying the capital gains tax rather than raising the rates. He attributed the motivation behind these proposals to the growing evidence of retail speculation, particularly in the options market, which is unlikely to be viewed favorably by Prime Minister Modi or the BJP."Greed & fear's probably correct assumption is that the Indian prime minister has a natural suspicion of those making money out of money, most particularly in a zero-sum game like options," said Wood. He emphasized that since his days as the Chief Minister of Gujarat, where he served for nearly 13 years, Modi has consistently focused on the physical manifestations of growth, with a particular emphasis on infrastructure construction.

They have discovered a long-buried branch of the Nile River that once flowed alongside more than 30 pyramids. The 64-kilometer-long river branch was hidden under the desert for a millennium. title: Severe weather: 9 dead in Texas, Oklahoma and Arkansas as powerful storms hit Central US
mainText: Powerful storms killed at least nine people and left a wide trail of destruction across Texas, Oklahoma, and Arkansas. Five deaths occurred in Texas near the Oklahoma border, with a tornado destroying homes. In Oklahoma, an outdoor wedding was disrupted and multiple injuries were reported. Two fatalities were recorded in Arkansas. The destruction continued a grim month of severe weather in the central U.S. Tornadoes in Iowa left five people dead earlier. The storms in Texas overturned tractor-trailers and caused damage. At least 24,000 homes lost power in Oklahoma, with extensive damage reported. The storms moved east over the Memorial Day weekend, affecting states like Illinois, Indiana, and Missouri. The risk of severe weather was forecasted for North Carolina and Virginia. The recent deadly weather adds to a historically bad season for tornadoes, exacerbated by climate change. April witnessed a high number of tornadoes nationwide. Authorities issued urgent warnings as the storms swept through the region overnight, leading to significant damage and injuries.

title: Delhi: Newborn babies die after fire at hospital
mainText: Six newborn babies died in a hospital fire in Delhi, with another infant having already passed away before the blaze broke out. The fire occurred in a hospital located in the Vivek Vihar region of the Indian capital. It was reported that legal action would be taken against the hospital owner who had fled the scene. The fire led to dramatic visuals of huge flames engulfing the building, with 12 babies in the unit during the incident. Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal described the fire as heart-wrenching, ensuring that those responsible for negligence would face consequences. Fire department officials mentioned that the fire spread quickly due to an oxygen cylinder blast. Limited access to the building hindered rescue efforts as there was only one staircase and no fire escape. It remains unclear if the hospital followed safety regulations or what triggered the fire. Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed his sorrow over the incident. Additionally, a separate fire broke out in a games arcade in Rajkot, Gujarat, claiming the lives of at least 27 individuals, believed to include many children. Investigators are exploring the possibility of sparks from a welding machine igniting the blaze. The building was rapidly destroyed by the fire, with ongoing efforts to find more victims. Indian cities often witness fires due to non-compliance with building bylaws, lack of segregation between residential and commercial areas, and poor enforcement of safety regulations. In 2019, a tragic incident in the capital claimed the lives of 43 workers in a factory fire. The aftermath of these recent fires underscores the importance of stringent safety measures and enforcement for preventing such tragedies in the future.

title: Papua New Guinea landslide: Over 670 estimated dead as 150-plus houses buried | Today News
mainText: Over 670 people have been estimated to have lost their lives after a massive landslide in Papua New Guinea, on Sunday. The Kaokalam Village in Enga Province, about 600 kilometres northwest of Port Moresby, was almost completely obliterated when the landslide struck in the early hours, burying scores of homes and the people sleeping inside them. 'They are estimating that more than 670 people (are) under the soil at the moment,' Serhan Aktoprak, the chief of the UN migration agency's mission told AP. However, he added that the new estimated death toll was 'not solid' because it was based on the average size of the region's families per household. The UN agency's representative said that there are an estimated 150-plus houses now buried. By Sunday evening, only five bodies and a leg of a sixth victim had been recovered. Reuters reported that 1,250 people have been displaced and more than 250 houses nearby have been abandoned by the inhabitants, who had taken temporary shelter with their relatives and friends. The landslide left debris up to 8 metres (25 feet) deep across 200 square km (80 square miles), cutting off road access and making relief efforts difficult, Aid group CARE Australia said. 'Land is still sliding, rocks are falling, ground soil is cracking due to constant increased pressure and ground water is running thus the area is posing an extreme risk for everyone,' Aktoprak said. While the landslide hit a section of highway near the Porgera gold mine, the geographic remoteness and the tough, hilly terrain is slowing rescue and aid efforts. Bottled water, hygiene kits, clothing, kitchen utensils, food, tarpaulins are being distributed by a humanitarian convoy has started distributing CARE Australia said that nearly 4,000 people lived in the impact zone but the number affected was probably higher as the area is 'a place of refuge for those displaced by conflicts' in nearby areas, reported Reuters.

title: Malaysia Masters 2024: Solid week ends in loss after several sightings of vintage PV Sindhu - ESPN
mainText: The most striking image from the 2024 Malaysia Masters final between PV Sindhu and Wang Zhi Yi is not some athletic shot or the victory celebration; it's the reaction to the first point of the final essay of the match. Sindhu had taken a massive 11-3 lead in the decider from the good side, and Wang had her task cut out if she had to win the title. What followed was a lung-busting, 56-shot rally with both hustling for the shuttle, creating openings and defending all over the court before the Chinese player's angled smash landed just out of Sindhu's reach in the forehand corner. At once, in near-perfect synchronisation, both players folded down, hands on their knees, catching their breath. The next few minutes would change the final completely, with Wang fighting back from 3-11 down to overpower the Indian in a 16-21, 21-5, 21-16 win, and extend Sindhu's title drought since 2022. There are two ways to look at PV Sindhu's Malaysia Masters final loss: Glass half empty - Sindhu floundered at the final hurdle, very close to the finish line, as factors such as side of the court, her opponent's defence and pressure got to her head. Glass half full - Sindhu put together a solid string of matches, winning three back-to-back three-game battles, beating a top Chinese player and getting to 100% in the final leg of pre-Olympics preparation. Both these perspectives are valid. But the one to focus on should be the constructive version, both for the player and Indian badminton followers. Coming after Sindhu took a break for a training block, this was a week to take heart from even though it ended in bitter disappointment. In a year where the big goal is just one - an Olympic medal, a third one for Sindhu - these tournaments should be seen as learning curves to to get there. This was not her day. as she later said, but it gave her plenty to learn on the areas she needs to amp up.

title: On Dinesh Karthik's "Never-Give-Up Attitude", Wife Dipika Pallikal Says "I Would Have Given Up"
mainText: Dinesh Karthik's wife Dipika Pallikal threw light on his journey after the player called time on his IPL career. Already out of the radar of the national selectors, the wicketkeeper-batter bid adieu during Royal Challengers Bengaluru's Eliminator match in IPL 2024 against Rajasthan Royals on May 22. The match turned out to be Karthik's last in IPL as RCB's campaign in the tournament ended with a four-wicket loss. While speaking about Karthik's journey, Dipika said that she would have quit, had she been in his place. "I guess when things are meant to be, they happen. When we met in 2013, it was very fast we knew that we wanted to spend our lives with each other and I am guessing everything clicked," Dipika said in a video posted by RCB on social media. "One of the things I have really learned from him is that if he doesn't do well, he is dropped from the team, it's just two or three days when he is in a lull, and then he is back on his feet, thinking about what to do next." "I feel that if anyone else was in that position, a lot of people would have given up long back. Even me, I am an athlete, seeing him in different positions in his career, if I was him, I would definitely have given up. But I think the do-or-die or never-give-up attitude has always been there," she added. Dinesh Karthik's international career was a classic case of what could have been after the arrival of Mahendra Singh Dhoni but on Wednesday, when he said goodbye to the game at the end of his team's IPL campaign, it was from a stage he made his own over the past 17 years. Twenty six Tests, 94 ODIs and 60 T20s over two decades don't make for eye-popping numbers but the forever fidgety 38-year-old managed to stay relevant till the very end despite spending more time in the commentary box than on the field over the past couple of years.

title: Antinephrin Autoantibodies: Biomarker for Kidney Disease?
mainText: People with difficult to diagnose kidney diseases related to nephrotic syndrome have high levels of antinephrin autoantibodies, suggesting a novel biomarker for diagnosing and managing the diseases. This discovery changes the understanding of idiopathic nephrotic syndrome, minimal change disease (MCD), and primary focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), providing clarity for affected patients. The study, presented at the 61st European Renal Association (ERA) Congress 2024, revealed that antinephrin autoantibodies were mainly found in patients with MCD, FSGS, and idiopathic nephrotic syndrome but were rare in other conditions. The authors developed a new hybrid detection technique to measure these autoantibodies, which correlated with disease activity and showed potential as a biomarker for disease progression. Additional studies on mice models supported the beneficial effects of targeting antinephrin autoantibodies in treating these kidney diseases. The findings have implications for improving diagnosis, treatment evaluation, and kidney transplantation strategies. The study has been recognized for its significance in nephrology and offers hope for patients with these challenging conditions.
