author: Sukanya Nandy
title: JKCET 2024 Answer Key Released on jbopee.gov.in, How to Check
mainText: The Jammu and Kashmir Board of Professional Entrance Examinations (JKBOPEE) has released the answer key for the JKCET 2024 exam. The exam took place on June 9, and the answer key is available on the official website, jkbopee.gov.in. The state-level Common Entrance Test (CET) is used to admit students to undergraduate engineering programmes at various government and private institutions in Jammu and Kashmir. Moreover, candidates can contest the answer key by submitting their objections and paying Rs 1000 per paper at the council’s offices in Srinagar or Jammu. These challenges must be submitted by June 12. How To Check JKCET 2024 Answer Key? Step 1: Go to the official website of the Jammu and Kashmir Board of Professional Entrance Examinations at jkbopee.gov.in Step 2: Locate the JKCET-2024 Answer Key link on the notice board column on the site Step 3: To access the answer key page, click the provided link. Step 4: Use the download link to save the answer key to your device. Step 5: Use the downloaded answer key to cross-check your answers and compute the probable score you might secure. How to Determine Your JKCET 2024 Score? The JKCET 2024 consisted of three sections: physics, chemistry, and mathematics, each with 180 multiple-choice questions worth one mark. The exam was held offline for three hours. To calculate their JKCET 2024 exam scores, students must add up their correct and incorrect answers. According to the exam pattern, applicants receive one mark for each valid response and a 0.25-mark penalty for each erroneous answer. — Multiply the correct answers by one. — Multiply the incorrect answers by 0.25. — To get the final score, subtract the sum of erroneous answers from the total of correct answers. JKBOPEE will soon make the JKCET 2024 results available via their official website. Candidates will need to use their login credentials to see their total score, rank, and merit list for counselling. Qualified candidates will take part in the online counselling procedure for seat allocation in engineering courses. Counselling will be done in several rounds, with a mop-up round if necessary to fill any open seats. Stay ahead with all the exam results updates on News18 Website.

author: Sumaila Zaman
title: JEE Advanced 2024 Topper: ‘Devoted 3 to 4 Hours for Self-Study,’ Read AIR 1 Ved Lahoti’s

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Retired Madras HC Judge recommends TN govt to scrap NEET for medical admissions, wants 12th marks as sole criteria
mainText: Retired judge of Madras High Court, Justice A K Rajan, is recommending the Tamil Nadu government to eliminate the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) for medical admissions and to solely consider 12th-grade marks for admission to first-year medical programs. The committee, led by Justice Rajan and formed by the DMK government in 2021, studied the impact of NEET and recommended its removal. The report emphasizes equality in opportunity for students from different educational boards and suggests normalization of scores. The committee suggests legal or legislative measures to abolish NEET and proposes using higher secondary scores as the exclusive criterion for medical admissions. It highlights the need to identify socio-economic adversities affecting student performance and proposes a framework for score re-profiling based on adversity levels. The report advocates for reforms in school education to focus on learning over coaching and to promote subject knowledge and higher-order skills. It recommends eliminating rote learning assessments and fostering acquired knowledge and skills. The report also calls for bringing all deemed universities in Tamil Nadu under the purview of state legislation to ensure alignment with the state's educational policies. A bill seeking NEET exemption has been passed by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly and awaits Presidential assent. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M K Stalin, in response to the growing opposition to NEET, has shared the committee's report in multiple languages to raise awareness about the negative effects of NEET.

title: Take steps to eliminate NEET, says panel; wants Plus 2 marks as sole criteria for medical admission
mainText: Chennai, Retired judge of Madras High Court Justice A K Rajan has recommended to the Tamil Nadu government to eliminate National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) and make higher secondary examination marks the sole criteria for admission to medical programs. The high-level committee led by the judge was formed to study the impact of NEET-based admissions, particularly focusing on the disparities it creates. The committee's report highlighted the anti-poor and anti-social justice nature of NEET. The report recommended steps for the government to eradicate NEET through legal or legislative measures, emphasizing the importance of using higher secondary exam scores for admissions. The committee also stressed the need for equal opportunities for students from different educational boards and proposed a normalization process for scores. Additionally, the report suggested identifying and addressing socio-economic adversities that affect student performance and fostering a learning-focused approach in school education. The recommendations included passing an act to eliminate NEET in medical education, restructuring admission criteria, and bringing deemed universities under the state's purview. The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly passed a bill seeking NEET exemption based on these recommendations. The Chief Minister shared the report in multiple languages to raise awareness about the negative impacts of NEET. The push to eliminate NEET gained momentum due to recent controversies and discrepancies in the exam, reflecting a nationwide opposition to the test.

author: Shanthi Rexaline
title: 'Wow:' Elon Musk Applauds Nvidia's $3-Trillion Milestone — Here's How Tesla Stock Stacks Up Against AI Gi
mainText: Nvidia Corp. NVDA shares have been on a stratospheric rally since early 2023, thanks to the head-start it had in artificial intelligence technology, and riding on its AI prowess, the Jensen Huang-led company’s market capitalization swelled past $3 trillion on Wednesday. Elon Musk was among the first to laud the feat even as the shares of his flagship venture, Tesla, Inc. TSLA have paled in comparison to Nvidia’s. When a Tesla influencer shared a screenshot of Nvidia’s stock performance on Wednesday when it became the second-most valued company, Musk expressed his appreciation with a one-word comment: “Wow.” Last week, Musk faced criticism after a report suggested that the billionaire had asked Nvidia to prioritize chip supply to X, a social-media platform he owns, and x.AI, an AI venture he has set up, over Tesla. Despite the bonhomie between Musk and Huang, from an investor perspective, Nvidia has generated mind-boggling returns since 2023, while Tesla has not been much of a profitable trade. Nvidia shares have been up about 730% since the start of 2023 compared to the merely 44% gain by Tesla. The difference is more glaring when one compares the year-to-date performance. Nvidia has added 144% this year, while Tesla has lost about 29%. Nvidia’s outperformance is a function of the company’s strategic decision to plunge headlong into an opportunity that is going to grow bigger in the years to come. Huang’s visionary leadership set the company on a course of astounding multi-year growth. Nvidia has evolved from its modest beginnings as a gaming chipmaker to as one which has a monopoly position in the AI accelerator market. For Tesla, it is the case of a series of missteps that pushed the company to the current predicament. Ever since 2022, the company has seen its volumes contract amid an industry-wide demand slowdown. To counter the macro-induced demand weakness, the electric-vehicle maker chose the wrong strategy of discounting and price reductions that set in motion a price war in the industry. Tesla’s margin continued to contract. Tesla settled Friday’s session down 0.26% at $177.48 and Nvidia closed at a split-adjusted $120.89, down about 0.1%.

author: Volker Wagener
title: 25 years later, what happened during the Kosovo war?
mainText: The war in Kosovo ended on June 10, 1999, with the adoption of UN Security Council Resolution 1244. Prior to this, NATO had started bombing Yugoslavia in March 1999 without a UN mandate, aiming to stop human rights violations against Kosovo Albanians. The Kosovo war stemmed from the breakup of Yugoslavia in the early 1990s, escalating tensions between Kosovo Albanians and Serbia. The Kosovo Liberation Army emerged, leading to armed conflict. NATO intervened after the Racak massacre in 1999. Diplomatic efforts failed, leading to NATO's intervention without a UN mandate due to accusations of planned genocide by Serbia. The German government's controversial decision to join the intervention was influenced by the alleged Operation Horseshoe and the displacement of Kosovo Albanians. Milosevic eventually backed down under pressure, leading to the Kumanovo Agreement and UN Resolution 1244, which granted autonomy to Kosovo within Yugoslavia. Kosovo declared independence in 2008, unrecognized by Serbia and certain countries. The conflict highlights the complex historical and geopolitical dynamics in the Balkans.

title: Susan Jaffe Wants to Build a New Era at American Ballet Theater
mainText: “I look forward,” she told the crowd, “to all the great strides we are going to make together.” It was the 531st day of her tenure, and Jaffe, 62, was drained. For almost a year, she had served not only as Ballet Theater’s artistic chief — coaching dancers, hiring choreographers, planning seasons — but also as its executive director following the sudden resignation last year of Janet Rollé, who previously served in that position. Wearing two hats has meant that she is sometimes working 18-hour days, leading rehearsals of “Giselle” and “Swan Lake” one minute, scrutinizing tour schedules and budgets the next. “I start my day with back-to-back meetings — just back to back to back to back to back to back to back meetings — and then I go directly into rehearsal,” she said in an interview at her office in the Flatiron district of Manhattan.

author: Rebecca Hersher
title: Climate change is deadly. Exactly how deadly? Depends who's counting
mainText: No one in eastern Kentucky could remember rain as intense as what fell in July 2022. In just five days, more than 14 inches of rain inundated the region's rural counties, causing deadly flash floods. However, determining the exact death toll from such climate-driven disasters is complicated due to inconsistent counting methods among government agencies. The National Climate Assessment estimates that upwards of 1,300 people die in the U.S. each year due to heat alone, but definitive and consistent data collection is lacking. Disparities in death counts were noted after Hurricane Maria hit Puerto Rico in 2017, highlighting the need for standardized counting methods. Heat waves are the deadliest form of climate-related extreme weather, closely linked to climate change, yet the number of deaths attributed to heat waves in the U.S. varies widely across different agencies. Similarly, wildfire-related deaths are often undercounted, with suicides after wildfires not being included in official counts. Indirect deaths related to weather events, such as those caused by power outages during disasters, are not consistently counted. The lack of uniformity in counting standards leads to confusion and affects disaster response efforts and resource allocations. Standardized and accurate data about disaster-related deaths can help save lives by informing mitigation measures, evacuation plans, and resource allocation. Accurate death counts are also important for providing financial assistance to families of victims and shaping policies to combat climate change on national and global levels. Policymakers rely on mortality data to understand the human cost of climate change and justify actions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Accurate death counts after disasters have personal, political, and financial significance, influencing relief fund disbursement, policy decisions, and public perception of disasters.

author: Science X
title: India's heat wave longest ever, worse to come
mainText: India's heat wave is the longest ever to hit the country, the government's top weather expert said Monday as he warned people will face increasingly oppressive temperatures. Parts of northern India have been gripped by a heat wave since mid-May, with temperatures soaring over 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit). "This has been the longest spell because it has been experienced for about 24 days in different parts of the country," the head of India's Meteorological Department (IMD), Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, said in an interview with the Indian Express daily. The mercury is expected to fall as the annual monsoon rains move north this month, but Mohapatra cautioned worse will follow. "Heat waves will be more frequent, durable and intense, if precautionary or preventive measures are not taken," he said. India is the world's third-biggest emitter of greenhouse gases but has committed to achieve a net zero emissions economy by 2070 -- two decades after most of the industrialized West. For now, it is overwhelmingly reliant on coal for power generation. "Human activities, increasing population, industrialization, and transport mechanisms are leading to increased concentration of carbon monoxide, methane and chlorocarbons," Mohapatra said. "We are endangering not only ourselves, but also our future generations." Scientific research shows climate change is causing heat waves to become longer, more frequent and more intense. The latest heat wave has seen temperatures in New Delhi match the capital's previous record high: 49.2C (120.5F) clocked in 2022. As people sought relief from the scorching temperatures, the electricity grid groaned under a record peak power demand of 8,302 megawatts. On May 29, an automatic weather station in the Delhi suburb of Mungeshpur recorded a high of 52.9C (127.2F), but the temperature was the result of a faulty sensor. Elsewhere in Delhi, 17 other city stations hit a maximum of 49C (120.2F) the same day. "We constituted an expert committee, which observed readings for the next two days and found there were problems with the sensor," Mohapatra said. While the IMB had raised its concerns about the recording within hours, Mohapatra confirmed for the first time that the sensor was faulty. "We inspect the AWS (automatic weather stations) every six months," he said. "But in between a bird or a monkey can disturb it". © 2024 AFP

author: Science X
title: Flooding and landslides kill three in Vietnam's north
mainText: Flooding and landslides in northern Vietnam have killed three people, state media said Monday, after days of heavy rain that partially submerged thousands of homes. Images on state media showed water gushing down the steep roads of mountainous Ha Giang province, a popular spot for motorcycle tours, with vehicles overturned and abandoned in the floodwater. Residents in Ha Giang city stood on rooftops waiting for rescue. Around 400 foreign tourists were evacuated from the flooded area. It has been raining heavily and continuously in the province since Saturday. Thousands of homes have been partially submerged and many roads damaged, state media said. High water on the Lo river had triggered "floods and landslides", according to a statement on the website of the provincial authorities. Access to three communes bordering China had been cut off due to landslides, the statement said. Three people died after being swept away in floodwater or buried in landslides, according to state-run Voice of Vietnam. Serious flooding was also reported over the weekend in the northern port city of Hai Phong and Quang Ninh province where UNESCO World Heritage site Ha Long Bay is located. Vietnam is frequently lashed by harsh weather in the rainy season between June and November. Last year, natural disasters including floods and landslides left 169 people dead or missing in the Southeast Asian nation. Scientists have warned that extreme weather events globally are becoming more intense and frequent due to climate change. © 2024 AFP

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Weather tracker: May sets new global temperature record
mainText: May 2024 has set a new global temperature record, with an average surface air temperature of 15.91C. This figure is 0.65C above the 1991-2020 average for May and 0.19C higher than the previous record set in May 2020. This continues a remarkable series, as it marks the 12th consecutive month of record-breaking warmth for each respective month. The significance of May 2024’s temperature extends beyond recent records. It is 1.52C above the estimated average for May during the pre-industrial period of 1850-1900, underscoring the long-term impact of global warming. Additionally, the global average temperature for the past 12 months (June 2023-May 2024) reached an unprecedented level, standing 0.75C above the 1991-2020 average and 1.63C above the pre-industrial baseline. In Europe, May 2024 was notably warm, with average temperatures 0.88C above the 1991-2020 average for May. This makes it the third warmest May in history for the continent. While temperatures soared in many regions, the eastern equatorial Pacific showed below-average temperatures, suggesting a developing La Niña event. However, air temperatures over the ocean remained unusually high in many areas, contributing to the overall global temperature increase. Sea surface temperatures (SST) also hit a new high in May 2024 despite the developing La Niña as the average SST over the area between 60 degrees south and 60 degrees north was 20.93C, the highest ever recorded for May. Extreme heat has continued into early June for many parts of the world, with heatwaves gripping southern parts of Europe, the Mediterranean, Northern Africa, the Middle East and Asia. It was reported that in just the first six days of June, 80 countries had already broken monthly or all time temperature records. In Egypt, temperatures reached an all-time record of 50.9C in Aswan on Friday 7 June, exceeding the previous national high of 50.3C from 1961 in Kharga. Additionally, this has set a new record for the highest temperature ever reliably recorded across the whole of Africa for the month of June. It is also very hot around the Middle East and eastern Mediterranean too as further temperature records are expected to fall during the rest of the month with no signs of the relentless heat to end anytime soon.

author: Mark Stevenson
title: In Mexico’s heat wave monkeys are still dying and lions are getting popsicles
mainText: Amid Mexico’s heat wave and drought, various animals are suffering, and efforts to rescue and care for them are underway. NGOs are rescuing monkeys with heatstroke, while the government is focusing on cooling animals in state-run zoos, such as giving lions frozen meat popsicles. A heat dome over the southern Gulf and Central America has caused extreme heat and drought, affecting wildlife especially in central and southern Mexico. Monkeys in Tabasco are facing severe fluid loss, with over 250 howler monkeys dead. NGOs like COBIUS are leading rescue efforts, as government budget cuts have limited official support. Birds and other animals are also being affected, with rescuers struggling to rehydrate and care for them. Some areas have seen temperatures reach 120 degrees Fahrenheit, leading to mass animal distress. The incoming environmental scientist president has expressed commitment to environmental causes. Despite challenges and lack of resources, efforts are being made to save and care for distressed wildlife in Mexico.

author: Audrey Conklin
title: Kansas high school ‘assassin’ game ends with girl’s father allegedly shooting, paralyzing teen
mainText: A group of Kansas high schoolers' "senior assassin" prank involving gel bead guns erupted into chaos last month when it ended in a teenager being shot with a real gun and paralyzed from the waist down, a recently filed affidavit shows. Sedgwick Sheriff's Office deputies initially responded to a shooting outside a Goddard Walmart just before 5 p.m. May 11 and found 18-year-old Anakin Zehring suffering from a gunshot wound to his back, which hit his liver, kidney and spinal cord, paralyzing him, according to police and a GoFundMe organized by Zehring's parents. "On May 11th, our lives changed forever when my son was involved in the tragic incident at the Goddard Walmart shooting," his parents wrote on the GoFundMe page. "He sustained severe injuries, including a bullet wound that punctured his duodenum (upper part of the small intestine) and damaged his spinal cord, causing loss of sensation from the waist down. Despite undergoing four surgeries and intense medical care, his recovery journey is just beginning, and we need your help." A 16-year-old and 17-year-old boy were with Zehring in the vehicle when he was struck but ran from the scene. Authorities ultimately caught up with the two teenage witnesses and questioned them, an affidavit states. The three friends had been playing "senior assassin" – a social media-based game usually involving high school seniors targeting others with water guns and gel-bead guns. Participants often record the "attacks" and post them to social media. The game resulted in two Long Island schools going into lockdown on Monday, according to News 12. In Zehring's case, he and his friends allegedly shot at two other juveniles – a 17-year-old female identified as S.C. and her 17-year-old boyfriend identified as G.B. – outside the Goddard Walmart with a gel-bead gun. Zehring told police his friend shot the gel blaster while his friend told police it was Zehring who fired at the two teenagers. The female teenager called her father, Ruben Marcus Contreras, and told him what had happened. Contreras then drove to the Walmart and later found Zehring and his friends in their Chevrolet Spark, took a handgun out of his waistband and allegedly shot into the vehicle, striking the 18-year-old victim, authorities said in the affidavit. Contreras has since been charged with first-degree attempted murder and has been released from the Sedgwick County Jail on bond. His attorney could not be reached for comment. A Walmart employee overheard the teenagers in the Spark shout, "I'm your senior assassin," before shooting the gel blaster and contacted his manager. S.C. heard them shout the same thing. The three teenagers tried to enter the Walmart shortly after targeting S.C. and G.B., but a manager escorted them outside the store, according to the affidavit. "As G.B. and S.C. walked out of the Walmart, G.B. went to confront the males as they were walking into the Walmart and one of the males called him b— and later told him to meet him out back of the Walmart. G.B. and S.C. walked over to where they parked and moved their vehicle to the pickup area for online orders and waited for CONTRERAS to show up," the affidavit states. When Contreras arrived, his daughter and her boyfriend pointed out the three teenage "assassins" getting into their Chevrolet Spark in the parking lot. A witness told investigators that he saw Contreras approach them and try to open the car's door handle to stop them from leaving. The witness "stated he observed the vehicle move forward and then heard pop." The same witness "observed the vehicle pull forward and turn west and take off at high rate of speed and hit metal shipping container." The witness walked over to Contreras and asked what happened. Contreras allegedly said, "They shot my daughter," multiple times, according to the affidavit. The witness then walked over to the victim vehicle and apparently saw the driver, later identified as Zehring, suffering from a gunshot wound. Zehring told the witness he could not feel his legs. Original article source: Kansas high school ‘assassin’ game ends with girl’s father allegedly shooting, paralyzing teen

author: Fin24
title: India's heatwave longest ever, worse to come
mainText: India's heatwave is the longest ever to hit the country, the government's top weather expert said. Parts of northern India have been gripped by a heatwave since mid-May, with temperatures soaring over 45 degrees Celsius. Scientific research shows climate change is causing heatwaves to become longer, more frequent and more intense. "This has been the longest spell because it has been experienced for about 24 days in different parts of the country," the head of India's Meteorological Department (IMD), Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, said in an interview with the Indian Express daily. The mercury is expected to fall as the annual monsoon rains move north this month, but Mohapatra cautioned worse will follow. "Heatwaves will be more frequent, durable and intense, if precautionary or preventive measures are not taken," he said. India is the world's third-biggest emitter of greenhouse gases but has committed to achieve a net zero emissions economy by 2070 -- two decades after most of the industrialised West. For now, it is overwhelmingly reliant on coal for power generation. "Human activities, increasing population, industrialisation and transport mechanisms are leading to increased concentration of carbon monoxide, methane and chlorocarbons," Mohapatra said. "We are endangering not only ourselves, but also our future generations." Scientific research shows climate change is causing heatwaves to become longer, more frequent and more intense. The latest heatwave has seen temperatures in New Delhi match the capital's previous record high: 49.2C clocked in 2022. As people sought relief from the scorching temperatures, the electricity grid groaned under a record peak power demand of 8,302 megawatts. On 29 May, an automatic weather station in the Delhi suburb of Mungeshpur recorded a high of 52.9C, but the temperature was the result of a faulty sensor. Elsewhere in Delhi, 17 other city stations hit a maximum of 49C the same day. "We constituted an expert committee, which observed readings for the next two days and found there were problems with the sensor," Mohapatra said. While the IMB had raised its concerns about the recording within hours, Mohapatra confirmed for the first time that the sensor was faulty. "We inspect the AWS (automatic weather stations) every six months," he said. "But in between a bird or a monkey can disturb it".

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Homage in Huesca: George Orwell's son honours writer's Spanish civil war ambition
mainText: With a tender kiss, George Orwell’s son made a quiet gesture to his father: in a way, the writer had finally come home. Richard Blair, Orwell's son, along with Spanish historian Victor Pardo, led a campaign to erect a bronze relief of Orwell in Huesca, Spain, where Orwell fought in the Spanish civil war. This memorial, funded by campaigns in Britain and Spain, was a symbolic fulfillment of Orwell's wish to make it to Huesca. Blair expressed pride and emotion during the ceremony, feeling that it cemented their relationship with Huesca. Blair, adopted by Orwell and his wife Eileen, recalled moments with his father, highlighting Orwell's sense of humor and the near-death experience they had in Scotland. The region in Spain is currently embroiled in controversy over the civil war era, with right-wing coalitions accused of trying to whitewash Franco's dictatorship. While Spain introduced a Democratic Memory Law, the PP and Vox coalitions aim to replace it with 'harmony laws.' Despite his father's involvement, Blair hesitates to be drawn into Spanish political controversies. Orwell, who fought in the Spanish civil war and survived being shot, passed away in 1950. The campaign for the memorial received support from Blair, Eton College, and others. Spanish historian Pardo highlighted Orwell's time in Spain as the most important in his life, celebrating a man who sought truth and defended liberty. The memorial ceremony was emotional for Quentin Kopp, Orwell Society's chair, who emphasized the significance of Orwell's honest reporting during the war. Kopp, whose father Georges Kopp was Orwell's commanding officer, married into the Orwell family, connecting him as cousins with Richard Blair. The project was considered necessary to honor Orwell's legacy and the importance of his account in 'Homage to Catalonia' in Spain's history.

author: Juan Carlos Monterrey Gómez
title: Joe Biden’s TikTok crusade ignores the real China threat
mainText: The Biden administration’s preoccupation with TikTok is distracting us from a far more ominous danger. While China is frequently branded as the “greatest long-term threat” to US security, its most formidable weapon is not a viral dance app. The true peril lies in China’s swift technological advance, particularly in the clean energy sector. China currently manufactures 86 per cent of the world’s lithium-ion batteries, 80 per cent of solar panel components, 67 per cent of wind turbine nacelles, and almost two-thirds of electric vehicles. Its staggering investments in clean energy and low-carbon manufacturing account for almost half of global spending, leaving the United States woefully trailing. Last year’s COP28 climate change conference witnessed the signing of the historic UAE Consensus by almost 200 countries. Among their commitments were agreements to transition away from fossil fuels and to triple the capacity of renewable energy sources. As the world embarks on this “unstoppable” shift towards a new era of clean technology, China stands uniquely poised to meet the burgeoning demand and claim the rewards for itself. In stark contrast, the Biden administration’s ambitious trillion-dollar investment package is grappling against a web of bureaucratic red tape. Recent analysis tells us that less than 17 per cent of these funds have been awarded, with just six months left before a potential change in power that could see Trump overturn the entire initiative. Unless his administration can rapidly pivot, Biden’s legacy risks being marked by well-intentioned failures.

author: Leslie Bridgers
title: How a celebrity sighting influenced my Big Fin Poke order
mainText: When poke bowls first came into my life, it was the multitude of topping options that excited me most. I loved that, often at no extra cost, I could customize a bowl exactly to my preferences – kind of like a salad bar but with value-added items like crab salad and crunchy garlic in place of those pedestrian croutons and carrot shreds. But, in time, the novelty of concocting the perfect poke bowl has given way to the convenience of ordering a pre-selected combination, even if it has something like corn or pineapple that I’ll try to eat around. For a while, I’ve been eyeing the torched salmon special at fast-casual mini chain Big Fin Poke, but its simplicity kept me from ordering it. Aside from the main event – mayo-slathered salmon topped with shoyu sauce and togarashi – the rice bowl consists of green onion, avocado, cucumber and pickled ginger. Was it even worth getting a poke bowl without maxing out the mix-ins? Was it worth denying myself the mound of seaweed salad or the pop of masago until my next visit? I couldn’t quite get myself there until, like a true American, I was swayed by celebrity influence. I was at Big Fin’s location by the Maine Mall, fresh off a “New Girl” binge, when the actor who played Zooey Deschanel’s sometimes boyfriend walked in. Sure, I had to Google his name (David Walton), but I was still starstruck. And then, in an almost inaudibly deep voice, he ordered the torched salmon bowl. If it’s good enough for that somewhat famous guy, I decided, it’s good enough for me. And so, on a recent visit to Big Fin’s Rock Row location, I finally went through with the order. Another thing that had kept me from getting it was the lack of raw fish. I cook salmon myself all the time, so it didn’t seem special enough to order out. What I didn’t consider is that I have never torched salmon, and “torched” is definitely the operative word here. This fish tastes like it came off a campfire and, while it might not be for everyone, it’s worth giving a try. The other ingredients, which I mixed altogether, added creaminess and a kick that perfectly complemented the salmon, freeing me of my notions about what a poke bowl should be and marking the start of a new era in my Big Fin ordering. Torched salmon, $15.95. Big Fin Poke, 95 Rock Row, Westbrook. bigfinpoke.com

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Food
mainText: Amaretti Chocolate Cake Ingredients 250g plain chocolate 50g amaretti biscuits 100g ground almonds 150g caster sugar 100g softened butter 4 medium eggs 4 tbsps bottlegreen pomegranate & elderflower cordial 100g fresh cherries Icing sugar Method Pre-heat oven to 180c/gas mark 4. Line a 20cm springform tin. Melt 150g of chocolate. Blitz amaretti biscuits, ground almonds and sugar in food processor, add the butter, eggs and 2 tbsps of cordial, process again. Add melted chocolate and briefly process. Pour mixture into the tin, cook for 35-45mins. To finish the cake, cut melt remaining chocolate and mix with 2tbsps of cordial and cut star shapes out when it's set. Decorate cake with icing sugar, stars and chocolate dipped cherries.

author: Elisa Shoenberger
title: FYI, A Noisy Restaurant Can Impact Your Food Choices — Even How It Tastes
mainText: Nothing quite ruins a nice night out like a meal where you have to shout to talk to your dinner mate. There's scientific proof that loud noises aren't just drowning out conversations - they may also be influencing meal choices. SoundPrint found that 63% of restaurants were too loud for conversation. Loud noise can negatively impact hearing, with 70 dB being the threshold for healthy sounds. Researchers have studied how noise affects eating behavior, finding that people tend to drink more in louder environments, leading to overconsumption. Sound can also influence taste perception, with pitches of sound affecting how sweet or bitter food tastes. Other studies show how sound can enhance umami and affect food choices. Some high-end restaurants integrate soundscapes with their food. Customers can use apps like SoundPrint to find quieter places or ask for a table away from noise. Ultimately, enjoying some noise is okay as long as it's in moderation.

author: Ellen Coughlan
title: Geniuses walk among us! Quick thinkers share their creative solutions to fix tricky problems
mainText: Geniuses walk among us! Quick thinkers share their creative solutions to fix tricky problems showcasing how a little imagination can solve frustrating issues. People globally shared amusing fixes for broken items. Examples include a Dunkin' Donuts using a baby monitor when their speaking system failed, a woman patching her husband's car scratch with a sad-faced plaster, and a milk carton repurposed as a door handle. One craftsman rebuilt a car back with wood and hikers in Norway tried taping a cliff crack. Other ingenious solutions feature an oven opened by detaching cupboard handles, a homemade bin from an inverted stool, and a TV remote chained to prevent loss. Some amusing mishaps in DIY include an extreme elevator jump start and a chair 'fixed' with literal book stacking. Creative cooking methods like toasting waffles sans grill or toaster and makeshift door handles with duct tape also made the list. The article captures quirky ways individuals tackle everyday challenges with humor and resourcefulness.

author: Nikki Birrell
title: Mushrooms: A surprising superfood
mainText: Nikki Birrell shares fascinating information about mushrooms, highlighting their diverse varieties available in New Zealand and their nutritional benefits. Popular types like white, Swiss brown, and portobello mushrooms stem from the same species, Agaricus bisporus. She advises on selecting fresh mushrooms based on firmness and storing them properly in the refrigerator. Other exotic varieties like enoki, oyster, and shiitake have different shelf lives and storage requirements. Birrell stresses the importance of washing mushrooms sparingly to prevent water absorption. Mushrooms are praised for their low calorie content, rich nutrient profile, and numerous health benefits including immune-boosting properties and potential anti-cancer effects. Dried mushrooms are highlighted as a versatile pantry staple with tips on rehydrating and using them in various dishes. Birrell also provides creative ideas for incorporating rehydrated mushrooms in cooking. The article also mentions using leftover soaking liquid for enhancing the flavor of soups, gravies, and sauces. Birrell shares insights on mushroom recipes and her love for food and cooking, showcasing her expertise as a food enthusiast and world explorer.

author: Anna Rahmanan
title: Kitchen Smells You Should Worry About & Remove
mainText: When dealing with leftovers, or even fresh produce or meat products, one rule tops them all: If it smells bad, throw it out. When it comes to cheeses, though, a food that’s inherently smelly, the guidelines aren’t as straightforward. According to chef Kevin Ashton, the culinary adviser at Restaurantji, there are three ways to determine whether cheese has gone bad: the presence of abnormal mold, a change in color, or a strong smell. He notes that identifying a bad smell is the best way to determine whether cheese is safe for consumption. “If a mild cheese such as American or Jack smells strong like Limburger or blue cheese, you should throw it away,” Ashton explained. “Naturally pungent cheeses like Camembert will have a relatively strong ammonia smell when they go bad.” Ashton says, if you are familiar with the scent of a specific cheese and the one you have smells “like a more concentrated version of what you’re used to,” then you should avoid eating it. “Spoiled cheese can harbor different types of foodborne bacteria, each of which can cause specific illnesses,” Ashton explained. Salmonella, E. coli, and Listeria monocytogenes are mentioned as potential risks. Salmonella infections are characterized by abdominal cramps, vomiting, diarrhea, and fever. Escherichia coli can lead to various forms of gastroenteritis, including hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS), with symptoms like bloody diarrhea, stomach cramps, and vomiting. Listeriosis caused by Listeria monocytogenes presents symptoms such as nausea, muscle aches, fever, and diarrhea. Rule No. 2: If it smells like gas but there’s no fire, call the authorities.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Microsoft to help rural hospitals defend against rising cybersecurity attacks
mainText: Microsoft announced a new cybersecurity program to support rural hospitals in the United States facing a surge in cyberattacks, which threaten patient care and hospital operations. The healthcare sector reported a significant increase in ransomware attacks, with rural health clinics being prime targets. The program will provide free and discounted technology services, training, and support to help these hospitals improve their cybersecurity defenses. Microsoft will offer nonprofit pricing and discounts on security products, as well as free cybersecurity assessments and training. They will also provide advanced security solutions and Windows 10 security updates at no cost for eligible hospitals. The initiative was launched in collaboration with The White House, the American Hospital Association, and the National Rural Health Association, aiming to enhance cybersecurity for rural hospitals. The program aligns with Microsoft's broader efforts to support healthcare improvements in rural areas through initiatives like AI for Health. CEO of Microsoft Philanthropies, Justin Spelhaug, emphasized the importance of ensuring healthcare access across the U.S. and the role of technology in protecting rural hospitals.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Fear of stigma and rejection can lead to non-disclosure of STI status
mainText: In a recent review article researchers explored the literature on sexually transmitted infection (STI) disclosure, emphasizing the emotional complexities and strategies involved. Relationship factors significantly influence disclosure decisions, with a need for more research on recipient experiences. The review included 32 studies on STI disclosures, revealing key themes such as emotions affecting disclosure decisions, reasons for and against disclosure, and various disclosure strategies. Relationship factors play a significant role, with disclosures more likely in committed relationships. The study recommends enhancing disclosure models to consider pre-diagnosis beliefs and relationship milestones, emphasizing the need for comprehensive sexual health education and counseling to improve disclosure efficacy.

author: Anne Karpf
title: Is there asbestos in your makeup? Why women with cancer are suing big beauty brands
mainText: One place we don’t tend to think of asbestos is in the beauty industry; rarely do we consider nude eye-shadow palettes or peachy pink blushers as health hazards. Yet scores of British women are taking leading cosmetic companies to court in the United States, claiming that they contracted mesothelioma – a cancer of the lung, heart, or stomach – through their use of beauty products. The ingredient they hold responsible is talcum powder, which is ubiquitous in makeup. Almost all big brands use talc in their cosmetics, and they reject any suggestion that they may be tainted. Hannah Fletcher, diagnosed with peritoneal mesothelioma, took legal action in the US against cosmetic companies. In 2020, Jade Jenkins sued cosmetics companies in the US after being diagnosed with peritoneal mesothelioma. The world’s attention increased in 2018 with lawsuits against Johnson & Johnson (J&J) over alleged asbestos contamination. Cancer Research UK says there's no good evidence that talcum powder causes cancer, but calls for bigger studies. Some cosmetic companies have started using corn starch instead of talc. The question of risk is raised. All lawyers, doctors, and people with mesothelioma want to see cosmetic talc banned. A mass national or international campaign is needed. In the meantime, scanning cosmetics labels similar to food labels is advised. Some names have been changed.

author: Richard Eisenberg
title: Traditional Medicare or Medicare Advantage? Some retirees aren’t allowed to choose
mainText: Some retirees in 12 states are being forced to enroll in Medicare Advantage plans and are not allowed to choose traditional Medicare, risking losing their retiree health benefits if they reject the Medicare Advantage plan. The shift to Medicare Advantage has increased by 50% since 2016, with savings for companies and government employers. While there are benefits like dental, vision, and lower out-of-pocket costs, downsides include delays, treatment denials, and restrictions on preferred healthcare providers. Moreover, changing back to traditional Medicare may result in difficulties getting a Medigap plan. Public sector retirees are fighting against being forced into Medicare Advantage plans to protect their healthcare promise. Some key Medicare changes, Medicare coverage for women, medication coverage tips, and generic medications information are highlighted in the article.

title: Oculis Announces Positive Topline Results of Phase 2b RELIEF Trial with Licaminlimab, Designed to Transfo
mainText: Oculis announced positive topline results from its Phase 2b RELIEF trial with licaminlimab, a novel anti-TNFα biologic eye drop for dry eye disease. The trial showed improvements in multiple DED efficacy endpoints, with more pronounced effects in patients with the TNFR1 genetic biomarker. Licaminlimab demonstrated a rapid treatment effect on corneal inflammation, well-tolerated with no serious adverse events. The company plans to finalize Phase 3 development plans after an FDA meeting. Licaminlimab, designed with precision medicine, has the potential to transform DED treatment. It targets the root cause of DED, offering a personalized approach for improved patient outcomes. Licaminlimab has shown positive effects in treating both signs and symptoms of DED in previous trials and has been well tolerated. The Company is conducting an end-of-Phase 2 meeting with the FDA to discuss the registrational path for licaminlimab in DED and finalize Phase 3 plans. Oculis will host an analyst and investor call to discuss the trial results. DED affects about 40 million people in the US and can profoundly impact patients' quality of life. With licaminlimab, Oculis aims to address the unmet need in DED treatment and improve patient satisfaction. Licaminlimab has not received regulatory approval for commercial use. Oculis focuses on developing innovative eye care products to save sight and improve eye health globally. The company's pipeline includes candidates for diabetic macular edema, anterior uveitis, and acute optic neuritis. Oculis is committed to enhancing patient health and quality of life, supported by experienced management and leading investors.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: King Charles commits to being in Archie and Lilibet’s lives, vows to never break ties with Prince Harry
mainText: King Charles is reportedly not “content” with only seeing his grandchildren Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet on video calls from California. The youngsters live in the United States with their parents, Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, and they rarely get a chance to spend time with their grandfather, who is based in Britain. Now a source reports the King longs to see more of the children. An insider told the Mirror newspaper: “The King is absolutely committed to being present in all of his grandchildren’s lives. He values family above everything and whatever the course of his -relationship with his son he would never be content with just seeing his grandchildren on the odd video call.” Royal author Ingrid Seward also opened up about the King’s relationship with his US-based grandchildren, telling the publication: “It is a great sadness to him he doesn’t see more of Archie and Lilibet. “That is why he will never break ties with Harry. He does not want a FaceTime relationship with his son’s children. He wants to know them and be involved with their lives while they are still young enough to be able to learn from his wisdom.” However, an insider close to Harry insisted there’s nothing blocking the monarch from having a relationship with the kids, telling the Mirror: “There has never been an issue with the King being in their lives and there never would be. The door is always open.” The Duke and Duchess of Sussex stepped back from their duties as senior royals in 2020 and moved to Canada before later decamping to California with their son. Daughter Lilibet was later born in the US.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: A Person Dies Of Bird Flu In Mexico, Should You Be Concerned About The H5N2 Virus? Explained
mainText: The death of a person due to H5N2 bird flu in Mexico has raised concerns among scientists and experts. The 59-year-old man who died did not have any known exposure to infected animals, but an outbreak of H5N2 was reported in poultry in Mexico. The virus has also been found in house mice in New Mexico, suggesting a possible transmission route to humans. The man had underlying health conditions and the World Health Organization stated that his death was not solely attributable to H5N2. The risk of contracting avian flu through eating poultry is considered low by the UN's Food and Agriculture Organization. H5N2 is a type of avian influenza virus that belongs to a family of bird flu viruses primarily found in wild birds. H5N1, another subtype in the same family, has been detected in dairy cows in the US and in Kerala, India. Precautionary measures have been taken in India to prevent the spread of bird flu, including culling ducks and domesticated birds near outbreak zones. H5N1 has infected people in 23 countries since 1997, causing severe pneumonia and death in about half of the cases.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Energy drink intake linked to sudden cardiac events in patients with heart genetic disorders
mainText: In a recent study published in Heart Rhythm, researchers evaluated temporal associations between energy drink consumption and the risk of cardiac events among patients with genetic heart diseases (GHDs).BackgroundThe energy drink market has consistently grown in the United States (US). Most beverages claim to have natural ingredients, which are classified as dietary supplements. As such, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) monitoring of these products/manufacturers is not required. Energy drinks contain caffeine and other stimulants, such as guarana and taurine, that the FDA does not regulate. This raises concerns about the cumulative effects of caffeine and unregulated ingredients. Studies have suggested a potential correlation between high caffeine intake and sudden cardiac arrests (SCAs). GHD patients already exhibit a higher SCA risk. The increase in energy drinks’ popularity, higher caffeine content, and the presence of unregulated ingredients raise concerns about their use in GHD patients.The study and findingsThe present study investigated whether a potential temporal relationship exists between energy drink intake and cardiac events among GHD patients. They reviewed over 5,000 patients evaluated at the Mayo Clinic between 2000 and 2023 to identify SCA survivors. Among SCA survivors, the team identified those with a sentinel or breakthrough cardiac (BCE) event in temporal proximity to energy drink consumption. Sentinel events occurred pre-diagnosis, whereas BCEs occurred after event diagnosis and treatment initiation. Medical records were accessed for data on demographics, clinical characteristics, energy drink consumption, and its temporal relationship with SCA. Overall, 144 SCA survivors were identified; 73 were female. Seven patients, including six females, had a temporal relation between SCA and energy drink consumption. SCA was a sentinel event in six patients and a BCE in one patient. Further, three of these patients were diagnosed with SCA/idiopathic ventricular fibrillation (IVF).Long QT syndrome (LQTS) was diagnosed in two patients, and catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT) in the remaining two. Energy drink consumption was frequent in three patients and infrequent in four. The time between energy drink intake and an event varied from immediately preceding the event to within 12 hours. Different energy drinks were consumed, and their caffeine content ranged between 80 mg and > 200 mg per serving.

title: Taking the long way home from Alaska
mainText: The United States and Canadian authorities built a highway from British Columbia to Alaska after the Pearl Harbor bombing in 1941. The road is now just under 1,400 miles long and offers stunning landscapes for a family road trip. The journey passes through the Yukon, British Columbia, and Alberta, with opportunities to see wildlife. The trip is budget-friendly, with camping and picnic meals along the way. The route includes stops at national parks, hot springs, and unique attractions like Signpost Forest in Yukon. The trip continues through northern British Columbia, where travelers can spot bears, moose, caribou, and wood bison. The journey ends in Dawson Creek, British Columbia, where the highway construction began. From there, crossing into Alberta leads to Jasper National Park and Banff National Park with spectacular views of mountains, rivers, and canyons. The trip concludes in Kootenay National Park before heading to the U.S. border near Kimberley, British Columbia. Kimberley offers outdoor activities, dining options, and a charming atmosphere. The road trip is filled with natural wonders, wildlife sightings, and memorable experiences, making it a fulfilling adventure for travelers.

title: For Rs 5Cr Retirement Corpus, How Much Monthly SIP You Need To Start At Age Of 25, 30 Or 35 Years
mainText: If you start investing early there are various ways to build a good corpus fund for your retirement. Compound growth may boost your returns faster depending on the number of years you invest. The earlier you start the chances of getting more returns are high. title: Immerse Yourself In A Plate Of Chicken Yakhni Pulao This Summer, Recipe Inside
mainText: Yakhni Pulao is a beloved South Asian dish with fragrant rice, spices, and tender meat, originating in medieval Iran. It has evolved over the years with regional influences, making its way into fine dining menus. The recipe includes soaking Basmati rice, chicken pieces, spices, onions, garlic, ginger, and various seasonings. The method involves making a 'bouquet garni' with spices, boiling chicken in it, preparing a masala mix with onions, garlic, tomatoes, and spices, then adding chicken and rice. The dish is cooked on low heat with ghee and fried onions, sealed to allow flavors to meld. The Chicken Yakhni Pulao is served with Burani Raita. This recipe comes from Chef Mikhail Shahani, Cofounder and Chief Product Officer of House of Biryan. Enjoy the delectable and flavor-packed dish at a family lunch this summer.

mainText: Donald Trump made false claims and bizarre statements during an address in Las Vegas focused on immigration. author: Elissaveta M. Brandon
title: Inside one company’s plan to become the Topgolf of pickleball
mainText: The similarities between the two companies are obvious. Like Topgolf, Rally can track your play, collect player stats and automate your score. You can also play a wide selection of custom games inspired by Charity’s years-long experience coaching tennis players, and further “gamified“ by Worthington, who added fun features like fireballs shooting across the display. These include a pickleball version of the tennis game “King or Queen of the court,” which Charity used to play with her students. “I think we built [Rally] for us,” she says with a laugh. But there is one key difference between Topgolf and Rally, and that is the technology behind the game. Unlike TopGolf balls, which are outfitted with an RFID chip inside them, Rally’s balls are standard pickleballs, and you can even bring your own. Rally tracks where the ball goes thanks to four cameras equipped with a custom computer vision system and scattered around the court. (The system doesn’t use facial recognition.) The cameras work a bit like the famous Hawk-Eye system in tennis, which uses multiple camera angles to trace the ball’s trajectory and determine if it’s in or out—albeit less sophisticated. But the real magic comes from the software. If Hawk-Eye tracks the ball; RallyTrack tracks the game: it knows actual pickleball rules, and will call you out on that “kitchen fault” you just made.

author: Marcus Baram,Capital And Main
title: Kansas is—yet again—embracing trickle-down economics. The results could be devastating
mainText: Trickle-Down Economics Makes a Comeback The return of trickle-down economics—the much-criticized theory that tax cuts for corporations and the wealthy eventually result in job growth and higher wages for the middle class and working class—has inspired a fierce debate in the Kansas Legislature that has gone on for months. A bill that included a flat 5.25% personal income tax, an 8% reduction from the current rate for top earners, was approved by Republicans in both chambers, though critics say it would disproportionately benefit the wealthy in the state. The top 20% of earners in Kansas—those with average annual incomes above $315,000—would get nearly 40% of the benefits, with Koch himself receiving an estimated $485,000 in annual tax breaks under the proposal, according to the Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy, a nonpartisan research group that favors a progressive tax system. It would also cost the state almost $650 million every year once fully implemented, per ITEP. The bill was sponsored by two lawmakers who have received campaign contributions from Koch and who have significant ties to the American Legislative Exchange Council (ALEC), a national organization of conservative lawmakers and corporate interests that drafts “model legislation” for state legislatures to adopt and has long advocated for the elimination of state income taxes. Kansas state Sen. Ty Masterson was named the chairman of ALEC in December, and fellow Sen. Caryn Tyson was named the country’s legislator of the year in 2021 by the group. Neither lawmaker returned calls for comment to Capital & Main.

author: Justin Haskins
title: Europe is hell bent on forcing US companies to go woke and it has a new law to do just that
mainText: The European Union has finalized a new law called the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD), which will impact businesses globally. This law will enforce left-wing environmental and social justice rules on large companies, including those based outside the EU but providing products and services within the EU. The CSDDD mandates reducing biodiversity loss, limiting water and land consumption, guaranteeing labor union rights, and phasing out fossil fuels. Companies failing to comply could face fines up to 5% of their net worldwide turnover. The law applies to EU-based businesses with over 1,000 employees and a net turnover of $489 million, as well as non-EU companies with a net turnover of $489 million in the EU. This includes many prominent US companies operating in the EU. Businesses will be required to impose EU's ESG metrics on their supply chains, impacting numerous US businesses, large or small. CSDDD poses a threat to America's sovereignty, as EU regulations would affect US businesses and culture. The Biden administration has not taken action against the law, raising concerns about its potential negative impacts on the US economy and society. Lawmakers are urged to address this issue promptly to prevent the EU from imposing its regulations on American businesses and consumers. Time is running out to safeguard freedom and prosperity against the EU's overreach.

author: Janice Dean
title: Cuomo finally forced to tell whole truth about COVID-19 decisions that cost thousands of lives
mainText: Last year, I appeared before Congress at a hearing in Washington, D.C., to talk about how my family and thousands of others in New York lost loved ones to COVID-19 after they contracted the disease in nursing homes. Tuesday, June 11, will be the most important moment we have had when it comes to our fight for answers and accountability. It will be the first time that our former disgraced governor will sit down and be questioned under oath about his deadly decisions that we believe led to their preventable deaths. Many of you know how personal this story is for me. My husband lost both of his parents in separate facilities during the spring of 2020 after an executive order was issued, which stood for 46 days, admitting over 9,000 COVID-positive patients into a place where our most vulnerable reside. We were never warned of this decision, and there has never been a thorough investigation into why nursing homes were the first and only option to send in COVID-19 positive patients. Despite having other options, like the Javits Center, the USNS Comfort, and other makeshift provisional hospitals with thousands of empty beds, then-New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo decided instead to unleash COVID-19 into nursing homes and put the most vulnerable lives in danger. In 2022, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul hired a consulting firm based in Alexandria, Virginia, to look back at the policies and decisions made in New York during the pandemic, but it didn’t have subpoenas, and the contract will expire in just a few days. According to a recent report, the Olsen Group has billed the state for less than half of its allotted $4.3 million. There has been a proposed bill in Albany that promises hearings and investigations into state records and (most importantly) subpoenas to compel testimony from Cuomo and his former associates. Governor Cuomo, who was elected to serve and protect the people of New York through a once-in-a-lifetime pandemic, instead acted recklessly with deliberate indifference, causing thousands of avoidable nursing home deaths. He's finally going to need to answer questions under oath. I look forward to hearing Andrew Cuomo finally swear to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

author: Jake Traylor,Matt Dixon
title: After his historic guilty verdict, Trump is focused on revenge
mainText: After being found guilty on 34 counts related to falsifying business records, Donald Trump has been increasingly focused on seeking revenge against his enemies, blaming President Joe Biden and Democrats for orchestrating legal troubles against him. Trump's rhetoric of retribution has been a dominant theme in his recent interviews, where he discusses the idea of seeking revenge if he returns to the White House. Despite attempts by interviewers like Sean Hannity and Dr. Phil to discourage this notion, Trump remains firm in his stance on potential retribution. He has hinted at the possibility of imprisoning political opponents if he regains the presidency, insisting that 'revenge can be justified.' Trump's calls for revenge have resonated with his supporters, who view it as a form of accountability. However, critics and some within his own circle, like attorney Ty Cobb, have expressed concerns about the risks and dangers associated with Trump's focus on revenge. The renewed emphasis on seeking revenge comes amidst his legal battles and guilty verdict in New York. While Trump frames his calls for retribution as standing up for his supporters and seeking justice, many see it as a dangerous path that could undermine the nation's institutions. Supporters of Trump have rallied around the idea of seeking revenge, especially heightened by recent events like former adviser Steve Bannon being ordered to prison, leading to direct threats from Bannon and incendiary remarks from Trump against the Jan. 6 committee. Trump's unwavering commitment to seeking revenge has raised alarm among some observers, who fear the potential consequences of his vengeful approach.

author: Tyler Bartlam
title: 3 ways Republicans are trying to use Trump’s conviction to their advantage
mainText: For the first time in American history, a political party is set to nominate a felon as its presidential candidate. Republicans continue to rally around Donald Trump, who was found guilty in the New York hush money trial on May 30. He will be sentenced on July 11, just days before the Republican National Convention begins in Milwaukee. The team at NPR's Trump's Trials podcast analyzed three ways the GOP is leveraging Trump’s conviction to their advantage. Firstly, they are rallying the base by casting doubt on the judicial system and portraying Trump as a victim of a political conspiracy, highlighting signs of support like "our favorite felon" at rallies and fundraisers. Secondly, conservatives are seeking revenge by claiming the trial was rigged and talking about getting back at those they perceive as unjustly targeting Trump, suggesting legal actions against prosecutors and judges. Lastly, the Trump campaign is capitalizing on the situation financially, announcing a significant rise in fundraising after the verdict, with $53 million raised in the first 24 hours and $141 million in May. However, questions remain about how this money will be spent, given that some funds were previously diverted to cover legal fees. Trump is utilizing his conviction to shore up his base and funding. The article also mentions Trump's claim of legal immunity as a former president in relation to the 2020 election interference case, pending a Supreme Court decision. The outcome will impact whether the case proceeds to trial. To explore more details on how the Trump campaign is maneuvering through these circumstances, check out the full episode of the Trump’s Trials podcast.

author: Justina Otio
title: LP Not Offended Peter Obi Disowned Obidient Movement Directorate - Spokesman
mainText: The National Working Committee (NWC) of the Labour Party (LP) has said that it is not offended by the party’s former presidential candidate, Peter Obi’s statement over the controversial creation of the Obidient Movement directorate. The LP NWC opined that Obi had the right to air his grievance, adding that there was no plan or contemplation to relieve Obi of his party leadership role. Recall Obi had last week criticised the leadership of the LP over the newly created Directorate of Obidient Movement. According to him, the Obidient Movement is not under the control of any political party. In a swift reaction, the party’s NWC announced that it had rechristened the contentious directorate to reflect the Directorate of Mobilisation and Integration. Reacting to the former Anambra governor’s outburst, the National Publicity Secretary of the LP, Obiora Ifoh told Punch that the party had no hard feelings about Obi’s rebuttal. He said, “Why would the party be offended? The LP, as we always, say is united. We are not offended. I mean, if we were offended, we would make a statement in that regard. He is still the national leader of the Labour Party. “Again, how is what he said an outrage? The national leader of the party just made a clarification, which is clear enough. He said the Obidient Movement is a group of people looking forward to good governance. I agree. He also explained that the Obidient people are not necessarily members of any particular political party. As a matter of fact, you can find Obidients in other political parties. “He only advised that instead of having a directorate for the Obidients, we should have converted it to a directorate of mobilisation, which has been immediately corrected. We now have a directorate of mobilisation, which will be inaugurated tomorrow (Saturday). I think his information was very clear enough and we should respect it.”

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Protein Study May Propel New Antibiotic Development
mainText: A bacterial enzyme called histidine kinase is a promising target for new classes of antibiotics. An MIT-led team has made this enzyme water-soluble, making it easier to screen potential drugs that might interfere with its functions. By replacing hydrophobic amino acids with hydrophilic ones, the researchers created a version of histidine kinase that retained its natural functions. This enzyme is unique to bacteria, and targeting it could lead to the development of new antibiotics to combat antibiotic resistance. The study was published in Nature Communications with authors from MIT and Shanghai Jiao Tong University. The researchers used the QTY code to convert the hydrophobic histidine kinase into a water-soluble form, allowing it to retain its enzymatic function. The protein's structure was stabilized by forming hydrogen bonds with water, crucial for maintaining its function. Future applications could include targeting other enzymes like methane monooxygenase to combat climate change by converting methane into methanol. The QTY technique has broader implications for understanding how signals are transmitted across membranes, as highlighted by experts not involved in the study. The research was supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China.

author: Harsh Vardhan
title: Sunita Williams' Stay Aboard Space Station Extended; NASA Announces Return Date
mainText: Astronaut Sunita Williams, who launched to the International Space Station (ISS) last week, will spend a few more days aboard the orbiting lab. Her planned week-long stay has been extended by a few days and she will be making her return to Earth no earlier than June 18, NASA announced today. She flew to space on June 5 with astronaut Barry Wilmore in Boeing's debut crew mission onboard the Starliner spacecraft. .@NASA and @BoeingSpace teams set a return date of no earlier than Tuesday, June 18, for the agency’s Boeing Crew Flight Test. The additional time in orbit will allow the crew to perform a spacewalk on Thursday, June 13, while engineers complete #Starliner systems checkouts. Williams became the first woman to test a new spacecraft and visited the space station for the first time in 12 years in her third spaceflight. It is the third ISS mission for Wilmore as well after his previous trips in 2009 and 2014. "Ahead of turning their attention to space station support, the crew worked in partnership with Boeing engineers and flight control teams on the ground to efficiently tick through more flight test objectives and operational capability checkouts of the spacecraft," Boeing said in a statement. Williams and Wilmore are currently testing and evaluating Starliner while it is docked to the station. On June 8, the crew completed the safe haven demonstration to validate that Starliner can function as a habitat if the space station is passing a debris cloud or faces some other issue. They completed several other objectives like performing space-to-space audio checks, installing a window cover for long-duration missions and performed mock power up of undocked Starliner and propulsion system checkout procedures. Starliner's batteries have also been charged for the return journey, Boeing said. While everything is going smooth, there are a few issues facing Starliner. NASA revealed a day after the launch that a few more helium leaks were identified on the spacecraft after it entered space. The mission teams knew about the leak before the launch but they decided to go ahead anyway because it wasn't a huge concern, according to them. No new updates on the leak have been provided yet. Another problem was the failure of Starliner's thrusters as it approached the space station for docking. While four of the five failed thrusters were recovered, it remains to be seen if that will be a problem during undocking.

author: Boston University June
title: Interstellar Intruder: The Cosmic Event That Rewrote Earth’s Climate History
mainText: New astrophysical research highlights a significant cosmic event two million years ago when the solar system passed through a dense interstellar cloud. This possibly altered Earth’s climate by exposing it to enhanced cosmic radiation, supported by increased isotopes found in geological records. Earth was a very different place around two million years ago, with our early human ancestors living alongside saber-toothed tigers, mastodons, and enormous rodents. Scientists theorize that ice ages occur for a number of reasons, including the planet’s tilt and rotation, shifting plate tectonics, volcanic eruptions, and carbon dioxide levels in the atmosphere. Lead author Merav Opher, an astronomy professor at Boston University, found evidence that the solar system encountered an interstellar cloud two million years ago, affecting Earth's climate. She suggests that the sun's location in space could impact Earth's history significantly. A Local Ribbon of Cold Clouds system could have collided with the heliosphere, exposing Earth to the interstellar medium. Geological evidence shows increased isotopes in the ocean, moon, and Antarctic from the same period. Avi Loeb from Harvard University highlights the potential long-term impact of cosmic rays on Earth's evolution. Further research will focus on exploring how the solar system was influenced by external forces in the past and their impact on Earth's atmosphere and climate. Study published in Nature Astronomy.

author: Science X
title: Improved prime editing system makes gene-sized edits in human cells at therapeutic levels
mainText: Scientists at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard have improved a gene-editing technology that is now capable of inserting or substituting entire genes in the genome in human cells efficiently enough to be potentially useful for therapeutic applications. The advance, from the lab of Broad core institute member David Liu, could one day help researchers develop a single gene therapy for diseases such as cystic fibrosis that are caused by one of hundreds or thousands of different mutations in a gene. Using this new approach, they would insert a healthy copy of the gene at its native location in the genome, rather than having to create a different gene therapy to correct each mutation using other gene-editing approaches that make smaller edits. The new method uses a combination of prime editing, which can directly make a wide range of edits up to about 100 or 200 base pairs, and newly developed recombinase enzymes that efficiently insert large pieces of DNA thousands of base pairs in length at specific sites in the genome. This system, called eePASSIGE, can make gene-sized edits several times more efficiently than other similar methods, and is reported in Nature Biomedical Engineering. "To our knowledge, this is one of the first examples of programmable targeted gene integration in mammalian cells that satisfies the main criteria for potential therapeutic relevance," said Liu, who is senior author of the study, the Richard Merkin Professor and director of the Merkin Institute of Transformative Technologies in Healthcare at the Broad, a professor at Harvard University and a Howard Hughes Medical Institute investigator. "At these efficiencies, we expect that many if not most loss-of-function genetic diseases could be ameliorated or rescued, if the efficiency we observe in cultured human cells can be translated into a clinical setting." Graduate student Smriti Pandey and postdoctoral researcher Daniel Gao, both in Liu's group, were co-first authors on the study, which was also a collaboration with Mark Osborn's group at the University of Minnesota and Elliot Chaikof's group at the Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. "This system offers promising opportunities for cell therapies where it can be used to precisely insert genes into cells outside of the body before administering them to patients to treat disease, among other applications," Pandey said. "It's exciting to see the high efficiency and versatility of eePASSIGE, which could enable a new category of genomic medicines," added Gao. "We also hope that it will be a tool that scientists from across the research community can use to study basic biological questions." Prime improvements Many scientists have used prime editing to efficiently install changes to DNA that are up to dozens of base pairs in length, sufficient to correct the vast majority of known pathogenic mutations. But introducing entire healthy genes, often thousands of base pairs long, in their native location in the genome has been a long-standing goal of the gene-editing field. Not only could this potentially treat many patients regardless of which mutation they have in a disease-causing gene, but it would also preserve the surrounding DNA sequences, which would increase the likelihood that the newly installed gene is properly regulated, rather than expressed too much, too little, or at the wrong time. In 2021, Liu's lab reported a key step towards this goal and developed a prime editing approach called twinPE that installed recombinase "landing sites" in the genome, and then used natural recombinase enzymes such as Bxb1 to catalyze the insertion of new DNA into the prime edited target sites. The biotech company Prime Medicine, co-founded by Liu, soon began using this technology, which they called PASSIGE (prime-editing-assisted site-specific integrase gene editing), to develop treatments for genetic diseases. PASSIGE installs edits in only a modest fraction of cells, which is enough to treat some but probably not most genetic diseases that result from the loss of a functioning gene. So Liu's team, in the new work reported today, set out to boost PASSIGE's editing efficiency. They found that the recombinase enzyme Bxb1 was the culprit in limiting the efficiency of PASSIGE. They then used a tool previously developed by Liu's group called PACE (phage-assisted continuous evolution) to rapidly evolve more efficient versions of Bxb1 in the lab. The resulting newly evolved and engineered Bxb1 variant (eeBxb1) improved the eePASSIGE method to integrate an average of 30% of gene-sized cargo in mouse and human cells, four times more than the original technique and about 16 times more than another recently published method called PASTE. "The eePASSIGE system provides a promising foundation for studies integrating healthy gene copies at sites of our choosing in cell and animal models of genetic diseases to treat loss-of-function disorders," Liu said. "We hope this system will prove to be an important step towards realizing the benefits of targeted gene integration for patients." With this goal in mind, Liu's team is now working on combining eePASSIGE with delivery systems such as engineered virus-like particles (eVLPs) that may overcome hurdles that have traditionally limited therapeutic delivery of gene editors in the body.

title: What Cambridge Curriculum offers, how the board prepares students for international success!
mainText: In an increasingly globalized world, education systems are evolving to equip students with the skills and knowledge necessary for international success.
