author: By Erin Weeks
title: Schofield Middle School advocates for its band classroom
mainText: A classroom change is stirring up concern for the Schofield Middle School band community. Schofield Middle School’s current band class is reportedly being transferred into a classroom that was not designed for musical instruction despite currently residing in a room that was specifically built for those purposes. This has raised questions surrounding student and instructor safety and support for the arts in schools. At an Aiken County Public School District Board of Education meeting Tuesday night, Aiken High School Band Booster Club Secretary Kimberly Crapse and retired Schofield Band Director Stephanie Threlkeld voiced their opinions on the change. Crapse talked about Aiken High’s new $16M auditorium, saying that if middle school students aren’t retained by a band program, they won’t feed into high school programs. “I’m sure you’ve all seen the beautiful new auditorium investment that’s been made at the high school, but if we don’t have these programs at the middle school level, they won’t be coming along to play in that auditorium,” she said. Threlkeld talked about the current band room, saying: “It is evident that the school district spent a lot of time and money on a Schofield band room which was celebrated at its grand opening in 2003. This band room is known as one of the best middle school band rooms among state band directors … why are we spending taxpayer money renovating a room that is not designated for band when there is already a fantastic band room at Schofield Middle School?” The reason for the change has not yet been identified. A call left with Schofield was not immediately returned.

author: Travis Gettys
title: Jared Kushner's financial ties to Saudi Arabia fall under fresh scrutiny
mainText: The Senate Finance Committee has launched an investigation into Jared Kushner's overseas business activities. Sen. Ron Wyden (D-OR), who chairs the committee, asked Kushner's firm Affinity Partners for details about a $2 billion investment from the Saudi Arabian government’s Public Investment Fund in 2021 and funding from other foreign investors. “The Saudi PIF’s decision to invest $2 billion in Affinity so soon after Kushner’s departure from the Trump White House raises concerns that the investment was a reward for official actions Kushner took to benefit the Saudi government," Wyden wrote, "including preventing accountability for the Saudi government ordering the brutal murder of journalist and American citizen Jamal Khashoggi." A panel that screens investments for Saudi Arabia's Sovereign Wealth Fund warned against investing with the inexperienced Kushner, but the full board led by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman overruled that recommendation. Wyden asked Kushner's firm for details about its investments, any fees it has received and how much Kushner has been paid. "It is deeply concerning that several Middle Eastern governments are using funds managed by Affinity as a means to pay tens of millions of dollars in fees every year to former President Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, creating significant conflicts of interest and potential counterintelligence risks," Wyden wrote. "These arrangements also raise concerns that Affinity’s exclusively foreign-funded private investment funds are being exploited as a loophole by Mr. Kushner and other former U.S. government officials as a means to avoid complying with the Foreign Agents Registration Act and other U.S. laws requiring U.S. persons to disclose payments from foreign governments."

author: Meredith Colias-Pete
title: Gary mom testifies she heard shots outside before finding dying son
mainText: ZsaKenya Mathews testified she heard rapid-fire gunfire, then found her son Daqwuan Walker, 23, shot outside the front door “more than 10 times.” A young woman with him ran when the shooting started. Virgil “Reese” King, 23, of Gary, is on trial charged with murder in Walker’s death. Co-defendant Micah “Mike” Sanders, 25, took a plea deal on murder. He is facing a 45-year term if Judge Gina Jones accepts the agreement. Defense lawyer Adam Tavitas said the state didn’t have the evidence to prove the case. Gary Police Detective Daryl Gordon was called to the scene where Walker was found lying lifeless on his back, with several 9mm bullet casings nearby. A witness informed police that Walker was walking back from a gas station when gunshots rang out. A dog was shot dead not long after Walker’s slaying, allegedly with the same bullet type. King and Sanders were arrested at a house where officers surrounded them. A witness stated that the men were inside for 10 minutes before police came. mcolias@post-trib.com

author: The Arena Group
title: Duke Announces Death Of Legendary Announcer Bob Harris
mainText: The Duke University athletics department lost a beloved longtime member of its broadcast team with the passing of radio broadcaster Bob Harris this week. He was 82 years old. For 41 years Harris served as the voice of both Duke football and Duke men's basketball. He retired in 2017 as a three-time recipient of the North Carolina Broadcaster of the Year and tons of other accolades. A short while ago, the Duke athletics department released a statement on Harris' passing. Duke Vice President & Director of Athletics Nina King offered condolences and declared that his legacy will "live forever." "We are deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Bob Harris," King said. "We send our heartfelt condolences to Phyllis and the entire Harris family. Duke, the Atlantic Coast Conference and the entire collegiate athletics community has lost a true icon. For over four decades, Bob represented Duke with the utmost professionalism while delivering to our fans worldwide an acute account of Blue Devil football and men's basketball games. He will be greatly missed, but his legacy will live forever." Coach K also released a statement, calling Harris one of Duke's greatest treasures and praising him for telling the story of Duke athletics "better than anyone."

author: Barry Soper
title: Farmers should be treated as treasures, not as tyrants - Barry Soper
mainText: Barry Soper discusses the challenges faced by farmers in New Zealand under the Labour/Green Government, focusing on issues such as the ETS tax, high interest rates from banking sectors, and financial struggles. The announcement that farmers won't have to pay the ETS tax next year brings relief to many, especially those operating marginal farms that have been in families for generations. There is a sentiment among farmers that New Zealand shouldn't be the first to tax farmers on emissions, especially when they are already considered some of the most carbon-efficient food producers globally. Another concern highlighted is the high interest rates imposed by banks on farmers, which are significantly higher compared to rates in Australia where the major banks are based. Despite the banking sector's profits reaching billions, farmers are feeling the brunt as they borrow to invest in their properties for productivity. Farmers feel that they are being targeted by banks and are often encouraged to increase overdrafts at high rates instead of securing proper loans. This financial strain on farmers is seen as unfair, considering their significant contribution to New Zealand's exports. Soper emphasizes that farmers, who are the backbone of the export-driven country, should be valued as treasures rather than tyrants. He urges politicians to support farmers and allow them the freedom to continue their vital work for the country.

author: Thomas Coughlan
title: The $2 billion social housing cliff no one is talking about
mainText: The article discusses the disparity between two groups of New Zealanders with high social needs, where one group receives generous support and capped rents through public housing, while the other receives meager support through an accommodation supplement and faces high private rental costs. The Ministry of Social Development determines who qualifies for income-related rent subsidies (IRRS) and public housing. There is little incentive for those in public housing to leave, creating a 'cliff edge' between the two forms of assistance. A $2.4 billion difference is projected over four years between IRRS-supported housing and those on the accommodation supplement. Various reports highlight that social housing is not always accessed by those with the greatest need and that social housing tenants have little incentive to shift to more cost-effective options as their circumstances improve. The article also delves into the history of housing support in New Zealand and the challenges in addressing the disparity between social and market housing. The issue of housing assistance has persisted despite past attempts to solve it, leading to calls for ensuring appropriate assistance for those in need and reevaluating the effectiveness of current housing support programs.

author: Thomas Coughlan
title: Delicate China balance to continue with economics and security on the agenda as Premier Li visits NZ
mainText: Chinese Premier Li Qiang will touch down in Wellington today. The visit will be the first of a Chinese Premier since Li Keqiang visited in 2017. This makes it the highest-ranking official visit in seven years. Premier Li will land in a nation that is rethinking its relationship with the rising superpower in a way it perhaps was not back in 2017. The oppression of Uighur Muslims in Xinjiang was formally called out by the New Zealand Parliament in 2021, while the crackdown on Hong Kong in 2019 was criticised by the former Government. Both the former and current governments are looking at associating with non-nuclear pillar 2 of the Aukus nuclear-powered submarine agreement, which in 2017 was not even a radioactive twinkle in then-Australian Treasurer Scott Morrison’s eye. On the trade side of the relationship, exports to China grew by 30 per cent in the three years prior to the last visit. The growth rate is about 15 per cent in the three years to 2023. The pandemic is partly to blame - but there are worrying signs New Zealand is struggling to revive its services trade to pre-pandemic levels. Part of it is the fact that because the Chinese economy has grown so large, and New Zealand’s trade with it is so mature, a slowdown in the growth rate is almost inevitable. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon told Mike Hosking on Newstalk ZB this week that the focus would be the economy, in part because that is also the focus of Premier Li in the Chinese system. “He’s very much responsible for the economic agenda in China and he’s concerned because China is hitting headwinds,” Luxon said, citing China’s declining population, productivity crisis and moribund property market (on two of these three, Luxon and Li might find they have something in common - although the problem with China’s situation is that there is too much supply, rather than too little). “His interest is about productivity and the trade piece will be an important part of that,” Luxon said. New Zealand Contemporary China Research Centre director and Victoria University associate professor Jason Young told the Herald that Premier Li’s position second in the ranks of the Chinese communist party (behind General-Secretary Xi Jinping) made him part of the “loyalist inner circle of the Chinese Communist Party”. “He was a loyal deputy in Shanghai when he was head of the Communist Party there and did the lockdown and dynamic zero Covid policy and from that many observers say he is part of the inner circle,” Yong said. Premier Li’s other role was as Head of the Government of China. “He runs the Government and implements policy. In the Chinese system the Chinese Communist Party comes up with the direction and policy direction for the nation, but then policy is implemented through the government system. “He sits at the head of the government and therefore is charged with implementing the policy of the Chinese Communist Party,” Young said. He added that traditionally a big part of this was to “focus on the economy and economic development and international economic engagement”. Despite President Xi’s statist economic turn, Young said that some observers had concluded Premier Li to be a “proponent of a more market-orientated system for China and for China’s international engagement”. Young said it was “impossible to say” how this coloured his relationship with President Xi, given the extent to which state and market had been blended in China. “It seems contradictory [to be both pro-market and statist] but within the Chinese system, they would not see it to be contradictory. One of the areas for growth is in services trade. New Zealand has a sophisticated and far-reaching Free Trade Agreement with China, but the chief beneficiaries of this have been goods. In the year to June 2023, our top exports were dairy, meat, wood, and “milk preparations, pasta and baking products”. Dairy exports were worth $6.8 billion - that’s about $1b more than all of New Zealand’s exports to the European Union in that year. Services are often a tougher win for FTAs because the barriers they face to entering a market are not necessarily tariffs, as is the case with goods exports. Instead, services face non-tariff barriers like domestic regulations making it more difficult to compete. New Zealand’s FTA with China includes provisions for China to keep New Zealand education providers on its “study abroad” website to boost Chinese consumers’ confidence in those providers. Stephanie Honey, trade policy consultant at Honey Consulting told the Herald that “since the pandemic there has been a dip in services exports”. In 2019, services exports were worth $3.3b. In the year to June 2023. that figure was $1.6b - recovering slightly from pandemic lows. Honey said that this was dominated by the likes of tourism and education, with the rest of the services sector’s trade with China being “undercooked”. She said New Zealand should look to these sectors for deepening services trade. Potential sectors included business services and digital services like video gaming. “[Video gaming] has been an important sector, but it has been quite constrained over the last few years in China by how they regulated access to the market,” Honey said. Video games are an example of the way New Zealand could try to negotiate better market access for services exports. Video game developers need licenses to sell in China. Allowing Kiwi companies more licenses would make it easier for them to trade in the country. “There’s real potential for growth if we can get market access opened up,” Honey said. This wouldn’t require a wholesale revision of the FTA, but lower-level talks between the two countries and an agreement to change domestic regulatory settings within China itself. Thomas Coughlan is Deputy Political Editor and covers politics from Parliament. He has worked for the Herald since 2021 and has worked in the press gallery since 2018.

author: Michael Karlik, Colorado Politics
title: Late-filed appeal due to lawyers' carelessness not OK: court
mainText: Colorado's second-highest court ruled that an attorney's late-filed appeal due to submitting it to the wrong court is not excusable neglect. In a case involving a multimillion-dollar dispute over oil and gas extraction in Wyoming, attorney Stephen D. Rynerson's assistant filed the appeal in the Denver District Court instead of the Court of Appeals, missing the deadline. Rynerson cited office remodeling and remote work as reasons for the error, but the court rejected the appeal, emphasizing common carelessness and negligence. The court clarified that the responsibility falls on the attorney to supervise and verify submissions. The case is Riggs Oil & Gas Corp. et al. v. Los Feliz Oil Company, LLC et al.

author: Anne M. Stark
title: Study shows magnesium oxide undergoes dynamic transition when it comes to super-Earth exoplanets
mainText: Researchers have discovered new insights into the interiors of super-Earth exoplanets by studying magnesium oxide (MgO), a key component of Earth's lower mantle and believed to play a similar role in the mantles of massive rocky exoplanets. Super-Earths are planets larger than Earth but smaller than Neptune, with extreme pressures and temperatures in their mantles causing MgO to transform from a rock salt crystal structure to a cesium chloride structure. By conducting experiments at ultra-high pressures of up to 634 GPa, scientists observed the B1 to B2 phase transition in MgO occurring within the 400–430 GPa pressure range at a temperature of around 9,700 K. The study, published in Science Advances, provides essential data for developing accurate models of super-Earth interior processes. The research team also clarified the mechanism of the B1–B2 transition in MgO, shedding light on atomic-level changes under shock compression. Collaborators include scientists from Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Johns Hopkins University, University of Rochester, Princeton University, and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory.

author: Mike Wall
title: SpaceX launching 22 Starlink satellites from Florida June 13
mainText: SpaceX is scheduled to launch 22 more of its Starlink broadband satellites to orbit from Florida's Space Coast on Thursday (June 13). The Starlink satellites will lift off atop a Falcon 9 rocket from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station during a two-hour window that opens at 4:46 p.m. EDT (2046 GMT). SpaceX had planned to launch the mission on Wednesday evening (June 12) but pushed the try back by about 24 hours. SpaceX will stream the action live via its account on X, beginning about five minutes before launch. The Falcon 9's first stage will come back to Earth about 8.5 minutes after launch, if all goes according to plan, landing on the droneship Just Read the Instructions in the Atlantic Ocean. It will be the 16th launch and landing for this particular booster, according to a SpaceX mission description. Ten of its 15 flights to date have been Starlink missions. The Falcon 9's upper stage, meanwhile, will continue carrying the 22 Starlink satellites to low Earth orbit, deploying them about 53 minutes after liftoff. SpaceX has launched 60 orbital missions so far in 2024, which works out to an average of one liftoff every 2.7 days. Forty-three of these launches have been dedicated to building out the Starlink megaconstellation, which currently consists of nearly 6,100 operational spacecraft.

author: Emily Packer
title: Ants detect and monitor low levels of moonlight to navigate at night, new study shows
mainText: Nocturnal bull ants have been found to use low-level moonlight for navigation at night, as per a recent study published in eLife. These ants rely on detecting patterns of polarized skylight, known as e-vectors, when celestial bodies like the sun or moon are not visible due to obstructions like clouds or forest canopy. The research, led by Cody Freas of Macquarie University, aimed to investigate whether nocturnal bull ants could detect and monitor low levels of polarized moonlight. By studying bull ant foragers over a lunar cycle, the researchers found that the ants adjusted their direction of movement in response to changing rotations of overhead lunar light polarization. This behavior was consistent regardless of the lunar cycle stage, including under a crescent moon with only 20% illumination. The study also observed that foragers reduced their changes in direction when the moon was waning, indicating the importance of continuous tracking of moonlight polarization for navigation. The findings suggest that polarized moonlight is a stable cue for the ants to use in updating their path integrator, along with terrestrial cues, for navigation. The research team concluded that foraging ants can effectively use polarized moonlight to navigate, integrating this celestial cue into their path integrator using the same visual pathways as polarized sunlight. This ability allows the ants to adapt their navigational decisions based on the reliability of available navigational information, presenting a versatile navigational system that can operate both day and night without the need for mechanistic alterations. Overall, the study provides valuable insights into how insects utilize celestial cues, such as polarized moonlight, for navigation, expanding our understanding of nocturnal animal behavior and sensory ecology. The findings highlight the adaptability and complexity of animal navigation strategies and their reliance on environmental cues.

author: Science X
title: NASA's Roman mission gets cosmic 'sneak peek' from supercomputers
mainText: Scientists at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory collaborated on a project involving the creation of nearly 4 million simulated images of the cosmos using supercomputers. The images are meant to depict how NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory will view the universe. This simulation is part of the OpenUniverse project led by Michael Troxel from Duke University. The team has released a 10-terabyte subset of the data, with the remaining 390 terabytes to be released later. The simulation factored in the telescopes' instrument performance, providing an accurate preview of what they will see. Both telescopes will explore dark energy and dark matter, with Rubin starting operations in 2025 and Roman launching by May 2027. Simulations like OpenUniverse help scientists understand the instrument imprints on images and refine data processing methods for future data analysis. The project involved collaboration between NASA, DOE, Argonne, and SLAC. The simulations cover a patch of the sky totaling 0.08 square degrees, with the full simulation to be released later spanning 70 square degrees. The combination of data from Roman's space-based survey and Rubin's ground-based one will provide better constraints on cosmic phenomena. Scientists aim to make observing plans and data processing pipelines more effective for both telescopes. The simulated data is accessible to researchers to help them prepare for future data analysis effectively.

author: Mickey Pardo
title: African elephants shown to address one another with name-like calls, similar to humans
mainText: A recent study has revealed that African elephants have the ability to address each other with name-like calls, similar to how humans use names. Researchers have observed wild elephants for years and noticed that the animals interact with each other in unique ways that indicate the presence of names. The study, published in Nature Ecology and Evolution, focused on elephant vocalizations, particularly deep rumbles that are below the range of human hearing. Through machine learning analysis, researchers found that elephants could identify the intended recipient of a call based on its sound properties. Subsequent experiments showed that elephants could perceive and respond to their names when played recordings of calls addressed to them. Unlike some animals that use imitation to address others, like bottlenose dolphins and parrots, elephants do not necessarily imitate each other's calls when using names. This finding suggests that elephants, like humans, may have a more complex system of communication that goes beyond simple imitation. The research team plans to further investigate how elephants use names for specific individuals, along with exploring questions about name acquisition and social communication among elephants. The study also hints at the evolutionary implications of name-like calls in animals, potentially shedding light on the development of human language skills. Understanding the cognitive abilities of elephants can lead to a greater appreciation for these majestic creatures, especially amidst growing threats to their survival in the wild.

author: Lyall Thomas
title: Joao Palhinha: Fulham reject improved Bayern Munich bid for Portugal midfielder
mainText: Fulham have rejected an improved bid from Bayern Munich for Joao Palhinha. Bayern remain interested in the 28-year-old, whom they have been pursuing since last summer. The potential total value of the proposal, including bonuses, is understood to have been worth the second-most for a defensive midfielder aged 28 or over. The current second-highest fee in this bracket is £40m. Palhinha has four years left on his Fulham contract, with no release clause plus an option of a further year. New Bayern boss Vincent Kompany is eager to bring Palhinha to the Bundesliga with backing from sporting directors. Barcelona and Manchester United are also interested in the ex-Sporting player. Palhinha almost moved to Bayern on Deadline Day last summer after Fulham gave permission. Fulham also turned down a £45m bid from West Ham last July. The summer transfer window opens on June 14 and closes on August 30. The Premier League has brought forward Deadline Day to link up with other major leagues in Europe.

author: Sam Robinson
title: Titans to sign journeyman OL
mainText: Geron Christian agreed to terms with the Titans on Wednesday, KPRC2’s Aaron Wilson reports. Christian spent last season with the Browns and Texans, being a nine-game Cleveland starter during a season in which the AFC North club lost both its starting tackles. This will reunite Christian with former Browns O-line coach Bill Callahan. Christian marks the second former Callahan Cleveland charge to join the Titans this offseason. A former third-round pick, Christian has made 25 career starts. The former Washington draftee closed last season as Cleveland’s starting left tackle, with Jedrick Wills joining Jack Conklin and rookie RT fill-in Dawand Jones in suffering a season-ending injury. Christian, who went to training camp with the Dolphins before failing to make their 53-man roster, started the Browns’ final nine games and their wild-card outing in Houston. Pro Football Focus did not view Christian’s 2023 work fondly, though. Given how far down the depth chart the Browns needed to look at tackle last year, it is not exactly surprising their final LT option was inconsistent. The Browns signed Christian after the Texans had released him from their practice squad in October. The Louisville alum combined for 14 starts from 2020-21, playing with Washington and Houston, initially changing teams after being waived in 2021. A rebuilding Texans team used the 320-pound blocker as a regular starter moving forward; the Chiefs slotted Christian as a backup in 2022. Regarded as perhaps the NFL’s premier O-line coach, Callahan now has two of his recent pieces to help in Nashville. The Titans are expected to use Latham, 2023 first-rounder Peter Skoronski, free-agent signing Lloyd Cushenberry III and 2023 UFA pickup Daniel Brunskill as starters. Nicholas Petit-Frere remains on his rookie contract, with fill-in starter Jaelyn Duncan also standing to be a right-tackle option. Christian technically gives the Titans another option, but he has played left tackle for most of his NFL career. Still, the six-year veteran profiles as a candidate for a swing role in Brian Callahan‘s offense.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Chiefs' Travis Kelce reveals what he wants to do after his NFL career is over
mainText: When Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce decides to hang up the cleats, he will be a sure-fire Hall of Famer. He already has the most 1,000-yard seasons (7) and 100-yard receiving games (37) by a tight end all time, is just the third player to lead three Super Bowl champions in receiving yards and his 71.2 receiving yards per game are the most by a tight end in NFL history. Kelce is also an electric personality, meaning he's likely capable of attracting headlines even after his football days are over. What would Kelce want to do after football? During the most recent episode of his "New Heights" podcast, we found out the answer to that question. While having a conversation with brother Jason Kelce about hypothetically owning an NFL team, Travis said he would turn down the opportunity because he wants to do something else related to football. "I want to broadcast when I'm done playing," said Kelce. "I want to do that. I want to be the talking head that calls the games." Kelce wants to chase Tom Brady into the booth, and he would probably be great at it. At 34 years old, that transition could be on the horizon, but won't come too soon. Kelce signed a three-year extension that made him the highest-paid tight end in the NFL this offseason, and he clearly still loves playing football -- saying he's going to keep doing it "until the wheels fall off." "I can't put a time frame on it. I love coming to work every single day," Kelce said after Tuesday's minicamp session. "Obviously, I know that there's opportunities outside of football for me, and I think you have to keep in perspective that I'm still a little kid when I come into this building."

author: Kyle Wiggers
title: This Week in AI: Apple won’t say how the sausage gets made
mainText: Apple introduced Apple Intelligence at WWDC, featuring generative AI to power upgraded Siri, AI-generated emoji, and photo-editing tools. The company emphasized safety and personalization. However, there is criticism regarding the lack of transparency in Apple's model training practices, especially in terms of copyright issues. The newsletter also highlights other AI news, such as OpenAI's new executive hires, Yahoo Mail's AI capabilities, and a study on generative AI models and polarizing subject matter. A research paper by Google discusses a health-oriented generative AI model for personalized recommendations based on physiological data. Apple's new on-device and server-based generative AI models are discussed, with comparisons to models from Google and OpenAI. The newsletter also mentions the anniversary of GPT-1 and the advancements in deep learning. The field has evolved significantly, with models like GPT-3 training faster and more efficiently. Despite concerns about transparency and ethics in AI, advancements like Apple Intelligence and research on personalized health models show the ongoing progress in the field.

author: Mark Wilson
title: Samsung's wild new Shortcut sneakers let you play music and make phone calls by dancing
mainText: If you like the idea of starting a playlist on your phone with a spontaneous moonwalk, Samsung has just made a pair of limited-edition sneakers for you. The Shortcut Sneaker, which will sadly be limited to just six pairs, has been created by a combination of Samsung, Elitac Wearables and sneaker designer Roel van Hoff. The Shortcut's soles contain motion sensors that track their position, with five movements or gestures triggering five distinct actions. You won't see these sneakers in stores. Instead, the six pairs will be for competition winners, who need to be Samsung Members. With a design that contains multiple nods to Samsung's Galaxy phones, there certainly won't be a shortage of entrants among hardcore Samsung fans. While the Shortcut promises to be 'the first sneaker in the world with which you can call your friends', according to Samsung, it also isn't the first example of tech-filled footwear we've seen. Nothing can quite top the Back to the Future-inspired Nike HyperAdapt trainers, of course, but we'll still likely throw our hats into the ring for Samsung's Shortcut Sneaker while we secretly perfect our moonwalk.

author: Kunal Khullar
title: This new gaming handheld has a chance of dethroning the Steam Deck OLED
mainText: The Zotac Zone is a new handheld gaming console that has caught the attention of many at Computex 2024. It boasts unique features and stands out with its AMOLED panel, a display feature shared only with the Steam Deck OLED. In terms of price and availability, the Steam Deck OLED is currently available in two configurations, priced at $550 for the 512GB model and $650 for the 1TB model. In comparison, Zotac plans to launch its handheld with a 512GB storage variant, 16GB memory, and an expected price of $700 later in the year. While the Steam Deck OLED offers better value for its price, the Zotac Zone comes with more high-end features, including an AMD Ryzen 7 8840U APU, faster RAM, and dual USB 4.0 Type-C ports. The Zotac Zone's Windows 11 operating system allows access to a wide range of services and emulators. Performance-wise, initial testing showed promising results for the Zotac Zone, although further comparisons against the Steam Deck OLED are awaited. The Zotac Zone is expected to outperform the Steam Deck based on its hardware specifications. The article suggests waiting for the Zotac Zone's release and mentions upcoming handheld consoles like the refreshed Asus Ally X and the MSI Claw 8 AI+ powered by Intel's Lunar Lake-based chipset. The Zotac Zone, with its AMOLED display, fast performance, and unique features, is positioned as a strong contender to potentially dethrone the Steam Deck OLED in the handheld gaming market.

author: Cheryl Eddy
title: Game of Thrones Prequel Ten Thousand Ships Is Back in Action
mainText: Back in April, Oscar-winning screenwriter Brian Helgeland revealed details about his pitch for a Game of Thrones prequel that HBO ultimately passed on. Now, according to Thrones author George R.R. Martin, a Pulitzer-winning playwright has joined the prospective new HBO series. The series—variously referred to as Ten Thousand Ships and 10,000 Ships—has been in the ether since at least 2021, but you can go all the way back to 2014 to find Martin’s mention of a written project of the same title, focusing on Princess Nymeria, seen as a folk hero by later Westeros figures like House of the Dragon’s young Alicent and Rhaenyra, and “the final fatal war between the proud princes of the river and the dragonlords of old Valyria.” Today, Martin shared that Eboni Booth—who won the Pulitzer Prize for Drama earlier this year for her play Primary Trust—has now come aboard HBO’s Ten Thousand Ships. According to Martin, she is “working on a new pilot,” so expect a shift from Helgeland’s tease of what he would have brought to the table. In April, he told Inverse that “I think they felt the period of my show was too far removed from the pillars of the original ... My script was based on Queen Nymeria and this little blurb about her that was in a Westeros encyclopedia. Essentially, it was the story of Moses but swapping him out for Nymeria. Her country gets ruined and her people are forced to live on the water, which is why the show was called 10,000 Ships. They end up having to leave and find a new home like the Israelites leaving Egypt. She’s leading all these people, trying to hold everyone together but things are always in danger of falling apart as they travel around a fictionalized version of the Mediterranean, looking for a new home to settle in.” In today’s tease, Martin describes the show as “a Game of Thrones spinoff about Nymeria and the Rhoynar,” which isn’t much to go on, but adds “We’re all very excited about this one… though we’re still trying to figure out how we’re going to pay for ten thousand ships, three hundred dragons, and those giant turtles.

author: Nigel Bunyan,Arthur Parashar
title: Convicted baby-killing nurse Lucy Letby was caught 'virtually red-handed' trying to murder 'very...
mainText: Convicted baby-killing nurse Lucy Letby was caught 'virtually red-handed' trying to murder 'very premature' newborn in hospital, jury hears Baby killer Lucy Letby was caught 'virtually red-handed' as she tried to murder a newborn baby at the Countess of Chester Hospital, a jury heard today. Letby, 34, was convicted in August last year of the murders of seven babies and the attempted murders of six other infants at the Countess of Chester hospital between June 2015 and June 2016. The jury at Letby's 10-month trial at Manchester Crown Court was unable to reach verdicts on six counts of attempted murder in relation to five children. At the same court, the former nurse is now being retried over one of those counts - an allegation that she tried to murder a baby girl, known as Child K, in February 2016. Ravi Jayaram, a senior paediatrician on the neonatal unit, walked into the high-dependency Nursery 1 to see Letby alone in the room and standing over Baby K's incubator. The infant's saturation levels were falling to a critical level but the alarm that should have alerted staff was not sounding. 'We say Lucy Letby was caught virtually red-handed by Dr Jayaram'. The prosecutor said Letby had carried out frequent Facebook searches on some of the babies' relatives. The trial continues.

author: Patrick Finley
title: Caleb Williams eyes summer plan with Bears offseason program over
mainText: Not long after being drafted first overall by the Bears, quarterback Caleb Williams is already planning for the summer with his teammates. He aims to bond with both offensive and defensive players, work on techniques, and prepare for the upcoming season. Coach Matt Eberflus emphasizes the importance of preparation and execution, particularly in understanding the offensive playbook and terminology. Williams plans to focus on mental and physical preparation during the break, including studying film, working with his quarterbacks coach, and organizing his notes. The work he puts in during the summer will play a crucial role in his confidence and readiness for training camp. Eberflus hints at Williams getting significant playing time during the preseason games to continue his development. Williams is focused on growth and looks forward to returning in July ready to build on his progress.

author: John Esposito
title: Fortnite x Metallica live event: Start date, how to watch & more
mainText: Metallica's arrival to Fortnite is coming with a live event for fans to rock out to. Here's everything you need to know about the event. After many teases, Fortnite Festival Season 4 brings heavy metal legend Metallica to the musical mode. The band's arrival also introduces a variety of cosmetics to earn, new music, and an exciting Battle Stage mode. Metallica's reach will extend outside of Fortnite Festival, as the group will get a live event titled Metallica: Fuel. Fire. Fury. Featuring six fan-favorite songs, this will be an event you don't want to miss. Fortnite x Metallica event: date & time Metallica: Fuel. Fire. author: John Kennedy
title: Florida Gov. DeSantis signs $116.5 billion state budget after $1 billion in vetoes
mainText: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis signed a $116.5 billion state budget after vetoing approximately $1 billion in programs and projects, many of which were added by fellow Republicans in the Legislature. This budget was approved by the Republican-controlled Legislature and will take effect on July 1. DeSantis emphasized his frugality and highlighted key areas of spending, including increased funding for security at Jewish day schools and higher education recruitment efforts. The budget includes a $240-per-student increase for schools and a 3% pay raise for state workers. Environmental programs received significant boosts, particularly for water quality initiatives. Additionally, the budget allocated funds for a health-care bill, debt reduction, and member projects. DeSantis justified his vetoes by referencing the state's ability to maintain a significant reserve fund. Overall, the budget shows a conservative approach to spending and a focus on key priority areas. This article originally appeared on Tallahassee Democrat by reporter John Kennedy.

author: Sara Alhariri
title: Major airline to launch brand new routes to Orlando & Palm Beach this fall – with $49 one-way fares for a l...
mainText: ONE major US airline, JetBlue, is launching new routes to sunny Florida, including Orlando and Palm Beach, out of Long Island's MacArthur Airport. The flights will offer $49 one-way fares and are scheduled to start on October 24, 2024, for Orlando and West Palm Beach, with Fort Lauderdale flights starting the following day. JetBlue is known for its comfort and legroom in economy cabins. The vice president of network planning at JetBlue, Dave Jehn, expressed excitement about expanding services to Long Island, emphasizing the airline's commitment to low fares and great service. Senator Chuck Schumer praised the move, highlighting the benefits for Long Islanders and the local economy. The new routes aim to offer more travel options and promote tourism, creating potential job opportunities. To avail the $49 fares, bookings must be made by June 13, 2024 for fall travel.

author: Charlotte Everett,Daniel Nuttman,Adekemi Adefolalu,Jimmy Grant
title: How do you cancel a Ryanair flight and can you get your money back?...
mainText: RYANAIR does not usually allow passengers to cancel flights and get a refund; instead, passengers must go through the provider they booked with. Exceptions include flight cancellations by Ryanair or certain special circumstances. If Ryanair cancels your flight, you can apply for a refund or change your flight for free. Changing a flight with Ryanair can be done up until 2.5 hours before departure, with fees ranging from £45 online to £60 at the airport. Name changes are the only alterations allowed up to two hours before the flight, costing £115 online or £160 at the airport. If your flight is canceled by Ryanair, you are entitled to a full refund processed within seven working days, or vouchers for alternative flights. However, if you choose to cancel your flight, you will not receive a refund from Ryanair; consider exploring options with your insurance provider for coverage. Ryanair's refund policy is generally non-refundable if the flight is operational and you choose not to travel. Exceptions for refunds include flight cancellations by Ryanair, operational failures, or personal emergencies like a serious illness or death within the family. It's essential to review Ryanair's full refund policy and Passenger Rights Regulations for specific conditions and entitlements.
