author: Angela Symons
title: Albania, Cyprus, Ireland: Europe’s best non-Schengen countries for when you’ve used up your 90 days
mainText: Planning a year out to explore Europe could be hindered by the '90-day' rule which stipulates that non-EU nationals with a valid visa can only stay in Schengen Area countries for a total of 90 days in a 180-day period. This rule applies to 25 out of the 27 EU countries, as well as Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland. However, there are some non-Schengen countries that can be visited to break up the stay and remain compliant. Albania is highlighted for its stunning beaches, affordable living costs, and welcoming locals. Vlore and the Komani Lake Ferry journey are noted as must-visits. Moving on to Cyprus, which is not part of the Schengen zone, travelers can enjoy three months of lounging on Mediterranean beaches, exploring ancient Roman sites, and experiencing vibrant nightlife. The article suggests places like Ayia Napa, Cavo Greco National Park, and Paphos for various experiences. Ireland and the UK also offer alternatives, with Ireland not being in the Schengen Area but having its own 90-day limit. Tourists can explore Dublin, Galway, and the Cliffs of Moher or embark on a road trip along the Wild Atlantic Way. For a different experience, North Macedonia provides visa-free access for up to 90 days, enabling tourists to enjoy its beautiful nature, architecture, and clear waters in locations like Ohrid and Skopje. These non-Schengen countries offer diverse and enriching travel experiences that can help extend and enhance a trip across Europe.

author: Craig Paton
title: MSPs back government’s emergency prisoner release plans
mainText: MSPs have backed Scottish Government plans to release prisoners early to ease pressures on the system. Justice Secretary Angela Constance announced the move last month following a spike in inmate numbers and concerns about the capacity of the prison estate. The proposals were passed by 66 votes to 47, with five abstentions, after being narrowly backed by Holyrood’s Criminal Justice Committee. The Government has said there are around 550 prisoners eligible for early release under the proposals, and almost 65 per cent of them are otherwise due to be freed in the next 90 days. The emergency release is one part of a plan that requires long-term thinking. Those serving sentences of four years or under due for release within the next six months will be released, excluding those sentenced for domestic violence, terrorism, or sexual crimes. Scottish Labour also voted against the plans. Scottish Prison Service (SPS) chief executive Teresa Medhurst described the use of emergency release as appropriate and necessary to protect the security, good order, and safety of prisons, prisoners, and staff.

author: Munir Ahmed Associated Press
title: Pakistan’s new government presents its first budget as it seeks a new long-term IMF bailout
mainText: Pakistan’s new coalition government presented its first budget in parliament on Wednesday, promising an increase of up to 25% in the salaries of government employees and setting an ambitious tax collection target while talks with the International Monetary Fund about a new bailout continue. Analysts say the new budget of about $68 billion — up from $50 billion last fiscal year — is aimed at qualifying for a long-term loan of $6 billion to $8 billion from the IMF to help stabilize the economy, which in 2023 nearly defaulted on the payment of foreign debts. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said the government of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif wants to achieve 3.6% economic growth. Aurangzeb also said inflation in Pakistan is down to 12%. He announced that Pakistan is setting a challenging target of collecting 13 trillion rupees ($44 billion) in taxes, which is 40% more than in the current fiscal year. Pakistan will privatize the country's national carrier and encourage the private sector to manufacture solar panels and other equipment in Pakistan.

author: Sarah Marsh
title: ‘A first step towards conscription’: Germany proposes new selective military service to boost defence
mainText: Germany‘s defence minister has presented a proposal for a selective military service focused on volunteers, described as a first step towards conscription, to boost its depleted armed forces. The proposal is part of Germany‘s shift towards a more robust foreign and defence policy, announced by Chancellor Olaf Scholz as a “Zeitenwende” or “turn of era” in the days after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Around 13 years after Germany suspended mass conscription, Defence Minister Boris Pistorus said on Wednesday all men would be obliged to fill out a questionnaire to gauge their suitability for, and interest in, military service upon turning 18. The questionnaire would be optional for women. It would then select around 10% of those for mustering before narrowing down the selection to the most suitable and motivated to undertake the six-month basic service - with an option to lengthen this by up to 17 months. “Those who are most, most suitable and motivated should be selected for the military service,” Pistorius told reporters. This new model aims to increase to 15,000 the number of young people undertaking voluntary military service, a rise of 5,000, in the first year, the ministry said, growing that number year by year. The aim was to eventually reach 200,000 more reservists, which would enable Germany to swiftly expand its troops to around 460,000 in the event of war - nearly double what it could muster today. It currently has 180,000 soldiers, which it wants to increase to 203,000, and 60,000 reservists. And even then, Germany would have well fewer than the 500,000 troops and 800,000 reservists of the former West Germany in the Cold War. “No matter if we are better equipping our armed forces ... the principle of deterrence only works if you have enough soldiers who could eventually defend the country,” Pistorius. The minister has vowed to turn Germany into a “war-ready” nation, warning that war between the NATO western defence alliance and Russia could happen in five to eight years. The model is similar to the Swedish one, introduced in 2018, which aimed to enhance the status of military service through a degree of exclusivity and some incentives.

author: Namit Singh Sengar
title: Budget 2024: FM Nirmala Sitharaman To Present Budget Twice This Year, Here's Why
mainText: Nirmala Sitharaman on Wednesday assumed the charge of union finance minister for her second consecutive term and is set to present the full union budget in July 2024. All eyes are now on the full budget, where she is expected to outline the vision for the next five years along with key policy announcements. Additionally, she will focus on addressing unemployment by implementing measures to boost manufacturing. Sitharaman, the first full-time woman finance minister of India, has presented six budgets, including one interim budget. In the interim budget for FY25, she adhered to tradition by sticking to vote-on-account measures only. Interim Budget: Early in the year, the finance minister presented an interim budget on February 1. This interim budget is a temporary financial statement meant to keep the government running until the new government takes office. The interim budget includes expenditures and necessary allocations but usually avoids major policy announcements or changes. Full Budget: After the general elections, the newly elected government presents a full budget for the financial year. This year, it is expected that the government will present its budget in July. This dual-budget practice ensures that the outgoing government does not make long-term commitments or major policy changes right before an election, allowing the incoming government to implement its financial strategies and policies. A union budget is valid till the end of the financial year on March 31, hence the government has spending rights only till that date. For the government expenditure occurring between March 1, and a new government being formed, the incumbent government needs permission from the Parliament to incur costs in the interim period. Hence, the interim budget is released.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Kuwait fire: Toll goes up to 49; at least 11 Malayalis among deceased, 9 identified
mainText: At least 49 people, including several Malayalis, were killed in a massive fire in a building in Kuwait's Ahmadi Governorate. The casualties also include individuals from other Indian states. Seven of the 35 individuals in intensive care are critical, with five on ventilator support. The identities of nine deceased Malayalis have been confirmed, along with other Indian victims. Authorities are yet to confirm all identities. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has offered Rs 2 lakh each to bereaved Indian families. The building housed over 195 laborers from Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and North India, owned by NBTC group. Kuwait's Deputy Prime Minister ordered a police inquiry and detention of building owner, janitor, and employer. The incident occurred at 4:30 am, with the fire spreading quickly, exacerbated by gas cylinders. The injured have been admitted to hospitals. Indian Embassy opened a helpline, and External Affairs Minister expressed condolences. The cause of the fire appears to be a short circuit in the kitchen, leading to fatalities from burns and smoke inhalation. The fire has been contained.

author: Livemint
title: Rahul Gandhi says he 'doesn't get instructions from God', mocks PM Modi: 'His strange Parmatma...' | Mint
mainText: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday amid buzz over his Lok Sabha seats. He alluded to previous remarks made by the Prime Minister and noted that he — unlike Modi — was not ‘guided by God’. The newly re-elected lawmaker said that he was facing a ‘dilemma’ as he tried to choose between Wayanad and Raebareli. “You saw how the Prime Minister said ‘400-paar’ which disappeared and then came ‘300-paar’. After that, he said, ‘I am not biological. I do not take any decision. I have been put on this earth by Parmatma and he takes decisions’. His strange ‘Parmatma’ makes him take all the decisions in favour of Ambani and Adani. He tells him to give Bombay airport, Lucknow airport, and power plants to Adani and help him with schemes like Agniveer,” Gandhi jibed. The senior politician said that his God were the poor people of India and, more specifically, the people of Wayanad. “I go and talk to those people, and my God tells me what to do,” he added.

author: Toi City Desk
title: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and Ayodhya MP Awadhesh Prasad resign from UP assembly
mainText: LUCKNOW: Samajwadi Party national president Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday formally forwarded his resignation from Karhal assembly seat to the assembly speaker. Akhilesh Yadav, who won the Kannauj Lok Sabha constituency, also holds the Karhal assembly seat. The move has put to rest speculations over whether he will retain his position as Leader of Opposition in the state assembly or lead the party MPs in the Parliament. He was elected MP from Kannauj in the recently concluded 2024 Lok Sabha polls. 'I have met the workers of Karhal and Mainpuri and told them that as I have won the elections from 2 seats, I have to leave a seat. So I will inform you about leaving the seat of Vidhan Sabha soon,' Akhilesh Yadav said in a press conference on Tuesday. In the Kannauj Lok Sabha constituency, Akhilesh secured his family's stronghold by garnering 6,42,292 votes, surpassing the incumbent BJP MP Subrat Pathak by a margin exceeding 1 lakh votes. Samajwadi Party MLA Awadhesh Prasad has also tendered his resignation from the Legislative Assembly after being elected as a Member of Parliament from the Faizabad Lok Sabha constituency. In the Lok Sabha elections held in Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party (SP) clinched 37 seats, while the BJP secured 33 seats. The Congress party won 6 seats, and the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) obtained 2 seats. The Aazad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) and Apna Dal (Soneylal) managed to win 1 seat each.

author: Dinniah Bartholomew
title: ‘One more reason to stop shopping here,’ fumes Walmart customer over checkout issue – she’ll shop at Target...
mainText: A WALMART shopper has revealed that the retailer's newest policy was her final straw and she'll be shopping elsewhere instead. A customer blasted the policy, which only allows certain people to use self-checkout. The angry shopper posted a photo to Facebook, showing themselves in a long Walmart line with a cart full of things. "Yeah, Walmart. I needed just one more reason to stop shopping here and this seals the deal," they said on social media. "So apparently, only Walmart plus members can use the self-checkout now. Sorry Target for cheating on you." Walmart Plus is the retailer's paid subscription program made to compete with Amazon. Those who sign up for the $98-a-year plan can expect added benefits like free deliveries, fuel discounts, and scan-and-go shopping. At select Walmart locations, members have the exclusive right to self-checkout - a fact that has angered other customers as well. "So let me get this right," another shopper wrote on Facebook. "You want me to pay a subscription to check myself out?" And bonus, you don't have to pay a cashier?" The customer revealed that the change has caused longer wait times at the store, and has forced those who liked self-checkout to go to cashiers. Target shoppers have also had issues with its recent changes to self-checkout. In March, the company announced that it would be creating express self-checkout lines in many of its stores across the country, "Self-checkout was twice as fast at our pilot stores," a statement from the company read. "By having the option to pick self-checkout for a quick trip, or a traditional, staffed lane when their cart is full, guests who were surveyed told us the overall checkout experience was better, too." Despite positive feedback that the company got during testing, many customers have slammed the new change. "Someone at Target tried to tell me I couldn’t use self-checkout because it’s 10 items or less & I had maybe 15-20 things," explained one X user. "No registers open. What am I supposed to do?" "All of Targets self-checkout lanes are now '10 items or less' hahaha go f**k yourself," wrote another. "If b***ha** Target is being strict about 10 items or less at self-checkout then the least these lazy ass mfs can do is open the registers instead of having ONE cashier DAMN," shared another user. The U.S. Sun has reached out to Walmart for comment. The U.S. Sun has reached out to Target for comment.

author: Charlotte Graham-McLay Associated Press
title: Chinese Premier Li and New Zealand’s Luxon hail close ties as they sign trade deals in Wellington
mainText: WELLINGTON, New Zealand -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang met with New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon on Thursday in Wellington, where the two leaders played up the ability of “good friends” to respectfully disagree — while publicly diverging on little. Li, China’s No. 2 official, is the first Chinese premier to visit New Zealand since a 2017 visit by Li Keqiang. They signed a bilateral free trade agreement in 2008 — China’s first with an Organization for Cooperation and Development nation. Wellington in recent years has struck a more moderate tone with Beijing on security matters than many of its Western partners and has sought a consistent foreign policy approach. Luxon hailed Li's visit as a renewed opportunity for business and noted the potential for more trade with China's rising middle class. Luxon and Li expressed willingness to address disagreements openly, with Luxon stating that the ability to engage in direct dialogue is valuable for both countries. Li emphasized that differences should not hinder communication but instead serve as a catalyst for mutual learning and growth. Luxon also conveyed New Zealand's stance against foreign interference, while Li raised concerns about Wellington's potential involvement in a security pact with Australia, the U.S., and Britain. Li's visit to New Zealand was received warmly by the public, with minimal protests. Luxon refrained from categorically labeling China as a good global citizen. Li's forthcoming visit to Canberra aims to improve China-Australia relations, with a focus on economic collaboration amidst previous challenges related to security and human rights. China has been gradually removing trade barriers imposed on Australia in 2020 and aims to strengthen economic ties despite differences on security issues. Associated Press journalist Ken Moritsugu in Beijing contributed to this report.

author: Theresa Braine
title: Atlanta bus hijacker was witness to mall shooting hours earlier, gave rambling account to reporters
mainText: The man accused of hijacking a bus in downtown Atlanta Tuesday, and leading cops on a three-county chase after fatally shooting a passenger, had just witnessed the shooting mere hours earlier at the Peachtree Center food court and even spoke to reporters about what he had seen. Joseph Grier, 39, was charged Tuesday with one count of murder as well as one count of hijacking a motor vehicle, 13 counts of aggravated assault, 14 counts of kidnapping, one count of possession of a firearm by a convicted felon and one count of possession of a firearm or knife during the commission of a crime. During his rampage he allegedly wrestled a gun from a bus passenger, shot that passenger, pointed the gun at the driver’s head and led police on a 45-minute chase as it barreled through rush-hour traffic, sideswiping cars. The passenger, 58-year-old Ernest Byrd Jr., died. There were 16 other people on the bus, including the driver. Shortly before the hijacking, Grier had given reporters a rambling account of what he had seen inside the Peachtree Center mall, along with information about his mental health and 19 previous arrests. Both Atlanta Mayor Andre Dickens and Chief of Police Darin Schierbaum said mental illness may have contributed to Grier’s actions. In the mall shooting, Jeremy Malone, 34, had a brief altercation with a 47-year-old man from Grayson who he then shot, police said. Next he fired at two sisters, age 69 and 70, before an off-duty Atlanta police officer took him down. All four were expected to survive. Both Malone and Grier were being held without bond. With News Wire Services

author: Emily Allen
title: Prosecutors focus on patients during third day of Kennebunk doctor’s trial
mainText: Federal prosecutors have introduced the patients behind a 16-count indictment against a Kennebunk doctor on trial for allegedly writing life-threatening prescriptions without a legitimate medical purpose. The patients' names were withheld, and instead, another doctor testified about his impressions of each patient's treatment by Dr. Merideth Norris, who is facing multiple counts of illegal distribution of controlled substances, mostly opioids. The prosecution believes Norris put her clients at risk by prescribing these controlled substances without a legitimate medical purpose. Norris, who denies the allegations, has waited nearly two years for trial after being arrested and her office raided in October 2022. The patients, who had histories of substance use disorders, were prescribed various opioids by Norris, even while actively using non-prescribed controlled substances, according to testimony from the doctor who reviewed their records. He also noted red flags in Norris' patient records, such as prescribing sedatives and stimulants along with opioids, which put the patients at a greater risk of overdose. Differences in medical opinions were highlighted, as Norris, an outspoken critic of Maine laws limiting opioid prescriptions, clashed with the testifying doctor who emphasized the limited benefits and extreme dangers of opioids. The defense will likely question the credibility of the testifying doctor, as Norris' attorneys have complained about the timing of evidence disclosure from prosecutors.

author: Nicole Dorfman
title: Boulder County Sheriff’s Office closes Boulder Creek to tubers
mainText: Boulder Creek is closed to tubing and single chamber flotation devices such as blow-up rafts or inflatable paddle boards, from below Boulder Falls at Colo. 119 to 55th Street in Boulder, the Boulder County Sheriff’s Office said in a press release. The closure will remain in place until water flow drops to a level that is deemed to be safer for single chamber flotation devices, according to the release. Sheriff’s deputies will post notices and advise residents and visitors of the closure. “We historically close for tubing around 700 (cubic feet per second),” said Vinnie Montez, the Boulder County Sheriff’s office public information officer. “When there’s no runoff, it’s in the hundreds, and it could be faster or slower than that.” Boulder Creek was flowing at around 701 cubic feet per second on Wednesday and is expected to increase as temperatures rise, according to the release. Spring run-off and the normal scheduled release of water from Barker Reservoir causes the creek water flow to rise, increasing risks to people recreating and first responders performing water rescues. Increased risks present during higher water flows include cold water temperatures, floating debris and obstructions in the water. which can snag a person. Kayaks and white-water canoes are still permitted in the creek, according to the release. However, kayakers are strongly encouraged to exercise caution and wear personal protection equipment, including a life jacket, a wet or dry suit and a helmet. The sheriff is authorized to close waterways by state law. Violations of the closure are a civil infraction and can result in a $100 fine, according to the release. Spring runoff and high waters create dangerous situations every year, and emergency personnel warn people to be careful around all fast-moving water. A woman was pulled from Boulder Creek after reportedly crashing her bike in Boulder Canyon on May 31. Separately, searchers found a 68-year-old woman in the creek on June 4 after her family reported her missing.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Double kidnapping and assault in Colorado Springs, affidavit
mainText: The arrest affidavit of one of the suspects responsible for the double kidnapping and assault in Colorado Springs provided details about the violent incident. A man reported to the Colorado Springs Police Department that he and his girlfriend were kidnapped, held captive for over a day at gunpoint, and assaulted. The victims were confronted by a group of residents at an apartment complex, who were upset about the couple allegedly speaking with the police resulting in someone known to the suspects going to prison. The victims were taken at gunpoint to another residence, separated, and repeatedly beaten with firearms, fists, a glass beer bottle, and a baseball bat. They were threatened not to escape, and the female victim reported being ordered to dig their graves. The male victim managed to flee, hide, and seek help, leading to the discovery of the female victim. The suspects, Linda Guest and Joseary Arizmendi, were arrested based on evidence and victim statements. Arizmendi faces charges of first-degree assault, second-degree kidnapping, and aggravated robbery. The arrest affidavit of Guest was not available at the time of reporting.

author: George Mouratidis
title: Does mental illness beget great poetry? These 4 poets exposed the sickness of a society that sought to contain them
mainText: This article delves into the relationship between mental illness and creativity, particularly through the lenses of poetry and society. It explores the question of whether mental illness leads to great poetry and the complexities of romanticizing 'accursed' poets. The discussion involves the cultural tradition of treating madness as a source of vision and prophecy, contrasting clinical definitions of mental illness. Poets like Allen Ginsberg, Bob Kaufman, Elise Cowen, and Wanda Coleman are highlighted for their struggles with mental health and their poetic expressions that challenge societal norms. The article delves into Ginsberg's personal experiences with mental health, especially influenced by his mother's schizophrenia. It analyzes Ginsberg's poem 'Howl' as a cry of compassion and salvation, challenging societal structures. Bob Kaufman, known for his jazz poetry, faced harassment and mental health struggles in a segregationist America, reflected in his raw and improvisatory verses. Elise Cowen's poetry, influenced by Emily Dickinson, reflects a sense of alienation and paranoia, addressing societal and personal complexities. Wanda Coleman, a poet of witness, courageously voices her experiences as a Black woman navigating systemic injustice and mental health challenges. These poets offer unique perspectives that challenge societal norms, embodying authenticity and vulnerability. Their work illuminates truths often overlooked, promoting empathy and compassion in a dehumanizing world. The article concludes by emphasizing the revolutionary nature of these poets' salvations of the human experience, offering a poignant reminder of the power of art and vulnerability in shifting societal perceptions.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Skilled trades on the rise as college enrollment sags. ‘Ticket to the middle class’
mainText: The skilled trades sector is experiencing a resurgence as young adults are choosing vocational paths over traditional higher education due to soaring college costs and student debt. Enrollment in community colleges focusing on trades is up, with mechanical, repair, and construction programs seeing growth. Partnerships between employers and schools are helping attract teenagers to trade careers. High school graduates like Dan Tague are opting for programs in fields such as electrical technology, with some having their tuition covered by scholarships or employers. Trade schools are expanding offerings and facilities to meet the demand for trained workers. While college graduates tend to earn more over their lifetime, skilled trades offer a faster path to the middle class with good-paying jobs and lower student debt. Programs like STEP are aiming to engage high schoolers in skilled trades early. The shift in perspective and increased interest in trades have led to programs and partnerships that provide hands-on training and certification for careers like welding and HVAC. The shortage of workers in trades is being addressed as more young people like Jalen Watson and David Maloney pursue careers in fields like HVAC and welding. Programs and initiatives are helping bridge the workforce gap in industries such as plumbing and machining, offering job placement and advancement opportunities for individuals pursuing careers in the skilled trades.

author: Bernd Riegert
title: Giorgia Meloni riding high as G7 begins in Italy
mainText: The Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, a right-wing populist, is heading to the G7 summit in Italy in a strong position following her party's success in the European parliamentary elections. The G7, consisting of the US, Canada, Japan, France, the UK, Germany, and the European Union, is meeting in Puglia under Italy's presidency. Meloni is determined to showcase the economic progress in the region, partly due to EU funds. While Meloni is strengthening her position, other European leaders like Macron, Scholz, and Sunak are facing challenges at home. Meloni aims to have a greater say in the EU and G7, particularly in supporting Ukraine against Russia. At the summit, discussions will include providing aid to Ukraine for defense and reconstruction post-war. Additionally, Meloni wants to enhance cooperation with Africa, focusing on investment, energy production, and migration management. The G7 countries are urged to increase financial commitments to address world hunger and the growing debt crisis. The summit also addresses migration issues, with some Western countries imposing conditions on aid to African nations. Meloni has pledged to restrict Italy's borders to migrants and refugees. The G7 supports a US-proposed resolution for a cease-fire in Gaza, encouraging Hamas to accept the terms for peace. However, Israel's stance on the resolution remains unclear. Overall, the G7 summit in Italy covers a wide range of topics from international relations to humanitarian issues.

author: Deutsche Welle
title: Ukraine updates: Fatal daytime strike on Zelenskyy hometown
mainText: Russian President Vladimir Putin could pay a visit to North Korea as early as next week, according to several reports from the region. On Wednesday, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un sent Putin a congratulatory message to mark Russia's National Day in which he hailed the growing relationship between the two countries. "Thanks to the significant meeting between us at the Vostochney Spaceport in September last year, friendly and cooperative relations [between North Korea and Russia] developed into an unbreakable relationship of comrades-in-arms," Kim said in the message which was carried bv Pyongyang's official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) and referred to Kim's visit to Russia's far east last year. Their "meaningful" ties will "further consolidate the eternal milestone" in the new era, Kim added. The message came as Japanese public broadcaster NHK and South Korea's Yonhap news agency both reported on Wednesday that Putin could visit Pyongyang "as early as next week" as part of a trip to North Korea and Vietnam. NHK cited unidentified diplomatic sources including high-ranking Russian officials while Yonhap said that satellite images showed possible signs of a "large structure" being installed in Kim Il Sung Square in Pyongyang. Neither Russia nor North Korea have officially confirmed any plans, but Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov did tell a briefing in May that a visit is "in the pipeline, and we will make an announcement in due time." Should the visit materialize, it would be the third in-person meeting between Kim and Putin. During their September meeting in Vostochney, Kim invited the Russian president to visit North Korea at "a convenient time," which Putin accepted. Kim's visit to Russia's main space launch site in September was significant since western intelligence agencies believe that Moscow is providing Pyongyang with advanced technologies for its space program in return for artillery and missiles for use in Ukraine. Both North Korea and Russia deny allegations of arms transfers, which would be a violation of multiple UN Security Council resolutions. In the last month, tensions between North and South Korea have escalated as the two have traded trash-filled balloons and loudspeaker propaganda.

author: Nadia Bailey
title: God-kings and everyday people: NGV’s blockbuster isn’t just about pharaohs
mainText: Pharaoh is, by the numbers, an enormous exhibition. It boasts more than 500 objects. It spans 3000 years of history. It sprawls across the entire ground floor of the gallery. Yet while this year’s Winter Masterpieces exhibition at the National Gallery of Victoria more than captures the myth and grandeur of the ancient Egyptian civilisation and its celebrated god-kings, it also attends to something quieter and more intimate: the lives of everyday people. Take, for example, a statuette of the god Amun-Ra, created circa 1069-656 BCE. No taller than a Barbie doll, it would have been displayed in the innermost section of a temple and tended to by priests, whose role was to appease the pantheon of Egyptian gods through ritual and offerings. As curator Marie Vandenbeusch explains, the object tells us a particular story about privilege and access in ancient Egyptian civilisation: “Temples were closed to most people – only certain types of priests and the kings were allowed in,” she says.

author: Khayl Adam
title: Betrayal as OG Mass Effect Citadel Sprinting Revealed to Be a Lie
mainText: Developer BioWare has been pulling the wool over the eyes of fans for more than a decade, convincing gamers through clever technical tricks that they were going fast when, in fact, they were not. The veil was lifted after Dragon Age Inquisition's "horse sprinting" was revealed to be an illusion, and now it seems that Shepard never actually moved any faster on the Citadel, either; you just thought they did. Eurogamer has been on the bleeding edge of this one, noting as former BioWare veteran John Ebenger dropped truth bombs on Twitter. In the original version of Mass Effect (released in 2007, coming to PS3 in 2012), technical limitations prevented the game from loading any faster, so a change to the camera was made to give the illusion of moving faster: "Same thing in Mass Effect 1 when you try to run on the Citadel. No change in speed, just in the FOV of the camera to give the illusion you're moving faster. Can't remember if that stayed true for 2 and 3 or if load times were better by then." A proper sprint button was added to the bundled Legendary Edition, so this only applies to the original release. Did this technical trickery take you in, or were you aware that Shepard was only pretending to sprint this whole time? Discuss in the comments section below.

author: Mashable Team
title: NYT Connections today: See hints and answers for June 13
mainText: Connections is a popular word game by The New York Times where players have to find common threads between words. Like Wordle, the game resets daily and gets progressively challenging. Players have to group four words that share a similarity, with each set of words falling into four categories. The game allows up to four mistakes before ending and features color-coded difficulty levels. Players can rearrange the board to help find connections. Today's hints for Connections categories are given as Yellow: To like something, Green: The film of the summer, Blue: Things you give away on the campaign trail, Purple: Words After "Copy". The solution for today's Connections includes words like APPRECIATE, HIT, BUTTON, and CAT. The game provides a fun challenge with new puzzles daily. If you missed yesterday's, hints and answers are available as well.

author: Tyler Treese
title: Blade Director Yann Demange Leaves Troubled MCU Movie
mainText: The Marvel Cinematic Universe Blade movie has now lost its second director as Yann Demange has left the project. The Wrap is reporting that Demange, who is best known for his work on Lovecraft Country, left the project “a while ago.” He’s the second director to leave, with the first being Bassam Tariq. The move was said to be “amicable” and that Marvel is more concerned with getting the film right than rushing it forward. Currently, Blade is being written by Eric Pearson (The Fantastic Four). Previous scripts were written by Michael Starrbury, Nic Pizzolatto, and Michael Green. The project has undergone several changes to both cast and crew over the years. Blade’s production had a turbulent period throughout the last two years, with previous director Bassim Tariq leaving the project in 2022. Originally set to release on November 3, 2023, the movie ended up being delayed to September 6, 2024. Now it is set for November 7, 2025. It will star Mahershala Ali and Mia Goth, who is rumored to be playing the role of Lilith. Wesley Snipes previously starred as the titular Daywalker in the New Line Cinema Blade trilogy from the late ’90s to early 2000s. He was then played by Kirk “Sticky Fingaz” Jones in the 2006 Spike TV series. Most recently, in 2022’s Marvel’s Midnight Suns video game, the character was voiced by Michael Jai White.

author: Daniel Neira
title: ‘Inside Out 2’: How Maya Hawke added elements of her ‘own weird self’ into her character [EXCLUSIVE]
mainText: The second installment of ‘Inside Out’ brings back the fan-favorite emotions that captivated the audience in 2015. This time the storyline continues with Riley Andersen as a teenager, introducing new emotions that follow along for the journey, not only bringing an element of nostalgia for fans of the franchise but also giving an opportunity to a new audience to relate to the emotional situations in the movie. HOLA! had the chance to talk to the cast of ‘Inside Out 2,’ including Amy Poehler, who portrays Joy, and Maya Hawke, who is welcomed in the story as Anxiety. The pair detailed their experience working on the set of the movie and gave some insight into the importance of showing Riley’s journey and identifying her emotions on-screen. “I have no idea if this is true or not but I did do feel when I watched the movie that I saw some of my own hand gestures for the character in it,” Maya said, “You have to move your body in even crazy ways than you normally would to get the voice to go there, so I’m really happy to see little things I recognize from my own weird self,” she added. Tony Hale, who portrays Fear, and Liza Lapira, who voices Disgust, also talked to HOLA! about their time in the studio voicing their characters, and explained how they added some of their personality into the emotions. “I think with Joy what has been really fun is the process is so collaborative, you can try anything, I think it was my idea in the beginning for Joy to play the accordion,” Amy revealed, adding that Joy is a little “genderless.” “And I think that like there’s some really fun thing to play around with the way in which she presents herself and moves,” she said. “My character taught me and all of them, the emotions that are perceived as negative, it taught me that there is value here. It is protecting me, what is it protecting me from? what is it pointing me towards?” Liza said, while Tony admitted that for him “it was just a reminder to not beat myself up for emotions.” “It’s just a constant reminder of like especially in the end when they all embrace it’s like, ‘Yeah I need to have a lot more compassion towards myself,” he concluded.

author: Kaitlyn Humani
title: Takeru Kobayashi, Joey Chestnut to compete in Netflix competition
mainText: After Nathan’s Famous Fourth of July hot dog-eating contest organizers announced that Joey Chestnut wouldn’t compete due to a deal with a rival brand, Netflix quickly revealed a new hot dog-eating competition featuring Chestnut and his rival Takeru Kobayashi. The live Netflix special titled “Chestnut vs. Kobayashi: Unfinished Beef” on Sept. 2 will showcase the two eating all-beef hot dogs, possibly in response to rumors of Chestnut's deal with Impossible Foods. Major League Eating stated that Chestnut’s decision to withdraw was due to an exclusivity issue, but Chestnut disputed this, accusing Nathan’s and Major League Eating of the decision. Impossible Foods, although not confirming a relationship with Chestnut, supported his choice to compete. Both competitors expressed eagerness for the showdown, with Chestnut acknowledging Kobayashi as his fiercest rival, while Kobayashi vowed to defeat Chestnut one last time. The competition symbolizes Netflix’s expansion into live TV and emphasis on sporting events, including upcoming NFL games and WWE’s “Raw.”

author: Alana Brophy
title: Sizzling heat takes over the Wasatch Front with heat alerts in place
mainText: SALT LAKE CITY (ABC4) — Happy Wednesday, Utah! The heat is on across the state as a strong ridge is in place over the Great Basin this afternoon. The ridge is pushing daytime highs to near-record territory for some of northern Utah, potentially bringing the first triple-digit day of the year to cities along the Wasatch Front. Salt Lake City usually hits triple digits by July 7th, so this is ahead of schedule, though not a record; the earliest was June 4th. This early high heat is concerning, as the ridge could push temperatures 15 to 18 degrees above average. The hottest days are forecasted for today and Thursday, with an Excessive Heat Warning for Glen Canyon from 11 a.m. to 10 p.m. Thursday. Highs may reach up to 105 degrees, with overnight lows in the mid-70s. Northern valleys along the Wasatch Front are under a Heat Advisory, with temperatures likely in the upper 90s and possibly reaching 100 degrees in Salt Lake City. Thursday might bring some cloud cover, but a strong southwest flow could keep temperatures high with an expected record high of 102 degrees in Salt Lake by the afternoon, which would tie the record from 2021. By late Thursday into Friday, a low-pressure system will bring unsettled weather into the state, with moisture, scattered showers, and thunderstorms in south-central and eastern Utah. Cloud cover will increase over northern Utah on Friday as well, with a slight chance of storms over the mountain areas east of I-15. Temperatures will drop by about 10 to 15 degrees, with lower Washington County reaching near 99 to 100 degrees. With the risk of thunderstorms late Thursday into Friday east of I-15, we will be 4Warning you of potential flash flood concerns. This weekend, a low-pressure system over the Pacific Northwest will cool temperatures along the Wasatch Front starting Saturday. The forecast for Sunday and Monday is uncertain, but early next week should bring more seasonal temperatures, with many welcoming a return to the 80s, possibly even the upper 70s. Stay tuned.

author: Emily Beament
title: UK politicians test positive for ‘forever chemicals’ in their system
mainText: Political parties have been urged to address the issue of "forever chemicals" after a group of politicians and environmental leaders in the UK tested positive for PFAS. These toxic chemicals, also known as 'forever chemicals', can harm people and wildlife. The participants in the study, including former Green Party MP Caroline Lucas and Labour's Alex Sobel, tested positive for PFAS and other harmful chemicals like endocrine disruptors and heavy metals. Campaigners highlight the ineffective regulation in the UK and the risks that chemical pollution poses to the environment and public health. They call for bans on PFAS and endocrine disruptors, improved monitoring systems, and assessing the impacts of chemical cocktails on the environment. Forever chemicals are commonly found in everyday consumer goods and have been linked to health issues ranging from cancer risks to fertility problems. The presence of toxic chemicals in rivers and groundwater is widespread in the UK, affecting both wildlife and human health. Wildlife and Countryside Link (WCL) is leading the call for stronger regulations and protections against harmful chemicals. The research found high levels of PFAS, chromium, mercury, and endocrine disruptors in the participants, indicating the widespread presence of these chemicals in the environment and food chain. The CEO of WCL emphasizes the urgent need for action to address the growing threat of chemical contamination in the UK. The study highlights the alarming level of chemical contamination in bodies and the urgent need for governmental intervention to protect public health and the environment. Participants stress the importance of removing hazardous chemicals from consumer products and food to safeguard human health and the environment.

author: Katharine Hay
title: Why Scotland deer numbers have plummeted by more than half in a scenic Highlands location
mainText: An independent land management group in the Cairngorms, the Upper Deeside and Donside Land Management Group (UDDLM), has successfully reduced the red deer population by more than half since the 1990s. The group covers around a quarter of the national park and has seen the deer numbers drop from 8,411 in 1996 to 4,054 in 2024, resulting in about four deer per sqkm compared to eight previously. This reduction has led to improvements in native woodlands and moorland management. UDDLM covers 17 land management units managed by various owners for farming, grouse shooting, deer stalking, timber production, and conservation. By collaborating and understanding each other's objectives, the group has achieved successful deer management. The results highlight the benefits of cooperative working in deer management. The Scottish Government is considering proposals to legislate deer management, potentially requiring landowners to manage deer populations or face fines and jail time. UDDLM encourages collaborative working over heavy-handed regulation. The Cairngorms Deer Pilot, training locals in deer management, is to be expanded nationwide to incentivize increased management and investment in the venison supply chain, following the success of the pilot that started in 2023. The project aims to support more local consumption of wild venison, aligning with recommendations from the 2019 Deer Working Group report.

author: Laurence Darmiento
title: Regulators identify wildfire neighborhoods for insurance relief
mainText: California regulators disclosed the areas in the state that insurers are required to cover to resolve the homeowners' insurance crisis. The draft regulations from the Department of Insurance identify ZIP Codes in regions like the Santa Monica Mountains, the San Gabriel Mountains, and parts of the Santa Clarita Valley in Los Angeles County. The Sustainable Insurance Strategy introduced last fall by Insurance Commissioner Ricardo Lara includes new regulations expected to be enforced by the end of the year. The plan involves allowing insurers to factor the cost of reinsurance and using computer models to project future claims risks, replacing the use of historical claims data for rate hike requests. Large insurers must provide coverage in wildfire risk areas equivalent to 85% of their market share, while smaller insurers have to increase policies by 5%. The regulations utilize a three-part approach based on geographic diversity, aiming to maximize coverage in high-risk areas. They target entire counties with over 20% high-risk properties or ZIP Codes with over 15% FAIR Plan policyholders. The goal is to ensure coverage in areas where insurance is unaffordable based on income or premium costs. Insurers failing to comply could face rate reductions and premium rebates. Consumer advocates expressed concerns about insurers having too much time to meet targets and exceptions granted by regulators. Industry representatives welcomed the regulations, emphasizing the progress made towards insurance market health. Governor Gavin Newsom supported the reform plan, calling the regulations a critical step towards resolving California's insurance crisis. The Department of Insurance issued a state map and list of affected ZIP Codes, including neighborhoods in Malibu, Beverly Hills, and Catalina Island. A hearing on June 26 will gather input from insurers, consumer advocates, and policyholders.

author: Ariana Brockington
title: Joey Chestnut and Takeru Kobayashi Face Off In Netflix's Hot Dog Contest
mainText: Hot dog eating champions Joey Chestnut and Takeru Kobayashi have “Unfinished Beef” to settle. On June 12, Netflix announced that the two competitive eaters, who have faced off before at Nathan’s Famous Hot Dog Eating Contest, will battle it out to prove which one of them is the better hot dog eating champion. The live event will be called “Chestnut vs. Kobayashi: Unfinished Beef.” For the upcoming showdown, Chestnut, a 16-time Nathan's hot dog eating champion, and Kobayashi, a six-time winner, will see which one can scarf down the most hot dogs. They became adversaries after facing off at the annual Nathan's Famous Hot Dog Eating Contest held on July 4. But the two haven’t competed against each other since 2009. At that time, Chestnut bested Kobayashi in a five hot dog sudden-death event that determined the winner. Chestnut has been victorious at the Nathan’s contest for the past eight years and currently holds a world record for eating 76 hot dogs in 10 minutes. Kobayashi dominated the event from 2001 to 2006, but he was banned in 2010 due to a contract dispute. Now, 15 years after their last battle, the two are ready to put their impressive eating skills on display once again. When is the “Chestnut vs. Kobayashi: Unfinished Beef” contest? Netflix will stream the event live on Labor Day, Sept. 2. Did Takeru Kobayashi retire from competitive eating? On June 12, he confirmed that he isn’t ready to say goodbye just yet. What has Joey Chestnut said about his contest with Takeru Kobayashi? Chestnut referred to Kobayashi as his “fiercest rival” in a statement about their Labor Day event.

author: Jessica Green
title: Queen Maxima of the Netherlands swaps her protective gear at a tech hub to a stunning yellow dress...
mainText: Queen Maxima of the Netherlands swaps her protective gear at a tech hub to a stunning yellow dress as she and King Willem-Alexander visit New York Governor Kathy Hochul Queen Maxima and King Willem-Alexander are on a four-day trip to America Queen Maxima of the Netherlands once again proved she's queen of the quick change today as she continued her four-day tour of America with her husband King Willem-Alexander. The mother-of-three, 53, first toured NY Creates, a tech hub for semiconductor research and development, during a visit to Albany, New York. Next, Maxima and Willem-Alexander visited New York Governor Kathy Hochul and her husband William J. Hochul Jr., alongside Dutch Minister of Foreign Trade and Development Liesje Schreinemacher. For this visit, Maxima ditched the protective gear from earlier and donned a bright yellow gown, complete with cream floral detailing on the bodice. Standing alongside her equally smart-looking husband in one photograph from the event, Maxima carried a cream clutch and gloves in her hand. Willem-Alexander, meanwhile, appeared sophisticated in a pinstriped suit teamed with a white shirt and a bright blue tie. On Tuesday, the king and queen of the Netherlands spent the second day of their US tour in Georgia's founding city, Savannah, a tourism magnet for its wealth of historic architecture and a growing powerhouse in global trade. The Dutch royals took a stroll beneath majestic live oaks draped with Spanish moss in the prized historic district of the city founded by British colonists in 1733. Afterward, they toured the Port of Savannah, the fourth-busiest US seaport for cargo shipped in containers. The king and queen chatted with crane operators on the dock as containers were being loaded onto a mammoth cargo ship behind them. Total trade between Georgia and the Netherlands was $2.9 billion last year. The Dutch royals' four-day US trip began Monday in Atlanta. The king and queen met with Gov. Brian Kemp at Georgia's state Capitol, toured the burial site of the Rev. Martin Luther King Jr. and visited a recording studio in a city known for hip-hop artists. The king and queen are scheduled to spend Wednesday and Thursday in New York to wrap up their US tour.

author: Melissa Rudy
title: Tiger mosquitoes blamed for spread of dengue fever: ‘Most invasive species’
mainText: As dengue fever continues to spread throughout Europe, experts are blaming an invasive mosquito species as the culprit. Known as "tiger mosquitoes," the insects of the species name Aedes albopictus have spread into 13 EU countries. Elitza Theel, PhD, director of Mayo Clinic Laboratories, confirmed that tiger mosquitoes are a known vector for dengue virus. Climate change is one of the factors contributing to the spread of these insects. Dengue fever is a virus spread through bites from an infected mosquito. Typical symptoms include aches, pains, nausea, vomiting, and rash. Dengue fever is common in various regions globally.

author: Aami
title: Ethylene Oxide Sterilizer Standard Updated to Reflect Technological Changes
mainText: The Association for the Advancement of Medical Instrumentation has updated its standard on ethylene oxide (EO) sterilizers for use in health care facilities to reflect technological changes. The new standard, ANSI/AAMI ST24:2024, covers general-purpose EO sterilizers with automated process control and sterilant sources. It addresses labeling, safety, performance, and testing requirements for EO sterilizers used in health care facilities. The updated standard is relevant to medical device manufacturers, sterile processing departments, and healthcare facilities facing supply concerns and regulatory changes due to the Environmental Protection Agency's Final Rule on EO. Key areas covered include EO emission control systems, sterilizer construction, safety measures for workers, testing methods for conformance, and more. The standard was developed by AAMI's Hospital EO Sterilizers Working Group, with input from industry experts. The co-chair of the Working Group, Ted May, emphasized the importance of the updated standard in reflecting current practices and advancements in EO sterilization over the past two decades. The fourth edition of ANSI/AAMI ST24 aims to be a valuable resource for manufacturers and healthcare organizations utilizing EO sterilization. Interested parties can access or purchase the standard through AAMI ARRAY. For journalists and writers looking for a sample copy, they can contact the AAMI Media Team at dvisnovsky@aami.org.

author: Xinghua Xu
title: Minimally invasive surgeries for spontaneous hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage (MISICH): a multicenter randomized controlled trial
mainText: The study conducted between 2016 and 2022 involved 721 patients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) who were divided into three treatment groups: endoscopy, aspiration, and craniotomy. The demographics and baseline characteristics of the patients were similar among the groups. The mean hematoma clearance rate was highest in the endoscopy group, followed by craniotomy and aspiration group. Endoscopy and aspiration had less intraoperative blood loss and lower rates of blood transfusion compared to craniotomy. The incidence of stroke-related pneumonia was highest in the craniotomy group. Functional outcomes at 6 months varied, with the endoscopy and aspiration groups showing a higher proportion of patients with favorable outcomes compared to the craniotomy group. Young age, better GCS score, smaller hematoma volume, lobar hematoma location, endoscopic surgery, stereotactic aspiration, and no intracranial infection were associated with better functional outcomes. Endoscopic surgery and stereotactic aspiration resulted in significantly higher probabilities of favorable outcomes for supratentorial deep hemorrhages. Safety events were monitored, and specified safety thresholds were not exceeded throughout the trial. Mortality rates and rates of post-operative complications were similar among the three groups. At the 6-month follow-up, patients in the endoscopy and aspiration groups had better quality of life compared to the craniotomy group. The study concluded that minimally invasive surgeries such as endoscopy and stereotactic aspiration may offer better functional outcomes and quality of life for patients with ICH compared to traditional craniotomy.

author: Xanthe Clay
title: Vegan sausages: The hidden health hazards of meatless substitutes and their subsequent decline in popularity
mainText: These meatless substitutes contain a range of highly processed ingredients, leading to a decline in supermarket sales. New research from The Lancet suggests that ultra-processed vegan foods may increase the risk of heart disease-related deaths. A study of 118,000 Britons found that plant-based diets can be heart-protective, but only if based on whole foods. An increase in plant-based ultra-processed foods was associated with a rise in heart disease deaths. Despite a previous rise in sales of meat-free alternatives, recent data shows a decline in popularity. Notably, one British sausage maker reduced its vegan product range due to decreased demand. Sales of meat-free products in British supermarkets dropped by £37.3 million in one year. While the meat-free market remains substantial, there has been a recent reversal in sales trends. Vegan sausages are often composed of highly processed ingredients, including pea protein, textured soy protein, and mycoprotein, categorizing them as ultra-processed foods. The additives and oils used in these sausages may have negative health implications and contribute to excess consumption. Health claims on vegan sausage packaging should be approached with caution. Real meat sausages also pose health risks due to processed meat content and high levels of salt and saturated fat. Vegan sausages, with varying nutritional profiles, offer an alternative but may still contain unhealthy levels of salt and fat. While vegan junk food can provide a sustainable option, concerns exist regarding the environmental impact of ultra-processed foods. It is suggested to reduce meat consumption for the planet's sake and consider ethical concerns surrounding meat production. Despite their drawbacks, vegan sausages are likely to remain popular. For individuals preferring traditional pork sausages, selecting products with minimal ingredients and high-quality meat is recommended. Both vegan and meat sausages have their health implications, emphasizing the importance of moderation and informed food choices.

author: Mike Schneider
title: Disney and DeSantis reach final agreement, approves new development deal
mainText: ORLANDO, Fla. (AP) — Gov. Ron DeSantis’ appointees on Wednesday gave final approval to an agreement that buries the hatchet between Disney and the governing district for Walt Disney World, which the Florida governor took over after the company two years ago publicly opposed a state law critics dubbed “Don’t Say Gay.” The five DeSantis-appointed board members to the Central Florida Tourism Oversight District unanimously voted to approve a 15-year development deal in which the district committed to making infrastructure improvements in exchange for Disney investing up to $17 billion into Disney World over the next two decades. The agreement followed a detente in March in which both sides agreed to stop litigating each other in state court and work towards negotiating a new development agreement and a new comprehensive plan no later than next year. Disney will be required to donate up to 100 acres (40 hectares) of Disney World’s 24,000 acres (9,700 hectares) for the construction of infrastructure projects controlled by the district. The company also will need to award at least half of its construction projects to companies based in Florida and spend at least $10 million on affordable housing for central Florida. Disney would then be approved to build a fifth major theme park at Disney World and two more minor parks, such as water parks, if it desired. Leaders of Orlando’s tourism industry praised the agreement, telling the district’s board members that it will bring boundless jobs, tourists and attention to central Florida. Still up in the air was an appeal of a federal lawsuit Disney had filed against DeSantis and his appointees. After the settlement was reached in March, Disney asked the appellate court to put that case on hold while the development agreement was negotiated. Disney has until next week to file a brief with the court if it wants to move ahead with the case. The March settlement ended almost two years of litigation sparked by DeSantis’ takeover of the district following the company’s opposition to the 2022 law that bans classroom lessons on sexual orientation and gender identity in early grades. Disney filed counterclaims that included asking the state court to declare the agreements valid and enforceable. Those state court lawsuits were dismissed as part of the March settlement. Follow Mike Schneider on the social platform X: @MikeSchneiderAP.

author: Kaitlyn Huamani
title: Joey Chestnut, Takeru Kobayashi to compete in Netflix competition
mainText: After organizers for Nathan’s Famous Fourth of July hot dog-eating contest announced that Joey Chestnut would not compete this year due to a deal with a rival brand, Netflix quickly revealed a new hot dog-eating competition featuring Chestnut and his longtime competitor Takeru Kobayashi. The live Netflix special, titled 'Chestnut vs. Kobayashi: Unfinished Beef,' will showcase the two champions devouring all-beef hot dogs. Major League Eating, which oversees the Nathan’s contest, explained that Chestnut's decision to step back was due to an 'exclusivity' issue with a reported deal with Impossible Foods for plant-based hot dogs. Despite Chestnut's claim that the decision was made by Nathan's and Major League Eating, he expressed eagerness to compete again soon. The new competition on Netflix has sparked mixed reactions, with NYC Mayor Eric Adams urging for Chestnut's return to the traditional Fourth of July event. Chestnut and Kobayashi expressed excitement about their upcoming showdown, the first since 2009. The competition marks Netflix's venture into live TV sporting events, aligning with their recent focus on sports content. The hot dog-eating contest will be followed by other sporting events on the streaming service, including Christmas Day NFL games and WWE's 'Raw' in 2025.

author: Mark Footer
title: Could AI save Japan from selfie taking hordes? Can travellers avoid ‘world’s worst airport’?
mainText: Like a huge game of whack-a-mole, local authorities around Japan’s Mount Fuji are trying to keep overzealous tourists under control as the visitors all attempt to shoot the same pictures of Fuji-san for their social-media feeds. Post-pandemic, tourists have rushed back to Japan – a beautiful country whose appeal is now turbocharged by a weak yen – and an overwhelming majority have converged on the usual hotspots, with smartphones raised. After photos began appearing online of Mount Fuji seemingly perched atop a Lawson convenience store in Fujikawaguchiko, social-media-loving sheeple all suddenly “needed” to have that picture. In April, complaints by Fujikawaguchiko residents reached a crescendo, leading to the erection of a view-blocking barrier. It took just days before the barrier was having holes poked in it by those who would not be denied. Then it was the turn of the residents of Fuji City, on the other side of the mountain, to complain – this time over the ruckus developing around a decade-old bridge. The Mount Fuji Dream Bridge – they were perhaps asking for trouble with that name – aligns with the outline of the sacred mountain in such a way that, from some angles, its steps appear to lead towards the peak. The trouble “all began in December last year when a foreign influencer put images on Instagram”, Miyu Toyama, an official of the Exchange Tourism Division of the city government, told the Post. “The image soon spread and now almost all the people who visit the bridge are foreigners, not Japanese. “People even come when it is raining or if Mount Fuji is covered in clouds, which causes problems because they stay longer, hoping that it will clear and that means lots of people can be there at the same time,” said Toyama. Some even arrive with their luggage. Residents have complained about illegal parking, rubbish, loud noise and even public defecation. Multilingual signs asking visitors to behave and not run across a busy road by the bridge have proved useless, and purpose-built parking and bathroom facilities inadequate, so now plans are in place to erect a 1.8-metre-high metal mesh fence by the end of June, to thwart those seeking their stairway-to-heaven shot. Japan is 377,973 sq km (145,936 square miles) in size and most of it sees few tourists because the 3 million or so who descend on the country every month tend to be an unimaginative lot whose travel itineraries centre on selfies. That trail leads inevitably not just to Mount Fuji, but also to Kyoto. The ancient capital has long struggled with its visitors – “Overtourism in Kyoto reaches breaking point, with ‘half-naked hikers, trespassing travellers’ making life a misery for residents,” ran a Post headline in 2018 – and city authorities have brought in a series of innovative and/or desperate measures designed to ease the load on residents, including the much-harassed geishas. The latest attempt to corral the crowds is the introduction this month of the Sightseeing Limited Express Bus. This involves two routes that stop only at the city’s major tourist sites. The aim is to free up space on buses used by ordinary citizens. It’s difficult to know how best to balance the needs of residents and the desires of money-bringing visitors. Measures such as quotas and dynamic pricing have their appeal but also their drawbacks. Perhaps it won’t be long before tourism boards begin employing AI to send out deflection photos on Instagram, Weibo and TikTok, to lead the social media set off to random spots around their country. Gratis Macau In another one of those surveys wherein some company or other makes lists out of Tripadvisor or Booking.com information, Macau has been deemed one of the best places in which to find activities that cost nothing. Personal finance outfit CashNetUSA has analysed the Tripadvisor reviews of free attractions at nearly 1,000 of the world’s most popular destinations to conclude that, within Asia, Macau, with 10.06 per cent of its attractions noted as being free, beats the Malaysian trio of Melaka (9.79 per cent), Kuching (9.3 per cent) and George Town (7.87 per cent). Hong Kong comes in at 10th, with 5.62 per cent of its attractions counted as being free to enter. Unfortunately, the free stuff to do in Macau isn’t that great. The city doesn’t make it onto another list, which ranks the quality (average review rating) of Asia’s free attractions by destination, the top three spots of which are taken by Nepal; Antalya, Turkey; and Qatar. Terminal headache Elsewhere in Asia, visitors may have to negotiate what’s been called the world’s worst airport, by the writer of an opinion piece in British newspaper The Times. The best airports are in the Middle East, says Cathy Adams, who claims to have flown into hundreds, and those in Hong Kong and Singapore “are a connoisseur’s choice and both are frighteningly efficient”. Furthermore, Adams writes, “I will always have a soft spot for Koh Samui, where arriving passengers file through cute wooden Thai pavilions, but less time for Bangkok’s cramped Don Mueang, which is as budget as the airlines it handles.” She has even less time for the immigration queues in Mumbai, India, which “are so legendarily bad that there’s even a kiosk just to deal for people who miss their flights because of them, and every Chinese airport I have ever visited, from Shenzhen to Beijing’s old PEK, smells like fags [cigarettes] with bad food”. But Adams reserves most of her scorn for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport, in Manila, the Philippines, “a sprawling, non-air-conditioned Sodom and Gomorrah of four separate terminals only sporadically connected by shuttle”. “Your airline might think you can transit in 90 minutes, but from bitter experience I can tell you it will take four hours (and usually in the small hours). Which is awkward in a country for which transiting in Manila is the only way to get around.”

author: Kylie Knott
title: Circular fashion promoted by Hong Kong charities to reduce volume of clothing thrown away
mainText:
The 16-tonne mountain of clothes, spread several metres high and wide on the 11th floor of an office tower in Hong Kong’s Quarry Bay district, is a jaw-dropping sight. Sifting through it are volunteers taking part in a three-day “Sort-A-Thon” organised by Redress, a Hong Kong-based charity that raises awareness about the fashion industry’s damaging environmental impact. The floor in Lincoln House is a hive of activity as garments are sorted into boxes labelled according to category, from baby clothes and business shirts to shoes and sportswear.
The scale of the pile may be shocking, but the director of Redress’ circular fashion programme, Aurianne Ricquier, says it represents just a fraction of the volume of waste textiles thrown away in Hong Kong every day. “In 2022, an average of 388 tonnes (428 tons) of textiles were discarded into Hong Kong landfills every day, with 50 per cent estimated to be clothes,” Ricquier says. A 2020 Redress report on consumer usage and disposal habits found that two out of five Hongkongers discard their clothes after wearing them for a year or less, she notes.
The collection is the result of a clothing drive held in May as part of Get Redressed Month, the city’s largest clothing consumer awareness campaign. With the motto “Your Clothes, Our Planet”, the campaign encourages consumers to rethink their relationship with clothing and the environment by highlighting the benefits of circular fashion, a system that aims to extend the life of garments through innovative design, repair and recycling initiatives. Past “second life” campaigns have been successful: in 2022, Get Redressed Month collected 16.2 tonnes of clothing, with 60 per cent redistributed to Redress’ charity partners and 17 per cent resold at Redress’ pop-up shop.

author: The Arena Group
title: Video: Peyton Manning Receives Standing Ovation At Tom Brady Hall Of Fame Ceremony
mainText: The New England Patriots enshrined Tom Brady into their Hall of Fame on Wednesday night. Peyton Manning crashed the party at Gillette Stadium. After playing a video tribute at the induction ceremony, host Mike Tirico introduced Manning to an unsuspecting Brady. "There was one person not in that video who said they refused to talk about Tom Brady into a camera again," Tirico said. "And instead, you don't know this is coming, a surprise guest. Ladies and gentlemen, Peyton Manning." In a rare turn of events, Patriots fans gave Manning a standing ovation. Per The Athletic's Jeff Howe, the former Indianapolis Colts legend joked that they like him "because I always lost here." Although they spent years jockeying for AFC supremacy, Manning admitted that they once worked out together during the offseason. In a moment that feels reminiscent of his famous Saturday Night Live sketch, Manning recalled the iconic duo jokingly threatening a group of teenagers who saw them.

author: The Arena Group
title: World Aquatics Doesn't Hold Back On Lia Thomas Ruling
mainText: World Aquatics, a governing body in swimming, has reacted to a court's ruling on Lia Thomas' attempt to compete in the 2024 Summer Olympics. The court ruled in favor of World Aquatics on Wednesday, meaning Thomas is unable to compete in the Summer Olympics in Paris, France. Thomas, the former Penn swimmer, competed on the women's team in college, after transitioning. She began her career on the men's side. World Aquatics didn't hold back on the decision, celebrating it on Wednesday night. "World Aquatics is dedicated to fostering an environment that promotes fairness, respect, and equal opportunities for athletes of all genders and we reaffirm this pledge," the organization said in a statement. "Our policies and practices are continuously evaluated to ensure they align with these core values, which led to the introduction of our open category. "We remain committed to working collaboratively with all stakeholders to uphold the principles of inclusivity in aquatic sports and remain confident that our gender inclusion policy represents a fair approach." Former Kentucky swimmer Riley Gaines, who competed against Thomas, shared her reaction. "This ruling is a small victory for girls and women everywhere. I think we will see more wins like this both in the judicial courts and the courts public opinion as time goes on. Although he would never qualify, Thomas can still try out for the men's U.S. Olympic team. I hope the NCAA now takes a similar decisive action by stripping Thomas off all awards, titles, and records he stole from deserving female athletes."

author: Anabel Munoz
title: Nonprofits helping refugees, asylum seekers already seeing removals at US-Mexico border
mainText: Organizations supporting refugees and asylum seekers in Tijuana, Mexico, are closely monitoring the impact of President Joe Biden's directive to restrict access to asylum between ports of entry. The order was issued due to the high number of daily encounters exceeding 2,500, with the goal of limiting asylum processing. Erika Pinheiro, from Al Otro Lado, highlighted the challenges faced by individuals who cross between ports of entry, particularly affecting certain nationalities like Mexicans. The order has led to the removal of many individuals, including children, who are being flown to southern Mexico and may return to Tijuana. Amid concerns about the lack of time to find legal assistance and the absence of confirmed fear screenings, the impact is evident. The fiscal year 2024 saw the highest number of encounters with U.S. Customs and Border Protection from Mexico, with exceptions for unaccompanied children. The use of the CBP One mobile app is an alternative for appointments. The story portrays the struggles of individuals like Cristina from Guatemala waiting for asylum appointments, emphasizing the need for safe shelter. Immigrant advocacy groups have filed a lawsuit challenging the legality of Biden's asylum crackdown, drawing parallels with Trump's policies and raising concerns about violating federal immigration laws. The directive aims to push migrants to designated ports of entry and includes exemptions for humanitarian reasons. Those not meeting the criteria could face deportation or legal consequences. The new policy requires greater scrutiny for asylum-seekers expressing fear or intent to seek protection. The Biden administration stands by the legality and value of their actions, despite the anticipated legal challenges. The focus is on providing limited humanitarian protection to those who pass the screening process, ensuring compliance with international agreements like the U.N. Convention Against Torture.

author: Post Editorial Board
title: Adrienne Adams panders to City Council's Israel-haters with Gaza cease-fire bill
mainText: Gotham is home to more Jews than any other city in the world — and most Jews (and Americans!) want Israel to survive and Hamas defeated. So why on Earth is the City Council even considering a resolution calling for a cease-fire in Gaza that could help the terror group survive. The kindest answer: Speaker Adrienne Adams is letting far-left Israel-haters dictate the council’s agenda — at the expense of its saner members. Or perhaps she’s one of the Israel-haters herself? After all, she’s pushing the bill and is expected to sign on as a sponsor. Yet, remember: Israel isn’t just the Jewish homeland, a place Jewish Americans largely support and where many of their friends and family live. It’s also a key US ally, the only true democracy in the Middle East and a first line of defense for the West against Iran and blood-thirsty Islamist imperialism. Hamas snatched 14 Americans on Oct. 7, including six from the New York area. Do Speaker Adams & Co. want these monsters to rebuild and launch more attacks? It would be far more apt to demand Israel finish the job against Hamas (and President Biden support it) than call for a cease-fire. And though a council resolution won’t improve New Yorkers’ lives one bit, Hamas will read it as a sign of support, and reason to think the world will force Israel to end its anti-terror war prematurely. This after Adams blocked resolutions condemning Hamas after Oct. 7. The one upside to a cease-fire vote: It’ll force lawmakers to show whose side they’re really on, though Post sources say roughly 20 of them are “really unhappy” about that. Good. Let New Yorkers know whether if they truly support Israel — or the terrorists.

title: Coastal Road must be well-maintained and safe
mainText: Experts have a point of view concerning the opening of the northbound arm of the Coastal Road to vehicular traffic.
