author: Matthew Daly
title: Senate confirms new energy regulators, extending Biden's grip on panel that backs renewable energy
mainText: WASHINGTON (AP) — President Joe Biden's grip on a key federal energy commission will last beyond his first term, giving a boost to the Democrat's push for renewable energy regardless of the election results in November. The Senate ensured that political reality as lawmakers approved three new members of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, including two Democrats. The five-member commission oversees natural gas pipelines and other energy infrastructure, including transmission of electricity across state lines, hydropower and interstate transportation of oil and natural gas. The panel approved a long-awaited rule last month making it easier to transmit renewable energy such as wind and solar power to the electric grid — a key part of Biden’s goal to eliminate greenhouse gas emissions economy-wide by 2050. On Wednesday, the Senate confirmed the nominations of Democrat David Rosner and Republican Lindsay See for three and four-year terms, respectively, on the commission. Senators on Thursday confirmed Democrat Judy Chang’s nomination to a five-year term. The votes give Democrats a 3-2 majority on the commission until at least June 2026, when the term of Democratic Chairman Willie Phillips is set to expire. “A fully seated, bipartisan FERC provides more opportunity for advancing long-lasting, sensible energy infrastructure policy,'' said West Virginia Sen. Joe Manchin, a Democrat-turned-independent who chairs the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee. Rosner, See and Chang “are very different people, from very different backgrounds,'' said Manchin, who supported all three nominees. "What matters most is their willingness to work with one another, to consider and assess fairly different interests and points of view, and to put partisan passions aside in favor of the public interest.'' Democratic Sen. Tim Kaine of Virginia opposed Rosner and See, saying he continued to be unhappy about federal approval of the Mountain Valley Pipeline, a longtime Manchin priority. Americans for a Clean Energy Grid, an advocacy group that supports expansion and modernization of the electric grid, hailed the Senate votes, saying FERC "operates most effectively with a full slate of commissioners.'' Christina Hayes, the group's executive director, said she was pleased that all three new commissioners recognize the need to address growing power demand and strengthen grid reliability. Matthew Daly, The Associated Press

author: Christopher Jasper
title: Starmer rejects Sadiq Khan’s plan to extend his grip beyond London
mainText: Labour has rejected Sadiq Khan’s bid to seize control of rail routes serving commuter towns outside of London. In its manifesto published on Thursday, Sir Keir Starmer’s Opposition ruled out any further expansion of Transport for London (TfL), which falls under Mr Khan’s remit. The Mayor of London, who recently secured his third term, had campaigned to expand TfL’s operations as far as Sevenoaks in Kent and Stevenage in Hertfordshire, which he said would help deliver more frequent services, improved reliability and simpler fares. However Labour confirmed it had snubbed Mr Khan’s proposal as part of its manifesto announcement, which said mayors will be restricted to overseeing “services in their areas”. Instead the Opposition has laid out plans to bring the bulk of UK rail under state control, including routes outside of London that had been targeted by Mr Khan. The manifesto confirmed plans set out by shadow transport secretary Louise Haigh in March for the creation of Great British Railways (GBR), an arms-length body that would have overall responsibility for services. Labour says nationalisation is unlikely to lower fares but should simplify them and provide passengers with a “best-price guarantee.” A spokesman for Mr Khan said the mayor will “work closely with a Labour government to deliver a system that provides the service passengers deserve”. However, the spokesman added: “The existing commuter rail lines in London are clearly not fit for purpose, with cancellations, delays and poor reliability.” It comes after Mr Khan had hoped to run trains currently operated by Southeastern and Great Northern, which link towns across the commuter belt to stations in central London. His proposals had represented a diluted version of a plan mooted by Boris Johnson during his time as mayor, as he has sought to extend TfL’s network across the home counties. As for Labour’s GBR plan, this will not encroach upon Mr Khan’s TfL operations – which include the London Underground, Docklands Light Railway, London Overground and Elizabeth Line. The latter two networks include trains operating as far as Watford and Reading. A source close to the situation said TfL and the mayor’s office would continue to press a Labour government for the right to run more routes, especially those mostly within Greater London.

author: Eve Young
title: Students call on government to accept hostage deal
mainText: Students from dozens of colleges and universities went on strike across the country Thursday to mark 250 days of captivity for Israelis held hostage by Hamas, and to call for the hostage deal currently in discussion to be approved.The strike, accompanied by protest installations and protests, was organized by the National Union of Israeli Students in coordination with the organization of young family members of hostages.Family members also gathered on campuses to share thoughts about siblings in captivity. Roni Elbag, sister of observer Liri Elbag, whose abduction was captured on a video made public last month, spoke at Reichman University, where she is a student.“We have not forgotten them”“The last thing Liri said to the hostages [with her] who were freed was ‘don’t forget us.’ I want us to prove to Liri that we have not forgotten her, and that the state and citizens are doing everything to bring her home. That we are not giving up on 120 hostages.”Some universities supported the strike by relaxing attendance policies to accommodate striking students. “The University management decided to adopt a policy of inclusion on this day. All classes will take place as planned, but no mandatory attendance policy will be enforced,” the student union told Hebrew University students.Liri Albag (credit: Courtesy)The strike in Jerusalem concluded with a march from Hebrew University’s Givat Ram campus to the Knesset, where students called for a hostage deal.Also on Thursday, Highway 4 was blocked by protesters from the “Enough!” organization who set tires alight to block the road, calling for elections now.

author: Josh Payne
title: Dunn family accuse US government of obstructing inquest after coroner criticism
mainText: The family of Harry Dunn, a teenage motorcyclist who died in a collision with a car driven by Anne Sacoolas, have accused the US government of obstructing their son's inquest by not attending. They are seeking a public inquiry into the circumstances that allowed Sacoolas to leave the country after claiming diplomatic immunity. The Northamptonshire coroner criticized the US government for inadequate training of diplomatic personnel and issued prevention of future death notices related to paramedic drugs and driver training. Dunn's mother expressed disgust at Sacoolas and the US Embassy for not attending the inquest. Sacoolas pleaded guilty to causing death by careless driving and received a suspended prison sentence. Spokesman Radd Seiger condemned the US government's handling of the situation, accusing them of obstructing the inquiry and disrespecting UK citizens like Harry. He called for a public inquiry and criticized both the Tory and Labour governments for their responses. Seiger also highlighted the lack of bravery and contempt shown by the US government towards UK citizens like Harry, emphasizing the need for accountability and justice. The Dunn family is determined to hold the US government accountable and is committed to working with the next government to establish a public inquiry.

author: Emily Allen
title: Family of man shot in Portland confronts his killer in court
mainText: The family of Derald Coffin, who was shot and killed in Portland, confronted his convicted killer, 24-year-old Damion Butterfield, in court. As Coffin's young son Levi held his mother's hand, a victim witness advocate read a statement on behalf of Coffin's mother, Dana Wallace, detailing the milestones Coffin would miss with his son. Butterfield was sentenced to 35 years as part of a plea deal for killing Coffin and injuring Annabelle Hartnett during a botched robbery in 2022. He was one of four men involved, but the only one to go to trial. Butterfield's attorneys claim he is innocent and mentally ill. Coffin's family expressed their pain and called out Butterfield's lack of remorse in court, stating that he was not a kid as portrayed by his lawyer. Jonathan Geisinger and Thomas MacDonald are also involved in the case, with Geisinger facing a felony murder charge and MacDonald waiting to be sentenced. Coffin, a father of two, had struggled with substance use disorder but was described by loved ones as more than his addiction. He was remembered for his desire to return home, recover, and help others in need. Coffin's family continues to seek closure and justice throughout the legal proceedings.

author: Pat Hurst
title: Childminder branded ‘a monster’ by family of baby she shook to death
mainText: A heartbroken mother labeled a childminder who fatally shook her baby boy a 'monster' who deserves to be 'haunted' by her actions. Karen Foster, 62, was sentenced to 12 years and seven months for causing the death of nine-month-old Harlow Collinge. Foster, a registered childminder with Ofsted, had initially blamed the child's mother before admitting guilt. Harlow's family expressed their deep loss and the suffering the baby endured before his death. Foster, despite health issues and exceeding her childminding limits, lost her temper while caring for four children. She admitted to forceful shaking leading to Harlow's demise. The court highlighted Foster's failure to adhere to Ofsted rules and her web of lies. Detective Superintendent Allen Davies praised the family's dignity amidst the tragic loss. The case revealed Foster's dishonesty about her personal life and health struggles, as well as her disregard for safety guidelines. The family's impact statements conveyed their ongoing pain and the guilt they feel. Foster's actions and betrayal were condemned by the family and the court as they described the horrific loss of a young life. The sentencing judge emphasized Foster's responsibility as a trusted childminder and her unforgivable actions. The tragic incident underscored the importance of following childminding regulations and prioritizing children's safety above all else. Foster's betrayal and deceptive behavior were met with rightful condemnation and a significant prison sentence.

author: Nick Forbes
title: Sheku Bayoh inquiry should examine why police were not prosecuted, say family
mainText: The family of Sheku Bayoh is calling for the public inquiry into his death to investigate why the police officers involved were not prosecuted. They met with Deputy First Minister Kate Forbes to express their anger and disappointment over the lack of charges against the officers. The family's lawyer criticized Police Scotland for allegedly backtracking on acknowledging institutional racism within the force. He called for meaningful change to follow the inquiry's completion. The inquiry was initiated after Mr. Bayoh, a father of two, died in police custody in 2015. The family is demanding a commitment from the government for legal and regulatory changes. The former chief constable of Police Scotland had previously admitted to institutional racism in the force. The family also wants the inquiry's terms of reference to be expanded to investigate why no officers were prosecuted after Mr. Bayoh's death. They believe it is unacceptable for law enforcement to avoid scrutiny. Deputy First Minister Kate Forbes emphasized the government's commitment to establishing the truth about Mr. Bayoh's death through the public inquiry. The inquiry's independence from the government was stressed, and Police Scotland reiterated their dedication to anti-racism and transparency. They highlighted the importance of respecting the inquiry's role and independence to ensure justice. An assistant chief constable has been appointed to lead the work on building an anti-racist and anti-discriminatory police service.

author: John Uri
title: Flag Day – One Small Flag’s Incredible Journey
mainText: This story tells the tale of one small American flag fortunate enough to embark on an incredible journey. Workers packed me away with many other small flags like me aboard space shuttle Columbia's first mission in 1981. Later, I went on the last space shuttle mission, STS-135, and was aboard the International Space Station. President Barack Obama called me a unique American flag. After being on display, I may have another journey ahead.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Students tour Community Regional Medical Center as part of summer academy
mainText: FRESNO, Calif. (KFSN) -- Local students are learning what it takes to work in the medical field. On Wednesday, students in Clovis Unified's Patient Care Pathway program toured Community Regional Medical Center in Downtown Fresno. The group is taking part in a one-week summer academy spotlighting healthcare careers. Participants saw the inner workings of the ER, burn unit, labs and the helipad on top of the hospital. Students were also taken to the kitchen and got to prepare pizzas. All the participants are going into eighth or ninth grade next school year. That includes Alta Sierra Intermediate student Isabela Elizondo, who's already narrowing down what she wants to study. "I took a career test in sixth grade, and it matched me up with the medical field, like physical therapy, occupational therapy, and I looked into what they actually do, and I thought it was really interesting," she said. Clovis East High is in charge of the program. The instructors say tours like this can help guide young students as they decide which classes to take in the future.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: ThoughtExchange Takes the Student Privacy Pledge and Appoints New Chief Trust Officer
mainText: ThoughtExchange, an AI Engagement and Experience Platform, has taken the Student Privacy Pledge to protect students' data in the education technology space. The pledge includes commitments not to sell student data, target students with advertising, use data only for educational purposes, enhance security measures, ensure transparency, and provide data access to parents, educators, and students. Additionally, ThoughtExchange has appointed Chris Mussell as the Chief Trust Officer to focus on expanding security and privacy efforts, including responsible AI practices. The company aims to uphold the highest data privacy and security standards. ThoughtExchange utilizes responsible AI to analyze data and empower leaders with clarity while minimizing risks like bias, discrimination, and privacy violations. Their AI systems are fortified against manipulation and threats to ensure data security and accountability. The platform aims to accelerate positive change and inclusive problem-solving at scale. ThoughtExchange combines AI capabilities with qualitative survey methods to provide leaders with actionable insights and bridge the gap between sentiment and solutions. Their platform allows for candid responses and instant AI-powered analysis, facilitating efficient feedback processes. Since 2009, ThoughtExchange has been unlocking collective intelligence to solve organizational challenges and promote thoughtful discussions and understanding. The company serves large education, public, and corporate organizations in facilitating engagement and problem-solving. ThoughtExchange aims to provide leaders with accurate and nuanced data to drive effective actions in various sectors.

author: Chris Dunker
title: University of Nebraska will increase tuition, cut positions to close remaining budget shortfall
mainText: University of Nebraska has announced plans to increase tuition fees and reduce positions in order to address the remaining budget deficit. The institution is taking these measures to overcome financial challenges. This decision comes as part of a series of actions being taken by the university. The adjustments in tuition and staff positions are seen as necessary steps to stabilize the university's budget. The focus is on finding a sustainable financial path forward amidst the ongoing budget shortfall. These changes will impact students and employees, but are deemed crucial for the university's financial health.

author: Deutsche Welle
title: Greece: Heat forces Acropolis closure for 2nd straight day
mainText: Greek authorities closed down the Acropolis in Athens on Thursday afternoon for a second day running as Athens experiences unusually high temperatures for this time of year. The Culture Ministry said tourists were unable to visit the Parthenon and other ancient masterpieces atop the UNESCO-listed site from noon until 5 p.m. local time (0900 to 1400 GMT). Temperatures of more than 40 Celsius (104 Fahrenheit) were anticipated on Thursday in much of central and southern Greece, including greater Athens, the Cyclades and Crete. Other Greek archaeological sites in Crete, the Dodecanese, the Cyclades and the Peloponnese were also closed as a precautionary measure. Wildfires alert Officials are on alert for wildfires, which have plagued Greece in recent years. The minister responsible for civil protection, Vassilis Kikilias, said Thursday's heat posed a particular wildfire risk. "The early start of the heat waves, combined with the dry winter, has led to a very difficult fire season," he said. The fire service also warned the wildfire threat would remain high on Friday. Meteorologists have noted it is the earliest heatwave — which for Greece is temperatures exceeding 38 C (100 F) for at least three days — on record. Authorities in Athens are providing air-conditioned areas to the public and have issued fans to secondary schools where end-of-year and university entrance exams are being held. Temperatures are expected to drop on Friday and Saturday. A record number of almost 4 million visitors flocked to the Acropolis last year, as post-COVID tourism thrived. Greece's top tourist attraction also shut down momentarily in 2023 amid a heat wave, but that was in July, when temperatures in the 40s are less unusual.

author: Nina Braca
title: ‘House Of The Dragon’ Apparently Deleted Scenes That Revealed More About Larys’ ‘Foot Fetish’ Than Meets The Eye
mainText: House of The Dragon has gifted fans with all different types of fun tidbits and behind-the-scenes anecdotes, but it also tortured fans in other ways. One of the most memorable (for better or worse) moments was a scene in which Larys Strong uses his foot fetish in an information exchange. Matthew Needham, who plays Larys, recently sat down for a roundtable interview where he told Consequence that Larys’ trauma was a lot more complex than viewers got to see. He explained (via Decider), “I mean, I always thought part of the reason that Larys is the way Larys is is because he’s come from a very traumatic background.” Needham also revealed that he has cut scenes which helped provide a better backstory for Larys. “There was [a deleted scene], it didn’t make the show sadly, but the first time you meet him, he is being harassed and abused by people because of his disability. And you get a sense that that’s how he grew up. Every day for him was something traumatic like that,” Needham said. “I think one of his things is to sort of re-inflict that harm on the world, the world outside of himself.” Hence his need to overpower Alicent. This brings us to the infamous foot fetish scene, which originally had more context. “That’s another one where sort of, you know, there was stuff that didn’t make the cut unfortunately,” Needham said. “When we discussed it, it was about — because he can’t touch her, but it’s a way of making her feel as ashamed for that part of her body as he does for his.” He added, “That does not translate completely, but that’s okay.” He explained that the scenes like that make a bit more sense when the character’s background was explored more. “Obviously if you cut like a line here and a line there and everything sort of ends up just like, you know, ‘It’s Tuesday!’” Needham said. “But it’s all good.” Needham also says he does not read what the fans are saying online. “I can’t do the online thing. Just I can’t. And also I’m just crap at it, so I don’t, but people come up and tell me a lot about a lot of wild things,” he said. House of the Dragon season two premieres June 16th on HBO.

author: Shrishti Negi
title: Natasa Shares Shocking Cryptic Post Amid Hardik Pandya Split Rumours: 'I Can't Wait Until Morals...'
mainText: Cricketer Hardik Pandya’s wife, Natasa Stankovic, has once again shared a shocking cryptic post on her Instagram story amid the ongoing rumours about their alleged separation. Natasa on Thursday took to her social media account to share a quote by acclaimed Hollywood actor Denzel Washington. “With so many things coming back in style, I can’t wait until moral, respect and intelligence become a trend again,” read the quote shared by Natasa on her Instagram story. Natasa on Wednesday shared some “happy moments” with son Agastya Pandya on her official Instagram account. The actress shared a series of photos and videos of her candid moments with her son. In the first picture, Agastya can be seen holding her mom close as they take a nap together. Another photo shows Natasa taking a mirror selfie in the elevator. She also posted a video of her son doing push-ups, while another video showed her doing dance workout in the gym. Sharing the post, Natasa wrote, 'Some happy moments.' On the other hand, Hardik Pandya debuted his new haircut as he gave a glimpse of the same on his Instagram story. Natasa Stankovic and Hardik Pandya’s divorce rumours have been making headlines for a long time now. The couple has not issued any official statement regarding the same as of now. Last week, Natasa posted a selfie on her Instagram, showing her enjoying a cup of black tea. She can be seen donning a white shirt with a blue scarf, as she smiled for the camera. She wrote, 'Hi' with a white heart emoji. In the second slide, one can see Natasa holding a cup of black tea. Former Bigg Boss contestant and dancer Natasa Stankovic has been married to cricketer Hardik Pandya since May 31, 2020. The couple renewed their wedding vows according to Hindu and Christian rituals in February 2023. They sparked divorce rumours after Natasa removed her full name on Instagram.

author: Alice Newbold
title: Nicola Coughlan Rounds Out The ‘Bridgerton’ Tour In Custom Botticelli-Inspired Rodarte
mainText: Nicola Coughlan wrapped the Bridgerton season three press tour last night with a toast–to her co-star Luke Newton, to her best friend from childhood and to her Derry Girls family, who all made the journey to London to see Nicola get her leading lady moment in the titillating period drama that has got the world humming along to rousing orchestral covers of Pitbull. Voicenoting Vogue post-red carpet, Coughlan is both overwhelmed and full of adrenaline, but every inch of her radiates Hollywood star. Championing bridal “mermaid” glamour, Coughlan and her longtime stylist, Aimée Croysdill, worked with Rodarte to create a custom champagne-colored gown that had “Botticelli meets Renaissance” connotations that felt perfect for a celebration of a fabulously OTT show about high society. “Instead of method dressing, we’re going in the opposite direction,” shares Coughlan, who has worn no fewer than 68 looks on this year’s Bridgerton promo trail. “I quite like to get as far away from the characters I play as possible, so this one is very far from Pen [Penelope Featherington].” With soft waves–“my hair has been through a lot”–perfected by hairstylist Halley Brisker and pink and purple-tinted summertime make-up masterminded by Neil Young, Coughlan said Rodarte’s hyper-feminine, gothic-tinged vision seemed like a natural step on from the whimsical looks she wore on the first Bridgerton leg. “I loved that, but when it’s my leading lady moment, like Pen to speak, I wanted to step up to the bar and deliver some really fun looks.” (Easter eggs, included!) As Nicola Coughlan, a true follower of fashion who brings a level of joy to the red carpet that can often be lost among seasoned celebrities, signs off before clinking glasses at Café Laperouse, she hopes that her mission to execute these major looks “her own way,” because “Penelope is a leading lady in her own way,” has translated. It has not only done that, it has been the talk of the ton.

author: Anita Markoff
title: BBC star reveals he has ‘only a finite amount of time left’ as he shares health update on terminal ill...
mainText: BBC RADIO 2 legend Johnnie Walker has revealed his terminal illness, with doctors warning him that he could die at any moment. Having worked for the BBC since 1969, Walker hosts Sounds of the 70s and The Radio 2 Rock Show. After a heart attack in 2019 and subsequent triple heart bypass, he was later diagnosed with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, making breathing difficult. His health decline led him to broadcast from home in Dorset with round-the-clock care from his wife Tiggy. The couple discussed the challenges of living with the possibility of imminent death on their BBC Sounds podcast during Carers Week. Tiggy expressed exhaustion and grief, revealing how antidepressants helped her cope. Walker acknowledged his limited time on Earth, empathizing with his wife's nightly worries. In a role reversal, he now receives care after caring for Tiggy post-her breast cancer diagnosis in 2013. Tiggy reflected on her changed caregiving responsibilities due to her age and fatigue. The couple now sleep in separate rooms due to Walker's oxygen needs. Their journey highlights the emotional and physical toll of terminal illness and caregiving.

title: Ammy Virk Hints at Diljit Dosanjh’s Marriage, Says Keeping Family Private is for ‘Security Concerns'
mainText: Diljit Dosanjh is one of the most loved singers in the entertainment industry. Ammy Virk hinted that Diljit might not be introducing his family to the public due to possible security concerns. Ammy praised Diljit for his achievements and expressed confidence in his future success.

author: Molly Rosbach
title: Public more confident connecting increasing heat, wildfires with climate change, study finds
mainText: Oregon State University researchers conducted a study on U.S. adults' confidence in linking wildfires, heat, and other extreme weather events to climate change. The study found that while people were fairly confident in connecting wildfires and heat to climate change, they were less so with events like hurricanes, flooding, and tornadoes. Political affiliation and personal experience influenced responses, with Republicans less likely to attribute extreme weather events to climate change unless they had personally experienced negative impacts. Overall, 83% of survey respondents believed in a link between extreme weather events and human-caused climate change. The study, published in the journal Climatic Change, surveyed 1,071 adults in September 2021, asking them to rate their confidence in linking different extreme weather events to climate change on a scale of 1 to 5. The study revealed that more than 47% of respondents were very or extremely confident in linking wildfires to climate change, and about 42% felt the same way about extreme heat. Republicans and Democrats were farthest apart in their confidence regarding extreme heat, and closest in their views on hurricanes. Factors such as race, education, and income also impacted responses. The study emphasized the importance of understanding and improving public perceptions of extreme weather related to climate change to maximize the impact of mitigation efforts. Lead author Chad Zanocco and co-authors highlighted the significance of public perceptions in shaping individual behavior and policy support.

author: Seth Borenstein
title: Bye bye, El Nino. Cooler hurricane-helping La Nina to replace the phenomenon that adds heat to Earth
mainText: The strong El Niño weather condition that added a bit of extra heat to already record warm global temperatures is gone. It's cool flip side, La Niña, is likely to breeze in just in time for peak Atlantic hurricane season, federal meteorologists said. The National Oceanic Atmospheric Administration Thursday pronounced dead the El Niño that warms parts of the central Pacific. The El Niño, while not quite a record breaker in strength, formed a year ago has been blamed, along with human-caused climate change and overall ocean warmth, for a wild 12 months of heat waves and extreme weather. The world is now in a neutral condition when it comes to the important natural El Niño Southern Oscillation, which warps weather systems worldwide. Neutral is when weather gets closer to long-term averages or normal, something that hasn't happened as much recently as it used to, said NOAA physical scientist Michelle L'Heureux, who is the lead forecaster of the agency's ENSO team. But it likely won't last, she added. She said there's a 65% chance that a La Niña, a cooling of the same parts of the Pacific that often has opposite effects, will form in the July, August and September time period. One of the biggest effects of La Niña is that it tends to make Atlantic hurricane season more active, and that storm season starts its peak in August. "The likelihood of a La Niña coupled with record warm sea surface temperatures is the reason the National Hurricane Center is forecasting an extraordinary hurricane season," said Kathie Dello, North Carolina's state climatologist. "States from Texas to Maine are making preparations for an active year." Both El Niño and La Niña create "potential hot spots" for extreme weather but in different places and of different types, L'Heureux said. "La Niña tends to, in the winter, bring drier conditions across the southern tier of the United States and if you put global warming on top of that, that could also mean those drier conditions could intensify into droughts," L'Heureux said. That's because storm systems, mostly in the winter, move slightly northward with a shift in the jet stream during La Niña years, bringing more rain and snow north, L'Heureux said. Even though a La Niña tends to be cooler, there will likely be a residual effect of the exiting El Niño on global temperatures, L'Heureux said. This year has seen each month breaking global records so far. No more than 8% of last year's record heat could be attributed to El Niño and other natural variability, a panel of 57 scientists concluded earlier this month. The rest was from human-caused climate change from the burning of coal, oil and natural gas. A 1999 economic study found that drought from La Niña cost the United States agriculture between $2.2 billion to $6.5 billion, which is far more than the $1.5 billion cost of El Niño. A neutral ENSO is best for agriculture. Given La Niña's connection to Atlantic hurricanes and drought in the United States it makes sense that they are generally costlier, but every El Niño and La Niña is different, so people and governments should prepare for them, said meteorologist and economist Michael Ferrari, chief scientific officer of AlphaGeo, a firm that works on financial investments and climate. A resident of a riverside community carries food and containers of drinking water after being distributed due to the ongoing drought in Careiro da Varzea, Amazonas state, Brazil, Oct. 24, 2023. The National Oceanic Atmospheric Administration Thursday, June 13, 2024, pronounced dead the El Nino that warms parts of the central Pacific. Credit: AP Photo /Edmar Barros, File Homes are flooded in the aftermath of Hurricane Ida, Aug. 30, 2021, in Jean Lafitte, La. The National Oceanic Atmospheric Administration Thursday, June 13, 2024, pronounced dead the El Nino that warms parts of the central Pacific. Forecasters expect La Nina to breeze in just in time for peak Atlantic hurricane season. Credit: AP Photo/David J. Phillip, File The El Niño that just ended "wasn't a record-breaker in anybody's book, but it was probably about top five," L'Heureux said. And it added to overall global temperature and brought more moisture to the southern United States this year, along with drier conditions in parts of South America and Central America, she said. The Horn of Africa got wetter. Coral reef experts say the combination of record ocean temperatures and the boost of heating from El Niño have led to a major global bleaching event threatening and at times killing vulnerable coral. Before this year's El Niño, the world had back-to-back-to-back La Ninas, which is unusual, L'Heureux said. Some studies have shown that the globe should expect more El Ninos and La Ninas—and fewer neutrals—as the world warms, but it's still an unsettled issue, she said.

author: Aaron Sidder
title: Expecting the unexpected could help us prepare for climate extremes
mainText: The U.S. Pacific Northwest experienced an unprecedented heat wave in summer 2021, with many locations in the region breaking all-time maximum temperature records by more than 9 °F (5 °C). Although weather models had forecasted the warmer-than-average conditions that summer, the extreme temperatures caught the climate science community by surprise. In the past year, so have catastrophic, deadly floods in such places as Libya and China and record-breaking wildfires in Canada. Our collective unpreparedness for such extreme climate events should be a cause for concern, argue Sherwood et al. In a paper published in Earth's Future, the authors contend that a reliance on models that don't account for enough relevant factors and a tendency toward linear thinking have narrowed perceptions of climate change risks. Central to their argument is the idea that society is too focused on the expected gradual consequences of climate change and not enough on high-impact, low-likelihood occurrences and tipping points—regime shifts in which systems can change rapidly and irreversibly. The authors suggest that as a result, we are overlooking critical potentialities in our efforts to adapt to and weigh mitigation options for a warmer future. The authors outline two questions for climate scientists to consider. First, what are the high-impact, low-likelihood hazards and irreversible changes that society should worry about, and how can their risks be measured and communicated? Second, how can scientists identify achievable and safe pathways to a future climate that also meets human needs? To answer these questions, climate scientists must consider a broader array of risks than they conventionally have, examining how these risks affect not just the climate but also society and the larger biosphere. This effort will likely involve working across disciplines and using new modeling approaches that better represent tipping points, low-likelihood events, and other aspects of physical and human systems compared with current approaches. The authors also emphasize that clear communication will be crucial in conveying climate risks to the public and coordinating across scientific disciplines. This story is republished courtesy of Eos, hosted by the American Geophysical Union. Read the original story here.

author: Zhang Nannan
title: Exploring effects of thawing permafrost on topography and periglacial environment along China-Russia crude oil pipeline
mainText: The buried China-Russia Crude Oil Pipeline (CRCOP), with its oil temperature above 0°C, interacts with the permafrost environment in a complex way, causing permafrost degradation, frost geohazards, and various environmental problems along its route. Prof. Li Guoyu's team from the Northwest Institute of Eco-Environment and Resources (NIEER) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences established a comprehensive on-site monitoring system to detect the geomorphological reshaping and water erosion caused by thawing permafrost along the CRCOP. The researchers observed a gradual increase in oil temperature, which caused the permafrost around the CRCOP to warm and thaw rapidly. At a distance of 2 m from the pipeline center, the permafrost table decreased at a rate of 0.68 m/a, reaching a depth of -11.4 m by 2022. The thawing of the permafrost caused settlement of the pipeline and subsidence of the ground surface, resulting in thermal erosion, ponding of water in summer, and icing in winter. The area near the pipeline experienced significant surface subsidence, creating lowlands that resulted in water ponding in summer. The thermal erosion of ponding accelerated the topographical changes. The subsidence rate in ponding areas was 8.18 cm/a, which was significantly higher than the rate of 4.81 cm/a in the non-ponding areas. Additionally, they proposed a series of technologies to mitigate permafrost thawing and control pipeline settlement, including thermosyphons, air ventilation ducts, and air convection pipeline embankments, to ensure safe operation of the CRCOP. Finally, they discussed the effects of climate warming, fire, and human activities on permafrost degradation, illustrating the evolution process of talik and surface characteristics under the influence of multiple factors. The study provides significant data for the safe operation and maintenance of the CRCOP. The study, titled "Permafrost thawing caused by the China-Russia Crude oil pipeline based on multi-type data and its impacts on geomorphological reshaping and water erosion," was published in CATENA.

author: The White House
title: SGS Pioneers Innovative Technologies in Critical Battery Metals in North America
mainText: RUTHERFORD, N.J., June 13, 2024 /PRNewswire/ - As a result of SGS' high visibility as the world's leading testing, inspection, and certification company, two of its experts were invited to speak at a meeting convened by The White House on June 10, 2024, and cohosted by the American Battery Materials Initiative, which highlighted the company's expert position in helping with the creation of a sustainable US Battery Supply Chain. David Anonychuk, SGS Global Vice President, Metallurgy and Consulting, and Niels Verbaan, Director, Hydrometallurgy, were the sole Testing, Inspection, and Certification experts invited to speak to the assembled group of industry insiders from the mining, chemical, and automotive sectors as well as US government officials. "Our main message during this meeting was centered around our market leadership positioning in the process development and de-risking of critical minerals and recycling projects by virtue of metallurgical testing and pilot plant testing facilities," said Anonychuk. "As an industry, we need to come together and candidly discuss the challenges we face and balance innovation and the desire to accelerate the supply chain. We need to consider exploring creative solutions where government can partner with private industry." SGS has the unique experience and knowledge to help advance these projects, assisting the US government with achieving its objectives and finding long-term solutions to increase the competitiveness of the North American battery materials industry. Verbaan spoke about the importance of metallurgical testing, piloting, and demonstration-style operations in developing critical mineral projects to avoid lengthy and expensive plant ramp-ups and emphasized that critical mineral projects require more de-risking than conventional mining projects. "The purpose of de-risking is to ensure a better chance of success and commercialization for a resilient and sustainable North American supply chain," said Verbaan. SGS is pleased to be in conversations with Abby Wulf, Executive Chair of the American Battery Materials Initiative, Department of Energy, and Alex Jacquez, Special Assistant to the President, National Economic Council at The White House, who are facilitating the US government's critical mineral and battery strategy.

title: Are plant-based burgers possibly harmful?
mainText: New research on the health effects of ultra-processed plant-based foods has sparked global attention, with headlines suggesting these foods could increase the risk of heart disease, stroke, and premature death. Despite alarming media coverage, the study found that consuming plant-based, ultra-processed foods was associated with a higher risk of cardiovascular disease and death, while non-ultra-processed plant-based foods were linked to lower risks. The study, based on data from the UK Biobank, followed nearly 127,000 participants for nine years. Plant-based, ultra-processed foods like bread and pastries showed increased risks, but fake meats accounted for only a small portion of participants' diets. Media attention on fake meats may have skewed perceptions, even though other plant-based processed foods made up a larger part of the diet in the study. The study did not focus solely on fake meats, and the impact of consuming large quantities of these products remains uncertain. Ultra-processed foods, including fake meats, may contain high levels of saturated fats, salt, and sugar, making moderation important. Consumers are advised to check labels for fat and salt content, and opt for whole plant-based protein sources like legumes for healthier choices. The article underscores the need for further research on the health effects of fake meats and emphasizes the importance of consuming all ultra-processed foods in moderation.

title: EXCLUSIVENew Bianca Devins documentary lifts lid on Instagram star's brutal murder by incel who posted pictures of her body online - as her family lays bare the trauma of seeing 'sick people' turning her death into a 'spectacle'
mainText: A new documentary has lifted a lid on Instagram star Bianca Devins' brutal murder by an incel who then posted gruesome pictures of her mutilated body online - as her family laid bare the trauma of seeing 'sick people' turn her death into a social media 'spectacle.' In July 2019, Instagram sensation Bianca, from Utica, New York, then 17 - who had gained a legion of followers from posting about emo fashion and video games - was killed by an older man who she had met online, named Brandon Andrew Clark, then 23. After slitting her throat, Brandon uploaded a slew of gory photos that showed her bloody body to Instagram and to the chat app Discord, where they quickly went viral. In the aftermath, members of the incel community - a group of men who are 'involuntary celibate,' meaning they're unable to find a partner - rallied around Brandon, posting horrific comments about Bianca online, calling her 'worthless' and 'disgusting' and branding Brandon as a 'legend' who 'did the world a favor.' Now, her loved ones have spoken out about the 'disgust' and 'anger' they felt after seeing the images of her body on the internet and the horrifying messages that followed in an upcoming episode of ID's new show Deadly Influence: The Social Media Murders. In an exclusive sneak peak at the episode, which will air on Monday, June 17 at 9pm ET/8pm CT, her mother, Kimberly Devins, detailed the 'devastating' pain she felt over not being able to 'protect' her daughter from not only her killer, but from the 'internet' after her death. 'People posted the picture [of her dead body] under my Facebook profile picture, they would send it to [Bianca's sister] Olivia and I constantly,' she recalled. 'They would tag us in it. It felt like as soon as we got one picture removed another one was posted. 'As a mother, it was very devastating because I feel like I couldn't protect her from that. 'I couldn't protect her from her murder and then I couldn't protect her from being exploited on the internet.' One of Bianca's friends, named Young Shim, recalled 'people reposting the images over and over.' 'They just shared it because it would garner clicks. I felt disgust, anger, hatred,' he said. 'I still carry a lot of resentment and negativity. Thousands of people online thought it was something to laugh or joke about.' Another one of the late Instagram star's pals, named Gianna Rosado, added, 'I could still see it in my head, she was just exposed. All these sick people can just look at it when I ever they want.' Bianca, who was preparing to study psychology at Mohawk Valley Community College, was murdered by Brandon after the pair returned to Utica from a concert in New York City the night of July 14, 2019. After she was killed, he shared numerous photos of her body, which remained up for almost a day before being removed. Immediately after the images began to circulate online, multiple people called 911 and law enforcement quickly started searching for Bianca. But Brandon then called the police himself to report what he had done, telling them, 'My name is Brandon, the victim is Bianca Devins, I'm not going to stay on the phone for long because I still need to do the suicide part of the murder-suicide.' He then cut his own throat - but police arrived just as he was stabbing himself in the neck. He was taken into custody and hospitalized, ultimately recovering. 'At first people who saw the post were incredibly disturbed. But when Brandon survived that suicide attempt, the incel community reared forward and presented themselves in a way that was celebrating Brandon,' Kelly Ruhl, true crime podcaster, explained in DailyMail.com's exclusive clip from the upcoming ID episode. As she spoke, screenshots of comments that said things like, 'Brandon Clark is a hero,' 'He did the world a favor,' and, 'She was disgusting and treated people like they were worthless, she was worthless,' popped across the screen. 'In the aftermath of Bianca's murder her social media accounts became a spectacle, and to this day people are still on her accounts leaving comments,' another woman explained in the show. But as the ordeal took over social media, she said Bianca's supporters quickly stepped in and tried to 'redirect what people saw when they looked up her name.' And even now, five years on from her passing, there are 'still people spamming the comments' of her posts with both 'negative' and supportive messages. 'If we were to go on there right now, the most recent comment would be two hours ago, and that to me is just insane,' her friend, Gianna, said. The status of Bianca and Brandon's relationship has been debated, with her loved ones insisting that they were only 'friends,' while others called him her 'boyfriend.' In addition, during his trial it was revealed that he had filmed a sex tape with her right before killing her. It was also said that he murdered her because he got jealous after she kissed another man at the concert they had attended together. He ultimately pleaded guilty to second-degree murder, and was sentenced to 25 years to life in prison. He apologized to the judge during his sentencing, stating that Bianca 'didn't deserve what happened to her.' 'I think I need to realize what I did I can't undo, as much as I want to,' he told the court. 'I have to face it. I apologize to all the people that knew and loved her. 'I apologize to everybody affected by this - everybody who had to see that horrific picture of her. 'I know sorry is not enough and it won’t take back what I did. I wish I had more to give.

title: Study demonstrates efficacy of treat-to-target in early axial spondyloarthritis
mainText: A study presented at the 2024 EULAR congress demonstrated the efficacy of a treat-to-target approach in early axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). The study followed 55 newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve axSpA patients and treated them with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) followed by golimumab if needed. The goal was to achieve sustained clinical remission or low disease activity. Results showed that 61.8% of patients achieved sustained clinical remission, with male sex, abstinence from smoking, and lower baseline BASDAI score being predictors of remission. However, 84.8% of those who achieved remission experienced relapse within 1 year of stopping treatment. The study highlighted the challenge of maintaining drug-free remission in axSpA despite the success of the treat-to-target approach. The findings suggest that while high rates of inactive disease can be induced with this strategy, maintaining drug-free remission remains difficult in axSpA.

title: Minister Parsons Announces Funding for Health Research Equipment - News Releases
mainText: The Provincial Government is supporting Memorial University in its purchase of a state-of-the-art piece of equipment not widely available in Canada which will give researchers the ability to support innovative health research in the province. The equipment is essential to conduct cutting-edge studies and further explore the potential causes of chronic diseases such as osteoarthritis, nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, Alzheimer’s and Multiple Sclerosis. The Honourable Andrew Parsons, KC, Minister of Industry, Energy and Technology, today announced an investment of $453,676 from the province’s Research and Innovation Fund towards the purchase of an Orbitrap Mass Spectrometry system. The Provincial Government’s investment helps to leverage a further $695,578 towards the purchase of this equipment. The equipment will enhance Memorial University’s research capabilities for future generations through the establishment of a Multidisciplinary Metabolomics Laboratory at the Core Sciences Facility. Through the project, researchers plan to train upwards of 45 professionals over the next five years, including laboratory technicians, postdoctoral, graduate, and undergraduate students, thereby increasing the number of skilled personnel in the field. The creation of the metabolomics laboratory is being spearheaded by Dr. Shyamchand Mayengbam, Dr. Kapil Tahlan, and Dr. Guangju Zhai, who specialize in biochemistry, biology and biomedical sciences. They have also worked extensively and contributed towards metabolomics-based studies in the area of nutritional biochemistry, microbial metabolism, and clinical settings. Their objective is to study small molecules of biological origin which are of critical importance to human health, microbiology, agriculture, and aquaculture, with hopes of laying the foundation for the development of new dietary interventions and the discovery of novel microbial metabolites and antibiotics.

title: 12 Military Watch Features That Are Now Standard Issue for Civilians
mainText: In the article titled '12 Military Watch Features That Are Now Standard Issue for Civilians,' the author discusses how many common features found in contemporary wristwatches have their origins in military use. The wristwatch itself became popular due to the inconvenience of relying on pocket watches during the First World War. Features like center seconds for easier timing tasks, 24-hour tracks for military accuracy, telemeter scales for distance calculations, 12-hour bezels for dual time zone tracking, and luminous dials for low-light visibility all originated from military needs. Other features such as hacking, dive bezels, fixed strap bars for durability, oversized hands for visibility, sandwich dials for luminosity, and onion crowns for easy access with gloves have also become standard in many civilian wristwatches. The article provides historical context for each feature and highlights the impact of military innovations on modern watch technology.

title: Kirsty McLuckie: the five best house types to make your money when you buy, not when you sell
mainText: A recent report showed that homeowners who sold a detached property in 2023 made an average profit of almost £140,000 compared to the original purchase price. Different house types resulted in varying profits, with bungalows yielding £102,000, semi-detached properties £81,000, terraced houses £65,000, and flats around £30,000. While most people buy homes for personal use, understanding popular house types and potential for value appreciation is crucial. Jonathan Rolande from the National Association of Property recommends considering the appeal of each property type to future-proof returns. Bungalows, often overlooked by younger buyers, are gaining popularity due to their characteristics like generous outdoor space. Well-maintained but outdated bungalows offer renovation potential. Garden flats, especially Victorian or Edwardian ones, offer charm and space at affordable prices, making them attractive to buyers, especially families. Homes with side gardens, despite privacy concerns, have potential for extensions or new constructions if permitted. The strategy of buying the "worst home in the best area" remains effective, as location plays a significant role in property value. Proximity to transport links is gaining importance as more people return to working from physical offices. Properties near stations and bus routes are in demand, especially among young buyers aiming to escape renting. These factors should be considered when purchasing a property to maximize future returns.

title: 'Wonder what flag will Mrs. Alito fly today': The View jokes after Supreme Court ruling
mainText: The Supreme Court ruled on Thursday to maintain the Food and Drug Administration's approval of the abortion drug Mifepristone and the co-hosts of "The View" were shocked to hear that it was a unanimous decision. All justices agreed that the doctors complaining about the drug didn't have standing to bring the case because they didn't use the drug in their practices and were instead only basing the case on their own personal objections. Former federal prosecutor Sunny Hostin predicted that it will likely come back to "states' rights" to decide for women's reproductive health. For now, however, she said, "It does restore a little bit of my faith in the court because the legal standard is, do you have standing to bring a case? Like can anybody bring a case in front of the Supreme Court? No. You have to have to prove that you have injuries resulting from it. So you've got a group of doctors and group of citizens, and all of these people bring this challenge to the FDA and say, we don't want this pill, and what [Justice Brett] Kavanaugh, he was the one that wrote it, said, they do not." It prompted Republican Ana Navarro to quip, "I wonder what flag Mrs. Alito is going to fly today." The reference is to the reports that Justice Samuel Alito's wife was responsible for flying an upside-down American flag and an 'Appeal to Heaven' flag, both of which were symbolic flags flown during the Jan. 6 attacks on Congress. A recording of Martha Ann Alito by a progressive activist released this week showed that she was also angry about the pride flags she said she had to look at while staying at their beach house. The new spot brings Lee-Marquez’s brand of border Mexican food into a larger space. The new restaurant will serve tequila and mezcal, along with a robust selection of Mexican beers and some wine, and allow the chef and owner to expand her community-focused approach to food.

author: David Maddox
title: Sunak’s Tories hit Truss level of all-time low support as Brexit voters turn to Farage’s Reform
mainText: The Tories have hit their joint lowest standing in the weekly tracker poll as Nigel Farage’s Reform takes its biggest share yet and the aftermath of Rishi Sunak’s D-Day gaffe takes effect. The prime minister apologised for skipping part of the commemorations to do an election interview for ITV last week but the first weekly tracker poll taken by Techne UK after the fiasco reveals the depth of public anger. According to Techne’s survey of 1,636 voters this week: Techne UK’s survey also saw Labour drop one point to 43 per cent but maintain its lead of 24 points over the Conservatives. The Lib Dem share was up one point to 11 per cent and the Greens stayed the same on 6 per cent. If this poll result was matched in a general election, the prediction website Electoral Calculus, which excludes local factors, suggests that the Conservatives would be reduced to 38 seats, Reform would make a breakthrough into parliament with three seats and Labour would have a “supermajority” of 374 with more than 500 seats. But the Techne poll was not the worst one for the Tories with YouGov suggesting that Reform has now passed them with 19 percent to the Conservatives’ 18 percent with Labour on 37 percent. It led Nigel Farage to claim that a Tory vote was “wasted” and Reform “are the opposition now”. The results were also reflected in a Redfield and Wilton poll that came out this evening putting the Tories on a “worse than Truss” 18 per cent and Reform just one point behind on 17 per cent. Labour has a 24-point lead on 42 per cent. The terrible poll results came after the Tory leadership appeared to run up the white flag this week and warn voters against giving Sir Keir Starmer a “supermajority”. But the Techne results make dire reading for the Conservatives. Labour now leads in every age, social, economic and education category. But the most painful statistics are the loss of core voters for the Tories. Mr Sunak was challenged in this week’s debate on Sky News by a former Tory chairperson who said she did not know how to vote at the election because of the D-Day fiasco and Partygate - a confrontation that appears to be symbolic of a wider problem. Of those who voted Conservative in 2019 only 37 per cent would stick with the party now, 22 per cent have defected to Reform and 11 per cent to Labour. Another 23 per cent will not vote or are uncertain. The desertion of pro-Brexit voters who supported Leave in 2016 is also a blow for Mr Sunak. Reform now has 26 per cent of them ahead of the Tories on 23 per cent while 15 per cent now back Sir Keir Starmer and Labour. The Techne poll was taken in the 48 hours after Mr Sunak unveiled the Conservative manifesto with an added pledge to end national insurance contributions for the self employed. But the glitzy launch at Silverstone Formula 1 race course - and its contents = appear to have failed to impress voters. Techne UK’s chief executive Michela Morizzo said: “With the general election in full swing our regular tracker poll released today of Westminster voting intentions makes for further grim reading for Rishi Sunak and his Conservative Party. “For Sunak’s party this is the joint lowest vote share we have given and as such maintains a 24-point lead for Labour. This dominant Labour lead is further exacerbated by Nigel Farage’s campaign continuing to cut through. Reform UK are up another point in national vote share to 16 per cent, just three points behind the Conservatives. “This means that Reform and Conservatives play on the same ground and this increases very much the difficulties for Conservatives, probably not prepared to battle on different fronts. “They should take a strong position deciding to fight against only one competitor; spreading their effort against both Labour and Reform in such a short period of time could only lead to nullify the efforts. If this could lead to a ‘cross-over’ between the Conservatives and Reform UK, it’s difficult to say: always remember that, for a voter, the real decision comes between home and the polling station!”

author: Murtuza Merchant
title: Biden Campaign Reportedly Working On Crypto Donations: 'They Think We're Going To Donate?,' Barks Industr
mainText: The Biden campaign is reportedly exploring the possibility of accepting crypto donations through Coinbase Commerce, in an effort to engage with the crypto community ahead of the election. This decision comes after Donald Trump's campaign started accepting crypto contributions through the same platform. Biden's team aims to show support for the industry and appeal to crypto-focused voters amidst a challenging political landscape. The move is seen as a response to backlash faced after a decision to block a regulation that crypto advocates believe restricts industry growth in the U.S. There is significant funding mobilized by pro-crypto donors, with crypto-backed super PACs amassing a $100 million war chest that could influence the election outcome. However, not all in the crypto community are supportive of Biden's approach, citing past actions against the industry by the administration. Critics question the sincerity of the campaign's interest in crypto donations given this history. The impact of these discussions on the election remains to be seen as the campaign progresses. The broader implications of integrating cryptocurrencies into political fundraising will be discussed at the upcoming Benzinga event on the future of digital assets.

author: Azaria Howell
title: Ministry of Health staff fire back against pay freeze; changes to Suicide Prevention Office revealed
mainText: Ministry of Health workers have pushed back against proposals to freeze remuneration increases to workers above a mid-range, in documents seen by the Herald. The documents, sent to staff amid confirmation of the total job cuts, reveal which roles are being slashed, the feedback the agency received, and how workers at each department found out their fate. In its change proposals, which had been under consultation before final decisions were announced, the Ministry of Health planned to not apply remuneration increases for those above the mid-point, this year. Workers opposed the plans, in feedback revealed in the agency’s blueprints, prompting a change of heart by the ministry. In feedback revealed in the documents, staff suggested the proposal “created feelings of being undervalued and marginalised, with others finding it demoralising and manipulative, and tone deaf given the current economic environment”. It was suggested those on higher incomes could withstand going without a remuneration increase, compared to those on lower-incomes. Suggestions were also made around reducing working hours on the same pay, and adding more paid leave. Vacancy freezes were also floated as a potential option. Documents seen by the Herald reveal Ministry of Health worker feedback prompted an apparent u-turn from the agency. After feedback, the ministry’s executive team decided to include a one-off lump sum payment, based on performance rating and position, for staff in pay bands from 12, a starting range, to 16.

author: Jessica Chasmar,Andrew Miller,Cameron Cawthorne
title: Secretary Blinken silent on past efforts to discredit Hunter Biden laptop after feds enter it into evidence
mainText: Secretary of State Antony Blinken is silent on whether he regrets his alleged efforts in helping discredit Hunter Biden's abandoned laptop that would later be used as evidence in Biden's federal trial resulting in a conviction. The ties between Blinken and Biden were brought into the forefront last year after former CIA Deputy Director Michael Morell testified to the House Judiciary and Intelligence Committees, a Fox News Digital review found. Morell testified that Blinken, as President Biden’s then-campaign senior adviser, "played a role in the inception" of the public statement signed by intelligence officials claiming Hunter Biden’s abandoned laptop was part of a Russian disinformation campaign just weeks before the 2020 presidential election. Three days after the letter from the former intelligence officials was made public, then-presidential candidate Joe Biden used the letter as a talking point in the final 2020 presidential debate to rebut criticisms made by then-President Trump. In the following years, numerous media outlets confirmed the New York Post's reporting that the laptop was authentic, and the laptop was used by the federal government as evidence in the recent gun crime trial against Biden, where he was convicted on all charges. Additionally, emails from the infamous abandoned laptop that Blinken sought to discredit showed that Biden has friendly personal ties to Blinken and his wife, Evan Ryan, dating back over a decade, having scheduled meetings with him while he was on the board of Burisma and Blinken was the deputy secretary of state. In an email on May 22, 2015, Hunter tried to schedule a meeting with Blinken, so he could get the deputy secretary of state’s "advice" on some things. However, the meeting appeared to be rescheduled to July 2015 due to the death of Hunter's brother, Beau, at the end of May 2015. Biden's assistant, Joan Mayer, would email Biden, months later, his weekly schedule on July 21, which showed a scheduled meeting with Blinken the following day. "12:00-1:30pm- Lunch with Tony Blinken (State Department)," Hunter's schedule read. Fox News Digital could not confirm what the meeting was about. Blinken previously denied having a role in the creation of the letter from former intel officials, and has stressed that he does not "do politics" despite his decades of political donations and campaign positions. Between Blinken and his wife, they have donated approximately $70,000 to Democrats over the last few decades.

author: Science X
title: Unraveling the auxin-sucrose nexus in Lily bulbil formation
mainText: A study reveals how auxin and sucrose metabolism regulate bulbil initiation in Lilium lancifolium. By manipulating auxin levels and examining key sucrose metabolism genes, researchers found that low auxin concentrations enhance bulbil formation. This discovery offers promising implications for horticulture, providing new strategies to improve bulb propagation through hormonal and metabolic pathways. Bulbils in lilies serve as crucial vegetative reproductive organs, ensuring plant survival and propagation...

author: Science X
title: Ripe for knowledge: Unraveling the genetic ties of banana softening
mainText: A recent study has identified the bHLH gene MabHLH28 as a key regulator of banana fruit ripening, influencing the softening process by upregulating softening-related genes, either independently or in synergy with MaWRKY49/111. This discovery could transform post-harvest fruit management, potentially reducing spoilage and prolonging fruit freshness. Fruit ripening plays a crucial role in determining quality, storability, and market value, with over-softening leading to challenges in storage and transportation, resulting in economic losses. The study from researchers at South China Agricultural University published in Horticulture Research on February 23, 2024, revealed that MabHLH28 significantly upregulates during banana ripening, directly affecting the expression of genes associated with softening. By binding to promoters of softening-related genes and enhancing their expression, MabHLH28 accelerates ripening when overexpressed and delays it when silenced. Additionally, MabHLH28 interacts with MaWRKY49 and MaWRKY111 to boost the transcription of softening-related genes. This finding highlights the crucial role of MabHLH28 in banana fruit ripening and its potential for improving fruit quality and extending shelf life. By manipulating MabHLH28 expression, it may be possible to control the ripening process, offering a sustainable solution to reduce post-harvest losses and enhance fruit quality during transport and storage.

author: Robert Lea
title: NASA's Chandra X-ray telescope captures closest super star cluster to Earth (image)
mainText: It's a bird... it's a plane... it's a super star cluster! NASA's Chandra X-ray telescope has imaged a star cluster that is "super" in every way. Westerlund 1 is super-large, super-massive, super-young, super-close — and it is creating stars at a super-fast rate. Westerlund 1 is located around 13,000 light-years away from Earth — meaning it's very close, relatively speaking — and the 3 million to 5 million-year-old star cluster is around 7 light-years wide. If that age doesn't seem particularly young to you, remember that our middle-aged solar system is about 4.6 billion years old. Westerlund 1 also has a mass equivalent to as many as 100,000 suns, and it is one of the few remaining super star clusters in the Milky Way. Down the line, studying Westerlund 1 could help astronomers better understand the internal workings of these cosmic star factories. The image is part of the first data released from the Extended Westerlund 1 and 2 Open Clusters Survey (EWOCS), led by astronomers from the Italian National Institute of Astrophysics in Palermo. As part of the EWOCS program, Chandra watched Westerlund 1 for a total of around 12 days. The X-rays from Westerlund 1, seen by Chandra and visible in the image as pinks and whites, are from young stars. Meanwhile, blobs of pink, green and blue represent diffuse heated gas throughout the supercluster. The new Chandra data has tripled the number of known X-ray sources in Westerlund 1. Prior to the EWOCS project, Chandra had detected 1,721 X-ray sources in the superstar cluster; the EWOCS data, on the other hand, has revealed almost 6,000 X-ray sources. These include faint stars with masses lower than that of the sun. To picture just how dense this region is with stars, consider that there are 4.24 light years between the sun and its closest stellar neighbor, Proxima Centauri. Not only could this aspect of this region help deliver a more precise mass estimate of Westerlund 1, but it could also help assess how this particular collection of stars came to be and how it has changed over time. The EWOCS results are discussed in a paper published in February in the journal Astronomy and Astrophysics.

author: John Uri
title: Flag Day 2024 – One Small Flag’s Incredible Journey
mainText: This article tells the story of one small American flag fortunate enough to be singled out from a group of one thousand flags just like it and embark on an incredible journey. The other 999 flags likely ended up as gifts, but this one flag had a loftier fate. Other American flags have flown on spacecraft not just to other planets but also out of the solar system. Space shuttle Columbia first lifted off from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center (KSC) in Florida on April 12, 1981. The Official Flight Kit carried on Columbia included 1,000 American flags for distribution after the mission. Many flags were given away, but some remained in storage at NASA’s Johnson Space Center (JSC) in Houston. In 2011, one of the flags from the first shuttle mission was reflown on the final flight. Space shuttle Atlantis delivered supplies to the International Space Station and crew presented the flag to the station. The Legacy Flag was placed on the Harmony module’s forward hatch during a televised ceremony and later safeguarded in a stowage bag. The flag embarked on its final journey in 2020 aboard SpaceX's Crew Dragon capsule, christened Endeavour. After a nine-year journey in space, the flag returned to Earth on Aug. 2, 2020. It went on display at SpaceX’s facility and toured the country before being stored at JSC. The Legacy Flag will continue its journey on possibly more distant missions. During its time on the space station, the flag saw 100 visitors from various nationalities and traveled more than 1.3 billion miles.

author: Marianne Stein
title: Organic farmers' beliefs about soil microbiome affect their practices, study shows
mainText: Organic farming can support soil microorganisms that promote plant defenses and reduce insect pests. A new study from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and Cornell University looks at how organic farmers' beliefs about the microbiome influence their soil management practices. The researchers surveyed 85 organic vegetable farmers in New York, gauging their microbiome beliefs, farming practices, and motivations. "Overall, 96% of the farmers believed that the microbiome on their farm is influencing plant defenses and pest suppression. We found that farmers who believed on-farm practices such as no-till or cover crops are important for influencing the microbiome also tended to adopt those practices." The researchers also looked at demographic characteristics such as farm size and farmer's age and how that influenced the adoption of practices. "To promote these ecosystem benefits, researchers need to think about how to bring no-tillage and diversified crop production to a larger scale so they can be more manageable for larger farms." If Extension services and land management agencies have a goal of encouraging farmers to maximize investments in the soil microbiome, it's important to know how to target messages. Understanding why different farmers might select different practices based on what they believe about the microbiome is a first step to understanding how to incentivize certain kinds of organic practices. Eventually, there could be market incentives such as a microbiome-friendly ecolabel on food.

author: Tim Reynolds
title: Analysis: West, Kobe a match from Day 1
mainText: In 2010 during the NBA Finals, Kobe Bryant expressed that he did not consider himself the greatest Los Angeles Laker, believing that title belonged to Jerry West. West, who passed away at the age of 86, was instrumental in the Lakers' success by drafting Bryant in 1996 and subsequently signing Shaquille O'Neal in free agency. This laid the foundation for the Shaq and Kobe Era, leading to five championships for the Lakers. West recognized Bryant's talent early on, arranging workouts where Bryant showcased his skills and 'Mamba Mentality.' The Lakers trusted West's judgment, and it paid off as Bryant matured into a basketball legend. The Lakers won championships in 2000, 2001, and 2002, with Bryant securing two more titles in 2009 and 2010. Bryant credited West for his pivotal role in his career and the team's success, acknowledging West as the greatest Laker ever. West's vision and bold decisions in drafting Bryant shaped both their legacies and the Lakers' history. The story emphasizes West's crucial role in identifying and nurturing talent, highlighting the enduring impact of his choices on basketball history.

author: Karine Hains
title: Maples Leafs Shouldn’t Pursue Patrik Laine Trade
mainText: Yesterday (June 12) on Insider Trading, TSN’s Pierre LeBrun revealed Patrik Laine wants a fresh beginning and that the Columbus Blue Jackets will do their best to accommodate him. Would it make sense for the Toronto Maple Leafs to chase the big Finnish winger? Laine’s NHL Career So Far When the Maple Leafs picked Auston Matthews first overall at the 2016 Draft, the Jets picked Laine. Both players started their NHL career the very next season. Laine's production dropped in some seasons due to various reasons including a reported divide between himself and Jets' veterans. After a season in Columbus, he signed a new four-year deal. Unfortunately, injuries and mental health issues have impacted Laine's recent seasons. After seeking help for mental health issues, it's understandable that Laine would want a fresh start. While hockey is a business, players are human beings with needs and feelings. Laine's recent struggles highlight the importance of addressing mental health in professional sports.

author: Avishek Roy
title: Three women wrestlers skip Hungary camp, to train on their own
mainText: Three of the five women wrestlers who have qualified for the Paris Olympics have skipped the ongoing international camp in Hungary to train on their own. Antim Panghal, Anshu Malik, and Reetika Hooda returned to India after participating in the International Ranking Series in Budapest. Vinesh Phogat and Nisha Dahiya are the only two wrestlers at the Olympic Training Centre in Hungary. The camp was planned by the Wrestling Federation of India on the recommendation of national coaches. WFI paid for the stay of the team but now has only one wrestler to train. The three wrestlers cited various reasons for skipping the camp. Anshu Malik is planning a trip to Japan, while Aman Sehrawat is looking to train in Dagestan, Russia. The IOA and WFI released a joint statement offering extensive support to the wrestlers for Olympic preparation with coaches, physiotherapists, nutritionists, and mental-conditioning coaches.

author: David Schoen
title: Famed poker pro ends WSOP drought, secures 11th career victory
mainText: Phil Ivey’s bracelet drought at the World Series of Poker is over. The renowned pro won the star-studded $10,000 buy-in Limit 2-7 Triple Draw Championship Six-Handed event on Thursday at Horseshoe Las Vegas, defeating Danny Wong in heads-up play. It is Ivey’s 11th career bracelet, breaking a tie with Doyle Brunson, Johnny Chan, and Erik Seidel for second on the all-time list. Phil Hellmuth owns the all-time record with 17 career WSOP victories. Ivey’s last bracelet came in 2014, as he has played fewer events at the WSOP over the years. “I’m motivated. If I can play, I will. A lot of times I’m not in town,” Ivey told WSOP.com. “I keep showing up, playing, performing. I want to keep winning.” Ivey, 47, earned $347,440 for the victory and added to his reputation as the best player of his generation. Wong, who was seeking his second career bracelet, took home $225,827. Jason Mercier lost a key pot against Ivey with both players getting low on chips and finished third. Wong had almost a 3-to-2 chip advantage entering heads-up play as a large crowd surrounded the table, but Ivey quickly took control and continued to make hands against his opponent. Wong survived one all-in before falling soon after when Ivey drew to a wheel (7-5-4-3-2), the best hand in 2-7 Triple Draw. This was Ivey’s first victory in a $10,000 buy-in tournament and his latest in a non-Hold’em event. None of Ivey’s 11 bracelets have come in Hold’em. Ivey said, 'It feels good to win always.'

author: Export Development Canada
title: Tesla shareholders to vote today on $56B pay package
mainText: Today is the big Tesla shareholder vote. We’ll finally get to learn, among other things, whether investors think Elon Musk deserves his $56 billion pay package. And if they don’t, will Musk make good on his threats and leave Tesla so he can focus on xAI or SpaceX or just X?! Before the shareholder vote commences, we think it’s worth a second look at why Chancellor Kathaleen McCormick struck down the “re-ratification” of the package in January. Her dominant theme? Musk holds so much sway over Tesla and its board of directors that there was no substantial negotiation when the company hammered out this deal with him in 2017-2018. A little bird came to senior reporter Sean O’Kane and told him that Ford was poaching employees at EV startup Canoo. Got a tip for us? Email Kirsten Korosec at kirsten.korosec@techcrunch.com, Sean O’Kane at sean.okane@techcrunch.com or Rebecca Bellan at rebecca.bellan@techcrunch.com. GM is giving Cruise an $850 million lifeline as the robotaxi company slowly starts re-entering markets. Other notable deals include Descartes acquiring BoxTop Technologies, FLO securing $136 million in capital, and Fly E-Bike going public on Nasdaq. Autonomous vehicle updates include Cruise returning to Houston, May Mobility launching in Detroit, and Waymo issuing a recall. Electric vehicle news features Aptera's crowdfunding challenges, the European Commission's tariffs on Chinese EVs, Fisker's first recall, and Rivian's strategic decisions. Revel in NYC is transitioning to a gig worker model, leading to driver layoffs.
