title: Mariners top prospect Jonny Farmelo tears ACL, will have knee surgery
mainText: Mariners top prospect Jonny Farmelo has torn his ACL and will undergo surgery after injuring his knee during a game. author: Ricki Green
title: Gavin McLeod’s Cannes Diary #1
mainText: Gavin McLeod, chief creative officer at CHEP Network is representing Australia on the Cannes Social & Influencer jury. McLeod, along with most of the other Australian and NZ jurors, writes exclusively for CB. I’m stoked to finally be in Cannes! It’s a long slog to get here and an even longer one working through the many hours of pre-judging that happens before even stepping foot in the Palais. Observations from pre-judging? Firstly, there’s a seismic shift at the Cannes Lions. Our jury briefings, which were impressively thorough, made it clear: it’s all about substance over style. Sure, the glitz is great, but this festival focuses on awarding work that delivers for real clients. As Amy Ferguson, our Jury President, has emphasised, results matter. If it doesn’t move the needle, it shouldn’t make the cut. Next, Brazil, the USA, and, perhaps surprisingly, the Middle East are powerhouses in Social & Influencer. The sheer volume of interesting work coming from these three regions, compared to Australia and New Zealand, is impressive. But the biggest trend (and already a cliché) was AI voiceovers on case studies. It felt like everyone started using them this year and almost universally decided their VO needed to sound like a cool US rapper. I miss the authenticity of voiceovers with a charmingly wonky grasp of English! Speaking of overused, note to self: making a song for social sung by a once-huge pop star is everyone’s go-to move. Nostalgia is powerful, but I’ve seen more ‘comeback tours’ in these case studies than I care to admit. Despite these gripes, there were some genuinely standout moments. Campaigns that not only ticked the boxes but also tugged at the heartstrings and made us laugh out loud. The kind of work that reminds you why you fell in love with this industry in the first place. Our shortlist sparked fascinating debate as we spent our first day of in-person judging refining it. The single biggest question asked was, “But what made it social?” It’s a worthwhile question, as there was a lot of work we loved, but under deeper examination, it felt more suited to categories like PR. We finished at 9pm with a finalised shortlist that we’re feeling good about. Judging was so enjoyable it didn’t feel like a long slog at all and I’m looking forward to tomorrow where we start awarding. Good luck to everyone who got through!

author: Brandon Cruz
title: Drivers warned over fake parking tickets ‘nearly identical’ to real thing – but a marking proves they’re no...
mainText: A new scam involving fake parking tickets is deceiving drivers in Calgary, Canada. The Calgary Parking Authority issued a warning after discovering that fraudsters are distributing counterfeit parking tickets with instructions to pay on a fake website, calgaryparkplus.com. Genuine parking tickets direct payments to calgaryparking.com/tickets or parkingtickets.calgaryparking.com. Two drivers fell victim to this scam and tried to pay the fines using legitimate city resources, only to realize the tickets were fake. Todd Sullivan from Calgary Parking emphasized the importance of reporting any fake tickets to the police and cautioned against sharing personal information online. This scam follows a previous one where scammers sent text messages instructing recipients to pay a parking fine through a bogus "self-serve portal." The city clarified that they do not use text messages for ticket notifications and advised recipients to ignore such messages. Sullivan reminded drivers that authentic parking tickets are issued in paper form, and residents can verify the legitimacy of a ticket by contacting Calgary Parking. While some fake tickets are harder to spot, drivers are urged to remain vigilant and verify any suspicious tickets. If in doubt, contact Calgary Parking at 403-537-7000 or verify online at calgaryparking.com.

author: Ricki Green
title: Karen Bryson’s Cannes Diary #1
mainText: Karen Bryson, freelance executive producer is representing Australia on the Cannes Film Craft jury. It’s been a few years since I have been to Cannes & love wandering around Old Town to shake off the jetlag. We arrive early for judging and so get to see the festival under construction. I am amazed at the army of art department & construction crews working around the clock. The dedication of the crew is impressive and the promenade transforms while we are locked in a dark room & stages are being set as we emerge at the end of our first day. The pre-judging has helped us to be familiar with the massive volume of entries, but it’s great to be able to come together to watch as a collective and discuss the merits of each. What’s most exciting is seeing brave work that reflects the importance of relationships, and the trust that is needed to produce work that pushes boundaries. The work that stands out both take risks and also highlights the importance of connection. Day 1 is all about deciding the shortlist and it’s a rigorous process given the wealth of exceptional work, with over a thousand entries. Film craft is complex and nuanced and there are many, many (many!) discussions to be had. Tomorrow we start deciding medal which promises even more passionate debate, so it’s an early night tonight. Congrats to all those to have been shortlisted & bring on Day 2!

title: 2024 U.S. Open: Rory McIlroy aiming to convert latest major opportunity after string of near-victories
mainText: Rory McIlroy, a golfer who has not won a major championship in a decade, is aiming to end his major drought at the 2024 U.S. Open. With two recent second-place finishes and a history of coming close to victory, McIlroy is determined to convert his latest major opportunity into a trophy-hoisting victory. Having finished in the top-10 20 times since his last major win in 2014, McIlroy faces the challenge of breaking through and taking home a major title. His consistent performance in recent majors, including a runner-up finish in the previous year's U.S. Open, shows his potential. Adopting a more conservative approach and embracing the unique challenge presented by the U.S. Open setups have led to improved results for McIlroy. Despite facing a three-shot deficit going into the final round at Pinehurst, McIlroy remains hopeful that he can produce the needed golf to secure a win. Learning from past experiences, especially the late bogeys in his current round, McIlroy recognizes the importance of finishing strong, making crucial shots under pressure, and handling setbacks effectively. By demonstrating excellence under pressure and rectifying previous close calls, McIlroy aims to capture his fifth major and put an end to his decade-long major drought.

author: Dinniah Bartholomew
title: ‘This is going to get interesting,’ say shoppers of new anti-theft measure with $1k fine – it’s not only for shoplifters
mainText: A new anti-theft measure in Mississippi has been announced, targeting shoplifters with more severe penalties. Under the new law, both shoplifters and anyone aiding in the crime can be charged with a felony if they steal items worth $1,000 or more. This law aims to combat organized retail crimes like smash-and-grabs. The mayors in DeSoto County played a key role in pushing for this legislation to address rampant theft. The new measure has been met with mixed reactions from shoppers, with some expressing excitement and others raising concerns about potential loopholes for petty theft. The spike in theft nationwide, including a 20% increase in shoplifting in Long Island, has prompted retailers to implement stricter anti-theft measures. The impact of theft extends beyond just retailers, affecting employees' sense of safety and making it challenging to hire new staff. Factors contributing to the rise in theft include staffing shortages, self-checkout services, and the increasing cost of living.

author: Summer Raemason
title: Brit holiday warning as tourists flying to Europe could face ‘lie detector’ test carried out by artificial intelligence
mainText: HOLIDAYMAKERS have been warned they could be caught out by a 'lie detector test' before being allowed into Europe. Artificial Intelligence could stand in the way of tourists hoping to reach their dream vacation destination. The EU plans to strengthen border security with AI software that tracks passengers' body and face movements to detect unusual behavior. While experts warn of potential discrimination against individuals with disabilities or anxiety, the technology aims to enhance security post-Brexit. The AI systems could be integrated into the upcoming Entry-Exit Systems and European Travel Information and Authorisation System. These measures include online immigration officers using AI to question travelers and scan social media, all within the guidelines of The Artificial Intelligence Act. Concerns have also been raised about the implementation of the new Entry/Exit system, which will replace passport stamps for British travelers heading to EU and Schengen countries. Additionally, Brits will need an ETIAS visa-waiver for stays under 90 days, similar to the ESTA for the US. The introduction of these systems has been delayed to 2025, requiring 1.4 billion people from over 60 visa-exempt countries to obtain travel authorization to enter most European countries.

author: Liz Gill
title: The English seaside town millions of tourists often forget about – with free Victorian pier and blue flag b...
mainText: Harwich is a historic English seaside town often overlooked by tourists, despite its rich maritime history and unique charm. The town was the birthplace of the Mayflower, the ship that carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America, shaping the course of history. Today, Harwich maintains its traditional character with events like the Guy Carnival and a town crier. Visitors can explore attractions such as the Wattle and Daub house, Redoubt Fort, radar tower from WWII, and the Victorian Ha’Penny Pier. The town also holds a statue commemorating the Kindertransport children who sought refuge from the Nazis in Britain. Harwich offers a mix of outdoor activities like crabbing and boat tours, as well as cultural experiences at the Electric Palace Cinema. With affordable prices and volunteer-run attractions, Harwich embodies local pride and a commitment to preserving its heritage. The town's eccentric traditions, such as the mayor throwing traditional spiced buns to crowds, add to its unique appeal. While neighboring Dovercourt has seafront cafes and arcades, Harwich stands out for its understated, old-fashioned charm and historic traditions that are still vibrant today.

author: Trisha Harbord
title: Eight summer holiday deals across Spain, France and Turkey – with waterpark hotels and bargain campsites...
mainText: SUMMER is on sale, so start dreaming of relaxing on a beach, swimming in clear blue waters and watching the sun go down with a cocktail. There are thousands of offers for school holiday breaks with many companies giving discounts and free child places. Here Trisha Harbord chooses a selection of deals showing you what is on the market. EGYPT EASYJET Holidays has thousands of free child places on three to 14-night getaways. Book before August 31 and families of two adults and two children sharing a room will also get £200 off. And a touch of luxury doesn’t have to cost a fortune, depending on your destination choice. The five-star Jaz Mirabel Park and Club, in Egypt’s Sharm El Sheikh, has a private beach beside the clear waters of the Red Sea. There are four pools, one with slides, right, restaurants, bars, kids’ clubs and playgrounds. Dive or snorkel off the hotel’s half-mile jetty or discover the reef of nearby Ras Al Mohammed National Park, which has more than 1,000 species of fish. GO: Seven nights’ all-inclusive, with flights from Bristol on August 31, costs from £1,797 for a family of four. See easyjet.com. ORLANDO TAKING the kids to Orlando in Florida is never going to be cheap but good deals on flights, accommodation and theme park tickets are out there. Save money by getting multi-tickets to attractions such as Universal Studios and Islands of Adventure and the four Disney parks. CoCo Key Hotel & Water Park Resort on International Drive is a fantastic base and offers a shuttle service to the parks. It has a superb canopy-covered waterpark with 14 slides and rides including Parrot’s Perch, right, a lagoon for little ones, a gaming arcade, restaurants plus a coffee bar. GO: Virgin Holidays is offering seven nights’ room-only for the price of six, with flights from Heathrow on August 28. Price for two adults and two children sharing a room is from £2,870. See virginholidays.co.uk. Attractiontickets. com has ten per cent off all park tickets until midnight tomorrow. TURKEY THERE’S a great choice of budget deals to Turkey this summer. Thomas Cook has free child places and accepts low deposits, with holiday balances due a month before travelling. The Mustis Royal Plaza might be a small, three-star hotel with just 70 rooms but it is big on hospitality. Plus it gets rave reviews for its rooms and food. In the heart of Marmaris, it has a pool with slides, Turkish steambath and playground. Plus its evening entertainment includes live music, dance shows, parties and DJ sets. The beach on the “turquoise coast” is a ten-minute shuttle ride away and Aquadream waterpark, 16th-century Marmaris Castle, an amphitheatre and marina are all nearby. GO: Seven nights’ B&B, including flights from Luton on August 19, based on two adults and one child, costs from £1,030. See thomascook.com. GRAN CANARIA TUI has £250 off selected holidays and free child places on flights, accommodation, meals and transfers this summer. Go online, enter the dates when you want to travel and the child place finder brings up hundreds of hotspot deals. The beachside 4T Tui Blue Orquidea in Bahia Feliz on beautiful Gran Canaria has a splash park and three pools. Plus there are kids’ clubs, activities galore as well as live shows and tranquil rooms to get a good night’s rest. Watersports lovers can go windsurfing, kayaking or surfing in the bay and you can take a helicopter for a bird’s eye view of the island’s mountains, valleys and beaches. For duty-free shopping, take the direct 15-minute bus ride to the malls in Playa del Ingles. GO: Seven nights’ all-inclusive with flights from East Midlands on August 5, costs £852pp, based on two children and two adults sharing a room. See tui.co.uk. MED CRUISE DON’T want to fly? Check out one of the summer cruise deals with sailings from the UK to the Mediterranean and Fjords. If you’ve got younger children and can get away before the schools break up, you are quids in. P&O has a 14-night cruise from Southampton on Arvia – a 5,000-passenger ship with activities galore, -entertainment including kids’ clubs, cinemas, sports and 30 places to eat and drink. There’s enough fun on board to never want to leave the ship but stops include ports in Spain and Italy, with the chance to tour Florence and Pisa. GO: Fourteen nights’ full-board in an inside cabin, departing Southampton on July 7, costs from £999 per adult, £299 per child aged two to six and from £99 per toddler aged six months to two. See pocruises.com. FRANCE HERE’S a Eurocamp bargain – more than a third off a week-long break in its summer sale. And you’ll be staying alongside a 16th-century French chateau. Kids will love the Chateau de Fonrives’ clubs, aquatic centre with slides horse-riding and crazy golf. Adults are catered for too with a spa and wellness centre. The five-star resort in the -Dordogne also has a bar and restaurant, sports, evening shows, -karaoke and watersports. The nearby town of Villereal has half-timbered houses, a medieval hall still used for markets, cafes and shops. GO: Seven nights for a family of four -staying in a two-bedroom holiday home from August 10 costs from £651, saving 34 per cent. See eurocamp.co.uk. Return LeShuttle for a car and passengers from Folkestone to Calais costs £241. See leshuttle.com. GREECE RELAX on a beautiful Greek island in an all-inclusive beach hotel. First Choice have deals to super sunspots such as Kos, Corfu and Zante for all budgets – and there are free child places. Active families will love the range of sports at the 3T Suneo Atlantica Thalassa, including beach volleyball, football, tennis and minigolf. There are pools, a buffet restaurant and three bars too. The hotel in Lambi is a ten-minute bus ride to bustling Kos town, which has a great indoor market, shops, cafes and restaurants. Wander through the streets and visit the 14th-century Castle of the Knights of Saint John. GO: Seven nights’ all-inclusive, with flights from Gatwick on August 29, costs from £673 per person, based on two adults and two children sharing a family room. See firstchoice.co.uk. MALTA THERE’S no harm in waiting to book a summer holiday if you don’t mind where you go. Travelzoo prides itself on having last-minute package and cruise deals that are well worth the wait. It is offering 24 per cent off a five-night, all-inclusive holiday to Malta next month, which works out at less than £500pp. The 4H luxurious Qawra Palace Hotel has pools and terraces with fabulous views over the Mediterranean. There’s a spa, gym, watersports and range of restaurants. Kids will love rockpooling on the adjoining beach, which has flat limestone platforms for sunbathing. The holiday also includes a free day’s cruise to the island of Comino where you can swim in the crystal clear waters of the Blue Lagoon. GO: Five nights’ all-inclusive, including flights from any London airport in July and a boat trip, costs from £459pp. See travelzoo.com.

author: Brodie Stone
title: Severe thunderstorm watch in place for Northland from 6pm Sunday
mainText: MetService has issued a severe thunderstorm watch from 6pm until midnight for Northland as an unstable northwest airflow lies over the north, bringing possible thunderstorms and rain. The warning also covers Auckland, Great Barrier Island, the Coromandel and Bay of Plenty with watches ending at varying times. There is moderate risk of thunderstorms for Northland with the chance of localised downpours of 25 to 40mm per hour. Rainfall of this intensity may cause surface or flash flooding, especially in low-lying areas such as streams, rivers or narrow valleys. Conditions should start easing in the north after 10pm. Motorists are advised to take care as driving conditions may be hazardous with surface flooding and poor visibility in heavy rain. According to its website, Metservice issues a severe weather watch whenever there is an expectation that conditions may deteriorate to the thresholds specified for the issue of a severe weather warning after the next 24 hours but within 48-72 hours, or if there is a high level of uncertainty within the next 24 hours.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: 8 Israeli Soldiers Killed In Rafah In One Of The Deadliest Incidents For IDF In 6 Months
mainText: Tel Aviv: A devastating blast in southern Gaza’s Rafah claimed the lives of eight Israeli servicemen on Sunday morning. This distressing event marks the most severe loss the IDF has suffered in the Strip since the start of the year as per reports from the Times of Israel. Among the brave souls who made their ultimate sacrifice was a young officer 23-year-old Cpt Wassem Mahmoud. He hailed from Beit Jann and served as a deputy company commander in the Combat Engineering Corps 601st Battalion. Information about the remaining seven soldiers will be made public once their loved ones have been suitably notified. Initial findings from an IDF investigation indicate that the soldiers were inside a Namer armoured combat engineering vehicle (CEV) when the explosion occurred. The incident took place around 5 am as the convoy following an overnight offensive against Hamas in Rafahs Tel Sultan neighbourhood was en route to secure buildings for rest as reported by The Times of Israel. The Namer CEV positioned as the fifth or sixth vehicle in the convoy was struck by a powerful explosion. It remains unclear whether the blast resulted from a pre-planted bomb or if Hamas operatives directly placed an explosive device on the vehicle. Investigators are also considering whether explosives stored outside the CEV contributed to the intensity of the explosion. According to the IDF there was no exchange of gunfire during the incident and the vehicle was in motion at the time of the explosion. The deaths of these soldiers bring the total toll of IDF casualties during the ground offensive against Hamas and operations along the Gaza border to 307. This figure includes a police officer killed in a recent hostage rescue operation and a civilian Defense Ministry contractor also lost in the conflict according to The Times of Israel. The deadliest incident prior to todays tragedy occurred in January when 21 soldiers perished in a blast triggered by Hamas RPG fire that resulted in the collapse of two buildings. The IDF continues to investigate the circumstances surrounding todays devastating loss emphasising the ongoing challenges and risks faced by military personnel operating in volatile regions The Times of Israel reported.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Iranian war criminal freed by Sweden in prisoner swap deal
mainText: Sweden has released a convicted Iranian war criminal as part of a prisoner swap deal. Tehran and Stockholm carried out the switch, which saw a European Union diplomat and another man released in exchange for Hamid Nouri, who was found guilty of being complicit in the 1988 mass executions in the Islamic Republic. Nouri was arrested in 2019 as he travelled in Sweden as a tourist. This likely prompted the detention of the two Swedes, part of a long-running strategy by Iran to use those with ties abroad as bargaining chips in negotiations with the West. While Iranian state television claimed that Nouri had been 'illegally detained', Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said diplomat Johan Floderus and a second Swedish citizen, Saeed Azizi, had been facing a 'hell on earth'. 'Iran has made these Swedes pawns in a cynical negotiation game with the aim of getting the Iranian citizen Hamid Nouri released from Sweden,' Mr Kristersson said on Saturday. 'It has been clear all along that this operation would require difficult decisions - now the government has made those decisions.' State TV showed film of Nouri limping off a plane at Mehrabad International Airport in Tehran and embracing his family. 'I am Hamid Nouri. I am in Iran,' he said. 'God makes me free.' Oman mediated the release, its state-run news agency reported. In 2022, the Stockholm District Court sentenced Nouri to life in prison.

author: Toi Science Desk
title: Nasa restores Voyager 1: Months after going dark, spacecraft transmits data on outer planets
mainText: Nasa has successfully restored Voyager 1 to working order several months after it encountered a grave computer problem. The spacecraft faced a significant issue that threatened its mission. Engineers spent months diagnosing and resolving the issue. Since last year, the space community has been anxious about the aging probe's prospects. Voyager 1 embarked on a mission to explore the outer planets. In 2012, Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to enter interstellar space. Each Voyager spacecraft carries a golden phonograph record filled with sounds and images depicting life on Earth. Nasa reported significant progress in restoring Voyager 1. By late last month, they managed to restore functionality to two of Voyager 1’s science instruments, enabling it to continue its mission and send back science data. Nasa revealed that it had fully restored the remaining science instruments, bringing Voyager 1 back to normal operations. Despite this success, Voyager 1’s extended mission could be short-lived. Nasa estimated that the nuclear-powered generators on both Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 might expire around 2025.

author: Akanksha Arora
title: Surge In Obesity And Type-2 Diabetes Could Trigger Fatty Liver Cases In Britain, Warns Experts
mainText: The United Kingdom can soon witness a spike in fatty liver disease cases. Experts from the British Liver Trust have warned that these cases will be fuelled by an obesity epidemic. This cancer-causing disease is mostly seen in individuals who are obese, and or have type 2 diabetes. According to media reports, experts from the trust fear that "increasing prevalence of type 2 diabetes and obesity" will bring with it a "fatty liver tsunami." Vanessa Hebditch, a member from the charity said, "There is a need for greater awareness of the link between diabetes and liver disease." She added, "It is will known that type 2 diabetes can increase the risk of many health issues including cardiovascular and kidney disease but it can also significantly raise your risk of fatty liver disease." What is fatty liver disease? As the name suggests, fatty liver disease refers to an increased build-up of fat inside the liver. The symptoms of fatty liver disease are: Fatigue, Not feeling well, or malaise, Pain or discomfort in the upper right belly area. Having high levels of fat in your liver is also associated with a risk of serious health problems such as diabetes, high blood pressure, and kidney disease. BLT revealed that two-thirds of people living with type 2 diabetes have a fatty liver. "This means that the UK could be facing a tsunami of people newly diagnosed with fatty liver disease." Who is at the risk of fatty liver disease? The exact causes of this disease are unknown so far. However, as per researchers, it is more common in people who have type 2 diabetes, prediabetes, obesity, are middle aged or older, Hispanic followed by non-Hispanic whites, have high levels of fats in the blood, high blood pressure, take certain drugs, have metabolic disorders, rapid weight loss, certain infections such as hepatitis C, exposure to some toxins. How is fatty liver disease diagnosed? As for the most part, there are no symptoms, it can be hard to diagnose this condition. Your doctor usually suspects that you have it if you get abnormal liver test results. For a diagnosis, your doctor will need: Your medical history, A physical exam, Various tests, including blood imaging and sometimes a biopsy. During the physical exam, your doctor aims to examine your body. A few signs of a fatty liver could be: An enlarged liver, Signs of cirrhosis: Jaundice.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: 'Consider my duty to thank PM': Sharad Pawar's backhanded compliment for Modi
mainText: NEW DELHI: Nationalist Congress Party-SP (NCP-SP) leader Sharad Pawar on Saturday took a cheeky dig at Prime Minister Narendra Modi and said that Maharashtra's opposition alliance, the Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA), secured victories in all those seats the PM campaigned in. MVA won 30 out of 48 seats in this year's Lok Sabha election. Taking a jibe at PM Modi, Sharad Pawar at a press conference said, "Wherever the Prime Minister's roadshow and rally took place, we won. That is why I consider it my duty to thank the Prime Minister."BJP, which on its own had received 20-plus seats in the last two polls, struggled to get even 10 seats in Maharashtra this year. BJP's vote share in Maharashtra stood at 26.18%. In contrast, Congress managed to slightly improve its performance, winning 13 seats in the state and Shiv Sena contributed nine seats. Speaking at the same press conference, Congress leader Prithviraj Chavan and Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Uddhav Thackeray, who faced a major political crisis in his party when the Shiv Sena split in 2022, declared that the doors are shut for all his former party members who abandoned his faction and joined the camp of his rival, Eknath Shinde. When asked if he would welcome back the leaders who had deserted his faction, Thackeray firmly stated, "Absolutely not. Those who left me will not be taken back." Sharad Pawar, when posed the same question, responded, "There is no question of taking them back."Regarding the acceptance of new leaders into his party, Thackeray said, "We will move forward with all those people who stayed with us, and struggled with us. If some people want to join us, we will see." Encouraged by the Lok Sabha poll outcomes, Thackeray also proclaimed that the MVA will jointly participate in the forthcoming Assembly elections in the state. "When three parties come together, it means everyone is together and everyone will fight together," he affirmed. Across the country, BJP's victory count fell short of their previous achievements. On the other hand, Congress witnessed a resurgence, clinching 99 seats, a significant increase from the 52 seats they won in 2019 and the 44 in 2014.(With inputs from agencies)

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Chandu Champion Box Office Estimate Day 2: Kartik Aaryan film jumps by 40% on Saturday
mainText: The Kartik Aaryan and Kabir Khan film, Chandu Champion has shown a 40% jump in collection on its 2nd day as per early estimates. The Sajid Nadiadwala production has collected in the range of Rs. 7.25 crore to Rs. 7.75 crores on Saturday, taking total collections to Rs. 13 crores. The Kartik Aaryan led sport drama will be looking at an opening weekend of Rs. 21 crore, and then take benefit of the holiday on Monday to set itself up for a long theatrical run at the box office. The critic reviews are outright positive and the same will soon start to reflect in the box office collections of Chandu Champion. The jump on Saturday is an encouraging sign, however, the overall numbers so far still remain on the lower side. Every day is going to be a challenge for Chandu Champion and the film also needs to go on and on without surrendering until it hits the bulls-eye. It has the benefit of 2-week free run and hopefully, this should push the film closer towards the Rs 100 crore club, like Satyaprem Ki Katha. The prices also went back to normal on Saturday and the same is reflecting in the collections too.

author: Neil Patel
title: Is It Too Late to Buy Apple Stock?
mainText: A company doesn't get to a market cap of $3.3 trillion without doing some things right. This is exactly the story with Apple (AAPL -0.82%), one of the most dominant businesses on the face of the planet. Shares have skyrocketed 838% in the past decade, a gain that outpaces the broader Nasdaq Composite index by 10 percentage points annually. Prospective investors might have their eyes on Apple right now. But is it too late to buy the stock? Apple has arguably the strongest brand in the world, one that has been built up over the years thanks to its popular products and services. And the combination of hardware and software creates an extremely powerful ecosystem that drives customer loyalty and stickiness. The company's operating margin has averaged a superb 28.1% in the past five years. Apple revealed its highly anticipated artificial intelligence (AI) push recently at its Worldwide Developers Conference. With Apple's latest foray into AI, the hope is that sales of the iPhone will accelerate. Growth has certainly slowed in recent years as consumers feel less obligated to regularly upgrade to the latest device. Apple shares are priced as if outsize growth is a certainty. Based on its limited growth prospects and steep valuation, I do believe that it's too late to buy Apple stock right now. Shares aren't likely to outperform the broader Nasdaq Composite over the next few years.

author: Maurie Backman
title: 3 Social Security Changes Retirees Need to Know About in 2024
mainText: In 2024, Social Security has experienced significant changes that retirees should be aware of. Firstly, benefits increased by 3.2% at the beginning of the year, with a projected 2.66% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for 2025 due to a slower pace of inflation. Secondly, the wage cap for Social Security taxes rose to $168,600 in 2024, as compared to $160,200 the previous year. President Biden has proposed taxing earnings over $400,000 for Social Security, potentially impacting higher earners' maximum monthly benefits. Lastly, the requirement to qualify for Social Security has become stricter, with workers needing to earn $1,730 per credit in 2024, up from $1,640 in the previous year. While changes may seem unexpected, staying informed about Social Security is crucial for retirees and individuals entering the workforce to navigate potential financial impacts.

author: Ellie Smitherman
title: Major coffee chain with 2,000 branches to abruptly shut ‘excellent’ site in HOURS as customers sob ‘sad to...
mainText: A major coffee chain, Costa Coffee, is abruptly shutting down one of its stores in North Wales located in Ruthin. This closure comes after another branch in Colwyn Bay also closed recently. The company spokesperson expressed sadness over the closures and thanked the local communities for their support. Customers who frequented the Ruthin branch expressed their disappointment on social media, praising the convenient location and excellent service provided by the staff. Some worried about the impact on the town's vibrancy and appeal to tourists. Despite the positive reviews and customer loyalty, the closures are part of a larger trend in the industry where companies reorganize to cut costs or face difficulties in negotiations with landlords. Costa Coffee has been temporarily closing and refurbishing some of its stores, showing that not all closures indicate financial struggles. However, the sudden closures have raised concerns among locals about the potential decline of Colwyn Bay and other areas where Costa Coffee branches have shut down. The chain has faced closures in various locations, with plans for more shutdowns in the upcoming months. Fans of the coffee chain have been left upset by the closures, highlighting the emotional attachment customers have to these popular coffee shops.

author: Anupama Jha
title: IRDAI Introduces Higher Surrender Payouts On Early Exit From Life Insurance Policies
mainText: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has introduced a higher special surrender value (SSV) for traditional endowment life insurance policies. This change allows policyholders to receive a portion of their premium back even if they exit the policy early, starting from the first year. The move aims to protect policyholders and ensure fair returns on early surrenders. There may be a slight impact on new business margins for insurance companies due to this change, but steps will be taken to mitigate it without compromising customer value. The increased surrender value will benefit policyholders who surrender their policies early, even though the increment will be lower for later years. IRDAI now requires the SSV to be at least equal to the present value of the sum assured and future benefits. The regulator also mandates life insurers to provide a Customer Information Sheet (CIS) to customers to explain policy details clearly. Additionally, insurers can now offer new product designs, including index-linked plans and variable annuity options. Stricter penalties are imposed on insurers regarding customer grievances.

author: Rom-Preston-Ellis
title: People 'scared to leave home' on London estate 'overrun by drug dealers
mainText: Residents of Townley Court in Stratford, East London, are living in fear on an estate overrun by drug dealers and sex workers, with reports of muggings, sex acts witnessed by children, and guns pulled on disabled residents. Locals feel abandoned by the police, claiming they have 'given up' on protecting them, leading to a lawless environment where criminal activities occur openly and frequently. Despite residents' calls for help, police inaction has left many feeling helpless and scared to leave their homes. The situation has escalated to the point where residents fear it will take a tragedy to prompt any action. Residents have witnessed disturbing incidents, including encountering sex workers and drug activities near their homes, with some feeling like they are 'under siege' in their own community. The lack of police response has led to residents giving up on reporting incidents, as they feel dismissed and unheard. The situation has worsened with addicts and sex workers reportedly misusing keys meant for firefighters to access residents' blocks for illicit activities. Residents have described a constant state of fear and unease, with incidents of violence, drug use, and public disturbance becoming a daily occurrence, impacting both adults and children in the community. Despite efforts to document evidence of criminal behavior, residents feel ignored and helpless, leading to a sense of resignation and hopelessness. Authorities have been criticized for ineffective responses, including 'pointless' patrols that do not address the nighttime issues plaguing the community. Residents have called for urgent action to improve safety and restore peace in their neighborhood, with some expressing concerns that the situation could escalate into a deadly outcome if left unchecked.

title: Can trauma cause a broken heart? - study
mainText: In the first of its kind, an Israeli medical study has found a correlation between so-called “broken heart syndrome” and national trauma, showing a 100% increase of cases since October 7. The research was presented earlier this month at Israelis Cardiology Association Conference.The research was carried out under the leadership of Prof. Eli Lev, director of cardiology, and Dr Yuhavl Kahila at Assuta Hospital in Ashdod and involved collaboration with centers across the country, including Barzilai Hospital in Ashkelon, Hillel Yaffe Medical Center in Hadera, Shamir Medical Center in Be’er Ya’akov, Wolfson Medical Center in Holon and Meir Medical Center in Kfar Saba.Broken heart syndrome, sometimes called Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, is a rare medical condition that can be triggered by intense distress or emotional suffering. It typically occurs in women. Symptoms may present like a heart attack, but the syndrome only accounts for about 2% of cases of people treated for heart attacks. console.log("2390 BODY2. Using data from six hospitals across Israel, the research team recorded 30 cases between October and December 2023, up from 16 the year before. Barzilai medical center staff, October 8, 2023. (credit: SETH J. FRANTZMAN)This is a syndrome that simulates a heart attack caused by mental or physical stress," explained Prof. Lev, "and this is the first time that we see a clear connection between the syndrome and a national trauma - and the fact that the data in the study was collected all over the country and not just from the South shows this.""So far, most patients' descriptions of the 'broken heart syndrome' have been reported following personal crises such as the death of a relative and other difficult events, and I am not aware of a description in the professional literature of the syndrome following a national trauma,” said the Professor."The syndrome manifests itself in a significant disturbance in the contraction of the heart muscle on an echocardiogram and can have significant complication and mortality rates," said Dr. Yuval Kahila.The Chairman of Israel Heart Society, Amit Segev, told Hebrew media that he was not surprised by the findings."Broken heart syndrome is related to an increase in stress, and in all kinds of situations where there is an increase in stress, it is expected that there will be an increase in this syndrome," Segev explained. "For example, following the earthquake in California, they saw a huge increase in heart attacks, some of which were broken heart syndrome."Case studiesIn November, the Hillel Yaffe Medical Center reported an increase in women around the age of 50, mostly mothers of soldiers, who were suffering from symptoms of a heart attack. In one case, a 49-year-old mother of three sons from Hadera was brought into hospital with severe symptoms. Two of her sons were called to fight in the South. She fainted at work but did not see it as a concern. However, a few days later, she received a message that her son’s commander had been injured severely in Gaza. She reported an accelerated heartbeat, shaking in her knees, and then loss of consciousness. After arriving at Hillel Yaffe Medical Center by ambulance, the doctors discovered that her heart arteries were normal and she was actually suffering from "broken heart syndrome."In another case included in the study, 40 year old IDF bereavement officer Capt. (res.) Sivan Sekeli Ben Zichri went into a stress-induced cardiac arrest upon witnessing 17 freshly dug graves at a funeral.Ben Zichri was responsible for delivering news of the fallen to families and organizing funerals. Despite a normal EKG reading at the hospital, she went into full cardiac arrest and was technically dead until successfully resuscitated. Doctors discovered she had a torn heart artery, which she was told was due to stress. "The eulogies were so difficult that my heart simply could not cope," she said.She has not yet recovered and is still undergoing rehabilitation.In October, Israeli media reported that ZAKA volunteer Motti Botzkin suffered a stress-induced heart attack following a long and traumatic search for human remains in Gaza border communities. Father of rescued hostageWhile not officially diagnosed as such, relatives of Yossi Meir, father of rescued hostage Almog Meir Jan, have attributed his death, the night before he could hear of his son's return, to grief.“The night before Almog’s return [to my brother], his heart stopped,” Meir’s sister Dina told KAN News. Rabbi Lior Engelman, a friend of Meir, told Israeli media outlets: “Yossi loved Almog with all his heart and was tormented daily. His heart could not stand it.”The daughter of released hostage Hannah Katzir also spoke of her mother's heart-related medical issues, stating that she, too, had "broken heart syndrome."More on the conditionA 2007 study, presented in the Cleveland Clinic Journal of Medicine, wrote that the syndrome was referred to as stress cardiomyopathy in a study in 2005, but "because several of the patients had presented following the death of a loved one, the name “broken heart syndrome” was also introduced".It continued by saying that 88.8% of the reported cases were in women, with an average age of 58 to 77. This remains consistent to this day. The in-hospital mortality of 'broken heart syndrome' was around 1.1% at the time of the study.Interestingly, the connection between Israel and the condition has been made before. A 2014 BBC article wrote of a 1995 research that found that "Israelis were more likely to die as a result of heart-related problems on 18 January 1991 than on any day in the preceding and subsequent two months, as well as for the same period of time the previous year."This was because this date marked the beginning of the Gulf War, said the BBC, which resulted in 18 missiles being directed at Israel from Iraq.

author: Belinda Feek
title: Kupa Koinaki busted for part in 120kg cocaine ship seizure
mainText: A man busted piloting his boat back from an unsuccessful 120kg cocaine pick-up from a ship in the Port of Tauranga told police he was out on the water at night “practising to be a boat captain”. Kuka Koinaki was deemed at the “lower end of the hierarchy” but he was still fundamental to the operation as his role was to bring the drugs back from the ship, Quest, in a newly purchased Nuline aluminium boat. Koinaki, 52, appeared in the High Court at Hamilton on Thursday where Justice Michele Wilkinson-Smith jailed him for four years on charges of conspiring to possess the class A drug, cocaine, for supply and driving while disqualified. He was also given an extra two months in remittance for $8861 in fines. The bulk carrier ship Quest entered New Zealand shores on December 22, 2022 carrying 120kg of cocaine concealed in four packages within the sea chest of the vessel. On January 3, last year, the Quest was finally given a berth in the Port of Tauranga. Police were already aware of the planned drug importation and had seized the drugs by the time Koinaki set off. According to a police summary of facts, about $70,000 was spent by other people over several days in preparation to retrieve the drugs, including buying a secondhand Toyota Hilux, the aluminium boat, along with kayaks and other diving equipment. On January 8 Koinaki towed a small aluminium boat from Auckland to Tauranga, and he went to check out the Quest in the harbour. By January 11, the plan to retrieve the drugs was put into action. At 8pm, Koinaki arrived at Pilot Bay and launched the boat from Sulphur Point 15 minutes later, heading out to the Quest. Koinaki was arrested when he returned several hours later. When questioned by police, he said he was “practising to be a boat captain and practising using the boat at night to get his boat skipper’s licence”. ‘Kicked out of rehabilitation’ Koinaki’s counsel Nicola Pointer said there was a direct correlation between the offending and his dysfunctional upbringing which had led him into a life of crime. She also urged the judge to issue a discount for his time on electronically-monitored bail to the Grace Foundation, despite being “exited” for using cocaine and cannabis. “It’s not perhaps surprising he fell off the wagon given his long-standing issues ... notwithstanding that, he’s reached out to Odyssey House [for treatment] and it’s what he hopes to do once he goes to the Parole Board.” She also asked that his $8861 in fines be remitted for extra jail time. ‘Inconceivable you didn’t know drugs were involved’ Judge Wilkinson-Smith found his offending was driven by commerciality rather than his life-long drug addiction. She also took aim at Koinaki’s continued stance that he didn’t know drugs were involved, labelling it “completely unbelievable”. “You towed a boat from Auckland to facilitate the offending and you were located in the sea awaiting the delivery of an item. “It is simply inconceivable that you did not know drugs were involved.” However, she accepted he was to be sentenced on the fact he didn’t know the exact drug or quantity. The judge acknowledged his dysfunctional upbringing which saw him living on the streets as a youngster, huffing petrol and glue. By 15 he was selling cannabis and went on to live in a cycle of drug abuse with little pro-social support. “On the other hand, you are a mature man and have been in and out of the prison system for years.” She noted an inconsistency in his reports; one noted he had been a patched senior member of the Mongrel Mob as recently as 2020 but he told the pre-sentence report writer that he left the gang 10 to 11 years ago. Ultimately, from an eight-year starting point, she agreed to hand down 50 per cent in discounts, arriving at a jail term of four years. He was also disqualified from driving for 12 months in the hope that when he was freed from prison, he could start his life again unimpeded. Belinda Feek is an Open Justice reporter based in Waikato. She has worked at NZME for nine years and has been a journalist for 20.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Released Israeli hostage describes return from Hamas captivity
mainText: Almost seven months after she and her daughters returned from Hamas captivity, Doron Katz Asher explained the struggles of continuing with daily life after being held captive in a Saturday Facebook post. Asher was kidnapped on October 7 at Kibbutz Nir Oz with her two daughters, Raz, 5, and Aviv, 3. Her mother was murdered by Hamas terrorists during the attack. Asher was released with her two daughters after 49 days in captivity. In her post on the 'Mamatzchik' Facebook group, she wrote that it took her over six months to build up the strength to write about what it is like to return from captivity. Asher explained that she continues to experience "nightmares at night, fear of noises, and questions from [her] little girls who don't understand why this happened to them—dealing with tough questions that break my break." Since returning, she has experienced flashbacks and other moments of trauma. She recalls "closing my eyes and seeing my captors still in front of me. It's endless longing for my mother, my heroic brother, and friends I will never see again," she added. "And it's mainly putting on a smiling mask to raise the girls in a happy home even though my heart is bleeding." Receiving support from Israel, Asher explained that following her return, her house became like "a train station for food and gifts without actually ordering anything" and that she ultimately had to dedicate a room in her house to store all the gifts sent to her and her two daughters. She wrote that the experience caused her to "discover how wonderful the people of Israel are with all their help and support." In a CNN interview in January, Asher described her experiences in captivity. Asher and her daughters were kept with a Gazan family. The three of them were watched over continuously by the children and grandchildren of the owner of the house and experienced psychological warfare while being held captive.

author: Sukanya Nandy
title: CSIR UGC NET 2024 Exam City Intimation Slip Released, Steps To Download
mainText: The National Testing Agency (NTA) released the CSIR University Grants Commission National Eligibility Test (CSIR UGC NET) exam city intimation slips for the June 2024 session on June 15. The exam city slips for the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research NET 2024 can now be downloaded on the official website at csirnet.nta.ac.in by entering the application number and birthdate. The CSIR UGC NET is a test that determines eligibility for Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) grants and lectureships. The life sciences exams will be held on June 25, chemical science, earth, atmospheric, ocean, planetary sciences, and physical sciences exams will be conducted on June 26, and mathematical sciences on June 27. All the tests will be held in two shifts — 9 am to noon and 3 pm to 6 pm. CSIR UGC NET June 2024 exam city slip: How to download Step 1: Visit csirnet.nta.ac.in, the official website for the CSIR UGC NET. Step 2: Go to the ‘Joint CSIR UGC NET 2024 exam city slip’ link and click on it. Step 3: Applicants will be sent to a different page. Step 4: Input your CSIR UGC NET 2024 application number, date of birth, and security pin here. Step 5: Click Submit. Your exam city slip will be shown on the screen. Step 6: Download and print a copy of the CSIR UGC NET June 2024 exam city slip. The test will be administered online. Each CSIR UGC NET June 2024 paper will be worth 200 marks. Stay ahead with all the exam results updates on News18 Website.

author: Deutsche Welle
title: Russian forces end prison siege, kill IS hostage-takers
mainText: Russia's special forces killed several men linked to the so-called "Islamic State" (IS) group who took two guards hostage at a detention center in the southern city of Rostov, Russia's Federal Penitentiary Service said Sunday. "The criminals were eliminated," Russia's Federal Penitentiary Service said in a statement, describing how a "special operation" had taken place to free the hostages. "The employees who were being held hostage were released. They are uninjured," the statement continued. The siege took place Sunday at Detention Center 1 of the Rostov region, the prison service said. The Interfax news agency said there were six hostage-takers. The men were said to have been armed with knives and other sharpened objects. Men had demanded vehicle and freedom The hostage-takers were allegedly able to remove the bars from their windows and enter a guard room, according to a Telegram channel cited by Reuters news agency. The Interfax news agency reported that the prisoners had demanded a car and free passage. Before the siege was quashed, one of the hostage-takers was shown on social media waving a knife next to one of the hostages. The hostage-taker wore a headband with the flag used by the IS. Russia has been targeted by IS in the past. In March, the jihadist organization claimed responsibility for an attack at a concert hall near the capital Moscow, in which 144 people died. State news agency TASS cited a police source as saying that some of the hostage-takers were due to appear in court on terrorism charges, while others were already convicted. Russian media speculated that they could be among those convicted of plotting an attack on the Supreme Court of Karachay-Cherkessia, a Muslim-majority Russian republic in the Caucasus. mm, dvv/ab (AFP, Reuters)

author: Sumaila Zaman
title: UGC NET 2024 Exam on June 18; Check Last-Minute Preparation Tips, Dress Code, Do’s And Don’t

author: Deepto Banerjee
title: TS Inter Supply Result 2024 declared: Direct link to check TS Inter IPASE 1st, 2nd year results
mainText: TS Inter Supply Result 2024: The Telangana Board of Intermediate Education (TGBIE) has announced the TS Intermediate Public Advanced Supplementary Exams (Inter IPASE) results for 2024. The TS supplementary exams for both TS Inter 1st year and 2nd year classes were conducted by TGBIE from May 24 to June 3. title: Job Alert: From UPSSSC To BSF, List Of Govt Jobs To Apply For This Week

author: Josh Halliday
title: Gordon Ramsay ‘lucky to be here’ after US bike crash
mainText: Gordon Ramsay has said he is lucky to be alive after a “really bad” cycling accident in the US. The celebrity chef said wearing a helmet saved his life after the collision in Connecticut. In an Instagram video, he showed a huge purple bruise that appeared to cover a significant portion of his torso and shared photos of a crushed helmet and torn clothing. Ramsay, 57, said: “Hey guys, it’s Gordon. I’d like to share a very important message with you all. You know how much I love cycling and triathlons and Ironman [races] etc and this week, unfortunately, I had a really bad accident and it really shook me and honestly I’m lucky to be here. “Those incredible trauma surgeons, doctors, nurses in the hospitals looked after me this week, they were amazing but honestly, you’ve got to wear helmets. “I don’t care how short the journey is. I don’t care … these helmets cost money, but they’re crucial, even with a kid’s short journey, they’ve got to wear a helmet. “Now, I’m lucky to be standing here. I’m in pain. It’s been a brutal week. And I’m sort of getting through it.” Ramsay’s hands could be seen shaking during the short video, posted on Saturday to his 17 million Instagram followers. Alongside the post, he wrote that he was “doing OK and did not break any bones or suffer any major injuries but I am a bit bruised up looking like a purple potato”. He added that he had been treated at Lawrence + Memorial hospital in New London, Connecticut, and that the helmet had saved his life. Ramsay, originally from Johnstone, near Glasgow in Scotland, has become one of the world’s most recognisable chefs after finding fame on British television 20 years ago. He owns a series of restaurants in the UK and US and is starring in the latest series of US show, Next Level Chef.

author: Geraint Llewellyn
title: Brooklyn Beckham and wife Nicola Peltz left 'heartbroken' and claim 'life couldn't get any worse'...
mainText: Brooklyn Beckham and wife Nicola Peltz shared the tragic and 'unexpected' death of their pet chihuahua Nala on Instagram. Nicola expressed deep grief over losing Nala, who struggled to breathe and passed away after being rushed to the vet. She described the loss as the hardest month of her life, mourned Nala's companionship over nine years, and hoped to reunite with her late grandmother. Brooklyn also memorialized Nala as being taken too soon and dearly missed. The couple, known for their love of animals, recently lost another dog named Bear and honored Nicola's late grandmother Bunny in a touching tribute last month. Bunny, who passed away at 95, was celebrated for her joyful spirit and positive impact on their lives. Brooklyn expressed gratitude for Bunny's influence and promised to take care of Nicola and her family. Bradley Peltz, Nicola's brother, also paid tribute to Bunny, describing her as an angel on earth with a big heart and a bright smile. The Peltz family, including billionaire Nelson Peltz, mourned Bunny's passing and remembered her lovingly. The couple, who had a lavish wedding in 2022, shared their deep sorrow over Nala's sudden departure, emphasizing her importance in their lives. The loss of Nala comes as another blow following the recent death of Bunny, adding to the emotional challenges faced by Brooklyn and Nicola.

author: Lapresse
title: Sean 'Diddy' Combs gives up much-loved gift over continued pressure after Cassie attack video
mainText: Sean " Diddy " Combs has returned his key to New York City after a request from Mayor Eric Adams in response to the release of a video showing the music mogul attacking R&B singer Cassie, officials said Saturday. The mayor's office said Combs returned the key after Adams sent letters to the embattled musician's offices in New York and California on June 4 rescinding the key and asking for it to be sent back to City Hall. The city received the key June 10. In his letter, Adams wrote he was "deeply disturbed" by the attack, adding "I strongly condemn these actions and stand in solidarity with all survivors of domestic and gender-based violence." Combs' career has been derailed by numerous accusations of sexual abuse, as well as a federal criminal sex-trafficking investigation that led to raids of Combs' mansions in Los Angeles and Miami. In May, CNN aired security video of Combs attacking Cassie in a hotel hallway in Los Angeles in 2016. Combs has said he is "truly sorry" for the attack on Cassie and called his actions "inexcusable." Cassie, whose legal name is Cassandra Ventura, sued Combs last year, setting off a wave of increased scrutiny on Combs. That case was settled a day after it was filed. Adams awarded Combs with the key at a ceremony last year that coincided with the release of a new album. Howard University this month rescinded an honorary degree awarded to Combs and ended a scholarship program in his name following the release of the video involving Cassie. Combs, founder of Bad Boy Records, is one of the most influential hip-hop producers and executives in the last three decades, turning musical success into a business empire. An email sent to a representative listed online for Combs was not immediately returned.

author: Kate Kulniece
title: I juggle two full-time jobs working from 9am to 10pm… trolls say I’ll have no life but I’ll be able to reti...
mainText: Jane, a 24-year-old Canadian, is working two full-time remote jobs - as a marketing specialist and a customer service representative - for a total of 73 hours a week. Her combined income from both roles is $120,000 a year, which she is saving to retire early in her 30s. She works from 9am to 5pm in marketing and then from 5pm to 9pm in customer service, with an hour-long lunch break in between. Jane hopes to achieve financial independence retire early (FIRE) by living frugally and maximizing her income. Despite facing criticism about sacrificing her youth for early retirement, Jane is determined to reach her goal and live a life of financial freedom.

author: Ryan-Fahey
title: UK weather: Exact date maps turn red as North African plume brings 29C scorcher
mainText: The UK is set to experience its first 29C heatwave of the year as a North African plume is expected to bring hot weather to the country. Despite a cold start to summer, weather maps indicate a rise in temperatures, with the heatwave forecasted to peak on June 29. Southern England, including parts of Sussex, Kent, and Essex, could see temperatures reaching 29C, while other areas like Greater London, Birmingham, Manchester, and Newcastle are expected to experience highs ranging from 22C to 28C. Wales is likely to see temperatures around 25C during this period. However, forecasters caution that this heatwave is not guaranteed, as it depends on various weather patterns, including jet streams and high-pressure systems. The Met Office's long-range forecast suggests that temperatures are expected to rise overall, with some unsettled weather likely in the north and west of the country. While there are no explicit predictions of a heatwave beyond June 29, temperatures nationwide are expected to be close to or slightly above average. The exact duration and intensity of the heatwave remain uncertain, with weather conditions potentially changing as the month progresses.

author: The Associated Press
title: Wildfire burning north of Los Angeles spreads as evacuation orders issued
mainText: GORMAN, Calif. — Strong winds pushed flames through dry brush in mountains along Interstate 5 north of Los Angeles on Sunday, and officials warned residents in the wildfire’s path to be prepared to leave if it explodes in size again. Los Angeles County’s first major wildfire of the year swiftly grew to more than 16 square miles, one day after it forced the evacuation of at least 1,200 campers, off-roaders and hikers from the Hungry Valley recreation area. The blaze, dubbed the Post Fire, was just 2% contained. No injuries were reported. The cause was under investigation. Firefighters working in sweltering conditions and steep terrain raced to douse spot fires that erupted as unpredictable winds blew embers ahead of the flames, said Kenichi Haskett, a section chief for the LA County Fire Department. The gusts also hampered efforts by aircraft crews to drop water and fire retardant, he said. The fire erupted Saturday afternoon near I-5 in Gorman, about 60 miles northwest of Los Angeles. Two structures burned within the evacuated recreation area. Flames were moving toward Pyramid Lake, a popular destination for boaters that was closed for Father’s Day. No houses were threatened Sunday, but officials warned residents of Castaic, home to about 19,000 people, that they should prepare to leave if the fire pushes further south. “If you’re in a warning area, be prepared with a ‘go bag,’ with overnight clothes and your cellphone, your medicines, your glasses. Have your car fueled up,” said Haskett. “Be ready to evacuate.” Low humidity and gusts around 50 mph were expected throughout the day, and winds could pick up speed after sundown, warned the National Weather Service office for Los Angeles. About 75 miles to the east, the 2-square-mile (5-square-kilometer) Hesperia Fire forced road closures and prompted evacuation warnings after it broke out Saturday near mountain communities in San Bernardino County. The blaze was 7% contained Sunday.

author: Lottie Limb
title: ‘The time of the whole car city is over’: How is Paris encouraging walking and cycling?
mainText: Paris is making strides to promote walking and cycling as part of its efforts to tackle pollution and reimagine the city for pedestrians and cyclists. Initiatives include expanding bicycle lanes, pedestrianising streets and squares, cracking down on polluting vehicles like SUVs, creating urban forests, and moving towards a 15-minute city concept where everything people need is within walking or cycling distance. The city is investing in green spaces, promoting car-free days, and prioritizing eco-friendly transportation options like cycling and public transport. These changes align with Paris Mayor Anne Hidalgo's vision for a more sustainable and people-friendly urban environment, especially as the city prepares to host the Olympics. The focus is on showcasing a new way of living in the city by 2040 under the challenges of climate change and promoting a greener, more sustainable urban landscape for residents and visitors.

author: Elizabeth Beattie
title: Japan’s gamified environment apps target a greener mindset
mainText: When we think of making a positive contribution to the environment, we might not immediately think of our phones, but as gamification creeps into our daily activities, researchers and developers are examining the potential for apps that spur greener behavior.Gamification, which sees game-like elements and principles applied to other contexts with the aim of boosting user engagement, has manifested itself in productivity apps, exercise trackers and language-learning tools. When you earn a digital badge, “streak” or other little emblems of progress, that is gamification in action — a proven motivator for shifting behavior.Gamification deployed for an environmental outcome is not new — it has long been used as a tool by educators and as a way to gather scientific data — but it has gained extra momentum in Japan in recent years.

author: Jessica Green
title: Wilkommen, WAGs! The glamorous support squad cheering on England ahead of their first Euros match in...
mainText: Wilkommen, WAGs!
