The Corstorphine Road premises, whose impressive façade has been restored by specialist stonemasons, also boasts LED technology which showcases the brand’s new global identity, as well as an energy-efficient heating, cooling and ventilation system. Roddy McAllister, General Manager of Rolls-Royce Motor Cars Edinburgh, said: “The official inauguration of our state-of-the-art new showroom in Edinburgh was a fabulous occasion completely befitting of the opulent setting. This is a stunning facility where luxury meets innovation, and it was a real pleasure to welcome guests inside the refurbished facility so they could appreciate the elegant design which perfectly captures the essence of the Rolls-Royce brand. “Our new Edinburgh dealership features a wealth of innovative new technologies which will provide guests with a truly immersive experience and help to reaffirm Rolls-Royce’s position at the pinnacle of the ultra-luxury car market.” For more information about Rolls-Royce Motor Cars Edinburgh, visit https://www.rolls-roycemotorcars.com/edinburgh. Further details about Grange can be seen at www.grange.co.uk.

author: Allen Farmelo
title: Pre-Owned Rolex Prices Just Keep Falling—Here Are the Best Deals Right Now
mainText: With Watches and Wonders and the spring auction season concluded, the watch market is stable in 2024, especially for pre-owned Rolex watches. Prices are down and supply is up, making it a buyer's market. The article advises that the market trends for individual watch brands, models, and references can vary. Vintage, neo-vintage, and recent-model pre-owned Rolex sports watches are currently good deals. Certain models like the Rolex Submariner, GMT-Master, Explorer II, and Oyster Perpetual 41 are available for lower prices than before. Factors such as the condition of the watch and specific references can impact the pricing. The article mentions specific Rolex models and their price changes. For instance, the Rolex Submariner reference 16610 is down by -3.84 percent over three months, offering opportunities for buyers. The article also discusses the fluctuations in prices for GMT-Master II models and the Explorer II. The Rolex Oyster Perpetual 41 has seen a significant decrease in price, while the Datejust 36 reference 126234 has gone up. The article highlights that it is currently a good time to buy Rolex watches, with some exceptions such as steel Daytonas remaining expensive. It advises buyers to do thorough research and consider factors like the watch's condition and market trends. Overall, it is a favorable buyer's market for Rolex watches with deals available on specific models.

author: Jessica Lindsay
title: 'Lovely part of the world' is most affordable UK area to buy a home
mainText: Property prices in the UK have reached record highs in 2024, with sales up by 6% year-on-year and demand from buyers up 5%. Yet despite the average British home now selling for an eye-watering £375,110, new research shows there are still a few enclaves around the country where you can bag a bargain. Angus ranked in first place as the most affordable area, with an average house price of £164,076 and other attractive features. Angus is a region in the East of Scotland known for its natural beauty, history, and access to cities like Dundee and Edinburgh. Residents praise the area for its quality of life and peaceful surroundings. Various activities such as exploring nature, visiting historical sites like Glamis Castle, and indulging in local delicacies make living in Angus a delightful experience. For those considering a home purchase in the UK, Angus presents an appealing option with its affordability and charm.

author: Cory King
title: From the Chamber: June 10 x 100 – primaries, parties and partnerships
mainText: In this article, the author, Cory King, provides updates on various topics in brief segments of 100 words or less each. He discusses the conclusion of primary races in Maine and encourages readers to reach out to candidates directly for information. King also mentions the abundance of community events and cautions drivers to be aware of non-vehicular activities. He announces the grand opening of the Midcoast Athletic and Recreation Complex and a partnership with the Yarmouth Chamber of Commerce. Additionally, he mentions upcoming business surveys, explains the significance of Juneteenth, promotes a Lean workshop, a social hour event for women in leadership, and previews the upcoming Heritage Days in Bath. King also anticipates the launch of a new website for the Bath-Brunswick Regional Chamber of Commerce.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Fire at former Beaufort nightclub stalls traffic
mainText: BEAUFORT — A fire at a shuttered Beaufort nightclub stalled traffic into this Lowcountry town. The structure — north of Marine Corps Air Station Beaufort and near the Highway 21 Drive-In movie theater — was the former location of a nightclub known as Angel, and it has burned almost completely to the ground. There were indications that people experiencing homelessness had been staying in and around the building, Daniel Byrne, assistant chief of the Burton Fire District, told The Post and Courier. No injuries were reported. Officials were first notified of the blaze at around 3 a.m. on June 17, Beaufort County Sheriff's Office spokesperson Sgt. Danny Allen told The Post and Courier. All lanes on Trask Parkway traveling into Beaufort were closed as of 4:30 a.m., according to a Sheriff's Office Facebook post. By 9:55 a.m., one lane on the road toward Beaufort was opened. Sheriff's deputies and the South Carolina Highway Patrol redirected traffic at the scene. As of 11:45 a.m., all lanes were open again. Fire departments representing Burton, Beaufort-Port Royal and Marine Corps Air Station addressed the blaze. Beaufort County Emergency Medical Services also responded. Officials are trying to track down the property owner, Byrne said. The property is owned by Heavenly LLC, which lists Antoine Iskandar as its registered agent. Iskandar founded a Bluffton-based custom homebuilding company called Arkiteknic Custom Homes. Officials believe the building was being used for storage. The origin of the fire is under investigation.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Manipur Unrest: Centre To Talk To Meiteis, Kukis in Manipur to Bridge Ethnic Divide
mainText: Amid the unrest in Manipur, Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced that the Ministry of Home Affairs will engage in talks with both the Meitei and Kuki communities to address the ethnic divide in the state. Shah emphasized the need for increased central forces deployment if necessary to strategically restore peace in Manipur, directing strict legal action against perpetrators of violence. The focus is on preventing further incidents of violence and promoting reconciliation between the Meiteis and Kukis. Additionally, ensuring healthcare, education, and rehabilitation for the displaced population is a priority. Shah highlighted the central government's commitment under Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership to uphold the safety and security of all northeastern state citizens. Ethnic clashes, triggered by a tribal rally protesting the Meitei community's ST status demand in 2023, have led to over 220 casualties. Recently, fresh incidents of violence have been reported in Imphal and Jiribam, prompting a detailed security review by Shah following a meeting with Manipur's Governor Anusuiya Uikey. The government aims to prevent further spread of violence, particularly in areas like Jiribam that have been relatively peaceful. In a high-level meeting attended by top security officials, including Manipur's Security Advisor and DGP, Shah assessed the situation to address the ongoing ethnic conflict. Key officials from the central government, including the Union Home Secretary and the Army Chief, emphasized the need for a coordinated approach. This review follows a similar assessment conducted by Shah on the situation in Jammu and Kashmir. Manipur's population includes the Meiteis, who constitute 53% and predominantly reside in Imphal Valley, and tribals such as Nagas and Kukis, making up 40% and primarily residing in hill districts. Efforts are underway to mitigate the ethnic tensions in Manipur and ensure the safety and well-being of all communities.

author: Adrian Marlow, Oliver Haslam, Amber Guetebier
title: Snap Up a Dollar Flight Club Premium Plus Lifetime Membership for Only $70
mainText: If your travel bucket list is long but your budget is small, you're likely on the lookout for any travel deal you can find. Thankfully, some services can help you save money on travel, like the Dollar Flight Club, which automatically alerts you to the best airfare deals for you at your preferred airports. Currently, you can get a Premium Plus membership for just $70 on StackSocial. That's a dramatic $437 savings, but the deal won't stick around forever. The Dollar Flight Club Premium Plus plan gives you access to savings on flights in business, premium economy, and economy seating. It includes both domestic and international deals. Once you sign up and add your home airports (choose up to four departing airports) you'll get instant alerts via email and can book whenever and wherever using the web or the app, which is available for iOS and Android devices. If high flight prices have been stopping you from booking the vacation of your dreams, now's the time to invest in a service that can help you find the best discounts, curated and delivered directly to you. StackSocial is also offering a lifetime Dollar Flight Club Premium subscription for just $40, which is a pared-down version that has access to around 70% of the deals and you can set a start and departure point.

author: Lori-Suzanne Dell
title: American Red Cross volunteers recognized at annual awards
mainText: The annual meeting and volunteer recognition awards of the Mid Coast Maine Chapter of the American Red Cross took place on May 13 at the Topsham Chapter house on Community Way. The event included a meeting of the Board of Directors, dinner and networking and a volunteer awards ceremony. Among the numerous awards of the evening, husband and wife disaster services team volunteers Paul and Loraine Duclos were the recipients of the Clara Barton Award 'for going above and beyond.' The award, named for Red Cross founder Clara Barton, is given annually to 'an individual, group of individuals, or corporation which exemplifies Barton's humanitarian spirit.' Clara Barton founded the American Red Cross Organization in 1881. According to Central and Mid Coast Maine Executive Director Sophie Piconi, the American Red Cross, whose mission is to prevent and alleviate human suffering, 'needs more volunteers.' Since July 2023, the Topsham branch has helped 626 families displaced by fire, held over 4,300 blood drives, served nearly 2,800 military families and educated over 35,000 people in first aid, CPR and water safety. The Topsham branch volunteers logged in nearly 125,000 hours in the last year and were pivotal in providing services and support to law enforcement, first responders and victims of the mass shooting in Lewiston on Oct. 25, 2023, and in responding to aid the numerous victims of flood this past winter as well as in deploying to many out-of-state disasters. If you would like to volunteer, you can call Piconi at (207) 729-6779.

author: Richard Wheeler
title: What does Nigel Farage hope to achieve with Reform’s election pledges?
mainText: Nigel Farage has launched Reform UK’s election promises in Merthyr Tydfil, South Wales, as his party looks to continue its strong showing in the opinion polls ahead of the July 4 General Election. Reform UK’s document was titled Our Contract With You because leader Mr Farage said the word “manifesto” had become associated with “lies” told by the main Westminster parties. The party was formed in 2021 as a relaunch of Mr Farage’s previous Brexit Party and this is their first general election.

author: Anna Mock
title: FACT CHECK: Did John Kerry’s Daughter Say Billions Must Die For ‘New World Order’?
mainText: A post shared on Facebook claims Vanessa Kerry, daughter of former U.S. climate envoy John Kerry, said billions of humans must die for the “New World Order.” Verdict: False There is no evidence Kerry said this. It originates from a site that is a regular source of misinformation and has been debunked by Check Your Fact several times in the past. Fact Check: Some studies have suggested that climate change may be causing more turbulence on airplanes, according to Washington Post. In spite of this, airlines are getting better at anticipating rough skies, meaning there may not be much change in the overall rate of turbulence, the outlet reported. A Facebook post suggests Kerry has said people must die for the “New World Order.” The claim is baseless, however. There are no credible news reports to suggest Kerry said this. Check Your Fact has debunked claims originating from this site multiple times previously. Check Your Fact reached out to a Kerry spokesperson for comment and will update this piece accordingly if one is received.

author: Thomas Coughlan
title: Granny flats will be easier to build following promised plan changes; Chris Bishop ponders whether house price falls would be a bad thing
mainText: The Government plans to make it easier to build 'granny flats' by allowing small dwellings of 60 square metres or less without the need for resource consent in rural and residential zones. This initiative stems from a coalition agreement between NZ First and National. Acting Prime Minister Winston Peters announced the consultation to fulfill this promise, emphasizing the affordability and flexibility of granny flats for various households. The proposal involves implementing a National Environmental Standard to permit granny flats without resource consent, along with adding a schedule to the Building Act for standalone houses up to 60sq m. This move aims to reduce regulatory red tape, save on building costs, and ensure quality and safety standards. Housing Minister Chris Bishop supports the changes, stating that falling house prices could benefit prospective buyers by increasing affordability in the market. Bishop's openness to the idea of price drops sets a unique tone compared to past housing strategies. The consultation process includes considerations for setbacks, building criteria, and licensed building practitioners. The Government aims to finalize these changes by mid-2025 to address housing affordability and offer more housing options for New Zealanders.

author: Mon Jun
title: The Irish Times view on the EU after the European Parliament elections: holding the centre ground
mainText: Bargaining over coalitions, positions and policies in the European Union will proceed apace now that the European Parliament election results are in. While there has been an overall shift to the right, the picture is uneven. It is most pronounced in Germany, France and Italy, three large states which deeply affect EU policy-making. Yet a centrist coalition still remains available between a stronger conservative group, working with weakened liberals, social democrats and Greens. That would be lost if the conservative group instead reaches out to stronger hard right parties. This strategic decision depends mainly on Ursula von der Leyen, leader of the conservative European People’s Party and outgoing president of the European Commission. Her group has increased its seats and she has offered a new pact with the social democrats and liberals. Their seat losses mean the Greens would be needed as a fourth partner to make up the parliamentary numbers required. That is difficult for von der Leyen because she backtracked on the EU’s compromise Green Deal in the campaign.

author: Azaria Howell
title: Public sector cuts: More than $8 million spent on one government ministry’s redundancy plans
mainText: One government ministry has spent over $8 million on redundancy payments due to cuts in the public sector. Several agencies in New Zealand are working towards cost-saving targets set by Budget 2024. The Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment (MBIE) spent $8,075,996.86 on staff redundancies. The New Zealand Customs Service has costs totaling $2,696,571.81 from disestablishing positions. Customs Minister Casey Costello emphasized efficiency and managing cost pressures for sustained fiscal health. MBIE has reduced positions by 346.4 roles, with further savings targeted. The Ministry for the Environment (MoE) estimates $1,540,000 for 45 redundancies. MoE is undergoing restructuring with a significant reduction in staffing numbers. Labour's spokesperson raised concerns about the impact of cuts on public service jobs, while the Taxpayers' Union sees the redundancies as necessary for overall savings. Public Service Association highlighted the emotional toll on affected individuals. The article highlights the financial, social, and environmental implications of the public sector cuts on New Zealanders, with various perspectives on the consequences of the restructuring efforts.

author: Talon Homer
title: Using Synthetic Division to Save Time in Calculus and Algebra
mainText: 1. Find the Degree of the Polynomial The degree of a polynomial is equal to the greatest power present in the function. For instance, if 2x3 is the largest power number present in the function, then that polynomial will be considered to have a degree of three. This value is important because it tells you how many times the polynomial will have to be divided to be completely factored out. 2. Sort by Leading Coefficient The leading coefficient of a polynomial is the variable of the function attached to the highest power. To perform synthetic division, you first must sort the polynomial by highest coefficients in descending order. For any coefficient that doesn't have a corresponding power, insert a zero value. This will be helpful for later steps. As an example, the polynomial x2 + 6 + 3x4 + 8x becomes 3x4 + 0x3 + x2 + 8x + 6 when sorted by leading coefficient. Now, we our going to take our sorted polynomial and divide it by the linear factor x + 1 using synthetic division. 3. Performing Synthetic Division The result will give you the quotient and the remainder of the division. The degree of the quotient polynomial will be one less than the degree of the original polynomial — and just like that, we've performed polynomial division. After we use synthetic division to factor the polynomial 3x4 + x2 + 8x + 6 divided by (x + 1), our final answer is a lower degree polynomial of 3x3 – 3x2 + 4x + 4 and a remainder of 2 divided by (x + 1). The result probably looks similar to what you would expect using the long division method, but hopefully you find this new method to keep the data much more organized.

author: K. W. Wesselink-Schram
title: Scientists use NMR spectroscopy to map polyelectrolyte distribution and solve a century-old chemistry riddle
mainText: When two solutions of oppositely charged polymers (polyelectrolytes) are mixed, phase separation occurs and leads to the formation of a polymer-rich phase and a supernatant phase. The precise distribution of all components, that is polyelectrolytes and counterions, had not yet been determined. Researchers at the University of Twente can now measure quantitatively exactly where these components are distributed using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy. For more than 90 years, chemists have been fascinated by polyelectrolyte complexes that form after solutions of two oppositely charged polymers are mixed. A better understanding of these complexes is crucial for the development of materials based on these complexes. New method To improve the applicability of these materials, scientists have developed a method to achieve a better understanding of the complexes. UT Ph.D. student and first author of the paper Giulia Allegri explains, "We introduced a new method based on NMR spectroscopy. It allows us to fully quantify the composition of the system, and measure how all the components are distributed after complexation occurs." This study marks the first time that all components have been quantitatively determined in both phases. Furthermore, NMR spectroscopy brings more advantages. "The protocol we developed is very fast; we can do a full analysis in less than 40 minutes," says co-author Ricardo Martinho. Allegri adds that this method is label-free and non-invasive. She says, "Polyelectrolyte complexes are very common in nature. We envision that our methodology will contribute to a better understanding of both natural polyelectrolyte complexes and will help to improve polyelectrolyte complex materials." Allegri is a Ph.D. student in the Molecular Nanofabrication research group (Faculty of S&T) supervised by Dr. Saskia Lindhoud. Dr. Martinho is a researcher at the Biomolecular Nanotechnology research group (Faculty of S&T). Together with Prof. Dr. Jurriaan Huskens, they published their findings in an article titled "Distribution of polyelectrolytes and counterions upon polyelectrolyte complexation," in the Journal of Colloid and Interface Science.

author: Yu Tao
title: Charming ambassadors with big appetites and universal appeal: China's long history of 'panda diplomacy'
mainText: During his visit to the Adelaide Zoo, Chinese Premier Li Qiang announced the gifting of two pandas to Australia, continuing China's long history of panda diplomacy. This practice began in the 1950s as a way to strengthen diplomatic ties and foster goodwill. While initially focused on socialist allies, panda diplomacy evolved to include Western nations under Deng Xiaoping. The current leader, Xi Jinping, has continued this tradition to enhance bilateral relations. Pandas symbolize peace and friendship due to their gentle nature and universal appeal. However, breeding pandas in captivity is challenging, and their care can be financially demanding for host countries. Despite their charm, the success of panda diplomacy in Australia remains uncertain amidst broader geopolitical tensions and public skepticism towards China. While panda diplomacy can improve perceptions, long-term relationship success requires tangible policy changes and mutual trust beyond symbolic gestures.

author: Fernando Lessa
title: Restoring climate-resilient kelp forests
mainText: Kelp forests play a crucial role in supporting coastal biodiversity and mitigating climate change effects. However, these ecosystems are under threat due to ocean warming and over-grazing by sea urchins. A team of researchers led by Julia Baum and Sean Rogers from the University of Victoria is working on regrowing kelp forests in collaboration with British Columbia coastal First Nations. The project aims to develop a roadmap for kelp forest recovery and establish large-scale reforestation techniques. The team, supported by a $3.68 million grant from Fisheries and Oceans Canada, is currently in the second year of a four-year project. They are growing and testing different kelp species in nurseries at Bamfield and studying their growth, tolerance, and resilience in various conditions. The project involves partnerships with multiple organizations and First Nations, emphasizing the importance of community involvement and awareness. The research aligns with UN Sustainable Development Goals and aims to future-proof kelp forests by developing resilient reforestation methods. While the project's ultimate goal is reforestation, it also aims to advance scientific knowledge and create a framework for kelp recovery. The urgency of the issue and collaboration between UVic and Bamfield drive the project's ambition and commitment to large goals. By integrating scientific research with fieldwork, the team hopes to pioneer methods that will ensure the long-term survival of kelp forests amidst environmental challenges. Overall, the project represents a significant effort to address the threats facing kelp forests and highlight the importance of these ecosystems in climate action and marine conservation.

author: Tom Cary
title: Golf’s biggest major chokes and where Rory McIlroy’s US Open meltdown ranks
mainText: Rory McIlroy’s collapse at the US Open evoked memories of famous golf meltdowns like Adam Scott at the 2012 Open, Jason Dufner at the 2011 PGA Championship, Ed Sneed at the 1979 Masters, Dustin Johnson at the 2010 US Open, Sam Snead at the 1947 US Open, Greg Norman at the 1996 Masters, and Jean van de Velde at the 1999 Open Championship. Despite McIlroy outscoring DeChambeau on the final day, his collapse from the lead was deemed one of the worst. Norman's 1996 Masters collapse, where he blew a six-shot lead to Nick Faldo, also ranks high. Van de Velde's collapse at the 1999 Open Championship, famously ending up in the Barry Burn, is remembered as one of the most spectacular in golf history.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Bangladesh successfully defends lowest total in T20 World Cup history
mainText: Bangladesh scripted history on Monday by successfully defending the lowest total ever in T20 World Cup tournaments. The Bangla Tigers achieved this milestone during their T20 World Cup 2024 Group D clash against Nepal at the Arnos Vale Ground in Kingstown. In a low-scoring encounter, Bangladesh defended a modest total of 107 runs by dismissing Nepal for just 85 runs in 19.2 overs. This feat surpassed South Africa's record in T20 World Cup 2024, where they defended 114 runs against Bangladesh, securing victory by a narrow margin in New York. This achievement also marks the third-lowest total successfully defended by Test-playing nations in T20Is. Previously, West Indies defended 97 runs against Ireland in Kingston in 2014, and Zimbabwe defended 106 runs against West Indies in Port of Spain in 2010. Opting to bowl first after winning the toss, Nepal's bowlers, led by skipper Rohit Paudel (2/20), Sandeep Lamichhane (2/17), Dipendra Singh (2/22), and Sompal Kami (2/10), restricted Bangladesh's batsmen. All-rounder Shakib al Hasan top-scored with 17 runs as Bangladesh were bundled out for 106 runs in 19.3 overs. In response, Nepal struggled with wickets falling at regular intervals despite efforts from Kushal Malla (27 off 40 balls) and Dipendra Singh Airee (25 off 31 balls). The duo managed a 52-run partnership for the sixth wicket, but Nepal fell short, finishing at 85 runs in 19.2 overs. Bangladesh's bowlers Tanzim Hasan Sakib (4/7) and Taskin Ahmed (3/7) spearheaded the defense, dismantling Nepal's batting lineup. Tanzim Hasan Sakib was awarded the Player of the Match for his stellar bowling performance. With this victory, Bangladesh secured the final Super Eight berth from Group D, finishing second with three wins and one loss, accumulating six points. In contrast, Nepal ended at the bottom of the points table with zero wins, three losses, one no-result, and one point. (With agency inputs)

author: Josh Erickson
title: Veteran goaltender expected to retire, join Blues front office
mainText: Veteran NHL goaltender Brian Elliott is expected to retire and join the St. Louis Blues' front office. Elliott began his NHL career with the Ottawa Senators in 2007-08 and later had successful stints with the St. Louis Blues, Calgary Flames, Philadelphia Flyers, and Tampa Bay Lightning. Known for his strong play and consistency, Elliott made a significant impact during his time with the Blues, including winning the Jennings Trophy for best team goals-against average. He also helped lead the team to multiple playoff appearances, including a run to the Western Conference Final in 2016. After his playing career, Elliott is set to transition to a role in the Blues' front office, where his experience and hockey knowledge will be valuable. At 39 years old, Elliott concludes his career with impressive statistics, including a 279-167-54 record, 45 shutouts, a 2.57 goals-against average, and a .909 save percentage in 543 regular-season games, along with a 17-26 record and .904 save percentage in 48 playoff games.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese get a brutal reality check about their WNBA rivalry
mainText: Another showdown between Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese ended with a victory for Clark's team -- and controversy centered on Reese. Dating to their college days, Clark has won the past three meetings with Reese after the Indiana Fever defeated the Chicago Sky on Sunday. But the game was controversial for a flagrant foul Reese committed on Clark in the third quarter, a swipe for the ball that went awry. While both players have dismissed the incident as a "basketball play," others have not been swayed -- and one analyst has even questioned the nature of their rivalry. Andraya Carter discusses the Clark-Reese "mid-off" ESPN's Andraya Carter on Monday said that as fun as it has been watching these two rookies square off and establish themselves in the WNBA, the fact of the matter is that airtime could be devoted to some of the league's elite teams and players -- a level that neither Clark nor Reese will reach as rookies. The Fever (5-10) and the Sky (4-9) are in a virtual tie for the final playoff spot in the W, with more than half the season still to play. While making the postseason in year one would be a tremendous learning opportunity for Clark and/or Reese, their teams are far from the league's top tier -- which includes the Connecticut Sun, the New York Liberty, and the two-time defending champion Las Vegas Aces. However, the media coverage devoted to Clark and Reese's every move is outweighing that afforded to players like Brittney Griner, A'ja Wilson, Sabrina Ionescu, and others. Carter is trying to draw attention away from the pair of influential rookies and back toward the league as a whole -- where there are plenty of intriguing storylines.

author: Jacco van Loon
title: Nations realise they need to take risks or lose the race to the Moon
mainText: The Nasa-led Artemis-3 mission aims to establish a permanent human presence on the Moon and create an economy based around it. This mission, scheduled for no sooner than September 2026, faces delays and technical challenges. The current lunar endeavor is seen as financially rewarding and essential for reducing the costs of space exploration by extracting water ice from the lunar south pole. The space industry is focused on the Moon due to its economic potential. Private companies like SpaceX and Blue Origin play key roles in the Artemis program, providing innovative solutions and cost-effective services. Recent attempts by various nations and companies to land on the Moon have shown the fine line between success and failure. China's space program is rapidly catching up, with plans to place boots on the Moon by 2030 and build an International Lunar Research Station. The US Department of Defense is also involved in lunar development projects. Ethical questions arise regarding activities like mining the Moon and ownership of lunar resources. International agreements like the UN Outer Space Treaty and the US Artemis Accords aim to regulate space activities. The evolution of lunar bases, resource utilization, and economic activities on the Moon will likely lead to two operational lunar bases by the mid-2030s, fostering international cooperation and economic prosperity. This lunar race offers opportunities for technological innovation, peaceful cooperation, and inspiration for future generations in the journey towards Mars.

author: William Gallagher
title: iOS 18 dramatically accelerates iPhone 15 Pro Max neural processing
mainText: Geekbench results comparing iPhone 15 Pro Max Machine Learning performance in iOS 17 versus iOS 18 are showing that there is a significant speed increase, even in beta. The iPhone 15 Pro Max hardware was already a considerable speed improvement over its predecessor, according to general Geekbench 6 figures. Now, however, the first results of the iPhone 15 Pro Max using iOS 18 and specifically its Neural Processing Unit, have shown that the device can be even faster. As first singled out in a thread on X/Twitter, the figures are surprisingly high. But they appear to be borne out by a series of results on Geekbench's site. After the iOS 18 update, Geekbench machine learning score has greatly improved(CoreML / Neural Engine Backend) So using iOS 17.5.1 -- and again, specifically for neural engine processing -- the iPhone 15 Pro Max earned a Geekbench score of 6249. Seemingly the same device updated to iOS 18, earned a score of 7816 on the same test. Scores and specifications don't tend to translate easily into universal real-world scenarios. That's especially true when the scores are solely for the Machine Learning element. But it still demonstrates that iOS 18 is optimizing the iPhone's neural engine cores more than iOS 17 did. The same source says that the results are even more dramatic over Geekbench's various text classification tests. There updating to iOS 18 improved one result over by 1,000%. AppleInsider still recommends that no one update to iOS 18, unless they have a business need, or they have a spare iPhone.

author: Mark Travers
title: 3 Ways To Respond To Passive-Aggressive Coworkers, By A Psychologist
mainText: Passive-aggressive behavior in the workplace can be challenging to handle, but there are effective strategies to manage it. One approach is to stay calm and collected when faced with indirect jibes or underhanded comments, as overreacting can escalate conflict. Mindful communication and asking for clarification can help address such behavior constructively. Another strategy is to confront passive-aggressive colleagues assertively without engaging in their behavior. Using 'I' statements to express feelings and addressing the behavior in the present moment can prevent patterns from forming. Setting clear boundaries, collaborating on solutions, and seeking support if needed are recommended to manage passive-aggressive behavior effectively in the workplace.

author: Web Desk
title: Idina Menzel goes 'off-script' to root for Cynthia Erivo at 2024 Tony Awards
mainText: Idina Menzel and Cynthia Erivo presented the award of best musical at the 2024 Tony Awards to The Outsiders on June 16, 2024. Menzel said to Erivo, "I'm just going to go off-script real quick to say how excited I am to see what I know is going to be an amazing performance in that movie you're doing", and further added, "I just wanted to say green girl power." The Let It Go singer found it difficult to accept not portraying Elphaba in the film adaption, but sent her love to Cynthia and Ariana (who is cast as Glinda) back in 2022 through Broadway.com. However, fans theorize that both Menzel and Kristin Chenoweth (who previously played Glinda) shall have cameos in the adaptation that would be out in movie theaters on November 27.

author: Julianna O'clair
title: El Paso County sheriff’s deputy gets 2 years of probation in felony menacing plea deal
mainText: An El Paso County deputy sheriff has pleaded guilty to felony menacing after allegedly pointing a gun at and assaulting a man in a domestic violence case, according to court records. Marie Lahoff, 34, pleaded guilty to felony menacing with a real or simulated weapon, a class five felony, on Monday and was sentenced to two years of probation as part of a deferred sentence, according to court records. She was arrested on Feb. 2 and charged with felony menacing and misdemeanor assault, harassment and false imprisonment. The other charges were dropped as part of a plea deal. Lahoff got into an argument about her drinking with a man in a home in Colorado Springs on Jan. 20. The argument escalated and she threatened to shoot herself before hitting the man with a gun, pointing it at him, kicking him and locking him in the house, according to the arrest affidavit. Lahoff worked in the Detention Security Division and was placed on administrative leave after her arrest, according to the sheriff’s office.

author: Shannon McGuigan
title: Flash sale! Shopping centre is being put on sale for £16.45million on site currently occupied by...
mainText: A shopping centre, which boasts numerous big brand names, is up for sale for an eye-watering £16.45million. Built over 55 years ago in 1969, St Martin's Shopping Centre has a staggering 92,000 square feet of retail space. The prime real estate - located in Caversham, Berkshire - already hosts some household names, including Waitrose, Iceland and Boots - so it's never short of footfall. Its long list of major outlets includes, Superdrug, Costa as well as several long-serving local shops including The Caversham Butcher and household good's store - Terry's. Even new businesses are set to move into the centre, meaning the shopping precinct will be completely packed out, according to the Reading Chronicle. Originally based in Pangbourne, optician business Eye Club is in the process of moving into what was Cara Shoes. Reading-based bakery goods business - BKRY - it setting up shop in the unit formerly belonging to House of Cards. However, a packed out shopping centre isn't all this retail paradise has to offer potential buyers. Not only is the shopping mall being auctioned off with a car park with a whopping 250 spaces, as well as ten flats currently leased on short-hold tenancies. The prospective buyer would also be given planning permission to potentially add more residential accommodation on the land. This commercial property has been listed by KLM Real Estate as instructed by Federated Hermes. This come a year after a shopping centre in West Wales sold for only £300,000 - less than the average price of a British house at the time. The once-prosperous Cambrian Way in the centre of Carmarthen, West Wales, was built just 35 years ago. In December 2023, it was sold in a private sale for only £300,000 with a local businessman believed to be behind the bid. The centre is home to eight shops, kiosks and a snooker hall although most are shut up and remain derelict as it struggles to attract more shoppers. The 13,000-population town in the heartland of southwest Wales has lost the likes of Debenhams, Topshop, River Island and H&M in recent years. More recently, Frankie & Benny's has since shuttered its doors in the formerly prosperous market town.

author: Raphael Franks
title: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon’s Defence Force plane trouble puts NZ’s reputation at risk, expert says
mainText: Other countries will make fun of New Zealand because of the poor state of the Defence Force plane used to ferry the Prime Minister. Christopher Luxon had to book a commercial flight to Japan after the Royal New Zealand Air Force (RNZAF) plane, a Boeing 757, broke down. The Air Force plane blew a fuse, and when replaced, it blew again. This incident may lead to the Prime Minister traveling commercially in the future. The plane trouble risks denting New Zealand's respect on the diplomatic stage, according to international law expert Al Gillespie. He highlighted the importance of presenting gravitas in diplomacy for gaining respect and conducting serious business. Around 30 top businesspeople, Minister of Trade Todd McClay, and others continued their journey to Japan from Brisbane on an Air New Zealand flight after the plane incident. The cost of this change of plan may fall on taxpayers. Minister of Defence Judith Collins indicated the possibility of the Prime Minister flying commercial to prevent future incidents, noting the challenges of funding new planes during a cost-of-living crisis. This breakdown is part of a series of embarrassing incidents involving Defence Force aircraft, such as a fault in March that led Luxon to fly commercial to Melbourne and a previous breakdown during a visit to China. Luxon had expressed confidence in the plane before this incident. The situation has attracted criticism and attention internationally, seen as a source of national embarrassment.

author: Roisin Chapman
title: Biggest theme park in the US to open in Orlando next year with more than 50 attractions including new...
mainText: UNIVERSAL Orlando is set to open the biggest theme park in the United States next year. Epic Universe will include everything from three new hotels to another installment in the Wizarding World of Harry Potter. The theme park, originally planned for 700 acres of land, is now being developed on 2,000 acres in downtown Orlando. Documents filed with the city outline the updated plan, which includes the theme park, hotels, shops, and food and beverage amenities. As well as adding a Ministry of Magic attraction to the existing Harry Potter universe, Universal is introducing some new lands. These include Super Nintendo World, Dark Universe, How to Train Your Dragon – Isle of Berk, and Celestial Park. Between the five lands, there will be 50 new attractions available to visitors. Universal has already unveiled Super Nintendo World, the Isle of Berk, and the Celestial Park. Earlier this month Universal opened a preview center for the new park at Universal CityWalk. The center includes a scale of the park, outlining each of the attractions available. An augmented reality experience is also available on mobile devices to bring the park to life. Epic Universe will join Universal Orlando's other famous parks Universal Studios, Islands of Adventure, and Volcano Bay. Also included in the development are three luxury hotels, two of which are cosmic-themed. The Stella Nova and the Terra Luna resorts are both owned by Loews Hotels and brought to life by Universal Creative. Between the two locations, they will offer 1,500 rooms to park guests. The Universal Helios Grand Hotel is also currently under construction at the site. Universal shared renderings of the accommodation at the beginning of 2024.

author: Angela Symons
title: Lufthansa City Airlines: What is the German flag carrier’s new airline and where will it fly?
mainText: The brand new Lufthansa City Airlines will take its first flight on 26 June, bringing new short- and medium-haul connections to Germany. Bookings for the new airline are already open, focusing on connecting flights for Lufthansa from its main hubs in Frankfurt and Munich. Here’s where it will fly and how it could change air travel in Europe. The new Lufthansa subsidiary’s debut flight will go from Munich in Germany to Birmingham in the UK. alongside the existing Lufthansa CityLine subsidiary, the new Lufthansa City will eventually serve domestic and European routes from its Munich and Frankfurt bases. In 2024, domestic destinations will include Berlin, Bremen, Cologne Bonn, Düsseldorf, Hamburg and Hannover. Outside of Germany, the airline will initially fly to Bordeaux in France, and Manchester and Birmingham in the UK. Further European flights are expected to be added down the line. In 2025, slated destinations include Paris Charles de Gaulle, Toulouse-Blagnac and Lyon-Saint Exupéry in France; Bilbao and Barcelona in Spain; Prague in Czechia; Ljubljana in Slovenia; Zagreb in Croatia; Krakow in Poland; Belgrade in Serbia; Sofia in Bulgaria; Bucharest in Romania; Helsinki in Finland; Gothenburg- Landvetter in Sweden; Oslo in Norway; Luxembourg; and Dublin in Ireland. Though similarly named, Lufthansa CityLine and Lufthansa City are separate subsidiaries of Germany’s flag carrier. According to Lufthansa, the new airline will serve markets not covered by its predecessor, help reduce costs, and strengthen the company’s short-haul competitiveness. But unions raised suspicions of the move when it was announced last year. German pilot union Vereinigung Cockpit (VC) said the subsidiary was created to circumvent contractual obligations for employees in the Lufthansa Group, who were being encouraged to apply for roles at the new airline. Similarly, the Centre for Aviation (CAPA) claimed Lufthansa City was “another new platform to help [the Lufthansa Group] around restrictive terms in pilot agreements, thereby lowering labour costs and increasing labour flexibility”. Euronews Travel reached out to both unions about their current stance but they did not respond.

author: Hope Brotherton
title: The huge river dubbed the ‘Amazon of Europe’ just a few hours from the UK with water buffaloes and wild hor...
mainText: The Danube Delta, dubbed the 'Amazon of Europe,' is a hidden gem for nature lovers, located just a few hours away from the UK. Originating in Germany and flowing through 10 countries, including Romania, before reaching the Black Sea, the Danube Delta is a vast nature reserve known for its diverse wildlife and wetlands. Spanning 580,000 hectares, it is home to a wide variety of fish species and hosts Europe's largest colony of white pelicans. Other animals found in the area include wild horses, beavers, and golden jackals. The region is also seeing the return of several species due to conservation efforts by Rewilding Europe. Visitors can explore the Danube Delta on slow boat excursions offered by travel company Wild Travel, providing a leisurely experience to admire the natural beauty and wildlife. Permits to visit the area cost 5 RON (85p) per person, with excursions starting from €50 per person for a one-day tour, including lunch. Accommodations and flights to the Danube Delta are easily accessible from towns like Tulcea, where visitors can find a range of hotels and restaurants. The region has received rave reviews from visitors on platforms like TripAdvisor, with many praising its unique landscapes and water channels. With easy access from the UK via flights to Constanta Airport and affordable accommodations, the Danube Delta offers a memorable and budget-friendly travel destination for nature enthusiasts.

author: Blox Content Management
title: Trump-endorsed candidate loses Indiana lieutenant governor race in rare contested convention
mainText: Indiana's Republican delegates voted against a Trump-endorsed candidate for lieutenant governor and instead nominated pastor Micah Beckwith. The contested convention marked the first time since 1996 that Indiana Republicans had a competitive race for lieutenant governor. Beckwith won by a close vote of 891-828, despite Trump's late endorsement of Rep. Julie McGuire. The victory signaled a shift in party loyalty, with many delegates supporting Beckwith over Trump's preferred choice. Indiana's nominee for lieutenant governor is traditionally chosen in a convention style, making Beckwith's win significant. Some delegates expressed skepticism about Trump's influence and questioned his alignment with traditional Republican values. Beckwith's nomination has highlighted divisions within the GOP, especially regarding his close relationship with Senator Mike Braun, the gubernatorial candidate. Beckwith has expressed support for Trump's positions, including claiming the Jan. 6 insurrection was divinely inspired and committing to fight against the Democratic 'woke' agenda. Indiana Democrats view the potential strain between the Republican governor and lieutenant governor as an opportunity to win the governor's race, highlighting the party's internal divisions. An internal memo from a GOP lawyer raised concerns about Beckwith's nomination and its impact on the election. Overall, Beckwith's victory in the lieutenant governor race has exposed ideological fault lines within the Indiana Republican Party, setting the stage for a contentious gubernatorial election.

author: Kim Willsher
title: Don’t vote for the far right, French sports stars urge public
mainText: More than 200 French athletes and sporting personalities have signed an open letter calling on voters to reject the far right in the snap parliamentary election called by Emmanuel Macron, describing it as “not only … a civic duty, but also an act of love for our country”. As the official election campaign kicked off with just two weeks to go before the first round of voting, the appeal called for “a more inclusive and democratic society” and accused rightwing politicians of exploiting differences and diversity and “manipulating our fears to divide us”. Their intervention came hours after France’s football captain, Kylian Mbappé, and his team-mate in Les Bleus Marcus Thuram urged voters to reject Marine Le Pen’s National Rally and Eric Zemmour’s Reconquest party at the election. Mbappé widened his appeal, calling on his compatriots to not let the “extremes” – either far right or far left – into power, saying it was a pivotal moment for French history. While the public alerts from star footballers were welcomed by leftwing parties, they prompted a dismissive response from Sébastien Chenu, an MP for the RN. The political statements prompted the French football federation to call for the national team’s neutrality to be respected and for Les Bleus not be politicised after the president’s shock decision to dissolve parliament in the wake of the RN winning France’s European elections by a large majority. The election campaign began officially on Monday after the deadline for parties to nominate candidates on Sunday. Macron’s announcement has plunged France into political turmoil with polls showing the RN winning the two-round vote but falling short of an absolute majority, leaving the party unable to govern without forming a coalition. Clément Beaune, Macron’s former Europe minister, said: “At such a serious moment, nobody can sit on the bench. It’s brave and necessary for great sports stars to get involved.”

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Editorial: Government must make a call on the future of New Zealand’s two ageing 757 NZDF planes
mainText: EDITORIAL This Government has made some tough fiscal calls since taking over the management of New Zealand and its finances. It has cut the Māori Health Authority, target="_blank">Matariki funding has been slashed, the public service has been given a number-one haircut and all ministries have been told to further tighten their belts. But the Government is going to have to spend taxpayers’ money, this time on replacing the two New Zealand Defence Force (NZDF) 757 planes that break down at the most inopportune times, like when Prime Minister Christopher Luxon and a group of trade delegates from New Zealand were heading to Japan during the weekend. The latest breakdown of the 757 resulted in Luxon leaving his trade delegation, and journalists covering the trip, behind in Papua New Guinea, where the plane had landed to refuel on its way to Japan. It was supposed to be an hour-long stopover, but turned into an overnight stay for everyone but Luxon. The PM caught a commercial flight to Tokyo via Hong Kong. The issue this time with the plane started with a blown fuse, and ended with the plane needing to be flown around, without passengers, to drain it of fuel to reduce its weight. The delegation later boarded the 757 and flew to Brisbane at low altitude and will catch up with Luxon – a day late. The Auckland to Tokyo flight, carrying other passengers, was to be diverted to Brisbane to collect the group. Defence Minister Judith Collins told Newstalk ZB’s Mike Hosking the consistent flight issues were “embarrassing”. This is the second time Luxon has been forced to switch to a commercial flight since he became Prime Minister. New Zealand has two Boeing 757-200 jets, which are used by the NZDF and political leaders on official duties. The problem is they are now more than 30 years old and well past their use-by date. Prior to the NZDF purchasing the two planes in 2003, they were used in a commercial capacity for a decade and the decision to buy them was by the Defence Minister at the time, Labour’s Mark Burton, for about $200 million, plus costs for upgrades and modifications. Those planes have outlived their lifespan, and no amount of No 8 wire or masking tape can fix them. It will cost the taxpayers millions to replace them, and no doubt many will criticise any Government which intends to spend a bunch of cash, when the country can least afford it. And that’s the message we have been told constantly. “No Prime Minister wants to spend a lot of money on something deemed as ‘nice to have’,” Collins said. But the longer this can is kicked down the road, the more money it will eventually cost to find a suitable outcome.

author: Reuters
title: US Surgeon General Vivek Murthy calls for social media warning labels
mainText: US Surgeon General Vivek Murthy on Monday called for a warning label to be added to social media apps as a reminder that those platforms have caused harm to young people, especially adolescents. Murthy wrote in the New York Times on Monday that a warning label alone will not make social media safe for young people but that it can increase awareness and change behavior as shown in evidence from tobacco studies. The US Congress would need to pass legislation requiring such a warning label. For a long time, Murthy has been warning that social media can profoundly harm the mental health of youth, particularly adolescent girls. In an advisory last year, he called for safeguards from tech companies for children who are at critical stages of brain development. A 2019 American Medical Association study showed that the risk of depression doubled for teenagers who were spending three hours a day on social media. "It is time to require a surgeon general's warning label on social media platforms, stating that social media is associated with significant mental health harms for adolescents," Murthy wrote on Monday. "A surgeon general's warning label, which requires congressional action, would regularly remind parents and adolescents that social media has not been proved safe," he added. Some US states have been working to pass legislation to safeguard children from the harmful effects of social media, such as anxiety, depression, and other mental illnesses as a result. New York state lawmakers this month passed legislation to bar social media platforms from exposing 'addictive' algorithmic content to users under age 18 without parental consent. In March, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis signed a bill that bans children under 14 from social media platforms and requires 14- and 15-year-olds to get parental consent.

author: Daniel McLaughlin
title: Kremlin decries Ukraine peace summit as Putin heads for North Korea
mainText: Russia has dismissed the impact of a global peace summit on Ukraine that it was not invited to, while President Vladimir Putin is set to visit North Korea. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy thanked over 90 states for attending the summit in Switzerland, where about 80 countries signed a joint statement supporting Ukraine's territorial integrity and various security measures. The Kremlin labeled the event a failure as it was excluded from the talks, with China citing Russia's absence as a reason for not attending. Key countries like India, Saudi Arabia, Mexico, and South Africa did not sign the final communique. Putin stated that Russia will discuss peace if Ukraine accepts its occupation of certain regions and abandons NATO ambitions. Additionally, the Kremlin announced Putin's upcoming visit to North Korea and Vietnam to enhance Russia's global influence. Heavy fighting continues in eastern Ukraine, with Russian airstrikes causing injuries and damage in the Poltava region. There have been recent shake-ups in Russia's defense ministry, including the appointment of a relative to a senior defense post. Despite ongoing tensions, Russia and North Korea deny allegations of arms trade, and the US accuses North Korea of supplying weapons to Russia for use in Ukraine. Sign up for push alerts to stay updated with the latest news.

author: Nandini Singh
title: Spread of deadly 'flesh-eating bacteria' in Japan raises global concerns
mainText: In the wake of the Covid-19 pandemic, humanity faces a new threat: a flesh-eating bacterial infection known as Streptococcal Toxic Shock Syndrome (STSS). Recent data from Japan’s National Institute of Infectious Diseases indicates a troubling surge in STSS cases, with nearly 1,000 reported infections this year, surpassing last year’s total. Streptococcal Toxic Shock Syndrome (STSS) stems from Group A Streptococcus (GAS) bacteria, which release toxins triggering an intense inflammatory response in the body. Last year saw 97 fatalities due to STSS, marking the second-highest death toll in six years. Prof Ken Kikuchi from Tokyo Women’s Medical University highlighted the disease’s swift progression, saying, “Most deaths occur within 48 hours of initial symptoms.” Preventive measures such as good hygiene and prompt treatment of injuries are crucial. Immediate medical attention is advised upon noticing symptoms like severe pain, high fever, and redness at a wound site. Japanese health authorities are actively monitoring the situation, intensifying efforts to curb STSS spread. International outbreaks of STSS have been reported in several countries. The CDC notes that experts don’t know how the bacteria got into the body for nearly half of people who get STSS.

title: Alia Bhatt posts cute picture of Raha walking with Ranbir Kapoor, internet reacts: ‘Papa’s Dilbaro’

author: Simone McCarthy, Anna Chernova
title: Russia’s Putin to visit North Korea in rare trip as anti-West alignment deepens
mainText: Vladimir Putin is scheduled to visit North Korea for a two-day trip, marking his first visit to the country in over two decades and showcasing a deepening alignment between Russia and North Korea. The visit signifies a strengthening partnership founded on mutual animosity towards the West, with Putin seeking support for his actions in Ukraine. The two leaders plan to sign a new strategic partnership agreement aimed at enhancing stability in northeast Asia. The visit comes amid ongoing tensions on the Korean peninsula and concerns about North Korea's military support for Russia's war effort. Despite denying arms exports, both countries face allegations of military aid exchange. The trip reciprocates a visit by Kim Jong Un to Russia last year and follows a recent G7 summit emphasizing support for Ukraine. Putin's efforts to bolster ties with North Korea are seen as a way to gain support for his actions in Ukraine and counter Western influence. The visit provides Kim with a platform to demonstrate global influence and seek economic support. Putin's recent diplomatic efforts, including visits to China and hosting foreign ministers from major economies, indicate a shift towards aligning with like-minded partners amid increasing tensions with the West. The visit to North Korea serves as part of Putin's strategy to enhance his presence on the world stage following the invasion of Ukraine. The growing partnership between Russia and North Korea reflects a broader shift in geopolitical dynamics.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Opposition To Get A Leader In Lok Sabha, But It May Not Be Rahul Gandhi
mainText: Congress's Rahul Gandhi, widely expected to shoulder the responsibilities of the Leader of the Opposition in the 18th Lok Sabha, is not inclined to take up the post, sources in the party have confided. Three senior leaders -- Kumari Selja, Gaurav Gogoi and Manish Tiwari -- are being considered for the job, sources said. The Opposition will have a leader in the Lok Sabha after a decade following its hugely improved performance in the recently concluded Lok Sabha polls. Ninety-nine of its 232 seats have come from the Congress, and as the largest party in the Opposition benches, it is expected to name the Leader of the Opposition. Mr Gandhi, whose Bharat Jodo Yatra was widely cited as the reason for the Congress boost -- the party won 44 seats in 2014 and 52 in 2019 -- was expected to take more responsibility in parliament. There has been considerable pressure on him from various leaders on this point. The post would have given him Cabinet rank, help coordinate better with allies in the INDIA bloc and helped the Congress project a strong face by spearheading the Opposition attack on the BJP in the Lok Sabha. But sources said Mr Gandhi, who even stepped down from the party chief's post following the rout in 2019, is not keen on it. He has avoided taking up any post since, sources added. Mr Gandhi has also decided to represent his mother Sonia Gandhi's constituency, Raebareli, in parliament, sources said. An announcement is expected this evening. He will give up Wayanad, from where his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra is expected to contest. The other family bastion in Uttar Pradesh, Amethi, is already back in Congress hands, with long-time Gandhi family aide KL Sharma besting the BJP's former Union minister Smriti Irani. Ms Gandhi Vadra had not contested in the general election, choosing instead to focus on campaigning for the party. Sources said she had reservations about all three Gandhis being in parliament, concerned that it would give ammunition to the BJP for its "dynastic politics" allegation. Sonia Gandhi is a member of Rajya Sabha, the upper house of parliament.

author: Ht Sports Desk
title: 'Virat Kohli failed, so what? You are leading Pakistan...': Babar Azam mercilessly slammed in hot-headed rant
mainText: Pakistan were eliminated from the group stage of the T20 World Cup last week, following the losses to the United States and India. The side's survival in the edition depended on Ireland's win over the USA, but the weather gods spoiled Pakistan's chances with rain ensuring no play was possible in Lauderhill. With a solitary point, USA qualified for the Super Eight stage, as they continue on a splendid run in the tournament.Pakistan ended their T20 World Cup run with a scratchy win over Ireland on Sunday, defeating the side by three wickets in a 107-run chase. It has been a low-scoring tournament, with the matches in Group A being particularly impacted due to sluggish pitches in the USA. The surface in New York gained notoriety for being too tilted in favour of bowlers; the highest run-chase at the venue was 111 by India, which provides a fair idea on how tricky the conditions were.During a chat show, Pakistan's batter Ahmed Shehzad was asked on whether it would be fair to be overly-critical of the Pakistan side when the conditions were difficult for batting. Shehzad, however, insisted that the side has been performing below-par for many years, and not just in the ongoing edition.“If you go back in time, you lost to Zimbabwe, then South Africa lost to Netherlands. Then you reached the final. We lost in Asia Cup to Sri Lanka. You look back at last three months... you lost to Afghanistan, Zimbabwe, Ireland, now USA. You couldn't chase 120 against India. This isn't just about this World Cup,” Shehzad told GEO News.“We get paid for it. If I dominate the team for 4-5 years, I won't have an excuse. You have to prepare yourself for every condition, that's why you are an international cricketer. You should know how to tackle conditions and win the match for your country.”When the host pointed out that Virat Kohli has also been poor in the USA leg – Kohli has scored only 5 runs across three matches in the edition – Shehzad stated that in Babar Azam's case, there was more to it than just batting.“It isn't important that you perform. You talked about Kohli. Okay, Babar also got out. So what? Where is the team effort? You've got to find the things in a method... conditions are for both teams. You need to execute things rightly, from captaincy to using bowlers, and lead the team to win. If you're not winning the matches, you will be blamed,” said Shehzad.

author: Paul Carsten
title: Oil prices stable as demand uncertainty persists
mainText: By Paul Carsten LONDON (Reuters) - Oil prices were stable on Tuesday, as traders awaited signs of a hoped-for summer demand boost to prop up prices even as strong supply threatens to blunt gains. Benchmark Brent crude futures were down 2 cents to $84.23 per barrel at 1231 GMT after climbing in the previous session. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures, which also rose on Monday, were up 3 cents to $80.36 a barrel. Both benchmarks gained around 2% on Monday, closing at their highest levels since April. Brent has clambered back from an early-June close of $77.52, though remains off its $90 peaks in mid-April. "The oil market shifted its focus back to fundamentals, which have been soft for some time," said BoFA commodity and derivatives strategist Francisco Blanch in a note, adding that global crude oil inventories and refined product storage in the United States and Singapore, among other places, was higher. Meanwhile, global oil demand growth slowed to 890,000 barrels per day year on year in the first quarter, and data suggests consumption growth likely slowed further in the second quarter, he said in the note. But U.S. crude inventories are expected to have fallen by 2.3 million barrels in the week to June 14, according to analysts polled by Reuters. "The critical data set this week, at least for us, will be the U.S. oil inventory data as it could confirm or refute the developing optimism that demand has started its ascent at the dawn of the summer driving season," Tamas Varga of oil broker PVM wrote in a note. Some analysts remained bullish on the price impact of an extension by the OPEC+ group of supply cuts in the near term. "The latest guidance provided by OPEC+, as well as their unchanged 2.25 million barrels per day demand growth outlook, signals a stagnation in oil supply growth for 2024 and an apparent downside risk to production in 2025," said Patricio Valdivieso, Rystad Energy vice president and global lead of crude trading analysis. "Under these conditions — and the disconnect between the OPEC+ demand outlook and all other agencies — it is hard to remain fully bearish when global oil supply growth appears decimated," he added.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Ecopetrol obtains authorization to execute a loan agreement with local banks for one trillion pesos - Eco
mainText: BOGOTA, Colombia, June 17, 2024 /PRNewswire/ -- Ecopetrol S.A. (ECOPETROLEC ("Ecopetrol" or the "Company") informs that, through Resolution 1671 of June 14, 2024, the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit ("MHCP") authorized Ecopetrol to execute a loan agreement for up to one trillion Colombian pesos (COP). The loan is expected to be executed with Banco de Bogotá S.A. (COP 642 billion), Banco de Occidente S.A. (COP 208 billion) and Banco Popular S.A. (COP 150 billion), as lenders. The term of the loan is expected to be seven (7) years, with a grace period of two (2) years from the date of the first disbursement. The amortization is expected to be made in ten (10) equal semi-annual installments once the grace period is over and the interest rate is expected to be indexed to the IBR in the terms previously agreed with the banks. Aligned with the 2024 financing plan and maintaining the gross debt/EBITDA target for the year, the resources of this operation will be used for non-investment expenses, including the payment of existing financial commitments. To obtain authorization for the loan, the Company complied with all the required internal procedures and approvals. The conditions obtained for this agreement ratify the support and confidence of the financial sector in the Ecopetrol Group's strategy. Ecopetrol is the largest company in Colombia and one of the main integrated energy companies in the American continent, with more than 18,000 employees. In Colombia, it is responsible for more than 60% of the hydrocarbon production of most transportation, logistics, and hydrocarbon refining systems, and it holds leading positions in the petrochemicals and gas distribution segments. With the acquisition of 51.4% of ISA's shares, the company participates in energy transmission, the management of real-time systems (XM), and the Barranquilla - Cartagena coastal highway concession. At the international level, Ecopetrol has a stake in strategic basins in the American continent, with Drilling and Exploration operations in the United States (Permian basin and the Gulf of Mexico), Brazil, and Mexico, and, through ISA and its subsidiaries, Ecopetrol holds leading positions in the power transmission business in Brazil, Chile, Peru, and Bolivia, road concessions in Chile, and the telecommunications sector.

author: Tamika Seeto
title: China's huge $110 offer to every Australian citizens: 'More powerful'
mainText: Australians will now be able to travel to China without having to pay and apply for a visa, making our passports even more powerful. Australia will join several other nations, including New Zealand, in the visa-free travel program. The change means Aussies can travel to China for up to 15 days for business, tourism and to visit loved ones without requiring a visa. This will save Aussies about $110, the current cost for a single-entry tourist visa. Other countries included on the visa waiver list include New Zealand, who was recently added to the program in May, along with Singapore, France, Japan, Spain, the Netherlands, Malaysia and Thailand. Chinese Premier Li Qiang made the announcement after a meeting with Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Canberra. "We agreed to provide each other with reciprocal access to five-year multiple entry visas for tourism, business and visiting family members — so as to better facilitate personal exchanges, China will also include Australia in its Visa Waiver Program," Li said. Multiple entry visas mean a person will be able to enter and exit the country as many times as they want during the time their visa is valid. Australia currently has the sixth most powerful passport in the world, according to the Henley Passport Index. With this change, an Aussie passport will now give visa-free access to 190 out of 227 destinations worldwide. Passport prices going up Australian passport prices will be going up from July 1. This is the second time prices have gone up this year and will make them the most expensive in the world. The price of a standard adult passport will increase from $346 to $398. That’s a price hike of about 15 per cent, or $50. It’s not the only change coming for Aussie passports next month. Announced in the budget, Aussies will soon be able to pay $100 to have their passport application fast-tracked and processed within five business days. This will be an extra option to the existing $252 fast-track option, which takes two days. Travellers usually need to allow at least six weeks to receive a passport.

author: Nicole Dorfman
title: Skier seriously injured after tumbling 2,000 feet during descent of Skywalker Couloir
mainText: A skier was rescued on Monday after sliding up to 2,000 feet while attempting to descend Skywalker Couloir. According to a release, at 10:37 a.m. Monday, Boulder County Communications was notified of a skier who had sustained serious injuries in the area of Skywalker Couloir on South Arapahoe Peak west of Nederland. The 47-year-old man was beginning a ski descent of the couloir when he fell, sliding and tumbling around 1,000 to 2,000 feet down on the snowfield before coming to a stop at a rock ledge. Two off-duty firefighters recreating in the area witnessed the fall and were able to call 911, according to the release. They also descended to where the injured man had stopped and were able to provide first aid and relay information to the responding rescue teams. According to the release, rescuers and medical personnel from Rocky Mountain Rescue Group were flown near the scene by MedEvac before climbing the rest of the way to the scene. They were also assisted by other bystanders who helped carry equipment to the scene and additional rescuers hiked in from the Fourth of July Trailhead bringing additional equipment. Rescuers were able to place the skier in a full body vacuum splint, and he was hoisted from the scene and transported by helicopter to Nederland Middle and Senior High School. The skier was then transported by ambulance to a local hospital. According to the release, the skier sustained serious injuries but 'remained stable throughout the incident.' Assisting agencies involved with this rescue effort include the Boulder County Sheriff's Office, Boulder County Parks and Open Space, Nederland Fire Protection District, the Rocky Mountain Rescue Group, the Colorado Search and Rescue Association, the Colorado Hoist Rescue Team, MedEvac, and American Medical Response.

title: US Democrats approve major arms sale to Israel
mainText: Two key Democrats in the US Congress have agreed to support a major arms sale to Israel that includes 50 F-15 fighter jets worth more than $18 billion, the Washington Post reported on Monday, citing three unnamed officials. author: Eric Young, The Gazette
title: Colorado program to provide financial aid to 2024 graduates
mainText: State funding approved during last year’s legislative session looks to open the doors for recent graduates while also filling the Colorado’s current workforce needs. Opportunity Next Colorado is a one-time $25 million scholarship program for Class of 2024 high school graduates and students with equivalent credentials for the 2024-2025 academic year. The scholarship is designed to aid students pursuing post-secondary education or training towards eight high-priority career pathways in the state, offering up to $1,500 for tuition, fees, books, and equipment in various fields. Pikes Peak State College in Colorado Springs offers programs for these career pathways, except transportation. The program also provides coaching and counseling to help students determine their career paths and navigate financial aid. The initiative addresses a workforce gap in the state, with Colorado currently having two available jobs for every unemployed person and a growing demand for educated workers by 2031. Graduates eligible for this funding may also qualify for other financial aid, including the Colorado Promise Program for tuition and fee reimbursement. The program aims to give recent graduates a sense of certainty following the uncertainties of the COVID-19 pandemic.

author: Joseph McClain. Note
title: A new approach to neuroimaging analysis
mainText: Their work, published in the journal Cerebral Cortex, outlines a method for the use of neuroimaging data to predict elements of cognition and behavioral variables. The technique involves examining widely used magnetic resonance images (MRIs) of brains to find associations to various behaviors, and then applying predictions from those associations to an independent unseen sample. Carolina Makowski, Ph.D., a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Radiology at UC San Diego School of Medicine, explains that researchers commonly use MRIs to examine specific structures of the brain to determine their role in behaviors or abilities including short-term memory, problem-solving ability or a wide range of cognitive functions. Makowski, the first and corresponding author on the paper, said the group's work shows a way around a commonly held belief that neuroimaging studies couldn't yield meaningful results unless the study included thousands of participants. She explains that multivariate studies take in a pattern of associations. Co-author Terry L. Jernigan, Ph.D., professor of cognitive science, psychiatry and radiology at UC San Diego and the director of the Center for Human Development, added that the team was able to get good results from smaller data sets by "training and tuning" large data sets using multivariate analysis methods. Dale added that the predictive power of the small-sample approach can be amplified when it's supplemented by other types of analyses, such as genetics studies or other types of imaging. author: Molly Morrow
title: Prospective candidates line up to enter Chicago’s elected school board race
mainText: Candidates for Chicago’s elected school board have filed their nominations with the Chicago Board of Elections, marking the city's first elected school board race. Twenty-one candidates submitted their nominations for the 10 board seats, with final numbers to be determined after the deadline. Candidates must collect 1,000 signatures, file necessary paperwork, and declare their economic interests. The nomination process ends on June 24, with the election scheduled for Nov. 5. Noteworthy candidates include Che “Rhymefest” Smith focusing on budget, curriculum, and personnel, and Jennifer Custer supporting selective schools. The election, a result of a new bill, expands the board to 21 members, with 10 seats elected and 11 appointed by Mayor Brandon Johnson. Candidates aim to improve financial oversight, funding equity, and school infrastructure. They prioritize transparency, public input, and accountability in managing Chicago's school system.

author: Sam Routley
title: A byelection to watch: What the Toronto-St. Paul’s vote means for Justin Trudeau
mainText: Residents of the federal riding of Toronto-St. Paul’s will soon be tasked with voting for their next Member of Parliament. Despite being a Liberal stronghold for decades, recent polls show a slim lead for the Liberals with the Conservatives closing in. The byelection on June 24 is crucial for Justin Trudeau's government as it can indicate ongoing trends. Voter discontent with Canada's economic issues, including stagnant growth and rising living costs in Toronto, may favor the Conservatives in this election. However, historical voting patterns suggest that the Conservatives are unlikely to win in Toronto-St. Paul’s due to the district's demographic makeup. The close race reflects growing dissatisfaction with the Liberal government, signaling a need for a change in course to avoid electoral defeat. While the discontent may limit the Liberals' ability to influence their electoral fortunes in the upcoming general election, it is not indicative of a permanent realignment in Canadian politics. The divisions between urban and suburban areas, as well as social and economic factors, will continue to shape Canadian politics. Toronto-St. Paul’s serves as an important indicator of these divisions and highlights the potential for swing districts to decide Canadian elections. In conclusion, the byelection in Toronto-St. Paul’s signifies a challenging period for the Liberals as voters express a desire for change, indicating a need for the party to adapt to evolving political landscapes.

title: Former NBA Player Darius Morris' Cause of Death Revealed
mainText: Darius Morris' cause of death has been determined one month after his passing. The former NBA point guard died of coronary artery atherosclerosis—also known as coronary heart disease—on May 2 at the age of 33, according to County of Los Angeles Medical Examiner records reviewed by E! News. Other "significant conditions" that contributed to his death included effects of cocaine, alcohol and hydrocodone, an opioid often used to treat severe chronic pain, per the medical examiner's office. His manner of death was ruled as an accident. Morris got his start in basketball with the University of Michigan's Wolverines, before being drafted by the Los Angeles Lakers in 2011. He played alongside the late Kobe Bryant for two season until he was reassigned to the L.A. D-Fenders, an NBA G League team. In September 2013, Morris signed with the Philadelphia 76ers but was waived in the following month. He went on to play for the Los Angeles Clippers and the Memphis Grizzlies on short-term contracts in early 2014, before joining the Antonio Spurs for the NBA Summer League that season.
