author: Matt Richardson
title: 4 questions to ask before your CD matures
mainText: Certificate of deposit (CD) accounts have historically been effective ways to protect and grow money, especially with recent surges in benefits due to elevated inflation and interest rates. As CDs mature, savers face various options and should prepare by asking key questions. Four important questions are highlighted: checking for rate changes, assessing changes in financial situation, exploring better rates with online banks, and considering alternative options such as high-yield savings accounts. It's crucial to be proactive in making the best decisions for one's finances before a CD matures.

author: Jon Rogers
title: Cost of family holiday rises £96 for every DEGREE of heat in Spain as families pay double for August...
mainText: THE price of a family holiday increases by up to £96 for every additional degree of heat in Spain, a study has found. Researchers have calculated how much the price of different holiday destinations rise as the weather warms up in peak season to help families keep costs down. The price of flights from London and accommodation in Benidorm, Spain, for two adults and two teenagers for a week-long trip in May when the temperature is 22 degrees will set you back £803 per family. But this rises to £1,570 in August when the mercury hits 30 degrees - £96 for each extra degree. Families who opt to travel outside of a peak weather window could be saving £235 for each degree lower in temperature, on average across seven popular destinations, and put it towards other aspects of the trip, such as activities with the kids, meals out or shopping. A week-long holiday for a family of four in Florida tallies up to £2,100 in May when the thermometer typically reads 29 degrees. But this nearly doubles to £4,043 in August when average temperatures are just two degrees higher at 31 – an additional £972 per degree. The research was commissioned by the Post Office, which also found trips to Cyprus set a family of four back £737 for a milder 24 degrees in May. And ramps up to £1,272, or £89 per degree, for a week in 30-degree heat in July. Greece is among the more reasonable options, with a family paying around £1,793 for 28 degrees in August, but costs just £1,285 in May at 23 degrees. It comes after research of 2,000 travellers found four in 10 who are planning a holiday this year intend to go ‘out of season’. Overall cost savings (58 per cent), fewer tourists (51 per cent) and a quieter journey to and from their destination (37 per cent) were among the reasons why. It also found one in 10 (11 per cent) who have travelled outside of peak season have saved over £400 as a result. Laura Plunkett, head of Post Office travel, which is launching its travel money card, said: “It’s evident from our research that holidaymakers feel warm weather is an important part of the holiday experience, and so are the memories we make while away.

author: Blox Content Management
title: Hunter Biden ‘gratuitously invoked’ father’s name in SEC inquiry, House Republicans say
mainText: House Republicans asked the Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday for records related to its inquiry involving Hunter Biden's business associates in 2016 after the lawmakers found the first son had referenced President Joe Biden during the SEC's investigation. Reps. James Comer (R-KY) and Jim Jordan (R-OH), who are leading an impeachment inquiry into the president, requested in a letter all SEC records connecting Hunter Biden to the commission's 2016 investigation, which resulted in the SEC charging seven people with fraud. 'To further the House's impeachment inquiry the Committees must determine the propriety with which SEC handled this matter,' Comer and Jordan wrote. They pointed to a subpoena Hunter Biden received in 2016 from the SEC seeking documents the first son had related to Rosemont Seneca Bohai, a company implicated in the SEC's fraud investigation. When Hunter Biden replied to the subpoena with the requested material, the first son's attorney also asked the SEC to be particularly confidential about the matter because of how it could affect then-Vice President Joe Biden. 'It would be unfair, not just to our client, but also to his father, the Vice President of the United States, if his involvement in an SEC investigation and parallel criminal probe were to become the subject of any media attention,' Hunter Biden's attorney wrote on April 20, 2016. Comer and Jordan found it out of line for Hunter Biden to use his father as a reason to request confidentiality during the SEC's inquiry, an observation that comes after the Republicans found during their impeachment inquiry repeated instances of the first son wielding his father's name in business dealings. 'Mr. Biden's response gratuitously invoked his father's position as the Vice President in what could be interpreted as an effort to discourage further SEC scrutiny,' the Republicans wrote. 'And on May 11, 2016, the SEC published a press release — announcing the charging of seven individuals — with no mention or charging of Hunter Biden.' author: Wire Content
title: Plastic surgeon charged in death of wife who went into cardiac arrest while he worked on her
mainText: A plastic surgeon in Florida, Benjamin Brown, was charged with manslaughter after his wife went into cardiac arrest and died following procedures he performed on her in his clinic. His wife, Hillary Brown, prepared anesthesia for herself and ingested pills before the procedures, which included arm liposuction and lip injections. During the procedures, she experienced adverse effects like blurry vision and muscle twitches, indicating lidocaine toxicity. Despite showing signs of distress, Benjamin Brown delayed calling 911, and it was a medical assistant who eventually made the call. Emergency room doctors treated Hillary Brown for lidocaine toxicity. Subsequently, the Florida Department of Health filed a complaint seeking penalties against Benjamin Brown, citing negligence and unsafe practices. An emergency order restricted his license, allowing him to perform procedures only in a hospital under supervision. The order criticized his disregard for patient safety, labeling his treatment of his wife as careless and haphazard.

author: Shristi Achar
title: Nvidia becomes world's most valuable company
mainText: (Reuters) -Nvidia became the world's most valuable company on Tuesday, dethroning tech heavyweight Microsoft, as its chips continue to play a central role in a race to dominate the market for artificial intelligence. Shares of the chipmaker climbed 3.2% to $135.21, lifting its market capitalization to $3.326 trillion, just days after overtaking iPhone maker Apple to become the second most valuable company. The surge in shares pushed the stock to a record high, adding over $103 billion to Nvidia's market capitalization on Tuesday. Increasing the appeal for its highly valued stock among individual investors, Nvidia recently split its stock ten-for-one, effective June 7. "A stock split can reduce the price per share, making it more affordable for individual investors to buy. With Nvidia doing a 10:1 stock split, retail investors are the real winners here," said Sam North, market analyst at investment platform eToro.

author: Toi Lifestyle Desk
title: Can vitamin A lower the risk of non-alcoholic fatty liver?
mainText: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a growing concern globally, linked to obesity and diabetes. Research suggests that Vitamin A plays a crucial role in reducing the risk of NAFLD by aiding in fat metabolism and preventing fat accumulation in the liver. Studies have shown that Vitamin A deficiency increases the likelihood of developing NAFLD, while supplements have been found to improve liver function and reduce inflammation markers in patients. It is important to include Vitamin A-rich foods in the diet to maintain adequate levels without overconsumption, as excess Vitamin A can be toxic. Foods like dairy products, sweet potatoes, carrots, and leafy greens are good sources of Vitamin A. Maintaining a balanced intake of Vitamin A through diet can potentially help lower the risk of NAFLD and support overall liver health.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: KCR's Power Deals Caused Rs 6,000-Crore Loss To Telangana: Sources
mainText: The Telangana government estimates that the state exchequer may have suffered a loss of up to Rs 6,000 crores because of what they allege were irregularities in the power purchase agreements drawn up by the previous Bharat Rashtra Samithi government. After being issued a notice by a Commission of Inquiry set up to probe suspected irregularities, former chief minister K Chandrasekhar Rao had said no investigation could be ordered into a decision of the Electricity Regulatory Commission. He had also questioned the neutrality of former Justice Narasimha Reddy who is heading the probe panel. On Tuesday, documents were made available to the media to show that the power purchase agreements (PPAs) with Chhattisgarh had not been ratified and sanctioned by the Telangana State Electricity Regulatory Commission (TSERC). Mr Rao, popularly known as KCR, has been critical of the Justice Narasimha Reddy Commission of Inquiry, even calling for the former chief justice of Patna High Court's recusal. Labelling the commission unlawful, he has argued that it lacks the authority to investigate PPAs and issues related to power plant construction once the TSERC has approved them. The officials have, however, clarified that although the agreement with Chhattisgarh was operational by the end of 2017, the power supply was only to the extent of 1,000 MW, which meant Telangana had to purchase additional power from the market, incurring an extra cost of Rs 2,083 crore between 2017 and 2022. "The previous government claimed to have paid Rs 3.9 per unit for power, but the actual cost was Rs 5.64 per unit, including other expenses. Between 2017 and 2022, Telangana purchased 17,996 million units for Rs 7,719 crore. The government claimed it had paid Rs 1,081 crore to Chhattisgarh for power, but the transmission charge for delivering the power was Rs 1,362 crore. Considering all these costs, the per unit expenditure was Rs 5.64, which is Rs 3,110 crore over the agreed price of Rs 3.9 per unit," a senior official explained. KCR, who played a pivotal role in the movement for a separate Telangana, became its first chief minister after its creation in 2014 and remained in the seat till last year, when his Bharat Rashtra Samithi was handed a comprehensive defeat by the Congress, which won 64 of the state's 119 Assembly seats. That number went up to 65 after a recent bypoll.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: H1-B visa holder warned against buying property in Florida, faces jail term
mainText: Jin Bian, a Chinese software engineer who has lived in the US for 12 years on an H-1B visa may face jail term for buying property in Florida. Bian, 31, who wanted to cut his one-hour commute by purchasing a house near office in Tampa was in for a shock when he discovered that he can be jailed. His fault? He bought property ignoring his immigration status. Based on a law enacted nearly a year ago, Chinese citizens on H-1B visas, like him, are prohibited from buying property in Florida.Chinese citizens without green cards face a felony charge and possible prison time if they purchase property in the state. Sellers and real estate agents can also be found liable under the law.A year back in July 2023, Governor Ron DeSantis signed this law, which restricts Chinese nationals without US green cards from purchasing real estate in the state. Florida Senate Bill 264 also imposes restrictions on citizens from Russia, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Venezuela, and Syria. It prevents them from buying property within 10 miles of military installations or critical infrastructure. However, Indians are not listed in the law.The law reflects Florida’s stance against what DeSantis describes as "the United States' greatest geopolitical threat — the Chinese Communist Party (CCP)."Bian is now reconsidering his future in Florida. "We’re ordinary people. We don’t talk about these political things. I think 99.99% of people here just want to have a good life… I don’t think California will ever have this kind of law," he told CNN. He remains hopeful the law might be reversed but plans to move back to California if there are no changes in the next year or two.The legislation is currently facing legal challenges in court, and other states are also considering similar measures.

author: Toi Lifestyle Desk
title: NASA warns that a giant 210 ft yacht-sized asteroid is set to pass by Earth "alarmingly close"
mainText: Asteroid 2024 LJ, a massive space rock roughly the size of a 210-foot yacht, is set to pass by Earth at a distance of 2.1 million miles on June 22, 2024. Traveling at 66,584 miles per hour, this asteroid has garnered attention from NASA and space enthusiasts. NASA's Planetary Defense Coordination Office monitors near-Earth objects like 2024 LJ to understand and track potential hazards. Despite its alarming speed, NASA assures that 2024 LJ poses no risk of impact. This event offers a chance for scientists to study the asteroid's characteristics. Telescopes and tracking equipment help us detect and monitor such objects with precision, contributing to our understanding of the universe. Other known NEOs like 2006 WB, 2010 RA91, 2015 VO142, and 2016 VA are closely monitored for potential impact risks. The orbits of these NEOs intersect with Earth's, necessitating advanced tracking systems for early hazard identification.

author: Ht Sports Desk
title: 'Indian hain yeh...': Fuming Haris Rauf charges towards fans in the USA, almost gets into a fight over selfie request
mainText: A video of Pakistan fast bowler Haris Rauf went viral on social media on Tuesday, where the cricketer is seen almost getting into a fight with a few fans in the USA. The video emerged on X, formerly known as Twitter, days after Pakistan incurred a group-stage exit from the 2024 T20 World Cup. In the 54-second clip, Haris was seen walking with his wife before being interrupted by fans requesting a selfie. Haris appeared to have lost his cool and charged towards them, but was stopped by one of the fans. One upset fan mentioned, "All I wanted was one picture with you." Haris assumed one of the fans to be Indian, although the fan clarified he was from Pakistan. Pakistan faced a forgettable campaign in the 2024 T20 World Cup, being shocked by the USA and losing to India despite a chance for a comeback. They managed wins against Canada and Ireland but were eliminated due to a wash-out match between the USA and Ireland, marking their third group-stage exit in T20 World Cups after being the runners-up in 2022.

author: Nagraj Gollapudi
title: Gambhir interviews for India head coach position
mainText: Gautam Gambhir, the frontrunner to replace Rahul Dravid as India men's head coach, has formally applied for the position and attended an interview with the BCCI's cricket advisory committee. The committee includes former India cricketers Ashok Malhotra, Jatin Paranjape, and Sulakshana Naik. Other applicants such as WV Raman have also been interviewed. Gambhir, who recently mentored Kolkata Knight Riders to their third IPL title, expressed his desire to coach the Indian team. He emphasized the honor of representing 140 crore Indians and the importance of fearlessness in achieving success. Gambhir emerged as the top candidate after VVS Laxman declined interest in the head coach role. The new head coach is set to lead the team in all formats for three-and-a-half years starting from July 2024.

author: Erica Yokoyama
title: Japan’s Exports Grow Most Since 2022 on Boost from Weak Yen
mainText: Japan’s exports grew at the fastest clip since late 2022, with a 13.5% increase from a year ago in May. This surge was aided by a 14.9% weaker yen against the dollar, benefiting exporters but also leading to increased costs for importers. The trade deficit widened to $7.7 billion, driven by stronger shipments and a weaker currency. Concerns over cost-push inflation have been raised, with the weak yen impacting consumer sentiment. Exports to the US rose by 23.9%, to China by 17.8%, while those to the EU fell by 10.1%. The increase in car exports was notable, with a 13.6% rise in the wake of automakers resuming operations after a safety certification scandal. However, the momentum may be affected by the scandal’s fallout. Other products that saw gains included semiconductor manufacturing equipment and electronic components. The potential for a resurgence in cost-push inflation due to the weakened yen is raising concerns, impacting private consumption and consumer sentiment. BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda stressed the need to monitor the yen and import prices' impact on the broader economy. The outlook is uncertain as mixed signals from key overseas markets, such as the US and China, indicate varying economic performances. Japan's export growth is an encouraging sign for the manufacturing sector amidst these challenges.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Luxury sales are flattening amid a self-inflicted creativity crisis and price hikes, study finds
mainText: MILAN -- The post-pandemic surge in global sales of luxury handbags, shoes and apparel is set to stall this year amid a creativity crisis and price hikes as brands shift focus to the biggest spending customers, a new study by the Bain consultancy said Tuesday. Bain is forecasting flat worldwide luxury sales in 2024 following a slight first-quarter dip, according to the study commissioned by the Altagamma association. The consultancy cited political uncertainty during a presidential election year in the United States as well as economic uncertainty in China that has brought on a phenomenon of “luxury shaming." Beyond socioeconomic factors and rising geopolitical tensions, the slowdown is also partly “self-inflicted,’’ said Bain partner Claudia D’Arpizio. She cited a “creativity crisis,’’ in the sector, as a number of major fashion houses are transitioning creative directors, and a new focus on the super-wealthy customers, at the expense of the aspirational middle class and Gen-Z youngsters who fueled growth before the pandemic. “There is a lack of clarity for many of these brands. They are making attempts to regain focus. It is five, six brands under turn-around, big ones. This is not helping the overall excitement,’’ D'Arpizio told The Associated Press. “This is a supply-driven industry. When you have the brands really in tune with customer needs, it usually reacts quickly.’’ She said some “tweaks” are needed on strategy and price points, adding that “you can’t grow without the middle class and younger generations.” Flat global luxury sales forecasts follow a pent-up post-pandemic spending surge that pushed sales during the 2021-23 period up 24% over 2019 levels. Last year, sales of personal luxury goods grew by 4% to 362 billion euros (about $388 billion) from 349 euros in 2022, due largely to a resurgence of U.S. and Asian tourism to Europe fueling purchases. Add in luxury travel, fine art, cars and yachts, the vast global luxury market expanded to 1.5 trillion euros last year — highlighting a trend toward experiences over tangible goods. Japan is a bright spot as the return of foreign tourists with the yen at the lowest level to the U.S. dollar in 20 years, while Europe continues strong trends due to tourist spending and an increase in local consumption, especially in French and Italian cities.

author: Benzinga Neuro
title: Nvidia's Rise To Surpass Microsoft And Apple As World's Most Valuable Company Linked To 'Once-In-A-Genera
mainText: Noted economist Mohamed El-Erian recently took to X, formerly Twitter, to acknowledge the extraordinary rise of Nvidia Corp. NVDA as a technological powerhouse. He highlighted the company’s journey from a little-known chipmaker to the world’s most valuable company. What Happened: On Tuesday, El-Erian shared his thoughts on the remarkable ascent of Nvidia. He referred to the company’s success as an “amazing, and once unthinkable phenomenon” associated with a once-in-a-generation technological transformation. El-Erian’s tweet was accompanied by a Bloomberg article detailing Nvidia’s journey from its IPO in 1999 to its current status as the world’s most valuable company, surpassing the likes of Microsoft Corp. MSFT and Apple Inc. AAPL. Why It Matters: Nvidia’s rise to the top is largely attributed to its strategic focus on graphics chips and the vision of co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang. The company’s chips have become the backbone of emerging technologies, from advanced graphics interfaces to autonomous vehicles to a new wave of AI products. Benzinga reported earlier that Nvidia’s market cap climbed to $3.33 trillion, making it the most valuable public company in the world. Furthermore, an investor pointed out that Nvidia’s projected free cash flow over the next two years is expected to exceed that of Microsoft, indicating a bright future for the company. While Apple recently unveiled its AI strategy, Nvidia’s continued success in the AI sector has positioned it as a leader in the industry. Price Action: On Tuesday, Nvidia shares closed 3.5% higher at $135.58 in the regular session and gained another 0.6% in the after-hours session, according to Benzinga Pro data.

author: Amy Beth Hanson
title: Canal pipe breaks, threatening a northern Montana irrigation project and drinking water
mainText: Two century-old steel pipes on the Blackfeet Indian Reservation in Montana failed, causing local flooding and threatening water supply for 14,000 residents. The pipes convey water to irrigate cropland, and their failure has raised concerns about drinking water availability, especially in Havre. The first pipe split open, leading to flooding and subsequent destabilization of a second pipe. No injuries were reported. The Bureau of Reclamation closed the headgates diverting water into a 9-mile canal after the breach, causing the canal to drain through the broken pipes over 36 hours. The 600 cubic feet per second flow reduced to a trickle by Tuesday. The pipes were part of a siphon system carrying water across a ravine to irrigate cropland. The failure occurred before a $100 million headgates replacement project, impacting farmers and businesses. Design work on replacing the pipes is 60% complete. The breach is labeled a 'catastrophic failure,' threatening an economic disaster for north-central Montana. Farmers with 120,000 acres of land rely on the irrigation water. The flooding caused damage to property and disrupted utilities, showing the extent of the impact.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Body found in hunt for missing man Ronny Okeke, police treating death as suspicious
mainText: Police have found the body of missing Auckland man Ronny Okeke and are now treating the death as suspicious. Police said yesterday the investigation team and Police Search and Rescue had been searching parts of the Kaimai Ranges. The location the body was found was some 130km from where Okeke was last spotted in Sandringham in late April. Auckland CIB Detective Inspector Glenn Baldwin said inquiries led the team to carry out a search that resulted in finding the body. He said police came across the body after searching a section of bush in the Kaimai Range. "A scene examination has been conducted and the body has now been removed from the site. Formal identification procedures still need to be carried out, however based on the information we have gathered to this point in the investigation we believe that this is Ronny." Baldwin said police had spoken with Okeke's family in Nigeria overnight. "This is news that no family ever wants to hear, and they are devastated that Ronny will not be coming home," he said. "A post-mortem is scheduled to take place over the coming days, and this will hopefully assist our team in shedding some light around Okeke's death." Police earlier said they believed he was involved in an altercation on or around April 27, the day he was last seen, but have not revealed the other party or parties in the dispute. "What we do know is that this altercation occurred, and Ronny has not been heard from since," Baldwin said last week. During the inquiry into his disappearance police repeatedly said they had grave concerns for him. Baldwin said police were committed to finding what happened surrounding the death. "Police have previously executed search warrants and spoken with a person of interest in this investigation. A forensic examination of Ronny's mobile phone is continuing after it was recovered as part of inquiries in previous weeks." Police wanted to hear from anyone with information about Okeke's death. Okeke, 60, was charged as part of a major money laundering operation in 2021, but the charges were dropped later that year. Money laundering charges Okeke was charged with two counts of money laundering as part of Operation Ida in May 2021.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: IDF officials under fire for mishandling Hamas raid intelligence
mainText: IDF officials, as well as the military's Unit 8200, are embroiled in a blame game over responsibility for an intelligence document that detailed Hamas's plan to raid Israel and kidnap 250 people on October 7. This document was highlighted in a report by Kan News on Monday, which revealed that the document's critical information was not properly processed or forwarded to relevant senior officials. The document, titled 'Detailed End-to-End Raid Training,' was distributed on September 19, 2023, by Unit 8200 and described in detail the series of exercises conducted by Hamas's elite units. According to sources within the IDF on Tuesday, Unit 8200 failed to draw clear conclusions from the document and did not distribute it to the highest-ranking officials. Instead, the document was discovered on October 1 by an intelligence officer in the Gaza Division, who recognized its significance but did not escalate it to senior commanders, opting to inform less senior officials instead. This mishandling of critical intelligence has led to significant embarrassment and a lack of accountability within the IDF and Unit 8200. An earlier report by Kan News on Monday revealed that the IDF had detailed knowledge of Hamas's intentions weeks before the October 7 massacre. The ongoing investigation aims to address how such a lapse in security could occur despite having detailed advance knowledge of Hamas's plans.

author: Nicole Dorfman
title: Ute Highway closed between Longmont and Lyons following motorcycle crash
mainText: Ute Highway is closed while emergency crews respond to an injury crash between Longmont and Lyons on Tuesday afternoon. According to Boulder County Sheriff’s Office public information officer Vinnie Montez, crews were dispatched to an injury crash around 3:11 p.m. Tuesday at North 53rd Avenue and Ute Highway. Crews were advised that the crash involved a motorcycle and a deer and Montez said that two people riding the motorcycle were injured during the crash. According to Colorado State Patrol Sgt. Patrick Rice, two people were transported to the local hospital via helicopter with serious injuries. Multiple roads surrounding the area have been closed down for the response and investigation, according to Montez. According to the Boulder County Sheriff’s Office post on X, eastbound traffic is closed on North Foothills Parkway and westbound traffic is closed at 61st Street and Ute Highway.

author: Nicky Andrews
title: Boulder man sentenced 36 years to life for child sex assault
mainText: A Boulder man has been sentenced to 36 years to life for sexually assaulting a Longmont girl after promising her drugs to lure her to his apartment multiple times. Ian Morrison, 39, was found guilty by a jury in April of sexual assault on a child with a pattern of abuse, aggravated sexual assault on a child, distribution of a controlled substance to a minor, two counts of enticement of a child, 15 counts of sexual exploitation of a child, contributing to the delinquency of a minor, and possession of a controlled substance. One count of possession of child sexual exploitation material was dismissed. On Tuesday, Morrison was sentenced to a total sentence of 36 years to life in prison. Under Colorado law, some sex offenses are subject to indeterminate sentencing, which means a defendant can be kept in prison until they can complete sex offender treatment and successfully petition for parole, even after their initial sentence period has passed. Morrison had 796 days of credit for time served. Salomone ruled that Morrison was not a sexually violent predator but sexual offender registration would be required. During the sentencing hearing, Deputy District Attorney Michelle Sudano requested a sentence of 50 years to life, while defense attorney Sam Dunn requested 16 years to life. Sudano said Morrison “groomed” the victim, leading her to drop out of school and feel “unsafe and worried.” Sudano said in one “terrifying” instance, the victim and her mother went to a restaurant in Longmont and the next day the victim received a rideshare request from Morrison that was from the restaurant to his apartment in Boulder. Sudano said to this day, the victim doesn’t know how Morrison knew she was at the restaurant. Sudano noted that Morrison also reached out to two other minors while his case was still pending. In response, Dunn spoke about Morrison’s character that he had seen through the letters Morrison sent to his family while incarcerated. “In those letters he was asking family about how they were doing, about their health, about loved ones, about people he hadn’t spoken with,” Dunn said. Dunn later described Morrison as, “an individual I’ve come to know as not someone who was concerned necessarily for himself which I think most people are in that situation.” “What I’m asking the court to do in terms to rehabilitation is take into account the fact he was law abiding through his life, this is despite a lot of the turmoil and struggles he went ...

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: El Paso County school districts receive BEST grant funding
mainText: Three school districts across El Paso County are among this year’s recipients of the Colorado Department of Education’s annual Building Excellent Schools Today (BEST) Grant funding. Widefield School District 3, Hanover School District 28 and Peyton School District 23-JT are among this year’s 19 recipients of approximately $183 million to replace aging infrastructure and, in some cases, entire schools. Since 2008, BEST has awarded about $3.7 billion in grants for the construction of schools as well as general construction and renovation of existing school facility systems and structures. During its June meeting last week, the State Board of Education approved 19 school construction grants for 15 school districts, two charter schools and one Board of Cooperative Educational Services. “Colorado students and educators need and deserve high-quality spaces and places for learning,” education commissioner Susana Córdova said in a news release. “BEST grants not only support school districts with new construction but also provide funding to keep existing buildings in good repair.” About $120 million for this year’s projects will be funded by income from the Colorado State Land Board, marijuana excise taxes, Colorado Lottery spillover and earned interest. For the remaining $63 million, applicants will be expected to contribute matching funds. In the event that an awarded project fails to secure its matching funds, a separate list of backup projects has also been prioritized this year and includes upgrades at Colorado Early Colleges Colorado Springs, James Irwin Elementary School-Howard and James Irwin Elementary School-Astrozon. Peyton Elementary School will replace its 30-year-old roof for $807,000 through a combination of grant funding and the district’s general fund, capital reserve and a previously passed mill levy. According to the district’s application for the grant, the roof’s construction is scheduled for summer 2025. “We are unable to predict when catastrophic failure of our roof system will occur,” the application reads. “We understand our roof is beyond its useful life span and the significance of the shrinkage, frequency and severity of the water entry events will increase.” Over in Fountain, Prairie Heights Elementary School will receive over $13.2 million to address its failing roof, inadequate water treatment, improper security measures, mechanical system failures, inadequate electrical systems, improper ventilation, and sewage backups stemming from aging facilities. Nearly $8 million will come from the grant, while 5.3 million will be funded by the district’s utilities department and a 2022 bond. In D-3, the grant worth up to nearly $2.9 million will finance a new roof, HVAC system and new boilers for Janitell Junior High School. Per the agreement, the district will match over $5 million toward the project. The funds come by way of a certificate of participation loan, which is financing for capital assets paid out of existing operating funds instead of selling bonds from an election. The district has been awarded six BEST grants since 2019, with over $5.2 million going toward improved safety and security, asbestos removal, boiler replacements and other building renovations across its schools. Elsewhere in Colorado Springs, Atlas Preparatory School, Harrison School District 2 and Mountain Song Community School were among last year’s beneficiaries of over $32.5 million in upgrades due, in part, to BEST grants. The current roof, rooftop units, and boilers at Janitell are over 50 years old and are among the renovation projects at 17 schools recently detailed throughout the district that have yet to begin. “With this BEST grant, the district will be able to offset some of the costs of the project which will allow us to put more district CAP (capital improvement projects) funds into needs for other sites,” said D-3’s chief operations officer Dave Gish in a separate news release. Though there are no plans for votes on this year’s November ballot, the hope is for future funding for the remaining projects to come from a future bond. “We will continue to apply for grants and seek additional funding opportunities, but we are looking at asking voters for assistance in 2025 to give our staff, students and community the facilities they need and deserve,” Gish said.

author: Grace Ptak
title: CU Boulder report shows how drinking tea saved lives in 18th-century England
mainText: Drinking tea (and boiling the water for it) was so popular that it may have accidentally saved lives in 18th-century England, according to a new study by an economics professor at the University of Colorado Boulder. Francisca Antman, a professor of economics and an associate dean in the College of Arts and Sciences, found quantitative evidence to answer the question: How important is water quality for human and economic development? Her data helped prove that the health benefits of boiling water before drinking it helped to propel human and economic development during this time period in England. Studying tea’s effects during this time period is ideal, said Antman, because it occurs before the importance of clean water was general knowledge. The English didn’t adopt the practice of boiling water before consumption because an outside source told them it would make them healthier. Rather, it was an internal choice, motivated only by the desire to drink a trendy beverage at the time, she said. “I’m looking at this time when water quality was improved by... exposure to water quality, establishing a relationship between the introduction of boiling water for tea and its impact on mortality rates in different areas of England. The study aimed to demonstrate the positive effects of this behavior on public health and economic development, offering insights for potential improvements in water quality in modern times. author: Rohan James Lloyd
title: Bohemian, artist, conservationist: breathing humanity into the man who fought to protect Queensland’s rainforest and reef
mainText: John Büsst, also known as 'The Bingil Bay Bastard', was a bohemian artist and conservationist who fought to protect Queensland's rainforest and reef. In the 1960s, he campaigned against deforestation and army weapons testing in north Queensland, leading to the protection of nearly 100,000 acres of land. Büsst played a crucial role in the Save the Great Barrier Reef Campaign, which successfully prevented mineral, oil, and gas exploitation on the reef. Despite his efforts, Büsst passed away in 1971 before witnessing the full impact of his work. Iain McCalman's book, 'John Büsst: Bohemian artist and saviour of reef and rainforest', portrays Büsst not as a calloused cynic but as a devoted brother, artist, and conservationist. The book sheds light on Büsst's early life, his transition from privilege to environmental activism, and his impactful conservation campaigns. Büsst's story is a reminder of the interconnectedness between humans and nature, emphasizing the importance of protecting our environments for future generations.

author: Victoria Minson
title: Early childhood educators are not ‘babysitters’. What do their jobs really involve?
mainText: A new push is underway to make early education and care more affordable for Australian families, with a focus on increasing access for children under five. However, this initiative faces challenges due to the critical need for more early childhood teachers and educators, who currently experience low pay and unattractive working conditions. Research indicates a lack of societal appreciation for the skilled and hardworking individuals in this sector, often misrepresented as mere 'babysitters'. Early childhood educators play a crucial role in laying the foundation for a child's development, engaging in activities that promote growth across various skills. The demand for early childhood staff is escalating, driven by free kindergarten programs in most Australian states. Early childhood teachers require university qualifications, while educators typically hold a Certificate III or diploma. Both professionals collaborate to design and implement educational programs, with teachers having additional planning and administrative responsibilities. The sector is undergoing significant changes to meet the growing demand for quality early education, highlighting the importance of recognizing and valuing the work of early childhood educators.

author: Star Wars
title: Star Wars: The Acolyte Episode 4 - Review
mainText: The fourth episode of Star Wars: The Acolyte ramps up the action and character development, as Mae, Osha, and their allies are brought back together, with Mae's Master finally revealed to the Jedi. The episode delves into Osha's potential return to the Jedi Order and explores Mae's complex motivations, hinting at possible redemption but leaving room for unpredictability. The installment features exciting Star Wars action and creature moments, along with Jedi teamwork rarely seen in live-action. The review discusses the characters' inner conflicts, the Jedi perspective on death and the Force, and speculates on Qimir's true identity. The episode sets up a compelling cliffhanger with the dramatic entrance of Mae's Master. However, the death of the wookiee Jedi character Kelnacca is deemed a disappointment to fans who were anticipating more from the character. Despite some narrative stumbling blocks, the episode offers engaging moments and character interactions, setting the stage for further twists and revelations in the series.

author: Star Wars
title: Star Wars: The Acolyte - Review
mainText: The review of Star Wars: The Acolyte Season 1, episode 4 delves into the character dynamics between Mae, Osha, and their allies, as Mae's Master is finally revealed to the Jedi. The episode explores Osha's conflicted feelings about rejoining the Jedi Order and Mae's ambiguous motivations. The reviewer highlights the predictable nature of Star Wars stories where Dark Side users tend to be redeemed, expressing hope for a different outcome for Mae. The episode showcases a rare team-up of Jedi characters and introduces prequel character Ki-Adi-Mundi. A thrilling encounter with creatures on Khofar adds an exciting Star Wars element, while the aftermath deepens the Jedi's perspective on death and the Force. The review speculates on a theory about Qimir possibly posing as his own master and discusses the unfortunate demise of the wookiee Jedi, Kelnacca. The intense cliffhanger involving Mae's Master using the Force against multiple Jedi is praised. Overall, the episode is praised for its character development, action sequences, and intriguing plot twists.

author: Mashable Team
title: NYT Connections Today: See Hints And Answers For June 19
mainText: Connections is a popular word game by The New York Times where players need to group four words that share something in common. Each set has 16 words split into four categories, and players can rearrange the board to help find connections. The game resets daily, and players have up to four mistakes before the game ends. Today's categories include Positions in Favor, Go Out With, Multitude, and Things Read in Divination. The solutions for June 19 are provided for each category. More hints and answers are available for those seeking to improve their gameplay. The game is gaining attention similar to Wordle due to its challenging and engaging nature.

author: Khayl Adam
title: Random: Fans Continue to Hollow, 737 Days Since Last Silksong News
mainText: Silksong, the elusive, highly anticipated follow-up to developer Team Cherry's Hollow Knight, was not shown during Summer Game Fest, Xbox's showcase, or Nintendo's recent Direct. In response, fans, long neglected, have continued to post memes and cope in whatever way they can As noted by PC Gamer, Silksong is always one of the most anticipated potential games at any given showcase, and it's been an age since we saw it last. Announced in 2019, and with the Not-E3 2024 season now over, the reality that the wished-for Silksong will not appear (again) seems to have sunk in. Team Cherry has not posted a video to its YouTube channel in five years; its Twitter account is similarly dormant, and the developer last updated its blog in 2019, wishing fans happy holidays. In April, Silksong was rated in South Korea, which suggests a pulse, but there doesn't appear to be any other outward signs of life from the studio. That doesn't suggest Silksong isn't coming; we're sure it is. But as Team Cherry consists of just three principal devs who live in the land of milk and honey (Australia), we'd imagine they're simply enjoying the good life, sunning themselves on pristine beaches and working at their own pace. According to Reddit napkin math and SteamDB, Hollow Knight may have sold 8+ million copies on Steam alone, which translates into a hell of a lot of dollarydoos, and that's before taking console sales into account. title: ACME opens its doors to the world's lead industry and to a greener future for lead recycling
mainText: TAIPEI, June 19, 2024 /PRNewswire/ -- Leading Taiwanese lead recycler ACME Metal Enterprise, based in the capital Taipei, hosted an open day for key global industry players to show ACE Green Recycling's revolutionary GreenLead™ process in action. Around 30 visitors were shown the world's first full deployment of this technology, many of whom remarked on the total absence of noise, smells, and dust – something unthinkable in a traditional smelter. ACE's technology completely replaces the smelting stage of lead recycling with a room temperature hydrometallurgical process which is fully electrified and produces zero Scope 1 emissions. This is in stark contrast to conventional furnace smelting that involves high temperatures, uses copious fossil fuels, and creates fumes and dust that must be captured in baghouses to avoid it being emitted to the environment. ACME is Taiwan's leading lead recycler, with over 40 years of successful operation. Through its partnership with ACE, ACME plans to set up a plant to recycle 20,000 metric tonnes per year of lead batteries to produce about 12,000 metric tonnes of environmentally friendly GreenLead™, generating nearly USD 30 million in annual revenue for the Taiwanese company. Overtime, ACME plans to become one of the largest producers of emissions-free lead and expand operations across Asia Pacific. The distinguished visitors from Europe, USA and Asia were drawn from other lead producers, major trading houses, engineering consultancies and investors, who were impressed by the high levels of process automation and intentional simplicity of the set up – the magic is in the chemistry, not the engineering, which has been kept as straightforward as possible to minimise costs and maximise reliability. There was universal agreement among the visitors that they felt that they'd witnessed the likely future of global lead recycling. This collaboration with ACME demonstrates ACE's deep commitment to the battery market. Sales of GreenLead™ from ACME's facility will reach the key markets of Taiwan region and Japan, including leading battery OEMs across Asia. ACE is a market leader in both lead and lithium-ion battery recycling technologies and is partnering with companies worldwide to help them set up environmentally friendly battery recycling facilities. The company has a team of over 70 people and is dual headquartered in the US and Singapore. SOURCE ACE Green Recycling

title: Rebounding temperatures through midweek
mainText: SALT LAKE CITY (ABC4) — Happy Tuesday, Utah! We’re seeing temperature shock across the state today following Monday’s wild cold front. Daytime highs are trending 10 to 15 degrees below seasonal averages this afternoon with upper 60s and low 70s for the Wasatch Front. St. George will reach the low 90s while most other areas will see 70s and 80s in southern Utah. The skies are clear today with breezy winds remaining. The unseasonable cold snap we’re seeing today will be very short-lived. Increasing southwest flow across the state into Wednesday will quickly warm temperatures back up to average highs for this time of year. High pressure will be situated to the east of Utah with a trough of low pressure to the west. This will keep a strong southerly component to our weather pattern and allow for another jump in temperatures on Thursday. Daytime highs will climb into the low 90s for the Wasatch Front Thursday afternoon with triple-digit heat returning to St. George. By late week, a surge of monsoonal moisture could be in the works for eastern Utah, bringing the threat of showers and thunderstorms. Moisture should clear out into the weekend and high pressure will build back in for the latter half of the weekend, allowing temperatures to spike once again. With this pattern in place, you expect a significant warm-up with temperatures reaching well-above-normal highs by Sunday. Salt Lake City has a chance to hit 100 degrees again, and St. George could see highs up 107+. Overnight lows may only drop to the mid-to-upper 70s once again, so we could see heat alerts return. It’s still early, so we will keep you forewarned as conditions change, but for now, enjoy the substantial cool down statewide. The 4Warn Weather Team will continue to monitor conditions and keep you posted on changing conditions both on our 4Warn Weather app as well as on-air and online. We are Good4Utah!

title: The era of super-wild weather is already here
mainText: Wildfires in Canada that burned continuously for over a year. Floods that brought Dubai to a standstill. Deadly heat blanketing the streets of New Delhi. The first half of 2024 has laid bare the catastrophic extremes that now characterize the rapidly changing climate on every continent.This week, millions of people along the eastern seaboard of the U.S. — the country’s most populated coastal region — will swelter under a heat dome. Temperatures in Manhattan’s Central Park are set to reach 35 degrees Celsius by Friday. At the southern end of the coast, meanwhile, Florida is in its second week of battling torrential rainfall so intense near Sarasota that it has odds of occurring just once in 500 to 1,000 years. Damages could top $1 billion.A new era of extreme rain prompted the U.S. National Academy of Sciences on Tuesday to recommend a major reboot of the country’s 'probable maximum precipitation” estimates, which guide infrastructure development. They haven’t been updated since 1999 nationally, and in some cases not for 60 years. More than 16,000 at-risk dams and 50 nuclear power plants, all of them aging, face new extremes.

title: New York's 'equal rights' constitutional amendment restored to ballot by appeals court
mainText: A proposed amendment to New York’s constitution, aiming to prohibit discrimination based on 'gender identity' and 'pregnancy outcomes,' has been restored to the November election ballot by a state appeals court. This amendment has been praised by Democrats for protecting abortion rights and criticized by Republicans for the perceived protections it may offer to transgender individuals. The decision by a panel of appellate judges overturned a previous ruling that struck down the Equal Rights Amendment due to procedural errors. New York Attorney General Letitia James hailed the court's decision as a victory for protecting abortion access and vulnerable communities. The proposed amendment would expand the existing ban on discrimination in the New York Constitution to include additional categories like ethnicity, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, and reproductive health care. While not explicitly mentioning abortion rights, the amendment would prevent discrimination against individuals for having the procedure. The lawsuit against the amendment was brought by Republican State Assemblywoman Marjorie Byrnes. Opponents argue that the broad language around sexual orientation and gender could have unintended consequences, such as allowing transgender athletes to compete on female teams. The state Republican Party plans to appeal the decision, contending that the legislature violated the constitution in approving the proposal. Supporters of the amendment assert that it will not affect parental involvement in medical decisions for minors. State Senate Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins expressed satisfaction that the case was dismissed and emphasized the importance of equal rights for all New Yorkers. The amendment will be on the ballot in the 2024 election, with voters needing to approve it for final enactment. Democrats are hopeful that the issue related to abortion will drive voter turnout. Former U.S. Rep. Lee Zeldin criticized the amendment as 'left-wing lunacy' and raised concerns about free speech and parental notification. The court's ruling reinstates the opportunity for New Yorkers to vote on equal rights in November.

title: AI based blood test can predict Parkinson’s seven years before symptoms, finds study
mainText: The findings of a new study has brought good news to a field of medical science which can benefit 10 million people across the globe. We are talking about Parkinson's disease, the world’s fastest growing neurodegenerative disorder. The study has been published in Nature Communications. A team of researchers, led by scientists at University College London (UCL) and University Medical Center Goettingen, Germany, have developed a simple blood test that uses artificial intelligence (AI) to predict Parkinson’s up to seven years before the onset of symptoms."Currently, people with Parkinson’s are treated with dopamine replacement therapy after they have already developed symptoms, such as tremor, slowness of movement and gait, and memory problems. But researchers believe that early prediction and diagnosis would be valuable for finding treatments that could slow or stop Parkinson’s by protecting the dopamine producing brain cells," UCL has said in a press release. To determine Parkinson's disease, the researchers found that when a branch of AI called machine learning, analysed a panel of eight blood based biomarkers whose concentrations are altered in patients with Parkinson’s, it could provide a diagnosis with 100% accuracy. 72 patients who had Rapid Eye Movement Behaviour Disorder (iRBD) were studied for the purpose. 75-80% of these people with iRBD go on to develop synucleinopathy (a type of brain disorder caused by the abnormal buildup of a protein called alpha-synuclein in brain cells) – including Parkinson’s. "When the machine learning tool analysed the blood of these patients it identified that 79% of the iRBD patients had the same profile as someone with Parkinson’s," the researchers have said. Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that primarily affects movement control. It occurs due to the degeneration of dopamine-producing neurons in the substantia nigra, a region of the brain crucial for regulating movement...

title: Guru Hargobind Sahib Birth Anniversary 2024: All You Need to Know About the Sixth Guru of the Sikhs
mainText: The sixth Guru of Sikhism, Guru Hargobind Sahib, was born on June 19, 1595, to Mata Ganga and Guru Arjan Dev, the fifth Guru of the Sikhs. Guru Hargobind is recognised as the driving force behind the Sikh community’s militarisation. With the community at receiving end of persecution by the Mughal rulers, he underlined the need for the populace to cultivate a martial mentality. Guru Hargobind Sahib was always seen with two swords, reflecting the “Miri-Piri” ideology. The first sword, Miri, signified power, whereas Piri represented his spiritual abilities. Guru Hargobind Sahib was an accomplished swordsman, horse rider, and wrestler. He raised an army called Sant Sipahi (Sain Soldiers) to combat the Mughals’ persecution of Sikhs. During Shah Jahan’s rule, the Mughal forces regularly attacked the Sikhs in Kartarpur, Amritsar, and elsewhere. Guru Hargobind fought with the army with courage and resilience, inspiring his fellow Sikhs and laying the foundation stone of the heritage of Sikh warriors. In addition to building the Army, Guru Hargobind actively promoted Sikhism by sending his adherents across the nation to spread Guru Nanak’s teachings. Guru Hargobind was imprisoned for twelve years by Mughal Emperor Jehangir for his efforts to build a formidable army. The Akal Takht, one of Sikhism’s five Takhts (seats of power), was established by Guru Hargobind. He was the Guru for 37 years, 9 months, and 3 days, the longest tenure of any of the ten Gurus. His army was able to overcome Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan four times. Guru Hargobind Sahib constructed the Lohgarh fortress near Amritsar. Its construction began somewhere in the 1620s and was finished in 1710. On March 3, 1544, he died in Kirtarpur, undivided Punjab. Before his death, Guru Hargobind Sahib chose his grandson Guru Har Rai as the heir to his legacy and the seventh guru in Sikhism.

During Tuesday night's MLB game between the Minnesota Twins and the Tampa Bay Rays, McCarthy was given the honor of throwing the ceremonial first pitch. However, McCarthy's throw didn't go quite as planned, as the ball ended up way off target, missing the catcher by a wide margin. Fans took to social media to troll McCarthy for his poor throw.

author: The Arena Group
title: Magic Johnson Sends Message To Cameron Brink After Horrific Injury
mainText: In Tuesday's meeting with the Connecticut Sun, Los Angeles Sparks fans found themselves holding their breath. Their recent top pick and new face of the franchise, Cameron Brink, went down with what appears to be a leg/knee injury after falling awkwardly. As she was driving to the hoop against the Sun's Brionna Jones, she appeared to slip with her leg also appearing to buckle. Cameron Brink was carried to the locker room after this play. Brink immediately grabbed her left knee, while screaming in pain as her teammates gathered around to check in on her. She was able to limp off of the court under her own power, but wasn't able to go much further as she was eventually carried off by a couple of trainers. As one can imagine, many fans are worried about the Stanford product, and have been sending some prayers and positive thoughts her way. One of the more notable figures to come forward was former Laker legend and NBA Hall of Famer, Magic Johnson. Sending prayers up for Cameron Brink right now. author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Only 4 Third Generation K-Pop Girl Groups Are Still Active - Koreaboo
mainText: The third generation of K-Pop, according to the majority of the fandom, consists of groups that debuted between 2012 and 2017. With such a huge impact made on the K-Pop industry, it’s hard to believe that so few girl groups from the era remain still active. In fact, under the criteria of not being officially disbanded and having a comeback at some point as a whole group within the last 18 months, there are only four third generation K-Pop girl groups that are still active: TWICE, Red Velvet, Dreamcatcher, and OH MY GIRL. TWICE is one of the most active, with their latest comeback being With YOU-th released in February this year. Red Velvet's last comeback was with Chill Kill in November last year, they're about to release their new album, Cosmic, on June 24. Dreamcatcher's most recent comeback was with the single album Luck Inside 7 Doors, released in March this year. OH MY GIRL's last comeback was with the album Golden Hourglass in July 2023. There are a couple of other girl groups like BLACKPINK and MAMAMOO and Cosmic Girls/WJSN who could be argued to still be active. In comparison, there are many more boy groups from the third generation that remain active to this day — over 20, based on the same criteria. Here’s how people are reacting to the revelation that so few third generation girl groups are still active.

author: M.l. Nestel
title: Jan. 6 rioter who walked out of debate loses GA House primary runoff
mainText: A Georgia Republican who served prison time for a conviction related to the Jan. 6 riot at the U.S. Capitol was defeated in a primary runoff for a House seat. Charles Hand failed to best former Trump administration official Wayne Johnson as they dueled to challenge Rep. Sanford Bishop (D-GA) in the general election come Nov. 5, The Associated Press projected. The result at the ballot box comes after Hand stormed out of a primary debate this month after he accused his Republican opponent of "orchestrating attacks on my wife." But Johnson proved he wasn't the one who lobbed attacks on Hand's wife, Mandy Robinson-Hand, who was a co-defendant in his Jan. 6 case. Rather, it was Michael Nixon, another former Republican rival who exited the race last month and endorsed Johnson who aired Hand's wife's criminal past. Robinson-Hand also "spent a year in jail and nine years in probation after she was convicted of a felony oxycodone charge" back in 2008. Hand served 20 days and six months of probation after being found guilty of illegally demonstrating inside the U.S. Capitol on the deadly January 6th riot. He admitted to having "broke off a piece of metal fencing and placed it in his back pants pocket" as rioters clashed with Capitol police. Prior to being punished, Hand didn't show contrition about his role in the riot, telling his wife, 'Like I said it was a perfect time to be a part of history!'. Johnson appeared to write Hand off after bailing out of their debate. “I would like to assume that Chuck Hand’s departure, the way in which he did it today, was his withdrawal from the race,” Johnson told reporters after the debate, per AP. “But it certainly should cause people to pause and think about why he did it and what he was trying to get by doing it.”

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Letter to the editor: Restore protections for dialysis patients
mainText: OPINION: My father’s battle with end-stage renal disease changed our family’s life. I cared for him as he endured dialysis for two years, showing immense courage. He received two transplants, including one of my kidneys, but sadly, he passed away. In his memory, I now advocate for kidney patients and am pursuing a master’s degree in physiology at Georgetown University. Dialysis patients, like my father, often face financial hardships. As a business owner, he paid up to $1,400 monthly for private insurance to receive better treatment options than state insurance could provide. Previously, end-stage renal disease patients could keep their private insurance for 30 months before transitioning to Medicare. However, a recent Supreme Court decision opened the door for private insurers to push new dialysis patients off of their plans, leading to fewer options and more uncovered expenses. D.C. Delegate Eleanor Holmes Norton should support the Restore Protections for Dialysis Patients Act to ensure 30 months of private coverage for new dialysis patients. It’s the least we can do for such a vulnerable community. KATE ROAM Washington

author: Amber Carlson
title: Boulder County GOP supports push to recall state GOP officers
mainText: The Boulder County Republican Party has joined a growing number of county GOP offices across the state in supporting a push to oust state party officers, including Colorado GOP Chair Dave Williams. Williams has been under fire, even from within his own party, in part because of anti-Pride emails he sent out to supporters this month. In a June 3 email with the subject line “God hates Pride”, Williams refers to LGBTQ+ people as “godless groomers” and “woke creeps” who are out to “attack what is decent, holy, and righteous so they can ultimately harm our children.” Colorado Public Radio reported that GOP leaders in several different counties have called for Williams to resign or be removed over his anti-Pride emails, with some accusing him of “continuing to incite hatred and further division in Colorado.” According to a statement, members of the Boulder County Republican executive committee voted to support the state central committee convening a meeting to consider removing “the elected state officers of the Colorado GOP.” As reasons, the statement cited Williams’ “divisive” anti-Pride emails “calling all people who identify as LGBT evil, threatening to dox members who disagree with his comments, and labeling anyone who questions his ethics and leadership as part of the radical left child-mutilating agenda.” In the statement, the committee also accused Williams of running his congressional campaign for the Fifth Congressional District, which includes Colorado Springs and the surrounding area... and cultural elitists,” Williams wrote.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Piyush Goyal rejects speculations on change of leadership in Maharashtra BJP
mainText: Union Minister and senior BJP leader Piyush Goyal rejected speculations on a change of leadership in the party's Maharashtra unit following the party's dismal performance in the recent Lok Sabha elections.Goyal said that the BJP leadership has no such idea and no such discussion has taken place in the party's core committee meeting. There were speculations that Rao Saheb Patil would be made the state president.Earlier on Tuesday, a meeting of the Maharashtra BJP core committee was held at the BJP national headquarters under the leadership of BJP National President JP Nadda and Union Home Minister Amit Shah.According to sources, the party's central leadership has given a road map for the assembly elections in Maharashtra. The reasons for losing the Lok Sabha elections were also discussed in the meeting, they said.After the meeting, Deputy Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis told reporters that all such issues were discussed, including those that had impacted the Lok Sabha election results, and how to overcome those shortcomings in the upcoming assembly elections.Fadnavis said that the BJP will enter the fray to contest the assembly elections with full force.Union Ministers Bhupendra Yadav, Ashwini Vaishnav, Deputy Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, BJP National General Secretary Vinod Tawde, State President Chandrashekhar Bawankule, Pankaja Munde, Ashish Shelar, Chandrakant Patil, and Rao Sahib Patil were present in the meeting.During the meeting, Bhupender Yadav was appointed as the in-charge for Maharashtra and Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw will be the co-in-charge for the state.The BJP dipped to nine seats in Maharashtra against 23 in the 2019 Lok Sabha polls. The vote share stood at 26.18 per cent. The Congress, on the other hand, marginally improved its seat share by securing 13 seats in the state.The Shiv Sena and the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) won seven and one seats respectively, taking the total tally of the NDA to 17. The Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackrey) got nine seats while the Nationalist Congress Party - Sharadchandra Pawar won eight seats. (ANI)

author: David Kroman
title: Seattle commission recommends against new test for police recruits
mainText: A new report from Seattle’s independent Civil Service Commission undercuts a key goal of legislation recently passed by the Seattle City Council aimed at improving the process for hiring new police officers. Andrea Scheele, executive director of the Public Safety Civil Service Commission, concluded it was neither practical nor advisable for Seattle to use a new police recruitment test that has a higher rate of candidates who pass than the current test. In her report, Scheele recommended Seattle continue using its current test, developed in 2012, and look to 2025 to launch a competitive bidding process if city officials want to make a change. Jamie Housen, spokesperson for Mayor Bruce Harrell, strongly disputed Scheele’s analysis, calling the conclusion 'incredibly disappointing.' For a Seattle City Hall that’s promised to grow the size of the Police Department, there are limited levers that can be pulled to slow the exodus of current officers and fill the pipeline with new ones. Pay raises, approved recently, were the top priority for the council and mayor. Applications have increased in the months since, Scheele wrote. The council ratified a new contract with the city’s largest police union this year, making Seattle officers the highest paid in the state. Both the mayor’s office and council President Sara Nelson zeroed in specifically on the city’s recruitment test. In Washington, most departments use a test from a different company, called the Public Safety Test. As they seek to compete with neighboring departments more directly for officers, members of the mayor’s office and City Council pushed for the commission to adopt the new test. However, staff with the provider of the proposed new test declined to answer Scheele’s questions and signaled they were uninterested in working with Seattle. Scheele raised several logistical and possible legal hurdles to adopting a new test, ultimately recommending Seattle stick with the National Testing Network test.

author: Sir Clive Woodward
title: SIR CLIVE WOODWARD: Here's what I really think of Eddie Jones... and why moving Marcus Smith...
mainText: SIR CLIVE WOODWARD: Here's what I really think of Eddie Jones... and why moving Marcus Smith mid-match against Japan would be madness! England's decision to start Marcus Smith at No 10 against Japan on Saturday is the right one. But I absolutely hate the idea that he will be moved from fly-half to full back at some point in the game in Tokyo to accommodate Fin Smith alongside him as head coach Steve Borthwick hinted at on Tuesday. I've really liked Borthwick's approach and team selection this year. But I can't stand this kind of premeditated diplomatic selection. When I was England coach, Matt Dawson and Kyran Bracken gave me similar headaches at scrum-half, but you must have a clear selection in your mind and avoid diplomatic substitutions. I do not see Marcus as an international full back. His talents make him passable at No 15, but playing him there is such a waste. The sooner Borthwick abandons the Marcus Smith full-back idea, the better. It's a strong England side. But make no bones about it, they need to win. It will be hot and humid in Tokyo, but England can thrive. England should have too much for Japan. But it's about how England play too. Of course they will be up against their old friend Jones who had a disastrous second half of his time in charge of England and who didn't cover himself in glory in his short stint with Australia.
