author: India Today World Desk
title: Five shocking points from Hinduja family trial
mainText: Four members of the Hinduja family, Britain's wealthiest, are being tried for human trafficking in Switzerland over charges that they grossly underpaid an Indian domestic help at their Lake Geneva villa. It was argued that they spent more on their dog than on the salary of an Indian domestic help. The prosecution's arguments in court have revealed five shocking facts, including that there were three more plaintiffs who withdrew their case.The Hindujas, who have vehemently denied the allegations, face up to five and a half years in prison if convicted.The human trafficking trial is against Prakash Hinduja, his wife Kamal, their son Ajay, and his wife Namrata.Prosecutor Yves Bertossa asked the court to hand five and a half years in prison to Prakash and his wife, while he sought four-a-half-year term for Ajay and his wife, according to The Daily Mail.Prakash and Kamal Hinduja, aged 78 and 75, did not attend the trial, citing health issues. Prosecutor Yves Bertossa criticised their absence, suggesting they could have managed a short flight from Cannes to Geneva.Here are the five shocking details that have been revealed by the prosecution against the Hindujas.1) SPENT MORE ON PET DOG THAN ON HELP'S SALARYThe prosecution claims the Hindujas paid an Indian domestic help just seven Swiss francs (approximately £6.19) for an 18-hour workday, while spending 8,584 francs (£7,616) on their pet dog annually. Prosecutor Yves Bertossa has demanded the family cover 1 million francs in court costs and pay 3.5 million francs into a compensation fund for the staff.The defence lawyers said salaries alone did not reflect the overall pay and benefits for staff, arguing that the staff were provided with lodgings. A lawyer also claimed that a staffer said her pay was good compared to what she earned in India. The woman came to the job in Geneva of her own free will, and came back again and again, the lawyer added, according to The Daily Mail.2) HINDUJAS SEIZED PASSPORT OF THEIR INDIAN HELPThe Hindujas allegedly seized the passport of the Indian domestic help, the prosecution claimed in a Swiss court. The family members are facing human trafficking charges which centre around claims they illegally brought staff in and out of Switzerland after confiscating their passports, according to The Daily Mail.The domestic helps couldn’t leave the house without their employer’s permission and had little to no freedom, they argued. 3) PAID IN INDIA, DIDN'T HAVE ANY MONEY IN SWITZERLANDThe Swiss prosecution team has alleged that the Hindujas paid for Indian domestic help in India and in Indian currency. This ensured that the person was hamstrung without any local currency in Switzerland."They were paid for their work in India, meaning they had no Swiss money and therefore limited freedom in the country," The Daily Mail quoted the prosecution as saying.4) EXTRA-LONG 18-HOUR WORKDAYSThe prosecution claimed that the Indian domestic help was made to work 18 hours a day by the Hindujas, and that the staff contracts didn’t specify working hours or days off as those employed had to be available as needed. However, the defence team argued that the prosecution had been misleading in its characterization of the workers' pay and had "exaggerated" working hours."When they sit down to watch a movie with the kids, can that be considered work? I think not," Ajay Hinduja's attorney Yael Hayat said. 5) SOME OTHERS WENT FOR OUT-OF-COURT SETTLEMENTWhile the prosecution tried to nail the four Hindujas in the case of the Indian domestic help, its argument revealed there were at least two other plaintiffs. The case, according to reports, follows a recent settlement where three plaintiffs withdrew their civil suit against the Hindujas, reported the Daily Mail.A financial settlement over exploitation was reached last week, reports the BBC. The Hindujas are being tried for human trafficking, a serious criminal offence in Switzerland, says the BBC.Published By: Sushim MukulPublished On: Jun 19, 2024

author: The Economist
title: Palmer Luckey and Anduril want to shake up armsmaking
mainText: Palmer Luckey owns six helicopters. He would like a seventh: a Chinook, the workhorse of Western armed forces. When your guest Schumpeter, meeting Mr Luckey in London, suggests that the British Army might sell him one, he laments that “eccentric US civilians” are low on the priority list of buyers. “I’ve been thinking,” he says, “I need to maybe hit up the Taliban.” Mr Luckey, who co-founded Anduril, a defence-technology company, in 2017, is joking. Still, coming from a mulleted 31-year-old in a Hawaiian shirt and flip-flops, who made his fortune selling a virtual-reality company to Facebook and has now branched out into Game Boy replicas, it sounds plausible. Despite his eccentricities, Mr Luckey is not a man to be taken lightly. Anduril is now nipping at the heels of America’s biggest armsmakers.

author: Nicholas Rossolillo
title: Is It Finally Time to Buy This Leading Chip Stock Again?
mainText: It's no secret that over the last three years, top semiconductor manufacturer Texas Instruments has underperformed both the S&P 500 and the semiconductor industry by a wide margin. So far in 2024, Texas Instruments stock has been heating back up, rallying nearly 20% since April. The latest earnings report provided limited reasons for optimism, but it turns out a notable activist investor purchasing shares might be the best reason investors may want to take heed. The activist investor in question here is Elliott Management, which disclosed a $2.5 billion stake in TI stock to return the business to free cash flow-per-share growth. TI's capex holiday turns into a spending spree. The spending began at exactly the time TI's revenue and profitability took a hit -- due to the chip shortage flipping to chip oversupply during the bear market of 2022 and 2023. Is the stock a buy if TI management listens? Elliott hardly owns enough stock to dictate this semiconductor company's future plans. However, I believe TI management should listen. The current pace of capex spending and facility construction would leave TI with a huge amount of unused manufacturing capacity in five years' time. TI should split the difference between Elliott's proposal and its own current trajectory. I'm not buying TI stock right now. If management eases up on forecasted capital expenditures, this could become a much better-performing stock than it has been over the last few years. Keep a close eye on this one.

author: Aine Fox
title: Windrush report author ‘delighted’ after court ruling on ditched recommendations
mainText: All recommendations arising from an independent review into the Windrush scandal must be brought in “without further delay” to ensure justice is served, the solicitor behind the report into the Government’s handling of the situation has said. Wendy Williams said she was “delighted” by a High Court ruling on Wednesday that a decision to drop some of the 30 recommendations was unlawful. Windrush victim Trevor Donald, 68, brought legal action against the Home Office over the decision not to proceed with all of the recommendations made to the Government by a review launched in the wake of the scandal. Ms Williams published her Windrush Lessons Learned Review in 2020 and all 30 recommendations were originally accepted by then-home secretary Priti Patel. But in January 2023 it was confirmed that Suella Braverman, who was in post as home secretary by that stage, had dropped three. The Windrush scandal – which campaigners have since said should be known as the Home Office scandal – erupted in 2018 when British citizens, mostly from the Caribbean, were wrongly detained, deported or threatened with deportation despite having the right to live in Britain. Many lost homes and jobs and were denied access to healthcare and benefits. The three recommendations dropped by the Home Office during Ms Braverman’s time in office were: a commitment to establish a migrants’ commissioner; to increase the powers of the independent chief inspector of borders and immigration (ICIBI); and to hold reconciliation events. In her judgment, Mrs Justice Heather Williams ruled that dropping two of the recommendations – related to the migrants’ commissioner role and the ICIBI – had a “disproportionately prejudicial effect upon Windrush victims” and indirectly discriminated against them. The judge also said it was unlawful and “conspicuously unfair” for the ICIBI recommendation to be shelved without consulting Windrush community representatives and Ms Williams. She said: “I conclude that an inference can be drawn from the evidence before the court that the decision not to proceed… was a matter of considerable concern and hurt to a significant number of Windrush victims, given, in particular, that a cause of the scandal was a failure to listen to the voices of those from the Windrush community.” The Home Office said it is “carefully considering” the judgment. Ms Williams, in a statement to the PA news agency after the ruling, said: “I’m pleased that I was able to provide information for the JR proceedings and delighted that Mrs Justice Williams has ruled that the decision not to proceed with all 30 of my recommendations was unlawful. “I hope the Government, and Home Office, will now ensure that all my recommendations are implemented without further delay, so that those affected by the Windrush scandal can fully receive the justice they deserve.” Mr Donald, who was born in Jamaica in 1955, arrived in the UK in 1967 and lived here for the next 43 years. Having visited Jamaica in 2010, he was refused entry when he attempted to return to the UK and at that point, his lawyers state, he became a Windrush victim. He was eventually allowed to re-enter the UK following the emergence of the scandal in 2018 and was recognized as having indefinite leave to remain, before being granted British citizenship in January 2022. In her judgment, Mrs Heather Justice Williams noted Mr Donald “missed critical moments in the lives of his children and lost his council flat and most of his possessions”. A further hearing is now expected to consider any damages due to Mr Donald. Dr. Connie Sozi, solicitor for Mr Donald, said the judgment “gives the Government, yet again, an opportunity to do the right thing and properly ensure that it has learned lessons from the past”. She suggested the Government could “show its commitment” to doing this by implementing all three recommendations.” She suggested an inquiry could be needed into the scandal. She said: “The ease at which the Government could renege (on previously accepted recommendations) suggests a stronger form of accountability is needed into the Windrush scandal. “That would be through an inquiry. Whether it’s the current Government or the next, public interest would be served by this.” Black Equity Organisation’s (BEO) chief executive Timi Okuwa said after the ruling: “With Windrush Day on Saturday, we remember and stand with all Windrush scandal victims, survivors and their descendants. “Therefore, BEO welcomes today’s decision that confirms that Suella Braverman’s decision to drop these recommendations was unlawful. “We are especially pleased that Mrs Justice Williams recognized the discrimination of the Windrush generation in her judgment. “We are committed to working with the next government to ensure that all the Williams Report recommendations are fully implemented. The work isn’t done. “We will continue to hold public institutions to account to ensure that institutional racism is eradicated from our society.” Following the ruling, Unison general secretary Christina McAnea said: “The hostile environment had devastating consequences for those affected by the Windrush scandal. “Rather than learning the lessons, the Government’s response has been dire.” She continued: “No government is above the law. “Thankfully the then-home secretary’s been caught bang to rights. “Ministers must treat all people with dignity and respect, and act with integrity. “The hope is the next government will act quickly to make amends to this disgraceful chapter in our history.” A Home Office spokesperson said: “We are carefully considering the judgment and will respond in due course.”

author: Craig Kapitan
title: Illegal gun collector Dennis Sukanaveita sentenced for New Windsor home clan lab
mainText: Dennis Sukanaveita, an alleged methamphetamine cook and illegal gun collector, was caught trying to purchase pistols online from an undercover police officer. He was raided by the police in April 2022, resulting in the discovery of a substantial gun cache, methamphetamine, and a clandestine laboratory in his New Windsor home. Sukanaveita, a convicted felon, was sentenced to four years and three months in prison. The judge noted contrasting aspects of Sukanaveita's character, acknowledging his family-oriented nature but also his reckless behavior of storing firearms and methamphetamine in the family home. The police found a variety of firearms, ammunition, methamphetamine, and drug paraphernalia on the premises. Sukanaveita pleaded guilty to several charges, including attempted possession of a firearm, drug-related offenses, and manufacturing methamphetamine. The prosecutor highlighted the seriousness of the offenses, indicating possible drug selling activities. Despite claims of remorse and efforts at rehabilitation, the defense argued that Sukanaveita was facilitating another individual's drug manufacturing rather than actively partaking in criminal activities. The judge wrestled with the defendant's past convictions but acknowledged his apology and aspirations for redemption. Sukanaveita expressed a desire for accountability and rehabilitation, aiming to pursue a carpentry apprenticeship post-release. The judge acknowledged Sukanaveita's contemplative state and expressed hope for his ability to make amends. This case sheds light on the intersection of drug-related crimes and illegal firearms possession, revealing a complex narrative of criminal behavior and personal transformation.

author: Tracy Neal
title: Seasonal worker Steven Garae sentenced to seven years' jail for raping Blenheim school girl, 11
mainText: A seasonal worker from Vanuatu, Steven Tari Tambean Garae, has been sentenced to seven years in prison for raping an 11-year-old schoolgirl in a railway station toilet block in Blenheim, New Zealand. The Crown described the attack as 'the stuff of nightmares', with the victim's grandmother stating that the trauma is still raw. Garae followed the girl and her friend before grabbing her and assaulting her in a public toilet, leaving her physically injured. Despite initially claiming the sex was consensual, he later admitted to forcing the victim. The judge noted the severity of the crime, emphasizing the impact on the victim's well-being and the community. Garae will serve a minimum of three-and-a-half years in prison. The defense cited Garae's poor mental health and lack of support as contributing factors, advocating for improved care for overseas workers in New Zealand. The prosecutor highlighted the vulnerability of the victim and the violence she endured, calling for justice. The victim's family and community continue to suffer from the repercussions of the assault, with the young girl facing bullying and mistreatment. The case underscores the need for safeguarding vulnerable individuals and providing better support systems for migrant workers.

author: Maariv Online
title: Lebanese man suspected as Israeli spy after accidentally filming strike
mainText: A Lebanese civilian got into trouble on Wednesday due to a recording of an IDF attack in Lebanon and was forced to turn himself into the intelligence services, according to Lebanese media. The reason for this individual to turn himself in was because he had filmed the target of the Israeli strike before it was attacked, and so, therefore, the moment of the bombing had been recorded. This had reportedly caused users on social media to speculate that he knew in advance of the planned attack and thus accused him of being a spy for Israel. The man provided intelligence services with longer documentation of the attack, where, according to reports in Lebanon, there was drone activity in the area, which was what initially caught his attention, and was thus urged to start filming. The massive attack caught on camera was completely by accident, according to his testimony. Incident comes after more IDF strikes in Lebanon. This report came hours after IAF fighter jets attacked a military structure of the Hezbollah terrorist organization in the area of Tsur and more infrastructure in the town of Khiam in southern Lebanon. In addition, it was reported that Israel successfully intercepted a suspicious aerial target from Lebanese airspace on Wednesday morning - which did not cross into Israel. View of a large fire caused from rockets fired from Lebanon, in the northern Israeli town of Kiryat Shmona, June 3, 2024. The IDF also stated, following rocket sirens that were activated in the Kiryat Shmona area, that about 15 launches from Lebanese territory were detected, some of which were successfully intercepted by the air defense fighters. There were no casualties from the attack. The IDF then attacked the sources of the shooting with artillery.

author: Sukanya Nandy
title: Karnataka TET 2024 Admit Cards Released at schooleducation.kar.nic.in, Exam on June 30
mainText: The Department of School Education, Karnataka has released the admit cards for the Karnataka Teacher Eligibility Test (KARTET) 2024. Candidates who applied for the KARTET 2024 can download the hall tickets by visiting the official website at schooleducation.kar.nic.in. The exam will be held on June 30. Karnataka TET Admit Card 2024: How to Download? Step 1: Go to the official website of the Department of School Education Karnataka at schooleducation.kar.nic.in. Step 2: On the homepage, go to the ‘Latest Information’ section and click on the Karnataka Teachers Eligibility Test – 2024 admit card link Step 3: Fill out the required details Step 4: The admit card will appear on the screen Step 5: Download and save for further use. Karnataka TET Admit Card 2024 Out: Know Exam Pattern The Karnataka Teacher Eligibility Test is divided into two parts – Paper 1 and Paper 2. The exams will be for 2 hours and 30 minutes. Paper 1 will occur from 9:30 am to 12 noon, while Paper 2 will be held from 2 pm to 4:30 pm. The exam consists of a total of 150 questions each carrying one mark. A negative of 0.25 is deducted for each wrong answer. As per the official website, the Karnataka Teacher Eligibility Test pass percentage is 60 per cent for the General Category candidates and 55 per cent for Other Backward Class (OBC), Scheduled Caste (SC), and Scheduled Tribe (ST). The minimum age requirement for the Karnataka TET 2023 is 18 years, and there is no upper age limit. Those applying for primary teacher (Class 1 to 5) should hold a pass certificate of class 12 with a minimum of 50 per cent marks. They must possess a two-year diploma in Elementary Education or a Bachelor of Elementary Education. Meanwhile, candidates applying for upper primary teacher (Class 6 to 8) must have a Bachelor’s degree with a minimum of 50 per cent marks. Applicants must also have completed a one-year Bachelor’s in Education or a two-year Diploma in Elementary Education. Stay ahead with all the exam results updates on News18 Website.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: NEET Aspirants Say Little Faith in NTA, Want Retest Option for All Candidates to Be Considered
mainText: Many NEET aspirants are calling for a retest of the NEET-UG 2024 due to allegations of irregularities, paper leaks, and a significant increase in the merit list. The decision to cancel grace marks for 1,563 students has not alleviated their concerns. Student bodies and political youth wings have been protesting nationwide over the alleged irregularities in the exam, which saw 67 students achieving a perfect score of 720, an unprecedented occurrence in the National Testing Agency's (NTA) history. With ongoing reports of paper leaks and other discrepancies, many students have lost faith in the exam's conduct. Some students are calling for a thorough investigation into the paper leak allegations, while others feel that the retest offered to 1,563 students is inadequate. There are demands for a reevaluation of all students' marks or a universal retest. The controversy has led to calls for a third-party investigation to ensure impartiality. The NEET-UG exam is conducted by the NTA for admissions to medical and related courses. The Union Education Ministry has formed an expert panel to review the grace marks issue, and a retest for the affected students is scheduled for June 23. The controversy has reached the Supreme Court, with petitions seeking the scrapping of the exam and a court-monitored probe into the irregularities. Amidst the uncertainty, students are advised to stay prepared for a potential retest. The Supreme Court has sought responses on the matter and stayed further proceedings on related petitions across various high courts.

author: India.com Education Desk
title: NEET UG 2024: Arrested Candidate Confesses Paper Leak to Police, Claims Uncle Gave Question Paper
mainText: In the midst of the NEET paper leak controversy, Anurag Yadav, a 22-year-old candidate from Bihar, confessed to obtaining leaked exam papers through his uncle, who is a junior engineer. Anurag admitted that his uncle provided him with questions and answer keys for the exam, and instructed him to memorize the answers. Anurag saw the same questions in the actual exam and was subsequently arrested by the police. The confession also implicated his uncle, Sikandar Yadavendu, as well as two others, Nitish Kumar and Amit Anand, in the paper leak scandal. Reports suggest that the question papers were provided to certain candidates a day before the exam in exchange for a significant sum of money. Anurag revealed that his uncle arranged the leaked NEET papers for him and claimed that Amit Anand and Nitish Kumar informed his uncle about the leak beforehand. Yadavendu, in turn, admitted to taking four students, including Anurag, to a location where the answers were being memorized, and asked for a higher sum of money than originally agreed upon. However, he was caught by the police. Nitish Kumar and Amit Anand also confessed to their involvement in the paper leak and detailed their collaboration with Yadavendu, which ultimately led to their arrest. The police raided the location where the leaked papers were provided to students and found remnants of burnt question papers. The chain of events surrounding the NEET paper leak has brought to light a web of deceit and corruption involving multiple individuals.

author: Toi Education
title: Admit cards of UGC NET candidates not retained by authorities as oppposed to NTA instructions: Was scrapping this exam pre-planned to make up for the NEET blunder?
mainText: UGC-NET 2024 exam was cancelled by the Ministry of Education due to potential examination integrity compromise. Recent mismanagement by NTA, especially the NEET UG 2024 exam with 67 rank 1 candidates, led to concerns and legal actions. The cancellation raised doubts about NTA's credibility. The cancellation followed I4C's warning about compromised integrity. Candidates were allowed to retain their UGC-NET June 2024 exam admit cards, defying NTA's usual practice. This deviation raised suspicions regarding the exam's pre-planned cancellation to address the NEET UG controversies. The decision to cancel aimed at preserving examination sanctity. The Ministry will conduct a new exam later. Despite NTA's instructions about retaining admit cards, authorities asked candidates to take them back after the UGC NET exam. The decision not to collect admit cards raised questions about the exam's scheduled cancellation. The Ministry assured prompt action following I4C's warning and handed the matter to the CBI for investigation to maintain students' interests and integrity of the examination process.

author: Laura-Carreno
title: ITV Love Island split 'sealed' for couple as fans fear history will repeat itself
mainText: Ronnie Vint's wandering eye may have found a new target and some Love Island viewers believe history will repeat itself. After a brutal recoupling led Samantha Kenny to leave the Mallorca villa, still reeling from her ill-fated connection with Joey Essex, couples were rattled once again by two new arrivals on Wednesday, June 19. Matilda Draper and Konnor Ewudzi made quite the impression upon their arrival, particularly after Grace Jackson, Tiffany Leighton and Wil Anderson were first introduced to viewers just days ago. While Grace rekindled her romance with TOWIE legend Joey, Wil Anderson is keen to explore his romantic potential with Uma Jammeh just as Tiffany Leighton and Ronnie Vint seemed to be on the same page. Unfortunately, due to Matilda's surprise arrival and his antics with Jess White and Harriett Blackmore, ITV2 viewers are convinced that Ronnie's latest connection with Tiffany could be in peril. Suspicions notably arose when it became clear to reality TV fans that Ronnie knew Matilda off-screen as she called his name out, hinting that Joey Essex and Grace Jackson may not be the only exes to throw the villa into chaos. Fans theorised that, much like Grace and Joey, Ronnie and Matilda may have shared their own romance prior to making their Love Island debut. Other viewers speculated that Matilda may actually have a link to one of Ronnie's friends. But in several other posts relayed on X, otherwise known as Twitter, viewers commented that Mathilda may make Ronnie forget all about Tiffany, like the latter managed to overshadow Harriett in previous scenes. Ronnie walked into the villa a single man before being partnered up with Jess White during his first week in Mallorca. But when Harriett caught all his attention, an explosive love triangle took shape and Jess decided to (unsuccessfully) move on from Ronnie with Sean Stone. Coupled up with Harriett, Tiffany quickly turned heads and picked Ronnie for an overnight stay in Casa Amor, leading the pair to share a smooch behind Harriett's back. The semi-professional footballer allowed history to repeat itself in recent scenes when he brutally dismissed Harriett in favour of Tiffany but as both he and Joey have proven, one girl is enough to leave everything in shambles. To top it all off, some fans have speculated that Tiffany may be a good match for Sean Stone, who has proven his interest on several occasions.

author: Paulo Kawanishi
title: Best shields in Elden Ring
mainText: Not everyone needs or likes to use shields in Elden Ring, but they can be powerful tools for those who learn how to use them. Shields are not only useful for blocking attacks and preventing damage but can also be used to attack enemies or parry their attacks for critical hits. When looking for the best shield, consider aspects like Guard Boost, Physical Damage Reduction, weight, and the ability to infuse Ashes of War for parrying. Some of the best shields in Elden Ring include the Fingerprint Stone Shield with a Guard Boost of 77 and 100 Physical Damage Reduction, the Brass Shield offering good balance with 100 Physical Damage Reduction and 56 Guard Boost, the Carian Knight's Shield for defense against magic with 100 Physical Damage Reduction and 71 Magic Reduction, and the Coil Shield with a unique Viper Bite skill that inflicts deadly poison on enemies. The Spiralhorn Shield stands out for its passive ability to increase the user's Immunity, Robustness, and Focus, along with causing blood loss buildup when hitting enemies. Each shield has different stat requirements and can be found in various locations throughout the game.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Kamal Haasan Reveals How Prabhas Thanked Him Being Part Of Kalki 2898 AD; 'Couldn't Believe Till Today...'
mainText: The makers of Kalki 2898 AD hosted a special event for the film and its cast which was attended by Deepika Padukone, Prabhas, Amitabh Bachchan as well as Kamal Haasan. While the former three are the leading roles in the film, Kamal Haasan is set to be part of the film for a cameo scene. The first look of his role has also been featured in the trailer which had fans excited for the release. At the event, Kamal Haasan revealed that Prabhas thanked him before the event for being a part of the film. He also said, "About my participation, nobody believed I was a part of Project K (laughs)." However, Haasan added that even Prabhas the leading actor in the film could not believe the same. He was quoted by reports saying, "The funny thing is, yesterday, the protagonist, Mr. Prabhas, just held my hand and said thank you. He said, ‘I couldn’t believe till today that you're a part of this'." In the trailer Kamal Haasan can be seen only for a few seconds and his look is unrecognizable. He will be seen playing the role of Supreme Yaskin as the villain. Talking about the same, he told the reports, “I was (telling) backstage to Amit ji (Bachchan) about how I always wanted to play a bad man because the bad man gets to do all the good things." The film directed by Nag Ashwin is set to hit the big screen on June 27, 2024.

author: Dishya Sharma, Sahas
title: Celine Dion Makes First Red Carpet Appearance Since Stiff Person Syndrome Diagnosis
mainText: Celine Dion recently made a dazzling return at the premiere of her documentary I Am: Celine Dion in New York City. This marked her first red-carpet appearance since being diagnosed with stiff person syndrome. At the special event, the Grammy-winning artist looked stunning in an all-white ensemble. Her last major public appearance was at the 66th Grammy Awards on February 4, where she presented Taylor Swift with the Album of the Year award. At the premiere, Celine made a rare appearance alongside her eldest son, Rene-Charles Angelil, who was elegantly dressed in a classic suit. The upcoming Prime Video documentary delves into Celine’s life and her journey with a rare condition. Through the film, the singer aims to raise awareness and support for those facing isolation during health challenges. Celine Dion received a thunderous response as she arrived on stage. The singer shared about her condition and journey, expressing gratitude to her children and the audience. Reportedly, Celine was diagnosed with stiff-person syndrome in August 2022, shared the news in December same year. Due to health issues, she canceled tours and underwent various treatments. The documentary, I Am: Celine Dion, is set to premiere on June 25.

author: Josh Butler
title: Three-eyed koalas and Dutton as Snow White: how Simpsons memes have been weaponised in nuclear debate
mainText: The debate over nuclear energy policy in Australia has taken a humorous turn with government MPs using online memes to attack the opposition's proposal. Labor MPs have retaliated by sharing memes criticizing the Coalition's nuclear plan, raising concerns over safety, cost, waste, design, and local consultation. Key figures like Peter Dutton and Michaelia Cash have condemned the use of cartoons like three-eyed koalas and Simpsons references in the debate. Labor MPs have used images of three-eyed fish, two-headed cows, and comparisons to characters like Mr. Burns from The Simpsons to mock the Coalition's stance on nuclear energy. The opposition has linked the Aukus nuclear submarine pact to the energy plan, despite using different technologies. The debate has led to a social media war of memes and jokes, with both sides trying to sway public opinion through humor and satire. While Labor has been making Simpsons jokes about nuclear policy for months, the Coalition has criticized these references as juvenile and distracting from the serious issue at hand. The use of memes and cartoons in political discourse reflects the evolving nature of communication and persuasion strategies in the digital age.

author: David Mouriquand
title: Just Stop Oil targets Taylor Swift’s jet – and fails to locate it
mainText: Just Stop Oil is keeping busy. Just one day after targeting renowned prehistoric UNESCO World Heritage Site Stonehenge, two demonstrators from the British environmental activist group, named by the group as Jennifer Kowalski, 28, and Cole Macdonald, 22, are said to have broken into a VIP private airfield at Stansted airport this morning. The pair attempted to target Taylor Swift’s jet, as the pop star is scheduled to perform at Wembley Stadium on Friday, Saturday and Sunday this week, as part of her worldwide Eras Tour. Unable to find the plane, they instead painted two other jets using fire extinguishers filled with orange paint. Cole Macdonald said: “We’re living in two worlds: one where billionaires live in luxury, able to fly in private jets away from the other, where unlivable conditions are being imposed on countless millions. Meanwhile, this system that is allowing extreme wealth to be accrued by a few, to the detriment of everyone else, is destroying the conditions necessary to support human life in a rapidly accelerating never-ending ‘cruel summer’.""Billionaires are not untouchable, climate breakdown will affect every single one of us,” Macdonald concluded. Just Stop Oil has warned of "resistance" this summer if the government does not take "meaningful action". "Whilst governments are allowing oil corporations to run amok destroying our communities, the actions of individuals mean very little," the group said. "That's why Just Stop Oil is demanding that our next government sign up to a legally binding treaty to phase out fossil fuels by 2030.” "Failure to defend the people they represent will mean Just Stop Oil supporters, along with citizens from Austria, Canada, Norway, the Netherlands and Switzerland will join in resistance this summer, if their own governments do not take meaningful action."

author: Msizi Khoza
title: OPINION | Why the Climate Change Bill is a big deal
mainText: Parliament has passed the Climate Change Bill. The Climate Change Bill will provide a legal framework to tackle the climate crisis and ensure South Africa is better prepared for its impacts, but it deserves far more attention than it has received, writes Msizi Khoza. A few weeks ago, lawmakers approved a historic and well-considered piece of legislation that has largely gone unnoticed, despite the transformative effect it could have on the country. The Climate Change Bill will provide a legal framework to tackle the climate crisis and ensure South Africa is better prepared for its impacts. It is also aimed at facilitating a transition to clean energy that is just and fair to those who rely on the fossil fuel sector for their livelihoods.

author: Stuti Mishra
title: India sees over hundred deaths and 40,000 cases of suspected heatstrokes
mainText: Over 40,000 cases of suspected heatstroke have been reported in India as gruelling temperatures continued to scorch the country this week in what is now confirmed to be its “longest heatwave ever”. At least 52 bodies were brought to hospitals in the past two days. Government figures say 110 deaths have been recorded between 1 March and 18 June. In the last 72 hours alone, five people have been killed due to heatstrokes in Delhi. Doctors at Safdarjung Hospital said at least 28 patients were diagnosed with heatstrokes. Higher body temperature can lead to long-term organ damage and death. The heatwave has exacerbated the water and electricity crisis. Fines have been imposed on people for wasting water. As the climate crisis continues to drive temperatures upward, the danger of humidity is also expected to rise. Just under a half-million deaths can be attributed to excess heat every year - a conservative count that lacks data from many low-income countries.

author: Lauren Hughes
title: This Morning prompts fierce debate over whether it's okay to snack while on the toilet - as Cat Deeley admits she enjoys a coffee while showering
mainText: This Morning has caused a furore after a debate broke out on whether it's okay to snack on the toilet. Speaking to the ITV today, presenter Cat Deeley said that one in four young adults enjoy a bite to eat on the toilet. This unsettling statistic prompted outrage among viewers and This Morning guests Vanessa Feltz and Tom Swarbrick, with the former saying the revelation had 'shocked her' to the 'core'. 'I'm absolutely horrified by this,' responded Vanessa. 'I'm flabbergasted by this. What kind of cannon of behaviour is this? What code of conduct does this adhere to?' She then continued: 'And also what parents or partners or even friends permit people into the lavatory - as that's what we should call it - with items of food to consume. I am shocked to the core.' Viewers were equally appalled, taking to social media to voice their dismay. 'Snacks in the bathroom, disgusting,' wrote one This Morning viewer. While another said, 'Snacks on the loo and in the shower b****y weirdos.' And a third wrote, 'Can't beat a turdburger.' 'Cat Deeley's is one that can hold her hand up and say you sort of do it,' he quipped.

author: Ellen Coughlan
title: Princess Leonor and Princess Sofia steal the show with their elegant outfits at a gallery event...
mainText: Princess Leonor and Princess Sofia, daughters of Queen Letizia and King Felipe of Spain, made a fashionable appearance at a gallery event to celebrate the 10th anniversary of King Felipe's reign. Princess Leonor, 18, wore a beaded pale blue two-piece outfit, while Princess Sofia, 17, opted for white wide-leg trousers and a matching top. The sisters showcased elegant hairstyles and subtle makeup, resembling their stylish mother. The royal family also attended a gala lunch at the Royal Palace, where Princess Leonor dazzled in a red suit and Princess Sofia wore a structured black dress. Later, they enjoyed a family night out at a concert, with Queen Letizia stunning in a gold pleated skirt, black top, and sandals. King Felipe looked dapper in grey trousers and a pink shirt. The day marked the 10th anniversary of King Felipe's ascension to the throne, with the family participating in various celebratory events. The article also references a book claiming alleged infidelities involving Queen Letizia and accusations against the royal family. Overall, the royal family's stylish appearances and public engagements captured attention and admiration.

author: Amanda Bechara
title: These are the five hidden 'red flag' traits that mean your partner is likely to cheat on you:...
mainText: A relationship expert has shared five hidden 'red flag' traits that could indicate a higher likelihood of future infidelity in a partner. The first red flag highlighted is parental infidelity, suggesting that individuals whose parents have cheated in the past might be more predisposed to cheating themselves. The second trait mentioned is having a high number of past sexual partners, as this can correlate with a thrill-seeking attitude towards sex that may undermine commitment in a long-term relationship. Another important indicator is past behavior, with a history of infidelity being a strong predictor of potential future cheating. Additionally, individuals with an avoidant attachment style may struggle to honor relationship commitments and seek intimacy elsewhere. Lastly, emotional and behavioral instability, characterized by dramatic mood swings, can also damage the emotional bonds necessary for fidelity. It is emphasized that these traits are predictive indicators and not guarantees of actual behavior. Rebuilding trust after infidelity requires commitment from both parties and a willingness to address underlying issues. The article also addresses emotional cheating as a form of betrayal and emphasizes the need for open communication and self-reflection in relationships.

author: Amy Maxmen
title: ‘We’re Flying Blind’: CDC Has 1M Bird Flu Tests Ready, but Experts See Repeat of Covid Missteps
mainText: It’s been nearly three months since the U.S. government announced an outbreak of the bird flu virus on dairy farms. The World Health Organization considers the virus a public health concern because of its potential to cause a pandemic, yet the U.S. has tested only about 45 people across the country. “We’re flying blind,” said Jennifer Nuzzo, director of the Pandemic Center at the Brown University School of Public Health. With only about 45 tests run, it’s impossible to know the extent of the infection among farmworkers, raising concerns about a potential pandemic. The CDC's bird flu test is the only one authorized by the FDA for use currently, with about a million tests available and more expected in the coming months. However, there are concerns that clinical laboratories, often where doctors order tests from, are not authorized for bird flu testing. As the outbreak grows, delays in allowing clinical labs to test are worrisome. Clinical laboratories play a crucial role in testing during health emergencies, highlighted by failures during the covid response. The U.S. needs to improve access to testing to detect cases early and prevent outbreaks. The current testing scheme could lead to missed cases and delays in treatment. Efforts to boost testing among farmworkers are facing challenges, such as language barriers and economic concerns. Involving clinical labs is crucial for rapid testing and scaling up if the virus starts spreading among people. The CDC has provided licenses for its tests to some companies, but delays in allowing referencing of CDC data have hindered progress. The CDC argues for maintaining test quality and insists that manufacturers generate their own data for proper use of the test. The process of developing and approving tests is facing obstacles, with confusion around FDA rules adding to delays. Uncertainty remains regarding demand for bird flu tests and how they will be covered by insurers or the government. The lack of testing and delays could lead to criticism and affect America's global standing.

author: Tapatrisha Das
title: World Music Day 2024: 7 amazing benefits of listening to music
mainText: World Music Day 2024: Music acts as the soothing background score to our lives. Be it any mood, music can add more depth, contemplation, perspective and peace to it. Music creates a sense of community and adds value to unity in diversity. Music, like any art form, does not require the understanding of language to get people connected. Musicians all over the world experiment with music, lyrics, and rhythm to bring new music to the world every day. World Music Day is celebrated every year to emphasise on the importance of music in our lives, and how it helps in bringing people closer. World Music Day is observed on June 21 every year. Musicians are urged to perform on the streets under the slogan - Faites de la musique, on this day. As we gear up to celebrate the beautiful day, here are a few reasons why we should listen to music every day. Elevates mood: Take a sad day and make it better with a song of your choice. Music helps in elevating our mood and makes you feel better. It helps us to have fresh perspectives and look at the world through a happier lens. Relieves depression: When we feel low or down in the dumps, we can trust music to pick us up and make us feel better. Music also helps us to distract ourselves from things that emotionally hurt us. Its heart healthy: Listening to music can help reduce blood pressure, decrease cortisol levels and regulate the heart rate. It helps in boosting cardiovascular health. Stimulates memories: Even though there is no cure for Alzheimer's or Dementia, music therapy has shown significant development in stirring up memories and relieving some of the symptoms of these conditions. Manages pain: Music helps in reducing stress levels by regulating Cortisol levels in the body. It also provides a strong competing signal to the brain against pain – this further helps in pain management. Increases workout endurance: During a tough exercise routine, playing the songs we like can help in having to enhance motivation and boost physical performance. Helps people eat less: Soft music in the backdrop with dim lighting helps people slow down while eating – this further helps people from overconsuming food in one sitting.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: How do humans become kind and caring? Review explores developmental-relational reasons and effects of adversity
mainText: In an article published in Nature Reviews Psychology, scientists have discussed key factors associated with the development of prosocial behaviors in children and childhood adversities that can potentially affect this development. Prosocial behaviors, such as caring, sharing, volunteering, and helping, positively influence well-being and social harmony. These behaviors emerge in children as early as three months of age and continue to develop throughout childhood and adolescence. The development of prosociality is influenced by environmental, psychological, and genetic factors, with child relationships and attachment playing a central role. Adversities like abuse, neglect, and community violence can impact prosociality development. Interventions to enhance prosociality include social-emotional learning programs, parenting interventions, and community-based activities. Culturally appropriate and developmentally tailored interventions are being emphasized to meet the unique needs of children and communities.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Study reveals cognitive benefits of ketogenic diet in aged mice
mainText: In a recent study published in Cell Reports Medicine, researchers examined the impact of cyclic ketogenic diet treatments in improving the age-related decline in brain function using long-term potential recordings and behavioral testing in aged mice. The study aimed to elucidate the molecular mechanisms regulated by ketogenic diets at the synaptic level and their impact on dendritic organization and the proteomic landscape in neurons.

author: Emily Woodruff
title: Anti-vaccine movement gains steam in Louisiana
mainText: All but HB46 and HB47 have been signed by Landry. Vaccinations drop Before the pandemic, anti-vaccine sentiment was more associated with left-wing extremists, said Charles Stoecker, a health economist who studies vaccine policy at Tulane University. Historically, Louisiana has had high vaccination rates, especially for a state that allows for school exemptions for any reason. Since the pandemic, the anti-vaccination movement has taken hold among conservatives. Louisiana’s rates for standard childhood vaccinations like the MMR and DTaP saw some of the biggest yearly drops among all states, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. In a single year, MMR vaccination dropped nearly 2 percentage points. The vaccine that protects against diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis dropped about three percentage points.

author: Ayuvallos
title: Alvin Yapan’s ‘Worship the Body’ is a gripping exploration of queerness, secrets, and intimacy
mainText: “Worship the Body,” the English translation of Alvin Yapan’s “Sambahin ang Katawan” drops this September. Author and filmmaker Alvin Yapan’s novel “Worship the Body” examines facets of queerness through the lens of social and cultural norms. The book tells the story of Jaime and Jun, exploring intimacy and secrets against societal expectations. Yapan, a professor at Ateneo de Manila University, engaged in the translation with Randy Bustamante. Yapan talks about his writing process, revisiting his work, and the goal of expanding readership through the English translation. Yapan's experiences as an author and filmmaker influence each other, focusing on rhythm in writing. The novel's potential dream cast includes actors like Paulo Avelino, Joem Bascon, Jasmine Curtis, and Mercedes Cabral. Yapan's message to queer individuals is to excel in what they love and let passion shape their identity. Photos courtesy of Penguin Books Southeast Asia.

author: Anirudha Yerunkar
title: RBI Cancels Licence Of The City Co-operative Bank; Check Update On Depositor Insurance Claim
mainText: The Reserve Bank on Wednesday cancelled the licence of The City Co-operative Bank Maharashtra for lacking adequate capital and earning prospects. The Commissioner for Cooperation and Registrar of Cooperative Societies Maharashtra has also been asked to issue an order for winding up the bank and appoint a liquidator RBI said. According to RBI the cooperative bank ceases to carry on banking operations with effect from the close of business hours on June 19 2024. What Will Happen To Depositor Insurance Claims ? On liquidation every depositor would be entitled to receive deposit insurance claim amount of his/her deposits up to a monetary ceiling of Rs 5 lakh only from Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC). As per the data submitted by the bank about 87 per cent of the depositors are entitled to receive full amount of their deposits from DICGC RBI said. As on June 14 2024 DICGC has already paid Rs 230.99 crore of the total insured deposits based on the willingness received from the depositors concerned of the bank. Why RBI Cancelled The Licence Of The Bank? Giving details RBI said the Mumbai-based cooperative bank does not have adequate capital and earning prospects. The bank with its present financial position would be unable to pay its present depositors in full it said and added that public interest would be adversely affected if it is allowed to carry on its banking business any further. Consequent to the cancellation of its licence The City Co-operative Bank has been prohibited from conducting the business of ‘banking’ which includes among other things acceptance of deposits and repayment of deposits. (With Inputs From PTI)

author: Sarah Bull
title: I thought I’d found a cool vintage shirt in the charity shop so wore it clubbing… then I realised my epic e...
mainText: A WOMAN has been left mortified after accidentally wearing a supermarket uniform on a night out clubbing. Holly explained that she'd been hunting for unique pieces in her local charity shop when she came across an oversized white and green striped shirt. Falling in love with the item - which she thought was "vintage" - Holly snapped it up, and couldn't resist wearing it when she hit the club with friends. However, she later realised that the shirt was actually a Waitrose uniform. In a video on her TikTok page, she said: "I have just realised that the shirt I bought from a charity shop last week and have been wearing all weekend is in fact a Waitrose uniform. "Like, what? I wore that to the club Friday night." She only realised when she spotted the buttons on the shirt, inscribed with the Waitrose logo. Holly added that she was hoping the "sexy DJ" she'd been eyeing up in the club was looking at her back, but joked he probably thought she had "just finished my shift at the cheese counter". The worst thing of all was that someone came up to Holly in the club and asked where she got her shirt from, to which she proudly said she'd got it in the charity shop as part of her "sustainable" fashion pursuit. She also told the person that she didn't think they'd "be able to get another one", but then laughed: "Go to Waitrose Holloway Road. "Everyone's f**king wearing one. Jesus Christ!" Holly also shared a screenshot of a man wearing the uniform in the TikTok video. "Do you have a bag had two different meanings in the club that night!" Holly captioned the clip. "I’m cackling as a former employee who hated that uniform," one person commented on the video. "When your shift's at 10 but you got the club at 9," another added. "That could very well be my shirt - I forgot to return my uniform and ended up putting it in a charity bag," a third laughed. "My friend thought she bought a vintage hoodie at a charity shop but it was a local schools sports kit," someone else said. "Kids walked past in the same thing!" "We agree, it’s a gorgeous look!" the official Waitrose account wrote in the comments section.

author: Zachary Petit
title: Inside the new high-tech vault that keeps Shakespeare’s rarest books safe
mainText: When the First Folios returned to their new home, they were placed in a vault that doubles as a public display and benefits from the full wisdom of a near century of institutional preservation knowledge. The case has its own climate system, set to 55 degrees, with a humidity range between 45% and 55%. The library also treats the threat of pests like booklice with utmost care, with multiple levels of staff trained to recognize and report it, among other measures. In the event of a fire, the Folger has highly targeted and precise sprinkler systems (after all, Prickman says, it’s easier to remedy water damage than it is fire damage); in the past, representatives of the Folger have also said the library has a system to remove oxygen from a vault in the event of a fire. The lighting, meanwhile, is carefully maintained at under 30 lux (by comparison, an office usually runs at around 500 lux). Prickman concedes that in a perfect world, the manuscripts would be kept in the equivalent of a cave. But that would defeat the whole point of the library and its holdings to begin with. '[The new vault represents,] in some ways, a tension between preservation and exhibition. And in my role, I don’t see those as mutually exclusive,' says Pickman. 'There’s no doubt that the best way to preserve these things is to keep them in the dark, and not disturb them—but . . . if we were to do that, there would be very little point in having them in the first place.'

author: Sophie O'brien
title: How employers can improve the hiring process for Gen Z candidates in 4 simple steps
mainText: If you’re thinking of making a new hire, you need to determine internally beforehand how many stages will be necessary to assess whether this person is a good fit. Communicate these stages to the candidate and let them know what will be assessed at each stage. This way you’ll avoid frustrations caused by miscommunication and your interviewee will be at ease by knowing what to expect, so they can put their best foot forward. Additionally, an unintended consequence of dragging out the interview process is that you can end up losing out on your preferred candidate, as they’ll be receiving offers while you’re insisting on another round of interviews. It’s also crucial to incorporate a feedback stage. Even if unsuccessful, a candidate has sacrificed their time to attend an interview, so they should at least be given feedback as to why. Plus, giving them feedback and constructive criticism is invaluable to them in their job search. This step is also essential for a positive candidate experience. Be transparent about your working culture Gen Zs are not afraid to leave jobs that don’t serve them. According to a report from ResumeLab, 83% of Gen Zs consider themselves to be job hoppers. The report also found that Gen Z workers prioritized a healthy work-life balance, satisfying job duties, a good relationship with coworkers, and meaningful job and career development over a high salary.

author: Patrick Sisson
title: These developers used to flip houses. Here’s why they’re pivoting to high-end remodels
mainText: Operating mostly in high-end neighborhoods in Los Angeles, San Francisco, Seattle, Denver, and Phoenix metro areas, the developer has pivoted a bit to helping homeowners in desirable neighborhoods—especially owners with low interest rate mortgages who don’t want to move—renovate and redevelop their homes without the stress and uncertainty of a custom build. This concept isn’t brand new, but Thomas James hopes to streamline and package the process. You could call it subscription boxing the McMansion. A new in-house app helps their sales teams provide this white glove treatment for high-earning households locked in during an especially challenging housing market. Flipping is out, and sitting on and reinvesting in your property is in. “We go into neighborhoods, tear down old homes, and build homes for the way people live today,” says Gina Nixon, head of customer and brand experience for Thomas James. “It’s an unusual business model. We actually use a lot of technology to keep it organized, simple, and stress-free for homeowners as much as possible.”

author: Stateline
title: This Kansas district is running out of water—and its leaders won’t do anything to stop it
mainText: Last year, Kansas lawmakers passed legislation squarely targeting the Southwest Kansas Groundwater Management District, which spans a dozen counties. Unlike the two other Kansas districts that sit atop the crucial aquifer, this one has done little to enact formal conservation programs that could help prolong the life of the aquifer. The new law aims to force action. The district has come under fire from legislators increasingly incensed by its substantial travel expenses, its lack of formal conservation policies, and its alienation of farmers who are trying to save water. At a hearing in February on a bill meant to help farmers in one county leave the district, a Kansas House member floated the idea of doing away with the organization, also known as Groundwater Management District 3, altogether. “Maybe that’s something that we need to consider—just dissolve GMD 3 so that these other boards that are doing good work are not affected,” said state Rep. Cyndi Howerton, a Republican from Wichita.

author: Jared Lindzon
title: Why your boss still values performative busyness—and what to do about it
mainText: According to a recent survey of over 1,500 American full-time workers conducted by BambooHR almost everyone feels pressure to prove they’re being productive, regardless of whether they work remotely, in-person, or hybrid. As a result, many are employing tactics to signify to their managers and bosses that they’re actually working while on the clock. According to the survey, 79% of in-office workers and 88% of remote workers feel the need to prove they’re being productive. In fact, 42% of hybrid and in-person workers say they come to the office just for visibility. 'Nearly two thirds, or 64%, of remote teams in our survey admit that they maintain constant online presence even when they may not be actively working,' says BambooHR’s head of human resources, Anita Grantham. 'Especially if you have these workplace apps on your phone, you can leave them on even though you’re at the lake or doing something else.'

author: David Marcus
title: Here's why shy Trump voters feel safe going public
mainText: The concept of shy Trump voters, who supported Donald Trump but were hesitant to express their opinions publicly, is now evolving as more individuals and institutions are openly standing up for Trump. The Biden administration's performance has led many to reconsider their views on Trump, recognizing him as a competent president rather than a villain. Factors such as rising prices, immigration issues, and global conflicts contribute to this shift in perception. Even individuals who were previously critical of Trump are acknowledging his successes in areas like the economy and immigration. Trump is regaining support from various groups, including high-profile figures in big tech and oil industries. The narrative around supporting Trump has shifted from being associated with extremism to a recognition that things were better during his presidency. This change is reflected in public support from Black and Hispanic voters, as seen in recent events and rallies. Biden's campaign faces challenges as more former shy Trump voters openly express their support, weakening the campaign's message about Trump being uniquely dangerous. The upcoming election is framed not just as a choice between candidates, but as a comparison of two presidencies. Biden must now focus on showcasing his performance to win over voters, rather than relying on fear tactics. The era of the shy Trump voter is over, with public opinion shifting towards a more normalized view of Trump as a political figure.

author: Hugh Hewitt
title: Morning Glory: Trump's short list for vice president all agree on one thing
mainText: North Dakota Governor Doug Burgum emphasizes that President Trump serves as a crucial deterrent against the threats posed by the People’s Republic of China to Taiwan and the United States. Burgum acknowledges the severe consequences of President Joe Biden’s perceived weakness in national security, leading to a loss of deterrence against autocrats worldwide. He highlights the necessity of adopting former Trump National Security Advisor Ambassador O’Brien's recommendations for new national security policies to restore deterrence. Burgum stresses the importance of re-electing Trump and restoring the GOP majority in Congress to address these critical issues. The article also discusses the potential for a "red tsunami" in the upcoming election and contrasts Trump’s perceived energy and effectiveness with Biden’s perceived decline and failures in various policy areas. The piece underscores the need for a strong leadership deterrent against global threats, mentioning potential vice presidential candidates like Senator Tom Cotton, former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo, Senator Marco Rubio, and Governor Glenn Youngkin, who all agree that President Trump acts as a deterrent. The author, Hugh Hewitt, is a prominent radio host and legal scholar who emphasizes the importance of understanding these national security challenges and the role of deterrence in protecting the United States and Western nations.

author: Nicholas Cecil
title: Farage would be carrying Trump's bags around US if Sunak had called autumn poll, says top Tory
mainText: Nigel Farage would have been carrying Donald Trump’s bags around America during the UK’s election if Rishi Sunak had called it for the autumn, a senior Tory has said. Lord Barwell, who was No10 chief-of-staff to Theresa May, said calling the election for July had been a “terrible mistake”. Many Tory MPs were stunned at the time when the PM announced the poll. Mr Farage, who was planning to head to the US to support Trump’s bid for a White House comeback, shortly afterwards did a dramatic U-turn and took over as leader of Reform UK. The party has surged in the polls putting the Tories facing a possible historic defeat. The peer argued that the Prime Minister had a “duty to the party” to “undo as much of that damage” as he could in the run-up to the July 4 polling day. Lord Barwell, a former Croydon MP, told ITV’s Peston show: “If he’d waited until the Autumn, Nigel (Farage) would be off carrying Donald Trump’s bag around America. “You wouldn’t have the issue we have now. “So he made a serious mistake, but he has a duty to the party and to all the candidates out there to undo as much of that damage as he can and he’s got two-and-a-bit weeks left to do that and he’s got to get out there every day and make the argument.” In London, Reform is on 10 per cent in the 20 seats that the Conservatives are defending, and its rise has put more of them at risk of being won by Labour.

author: Science X
title: Scientists devise algorithm to engineer improved enzymes
mainText: Scientists have developed an algorithm to enhance enzyme performance by introducing mutations with a high likelihood of improving functionality. Their work, published in Nature Communications, has broad implications for industries like food production and healthcare. Enzymes play vital roles in various biological processes and have evolved over billions of years. By altering the amino acid sequence that defines their 3D structure, enzymes can be modified to enhance their activity. However, random mutations can drastically reduce enzyme effectiveness. In this study, researchers used an algorithm to engineer a more efficient version of the enzyme beta-lactamase by considering its evolutionary history. By introducing coordinated mutations based on the enzyme's sequence diversity, they achieved significant improvements in activity and stability. The 3D structure of the redesigned enzyme remained similar to the original despite alterations to 30% of its amino acids. The study highlights the potential to engineer enzymes for enhanced performance in various industrial and medical applications.

author: Wire Content
title: Euro 2024: With masked Mbappé? France out to maintain dominance over Netherlands
mainText: Former champions France and the Netherlands are set to face off in their second match at the European Championship with France having won seven of their last eight meetings against the Dutch. The buildup to the match is centered around speculation regarding the availability of France star Kylian Mbappé, who broke his nose in the previous game. Both teams are tied on three points in Group D, with France winning their qualifying matches against the Netherlands 4-0 and 2-1. Dutch forward Xavi Simons returns to Leipzig, where he played on loan from PSG, and the Netherlands won Euro '88 with current coach Ronald Koeman as a player. France's coach Didier Deschamps led them to Euro 2000 victory and another World Cup win in 2018. France and the Netherlands have a history of close encounters with the Dutch scoring more goals in their previous meetings. France has been successful in recent major tournaments, reaching the final in three out of four.

author: Igor Bonifacic
title: The best SSDs in 2024
mainText: The best SSDs in 2024 offer fast and reliable storage for upgrading PCs or consoles. SATA SSDs are affordable and easy to install, suitable for older PCs with SATA connections. M.2 SSDs provide faster speeds, with NVMe drives offering the best performance. Gen4 SSDs are even faster but require compatible hardware. When choosing an SSD, consider factors like installation ease, compatibility, and physical size. Portable SSDs with USB 3.2 or Thunderbolt 3 connections are ideal for external storage. For console storage, Seagate's expansion cards are recommended for Xbox Series X|S, while high-capacity Gen4 drives with a heatsink work well for PS5. A 1TB SSD is generally recommended for PC or console upgrades, with SSDs offering better performance than HDDs. Larger SSDs provide more storage capacity but not necessarily faster speeds. It's crucial to consider read/write speeds when purchasing an SSD for optimal performance.

author: Am Et
title: Philadelphia aims to create a pipeline of affordable housing developers with access to capital
mainText: MICHEL MARTIN, HOST: Back here in the U.S., high mortgage rates and home prices continue to make buying difficult for people with lower incomes. In Philadelphia, a city program is helping to change that by training housing developers and offering easier access to financing. Since its creation, it's issued more than $50 million in loans and renovated nearly 500 homes. Aaron Moselle of member station WHYY went to one of them. ... The program defines that as homes affordable to people earning between $40,000 and $80,000 a year. Veteran real estate developer Ken Weinstein created Jumpstart. He says the program has chapters across Philadelphia and in a handful of states. KEN WEINSTEIN: We're showing people how to remove blight from their community, how to produce affordable housing for their community and how to improve their community with less displacement. MOSELLE: Vincent Reina is faculty director of the Housing Initiative at the University of Pennsylvania. He says Jumpstart provides financing for projects that banks don't typically give out. VINCENT REINA: And what this program's trying to do is not just to increase the pool of developers but also increase the diversity of the pool of developers, particularly for groups who haven't been able to engage in the space. MOSELLE: After saving the property from foreclosure, Martin secured an $80,000 construction loan through Jumpstart and got to work. He says the home was in a sorry state - a rotting shell. K MARTIN: Yeah. This is a total gut rehab. Due to rain and excessive erosion and rot, it just was a soft piece of wood. So they had to tear down the entire thing. And then we had to build it back up. ... He's already got his sights set on his next project. For NPR News, I'm Aaron Moselle in Philadelphia. author: Rapid Recap Team
title: Gaming Innovation Group signs platform agreement to expand Ontario market footprint
mainText: Gaming Innovation Group (GiG) has signed a Head of Terms agreement with Ventures Lab in Ontario to provide its iGaming platform, DataX, and LogicX AI tools, marking the fourth platform partner for GiG in the Canadian province. This partnership supports GiG's global strategy for regulated market growth and aims to fully utilize the platform's capabilities for speed to market. The agreement allows for potential multi-jurisdictional expansion in the future and focuses on driving revenue growth by offering a highly scalable iGaming platform with localized content and leading suppliers for the Ontarian market. The use of AI tools like DataX and LogicX is expected to enhance decision-making processes and increase player acquisition and retention. iGaming revenue in Ontario has been growing significantly, reaching €3.8 billion in the 2023-24 year. Andrew Cochrane, Chief Business Officer at GiG, highlighted the importance of attracting experienced partners to drive efficiency and profitability. author: Rapid Recap Team
title: At least 34 dead, 100 hospitalised in Tamil Nadu's Kallakurichi after consuming illicit liquor; four arrested so far
mainText: At least 34 people died, and around 100 were hospitalised on Wednesday after allegedly drinking illicit liquor in Tamil Nadu's Kallakurichi district, officials said on Thursday. The death toll is likely to increase, they said. So far, four people have been arrested.Critical patients have been admitted to hospitals in Salem, Tiruvannamalai, and Puducherry.Tamil Nadu chief minister MK Stalin said he was “shocked” by the deaths and stated that action was taken against those officials who were responsible for not preventing the incident.In a post on X, MK Stalin said, “I was shocked and saddened to hear the news of the deaths of people who had consumed adulterated liquor in Kallakurichi. Those involved in the crime have been arrested in this matter. Action has also been taken against the officials who failed to prevent it. Immediate action will be taken if the public informs about those involved in such crimes. Such crimes that ruin the society will be suppressed with an iron fist.”On Thursday, the opposition AIADMK's advocates requested the Madras High Court to hear an urgent petition on the liquor tragedy. A division bench comprising Justices D Krishnakumar and K Kumaresh Babu agreed to hear it on June 21.Stalin has ordered a Crime Branch-Crime Investigation Department (CB-CID) investigation for a thorough probe. The TN government has replaced Kallakurichi district collector Sravan Kumar Jatavath and suspended superintendent of police Samay Singh Meena, as per a statement. Additionally, nine other police officers, including those from the Kallakurichi prohibition wing, have been suspended, it added.MS Prasanth, the new collector of the Kallakurichi district, visited the patients receiving treatment at the Government Medical College Hospital. Rajath Chaturvedi is the district's new police superintendent.

author: Brian Bushard
title: Trump Slams Fani Willis’ Bid To Dismiss Appeal As ‘Hail Mary’
mainText: Former President Donald Trump criticized Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis for attempting to dismiss his latest appeal in a case where he faces 13 felony counts in Georgia for allegedly trying to overturn the 2020 election results. The case involves an alleged conflict of interest between Willis and a prosecutor named Nathan Wade. The judge overseeing the case ruled not to disqualify Willis but ordered either Willis or Wade to step down due to the appearance of impropriety, leading to Wade's resignation. Trump and his co-defendants appealed this decision, arguing for reversal. Trump's legal team accused Willis of being a 'deeply conflicted' district attorney and criticized the court's findings as irrelevant to judicial misconduct. The Georgia Court of Appeals scheduled a disqualification hearing for Willis, potentially delaying the trial until after the November election. Trump has pleaded not guilty to all charges and denounced the legal proceedings as a 'witch hunt.' He has also faced legal issues in New York, where he was recently found guilty in a separate case. Trump's efforts to delay the Georgia trial intensified amid criticism of Willis' relationship with Wade. The case highlights the ongoing legal battles faced by Trump and his associates as they navigate multiple criminal indictments and allegations. The complex legal proceedings reflect the challenges and controversies surrounding high-profile political figures like Trump in the judicial system. The developments in the case underscore the tensions and conflicts that can arise in legal matters involving influential individuals and public officials.

author: William White
title: Why Is Zapp Electric Vehicles (ZAPP) Stock Up 142% Today?
mainText: Zapp Electric Vehicles (ZAPP) stock is up alongside its latest earnings report. The company is seeing improvements in its net loss and operating loss. Zapp also updated its guidance for i300 deliveries and production in the report. Zapp Electric Vehicles (NASDAQ:ZAPP) stock is soaring higher on Thursday following the release of its latest earnings report. Zapp posted results for the first half of fiscal 2024. That includes its net loss of $5 million shrinking from the $8.6 million reported in the same period of the year prior. Operating loss reported for the first six months of fiscal 2024 came in at $3.1 million as well. Yet again, that’s an improvement over the operating loss of $3.9 million for the first half of 2023. Zapp Electric Vehicles founder and CEO Swin Chatsuwan said the following in the earnings report: “Of an estimated $130 billion and growing in two-wheelers sold globally, we see a large, underserved category of consumers that want superbike specifications but still need the maneuverability of a step-through for the city streets where they spend the most time. After first deliveries of i300 to customers in Europe and Thailand this summer, we expect to scale rapidly in Southeast Asia and India where urban mobility on two wheels is essential.” ZAPP Stock Outlook Zapp Electric Vehicles also updated its guidance in its latest earnings report. The company is expecting its first i300 customer deliveries in the fourth quarter of 2024. It also expects to sell more than 5,000 units in fiscal 2025. Following that, it plans to achieve annual deliveries of 25,000 units starting in fiscal 2026. ZAPP stock is up 141.6% as of Thursday afternoon. This comes with some 70 million shares traded.
