author: James Bricknell, Matt Poskitt
title: Best 3D Printer Filament Deals: Save Big on Big Brands
mainText: 3D printing has been a wonderful boost to all levels of creatives, allowing them to fully bring their ideas into the world in a tangible way. Whether you're making minis for your D&D campaign, new toy concepts for work, or you're just messing around, it's a lot of fun. Thankfully, there are also now more budget-friendly 3D printers than ever before too. While choosing the best 3D printer for your setup is crucial, you'll need some filament to get started, and it's important to get the right filament too. Filament comes in all different colors and chemical compositions -- which our best 3D-printing filament list explains in great detail -- and ranges in price from less than $20 to hundreds of dollars, depending on what you need. Thankfully, there are a fair amount of deals out there if you know where to look. Buying filament in bulk is often necessary so to save some time and money. We've scoured the web for the best discounts to take advantage of today.

author: The Conversation
title: How creativity defines the human species and is a source of wellness
mainText: How to bring creativity into daily life For those new to exploring art as a creative pursuit or for well-being reasons, engaging in creative activities begins with letting go of unrealistic expectations. Being creative isn’t about becoming a famous artist or even a mediocre one. It is about allowing ourselves to flex the creative muscle that we all have and enjoying all the sensory and emotional aspects of imagining. Next, think about activities that made you feel free to explore when you were a child. Did you like singing, playing in the outdoors, dancing, making up pretend plays, or writing little tales? Allow yourself to indulge in any and all of these creative pursuits that made you feel relaxed and joyful. A cultural tradition, tinkering with electronics, making a gift for someone or simply paying attention to everyday beauty—any of these can be a creative activity. And just like any muscle, the more you exercise it, the stronger it becomes. Over time, you will notice yourself getting more confident and adventurous in your creative practices.

author: Christine Sellers
title: FACT CHECK: Fact-Checking Trump's Claim That The US Left $85 Billion Worth Of Equipment In Afghanistan
mainText: During a June 15 event, Donald Trump claimed the US left $85 billion worth of military equipment in Afghanistan in 2021, but this claim is misleading. Reports from SIGAR suggest that the US spent $18 billion on equipment in Afghanistan. The Lead Inspector General's report from August 2022 stated that $7.12 billion worth of US military equipment was left in Afghanistan after the 2021 withdrawal. This equipment included military aircraft, ground vehicles, weapons, and more, with uncertainties about their condition and operability. The US military removed or destroyed most major equipment used in Afghanistan. CNN reported that the $7 billion worth of equipment had been transferred to the Afghan government over 16 years. Foreign policy experts debunked Trump's claim, with opinions varying on the actual value of equipment left in Afghanistan. The Pentagon claimed that only slightly over $7 billion worth of equipment was left behind. Different experts weighed in on Trump's numbers, with some criticizing the misinformation and others highlighting the broader implications of the US military presence and withdrawal from Afghanistan. The Washington Post, Fact Check.org, and Check Your Fact have also fact-checked Trump's claim, concluding that it is misleading. The Department of Defense has been contacted for comment on this matter.

author: Jennifer Bendery,Liz Skalka
title: GOP Rep. Bob Good Cites Suspicious 'Fires' In His District On Election Day
mainText: Rep. Bob Good (R-Va.), the House Freedom Caucus chairman, expressed suspicion on social media about several 'fires' at polling sites in his district on election day, two days earlier. He mentioned 3 'fires' at precincts and indicated a very low probability of these incidents occurring randomly. However, officials in the cited counties confirmed that only routine fire alarms went off, with no actual fires happening. Good's campaign later clarified that it was indeed fire alarms that led to polling locations being evacuated temporarily. Good is currently trailing in the election, making him the first House Republican at risk of losing a contested primary this cycle. He referenced these incidents in Albemarle, Hanover, and Lynchburg counties, where his primary opponent, state Sen. John McGuire, is leading in two out of the three. Good has a history of election objections, having voted against certifying Joe Biden's 2020 victory due to concerns about election integrity, despite the lack of evidence of widespread voter fraud. If Good loses, it would signify a significant defeat for him, as he has previously clashed with former President Donald Trump and former House Speaker Kevin McCarthy (R-Calif.). McGuire did not respond to inquiries about any involvement in the fire alarms on election day. Good's campaign stated that they are focused on canvassing efforts and do not have further information at this time.

author: Graham Kates
title: New York prosecutors ask judge to keep Trump gag order in "hush money" case in place
mainText: New York prosecutors are requesting the preservation of elements of a gag order preventing Donald Trump from publicly discussing specific individuals related to his New York criminal trial, even after his July 11 sentencing. The prosecutors argue that the order is necessary to protect jurors, attorneys, and staff from potential threats. They emphasize that since his conviction, Trump's rhetoric has not spared jurors, raising safety concerns. The gag order, issued on March 26 by Justice Juan Merchan, prohibits Trump from making public statements about witnesses, jurors, court proceedings, and prosecution staff, as well as their relatives. While prosecutors agreed that protections for witnesses could be lifted, they insist that other provisions should remain intact. Trump's repeated violations of the gag order, including inflammatory statements, prompted concerns about witness tampering and the integrity of the trial. His conviction on 34 counts of falsifying business records is related to a hush money payment before the 2016 election. Despite his denial of any wrongdoing, Trump faces the possibility of incarceration for both the conviction and further breaches of the gag order. Prosecutors hinted at the need to maintain the gag order post-sentencing, especially if Trump continues to challenge his conviction. The prosecutors cited numerous threats received by the office and implied that the protection of staff and their families from Trump's violent rhetoric may remain crucial during the appeals process.

author: Thomas Coughlan
title: Big Budget 2024 health spending question may be answered next week - Thomas Coughlan
mainText: The author discusses the delayed unveiling of details surrounding the health spending in Budget 2024 due to Labour's centralizing health reforms. Under the new system, a Government Policy Statement on Health will be developed, outlining priorities and funding allocations for Health NZ to execute. The statement is expected to cover around $27 billion to $29.5 billion annually, aiming for $85 billion over three years. Despite the lack of transparency in the budget documents, the new system promises to end the DHB system's inconsistencies while providing greater clarity through the GPS. The GPS is likely to focus on key priorities such as health workforce enhancement and community healthcare. Labour faces criticism over the funding level for health, with the opposition pointing out potential shortcomings in meeting demand due to increasing population and inflation. The Government's updated fiscal strategy targets an Obegal surplus by 2027/28, emphasizing economic growth while decoupling social service spending from population-driven costs. This strategy may face scrutiny given the challenges posed by rising inflation and population growth. The article highlights the potential implications of these fiscal and economic decisions on the health sector and the Government's overall fiscal approach.

author: Science X
title: After ISIS bombs, an urgent call to preserve an ancient Syrian temple
mainText: The Temple of Bel in Palmyra, Syria, was a significant archaeological site destroyed by ISIS in 2015 but not entirely. Authors Maamoun Abdulkarim and Jacques Seigne stress the urgent need for intervention to restore the temple and facilitate the return of the Palmyrene population. Built in the first two centuries of the Common Era, the temple served various functions over the years, including being used as a church, a mosque, and a residential shelter. The French mandate governance of Syria and Lebanon between 1920 and 1946 saw efforts to preserve Syria's antiquities. The villagers of Palmyra were displaced during this time but returned post-French archaeological mission. However, they were forced to flee again during ISIS occupations in 2015 and 2016. While ISIS bombs caused damage, the structure remains partly intact. Specialists confirmed that despite some collapsed walls and columns, certain parts of the temple stood firm. The authors emphasize the importance of the Palmyra community's return, as they are integral to the site's history. Preservation is crucial not only for visitor safety but also to stabilize the temple's place in Syria's history. The authors call for global cooperation to protect the Temple of Bel and restore a positive narrative for Palmyra.

author: Ingebjørg Hestvik
title: How E. coli defends itself against antibiotics
mainText: The pathogenic bacterium Escherichia coli reacts to exposure to the antibiotic Ciprofloxacin by experiencing damage to its DNA, leading to activation of an SOS response, according to a study by Bergum from the Department of Clinical and Molecular Medicine. Ciprofloxacin is a widely used antibiotic that attacks bacterial DNA. The protein that maintains DNA structure is targeted by the antibiotic, causing DNA damage and formation of incomplete DNA strands. This triggers an alarm within the bacterial cell, halting normal activities like replication and causing the bacteria to change shape. If repairs are unsuccessful, the bacteria mutate to develop resistance to antibiotics. Researchers at NTNU are studying the SOS response to understand how bacteria repair DNA damage and develop resistance. They discovered that all SOS genes are activated simultaneously, rather than sequentially. By analyzing gene activation, proteins, and small molecules during the response, researchers gained insights into the repair timeline. Preventing antibiotic resistance is challenging as not all bacteria are equally exposed to antibiotics during treatment. Bacteria can also develop resistance in natural environments, emphasizing the need to reduce antibiotic use. Understanding the SOS response mechanism can aid in developing new antibiotics and resistance-inhibiting substances. These inhibitors can be used in combination with existing antibiotics to prevent resistance development.

author: Nasa
title: Acquisition Integrity Program
mainText: The Acquisition Integrity Program (AIP) at NASA plays a crucial role in combatting procurement fraud by providing specialized guidance and advice, coordinating legal policies, representing NASA in interagency meetings, and responding to inquiries. The program is responsible for identifying, investigating, and prosecuting significant fraud allegations on NASA contracts and grants. It offers centralized services including case referrals, coordination of remedies, education and training for the NASA workforce, and outreach to the private sector. Contacts within the program include Director Monica Aquino-Thieman, Management and Program Analyst Laura Donegan, and Attorney Staff. The program operates under various regulations and policies, such as FAR Subpart 9.4, NASA FAR Supplement 1809.4, and NASA Policy Directive 2086.1. The website provides a disclaimer that the materials do not constitute legal advice.

author: Science X
title: New insights into methyl jasmonate-induced saponin biosynthesis in the balloon flower
mainText: Platycodon grandiflorus, also known as balloon flower, is valued for its medicinal properties due to its saponin content, known for anti-inflammatory and immune-boosting effects. However, challenges in cultivation and low saponin yield hinder its widespread use. Researchers studied the effects of methyl jasmonate (MeJA) on saponin biosynthesis in P. grandiflorus. They identified the PgbHLH28 gene as critical in saponin accumulation. MeJA at 100 μmol/l was found to optimize saponin accumulation. Overexpressing PgbHLH28 increased saponin content, while silencing it inhibited synthesis. The gene binds to promoters of PgHMGR2 and PgDXS2, enhancing saponin production. These findings reveal a regulatory network controlling saponin production. Dr. Tao Yang highlighted the potential for genetic modifications to enhance saponin content, offering new possibilities for medicinal plant development. These insights could lead to the creation of high-saponin-yielding P. grandiflorus cultivars with enhanced medicinal value, benefiting pharmaceutical and agricultural industries. This research could lead to improved natural treatments for health conditions and aid in cultivating other medicinal plants, promoting the use of natural compounds in modern medicine.

author: Science X
title: Unlocking broccoli's genome: Key to enhanced health benefits
mainText: Broccoli is renowned for its health benefits, primarily due to its rich glucosinolate (GSL) content, which has anti-carcinogenic and antioxidant properties. Despite extensive studies on Brassica species, the genetic basis for GSL diversity remains unclear. Understanding these mechanisms is crucial for enhancing the nutritional value of broccoli and related crops. Previous research has identified various GSL structures, but the specific genes and their roles in GSL biosynthesis need further exploration. Addressing these gaps is essential for developing genetically improved Brassica crops with enhanced health benefits. Researchers from Hunan Agricultural University have published a study in Horticulture Research, presenting a chromosome-scale genome assembly of broccoli. This study utilizes advanced sequencing technologies to provide a detailed analysis of GSL biosynthesis. The study successfully assembled a high-quality chromosome-scale genome of broccoli using advanced PacBio HiFi reads and Hi-C technology, achieving a total genome size of 613.79 Mb and a contig N50 of 14.70 Mb. This detailed genomic map allowed the identification of key genes involved in GSL biosynthesis, including the crucial methylthioalkylmalate synthase 1 (MAM1) gene. The research demonstrated that overexpression of BoMAM1 in broccoli significantly increases the accumulation of C4-GSLs, highlighting its vital role in GSL biosynthesis. Additionally, the study provided insights into the evolutionary mechanisms that contribute to the diversity of GSL profiles among different Brassica species. These findings offer a comprehensive understanding of the genetic factors influencing GSL production, which is essential for future genetic studies and the development of Brassica crops with enhanced nutritional properties. Dr. Junwei Wang, a corresponding author of the study, stated, "Our findings provide a comprehensive understanding of the genetic factors influencing GSL biosynthesis in broccoli. This knowledge is crucial for future genetic improvement and enhancing the nutritional value of Brassica crops." This genomic study offers valuable resources for molecular breeding programs aimed at improving the nutritional content of broccoli and other Brassica crops. By understanding the genetic basis of GSL biosynthesis, researchers can develop varieties with enhanced health benefits, contributing to better human health and nutrition.

author: Aaron Becker
title: Position battles to watch in Steelers training camp
mainText: The Pittsburgh Steelers had an active offseason with changes in key positions, leading to uncertainty about the starting lineup for Week 1. The notable position battles to watch in training camp include the quarterback battle between Russell Wilson and Justin Fields. Wilson was signed in free agency, while Fields was acquired through a trade, both seen as upgrades over the previous quarterbacks. However, only one can win the starting job, with Wilson currently having the edge. The wide receiver position also presents a battle, with George Pickens as the mainstay and players like Roman Wilson, Quez Watkins, and Scotty Miller competing to complement him. The team may look to trade for a more established receiver. In the offensive tackle position battle, rookies Broderick Jones and Troy Fautanu are vying for starting spots alongside Dan Moore Jr. and Zach Frazier. Jones, a first-round pick from the previous year, is looking to move to the left side, which could impact the lineup. Training camp will be crucial in determining the final starters for the team.

author: Sam Nestler
title: Will a Stanley Cup change the narrative around Stuart Skinner?
mainText: Edmonton Oilers goaltender Stuart Skinner was being dragged through the mud by fans and media for his poor play in the Stanley Cup Playoffs. He stuck it out, his coach and teammates believed in him and he has become a huge positive storyline in the Stanley Cup Final. In Games 4-7 in these playoffs, Skinner has gone 9-0 with a .938 save percentage and 1.56 goals-against average. But is his success a byproduct of better defending and more offensive support? Or has he found a new level that many believed he would never reach? More importantly, would bringing the Oilers back from 3-0 to win their first Stanley Cup in 24 years change the narrative surrounding him? Tyler Yaremchuk: Stuart Skinner... remarkable. And maybe what’s more impressive than that is in each of the last two games, he’s come through with timely, big saves early. Frank Seravalli: Does the narrative around Stuart Skinner change if he wins the cup? Or will he always be the NHL backup-caliber goalie who played with a really good offense in front of him? Carter Hutton: I think for now, that is going to be the case... Especially for a goalie that has a sub-900 save percentage here in the Stanley Cup Final. But I also think he’s going to be a legend forever if they can get this job done and come back from that… It’s hard to take away his credit, what he’s done is so amazing. But I also feel like there’s a little bit of that shadow cast because of McDavid.

author: Craig Smith
title: Calais Campbell's contract amount underscores a promising trend during the Miami Dolphins' offseason
mainText: $2 million is a sharp drop from what Campbell had been earning in recent seasons. He appeared in all 17 games last year for Atlanta with a solid 6.5 sacks and 10 tackles for loss. Odell Beckham, Jr.'s contract for one year, $3 million was surprisingly low - even though incentives will reportedly take that up to over $8 million. Jordan Poyer's deal was for one year, $2 million. Campbell is a six-time Pro Bowler. Poyer was a key part of some excellent Buffalo teams. Beckham is a Super Bowl champion and was one of the best players in the league during his time in New York. All three took less money than they probably could have gotten elsewhere on the market to come to Miami. That should give Dolphins fans a lot of confidence in what Miami could do in 2024.

author: Nick Geddes
title: Corey LaJoie, Skip Flores gives surprising take on Kyle Larson, Daniel Suarez wreck
mainText: Kyle Larson’s run in this past Sunday’s race at Iowa was ruined on Lap 219 when Daniel Suarez got into his left rear coming off Turn 4 and sent him into the wall. Throughout much of the race to that point, Larson looked as if he had the fastest car in the field. Of course, he had nothing to show for it, finishing a season-worst P34. Corey LaJoie and Skip Flores, tire changer for Ryan Blaney’s No. 12 team, discussed the accident on “Stacking Pennies” this week. LaJoie offered his perspective, saying it looked like Suarez got a little loose coming out of the old asphalt before Larson made it three-wide. Kyle Larson turning the page to New Hampshire Flores, meanwhile, believes there may have been a point earlier in the race where Larson used Suarez up. And when Larson made it tight coming off Turn 4, Suarez wasn’t gonna budge. Whatever the case, Larson missed an opportunity to win back-to-back races and will now turn his attention to this Sunday at New Hampshire. While he’s never taken the checkered flag in Loudon, he has been close multiple times. He finished P3 last season and has tallied four other top-three finishes at the track. Look for him to once again be in the mix this time around.

author: Rory Maher
title: LeBron James reportedly expected to decline player option
mainText: Woike’s report isn’t surprising. Rich Paul of Klutch Sports, James’ agent, referred to his longtime friend and client as an impending free agent during a TNT Sports altcast at the end of last month before attempting to walk back the comment. Opting out would give James, the NBA’s all-time leading scorer, the opportunity to negotiate a full no-trade clause if he re-signs with L.A., which is widely viewed as the likely outcome. Due to the Over-38 rule, James will be limited to a three-year contract, though the 39-year-old is reportedly only looking to play for another year or two. In his 21st season in 2023-24, James averaged 25.7 PPG, 7.3 RPG, 8.3 APG and 1.3 SPG on .540/.410/.750 shooting across 71 regular-season contests (35.3 MPG). He averaged 27.8 PPG, 6.8 RPG, 8.8 APG, 2.4 SPG and 1.0 BPG on .566/.385/.739 shooting in the Lakers’ first-round playoff loss to Denver. James extended his own NBA record last season by making his 20th All-NBA team, all of which have come consecutively. Kobe Bryant, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Tim Duncan are all tied in second place with 15 total nods each. James also made his 20th straight All-Star appearance in 2023-24.

author: Victor Tangermann
title: Tourists Dropping Dead From Heat in Greece
mainText: Heat Stroke Two French women and a US man have gone missing on the Greek island of Amorgos, with temperatures soaring over 100 degrees Fahrenheit, stoking fears that they may have passed away due to the unseasonally hot weather and highlighting the growing danger of climate change. As CNN reports, several tourists have already died in the extreme heat engulfing the European islands over the last couple of weeks, including a British health guru named Michael Mosley who went missing in early June after embarking on a long walk, with his body found several days later. The incidents and ongoing search-and-rescue missions highlight just how dangerous this summer's soaring temperatures can be to the human body. Scientists warn that extreme heat can reduce blood flow to the brain, impairing complex decision-making. Deadly Hike The latest disappearances come after a string of deaths on the Greek islands. The body of another American tourist was discovered over the weekend on the tiny island of Mathraki, though the exact cause of death has yet to be determined. A Dutch tourist was found dead on the island of Crete on Saturday after his car was spotted on a cliff edge. "There is a common pattern — they all went for a hike amid high temperatures," police spokesman for the Southern Aegean Petros Vassilakis told Reuters. Whether the deaths can be chalked up to global warming remains unclear, but it's certainly a possibility. Researchers have shown that the number of stroke-related deaths and disabilities linked to extreme temperatures has been steadily growing since 1990, suggesting a link to the wide-ranging effects of climate change. Now, all eyes are on the three individuals who were announced missing over the weekend. The brother of the American tourist has since spoken up, urging the US government to help out. More on hot weather: Climate Change Now Linked To Rise In Strokes

author: Lance Whitney
title: Apple brings Final Cut to the iPhone to help you shoot professional videos
mainText: Apple has launched the Final Cut Camera app for iOS, which allows iPhone users to create professional-quality videos with features like zoom, exposure control, focus adjustment, and more. The app also offers multi-camera capabilities when combined with up to three other iOS devices. While a subscription to Final Cut Pro for iPad and a monthly fee are required for advanced features, the standalone app provides ample tools for video editing. Users can adjust settings like temperature, exposure, focus, aspect ratio, and video format within the app. Other features include zoom controls, codec selection, HDR options, frame rate adjustments, stabilization, and on-screen grid alignment. The app supports shooting in 720p, 1080p, or 4K resolution. Additionally, the app can be used in a multi-camera setup by syncing with Final Cut Pro on an iPad, allowing for live streaming and editing. The Live Multicam feature enables streaming from up to four devices to Final Cut Pro on an iPad, with control over recording and editing. The resulting clips from the multi-cam shoot can be edited seamlessly in Final Cut Pro. This innovative app provides iPhone users with powerful video editing capabilities, making it easier to shoot and edit high-quality videos on their devices.

author: Isaac Schultz
title: A Bonus 'Hitchhiker' Will Come Back From Mars in Perseverance's Sample Tubes
mainText: The Perseverance rover has been toiling on the Martian surface for over three years, collecting rock samples that will eventually be brought to Earth if all goes according to plan. But the rover has also picked up hitchhikers, in the form of traces of Martian atmosphere that are squeezed into the “headspace” of the sample tubes. That’s very exciting for atmospheric scientists, who so far have only studied Mars’ air remotely, whether from orbiters characterizing the planet from on high or from rovers delivering readouts to experts on Earth. Should this all work, it’ll be an incredible bonus for these scientists to analyze Martian rocks in Earth-based labs. Forget the rock samples, the material stuff that planetary scientists hope will explain Mars’ evolution, and which astrobiologists hope will contain hints of ancient life on the fourth planet from the Sun. The Martian air will give researchers the chance to understand how Martian dust filters through the planet’s air, which sometimes whips up into Martian dust devils. The air samples could also reveal how much water vapor lies just above the planet’s surface. Mars’ air has recently been a great venue for exploration. But there’s one big problem keeping NASA scientists from exploring the samples of Mars’ surface and skies: the cost. The Mars Sample Return mission is an expensive one, leading to delays in the mission timeline. At this point, Perseverance has collected over two dozen rock samples, chosen for their potential to reveal aspects of the planet’s geochemistry, geological history, and other aspects of its makeup and evolution. At this point, using instruments capture, recover, and decipher the makeup of another planet’s skies seems like the easy part. The hard part is actually funding such an endeavor.

author: Simon Cohen
title: Samsung’s next Galaxy Buds could be its most comfortable design yet
mainText: If a recently discovered render — purportedly of the as-yet-unreleased Samsung Galaxy Buds 3 — is accurate, the company’s next wireless earbuds could offer big improvements in comfort for those who have traditionally found it hard get a good fit. A set of images for a silicone charging case sleeve made by Elago — apparently pulled from the website of Korean retailer Coupang by X (formerly Twitter) user @TEQHNIKACROSS, according to The Verge — appears to show an entirely new design for the Samsung Galaxy Buds 3, one that invites a lot of comparisons to Apple’s AirPods Pro. The product page is no longer on Coupang’s site, which lends credibility to the notion that the images are real. The pictured earbuds have a stem-based shape — which would be a first for Samsung — and feature venting and microphone covers with very similar placements to Apple’s flagship wireless earbuds. Even the charging case takes a clear inspiration from Apple’s design, though Samsung has apparently put its own spin on the concept by making the flip-top lid out of a transparent plastic. Stem-based wireless earbuds, like the AirPods Pro, tend to offer a more comfortable fit than those that use a stemless design. The stem allows engineers to place critical components like batteries, touch controls, and microphones outside of the main body of the earbud, which can substantially reduce the amount of space taken up in the ear itself. We’ve reviewed virtually all of Samsung’s wireless earbuds, including the Samsung Galaxy Buds, Galaxy Buds+, Galaxy Buds Pro, Galaxy Buds 2, Galaxy Buds 2 Pro, and Galaxy Buds FE, and we found each design to be perfectly fine comfort-wise. However, not everyone agrees with those assessments. A quick look on Reddit reveals that many buyers have struggled to get a comfortable and secure fit with their Samsung Galaxy earbuds. That’s not to say you won’t find disgruntled AirPods Pro owners too, but a stem-based design for the Samsung Galaxy 3 (if in fact that’s what Samsung is planning) will give its customers a choice that they have so far lacked. For those who prefer the fit of a stem-based earbud, Samsung might soon have a way to keep these buyers within the Galaxy family. Some of those buyers might actually own iPhones too.

author: Paul Tassi
title: ‘The Boys’ Viewership Up, ‘House Of The Dragon’ Viewership Down, With a Catch
mainText: The Boys/House of the Dragon Amazon/Max Two colossal new shows have returned this month (The Bear soon, too?) in the form of The Boys season 4 on Amazon Prime Video and House of the Dragon on Max. Though one is a clear win with a viewership increase, the other is a bit more wobbly with a decline, but there’s more to it than that. The Boys viewership is up 21% with season 4 after its premiere, says Amazon, which makes it the biggest returning season on the service outside of Reacher season 2. This 21% increase is up over season 3, and the show has only seen its viewership increase across the years as it gets bigger and bigger as one of Amazon's top series alongside Rings of Power, Reacher, and now recently Fallout. On Max, Nielsen reports that season 2 of House of the Dragon is down 22% from its series launch, below the 10 million season 1 launched with. The catch here is that a lot of this is due to a drop in linear viewing, ie. people actually watching it on HBO, where The Boys does not have a cable channel as an alternative. But in terms of streaming, this is Max’s biggest streaming day ever, they say, and the biggest season 2 premiere of any of its streaming services in Europe specifically. That region saw a 30% increase over season 1’s premiere in Europe. The Boys, meanwhile, debuted as a relatively unknown IP, and interest has just snowballed in time. House of the Dragon and The Boys have something in common, in that both are performing so well that it’s led to the greenlighting of multiple spin-offs/in-universe projects. The Boys already has an animated installment and Gen V, and even if it ends after season 5, as it’s supposed to, will have other shows like The Boys: Mexico starting up. House of the Dragon is the first of many Game of Thrones prequel series, the next one being A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, adapted from George RR Martin’s work. And others are on the way, including more Targaryen tales, potentially.

author: Mohua Chatterjee
title: INDIA builds pressure on govt: Mamata asks PM to review criminal Bills
mainText: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi urging him to defer the implementation of three criminal laws recently passed by the government. These laws were criticized for being rushed and for expelling 146 members from both Houses. Banerjee's letter marks the beginning of increased pressure on the Modi-led NDA government by the INDIA bloc of opposition parties. Senior Congress leader P Chidambaram met with Banerjee to discuss the legislation, signaling coordination within the opposition. The INDIA bloc is pushing for a review of several other Bills in addition to the criminal laws. TMC leader Derek O'Brien listed five such legislations for review by the government. Banerjee emphasized the need for a parliamentary review and upholding the rule of law in the country. The issue is expected to be raised in the upcoming Parliament session, showing a united front by the opposition parties.

author: Dominick Reuter
title: The new laptop-sized Starlink Mini could be the ultimate off-grid travel gadget | Business Insider India
mainText: SpaceX internet division Starlink is offering a new smaller, more portable satellite dish. The laptop-sized Mini device draws less power than the full-sized Standard, and can reach 100Mbps. Staying connected while off the grid is getting even easier. Starlink, the satellite internet division of SpaceX, is now offering a new smaller, more portable dish it calls the Mini. At 11.75 inches by 10.2 inches and weighing less than 2.5 pounds, the laptop-sized device fits easily into a backpack and can reach 100Mbps. It also draws less power than the full-sized Standard, which means the Mini is capable of running on a 100W USB-C PD battery pack, which The Verge estimates estimates could give you about an hour of run-time on a 10,000mAh pack. "I just set it up right now and am writing this post through space. Took less than 5 mins," SpaceX CEO Elon Musk wrote on X. "This product will change the world." Musk also claimed his connection achieved a remarkably low 23ms latency — fast enough for online gaming. The unit costs $599 in the US, but sales here are currently by invitation only as an add-on service to residential service plans. Additional regions will be available in the future, but for now only customers in Colombia, El Salvador, Guatemala, and Panama can purchase a Mini, where it is available at a lower price with a special standalone service option. "Our goal is to reduce the price of Starlink, especially for those around the world where connectivity has been unaffordable or completely unavailable," Starlink said. Outdoor enthusiasts and digital nomads alike welcomed the concept on X. "This would be a game-changer for me," Ron Stauffer posted. "I've spent the past decade awkwardly Wi-Fi-hopping from coffee shops to restaurants to coworking spaces and tethering from my iPhone. I always have my backpack with me, so this sounds like the perfect solution."

author: Tim Macmahon
title: GM: 'Warrior' Luka, rest of Mavs must improve, but team's core set - ESPN
mainText: DALLAS -- In the wake of an NBA Finals run, Mavericks general manager Nico Harrison said he plans for the team's rotation to return intact next season and has issued a challenge for "everybody to come back 10 to 15% better." That includes superstar Luka Doncic, an MVP finalist who just became the first player in NBA history to lead the league in total points, rebounds, assists and steals during a postseason. Asked how Doncic could make that sort of improvement, Harrison pointed to how the five-time first-team All-NBA selection responded to harsh criticism following the Mavs' Game 3 loss to the Boston Celtics. Doncic's poor defense and petulant demeanor were spotlighted after that loss, when he fouled out with 4:12 remaining. He bounced back with a poised, dominant performance in a Game 4 blowout that was Dallas' lone win of the series. "We're not where we're at without Luka," Harrison said Friday. "I think that's important to point out, and we also won't be able to get where we want to go without the best version of Luka. If you look at a guy who after Game 3 had the world on his neck -- the scrutiny, which was crazy, the amount of scrutiny that he had to face -- for him to focus in and do what he did in Game 4, I just think it just shows the character of him. He's willing to fight through adversity, and I think he's going to continue to get better. "He's 25 years old. I think just going through the Finals, him seeing what he needs to do to be at his best in the Finals after going through a grueling end of the year and then three tough, tough [playoff] matchups, I think you're going to see the best version of him." Doncic, who won his first scoring title by averaging 33.9 points per game this season, dealt with a variety of injuries throughout the playoffs. He sprained his right knee in the first round, had left ankle soreness listed on the injury report for several games beginning in the second round and suffered a thoracic contusion in the Finals opener that required pregame pain-killing injections for the rest of the series. Doncic was listed as questionable on multiple occasions during the Mavs' playoff run, but he played in every game, logging a league-high 899 postseason minutes. "He was hurting, but he's a warrior," Harrison said. "He's going to fight through all those injuries. That's just who he is. He loves to play." After the Mavs were eliminated Monday night, Doncic was noncommittal about whether he would play for the Slovenian national team this summer, saying that he was "just trying to get a little bit healthier." Harrison said he expects that Doncic, as he has every summer of his NBA career, will play for Slovenia, which will play in an Olympic qualifying tournament in Greece beginning July 2. "That's probably one of his biggest joys," Harrison said of Doncic playing for Slovenia, which he led to the men's basketball program's first Olympic berth and a fourth-place finish three years ago. "I think as long as he can walk, he's probably going to go out there and play for them." Harrison aggressively upgraded the supporting cast around Doncic and co-star Kyrie Irving over the last year, drafting All-Rookie center Dereck Lively II with a lottery pick and acquiring starting power forward P.J. Washington and center Daniel Gafford in separate deals at the trade deadline. The Mavs also got massive value by signing small forward Derrick Jones Jr. to a veteran's minimum deal last summer. Jones, who started and usually took the toughest defensive assignment, is the only Dallas rotation player who isn't under contract for next season. There is mutual interest in Jones returning to Dallas, but the Mavs are limited to offering the $5.2 million taxpayer midlevel exception unless they trim enough payroll to open up the $12.9 million nontaxpayer midlevel exception. "I don't know how we're going to do it, but he's a priority," Harrison said. He added that he expects the Mavs' "top seven or eight" players to return but will explore other avenues to upgrade the roster. "He's priority one -- 1A and 1B. I think he fits in with our team. He loves it here and we have to figure out obviously the dynamics to get him to stay. But that's a priority and we'll do what we have to do to get it done."

author: Isabelle Kliger
title: Barcelona Announces Plan To Ban Tourist Rental Apartments By 2028
mainText: The mayor of Barcelona, Jaume Collboni, has today announced a controversial and drastic move to get rid of all short-term apartment rentals for tourists by 2028. Rising living costs in Barcelona have led to a significant increase, making it difficult for many residents to afford apartments. This decision aims to address the issue of inequality, particularly among young people, by ensuring access to housing in the city. Spain, being one of the most-visited countries, has seen rising concerns over overtourism in Barcelona. The recent measures to regulate short-term rentals have already resulted in the shutdown of illegal tourist rentals. The latest step by Mayor Collboni involves phasing out licensed tourist apartments by 2028, a move that is expected to face opposition and legal challenges.

author: Laurie Werner
title: Four Seasons Yachts Announces Upcoming Launch And 23 Itineraries
mainText: Four Seasons Yachts is set to launch its first all-suite yacht, Four Seasons 1, in 2026. The yacht will offer luxury experiences at sea, with over 130 destinations across 33 countries and territories. The itineraries will include land options for pre or post trips at Four Seasons resorts. The yacht will feature 95 suites with modular walls allowing for various connection options, including large family or group accommodations. There will be seven signature suites with indoor and outdoor living spaces, splash pools, and more. The design of the yacht aims for elegance and simplicity, reflecting the Four Seasons style. Onboard, guests can enjoy 11 dining options, spa amenities, a 65-foot stern pool, and a 1:1 guest to staff ratio. The itineraries will cover destinations like the Mediterranean, Greek islands, the Caribbean, and ports of call such as Saint-Tropez, Cannes, and Capri among others. Offshore activities like rosé vineyard tours and truffle hunting will be offered to enhance the destination experience. The yacht is being built by Fincantieri in Italy and will provide a luxurious and personalized cruise experience for guests.

author: Alex Ledsom
title: China UNESCO Site Installs Restroom Timers For Tourists
mainText: China's Yungang Buddhist Grottoes in the Shanxi Province has installed timers in visitor restrooms to track the time spent by individuals inside each stall. The installation aims to address the challenge of inadequate public restrooms, which impact the overall tourist experience. The move also serves as a safety measure to monitor stall occupancy and offer assistance if needed. The site, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its 51,000 statues in 252 caves dating back to the 5th and 6th centuries, has seen a significant increase in visitors, with 3 million people in 2023 compared to almost 2 million in 2019 pre-pandemic. Various initiatives globally are working to enhance restroom access, such as Throne in the U.S. that offers modern mobile toilets and Peequal in the U.K. which provides women's urinals to reduce queue times and improve hygiene. Some cities like New York are introducing restroom accessibility initiatives, while places like Japan are implementing innovative restroom designs, including a transparent restroom that turns opaque when in use and turns into lanterns at night. 'Toilet tourism' has even become a niche concept, with tours in Tokyo showcasing modern restroom designs for interested visitors.

author: Sharnaz Shahid
title: How to save your battery at a festival - and other useful iPhone tips
mainText: With Glastonbury just around the corner, packing and preparing for the four-day music weekend is no easy feat. Here at HELLO!, we've listed the best ways to use your iPhone during the festival - and some tips that we will definitely be using ourselves! Since festivals are all about the experience, the music, and capturing memorable moments, nothing can dampen your mood faster than a dead phone battery. Here are some handy tips to keep your iPhone charged and functional throughout the event. Capture the moment Don't miss out on capturing your favourite festival moments. Use the camera remote with a 3-second timer on your Apple Watch to snap perfect selfies and group shots on your iPhone. No need to struggle with awkward angles or rely on strangers for photos! If you want to position your iPhone for a photo and then take the photo from a distance, you can use the camera remote on your Apple Watch to view the iPhone camera image and take the photo. Optimise battery usage Enable Low Power Mode: Activate this mode through Settings > Battery. It reduces background activity, automatic downloads, and visual effects, significantly extending battery life. Turn Off Unnecessary Features: Disable Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and AirDrop when not in use. These features constantly search for connections, draining your battery. Reduce Screen Brightness: Lowering your screen brightness or enabling Auto-Brightness (Settings > Accessibility > Display & Text Size > Auto-Brightness) can save a considerable amount of power. Use Airplane Mode Bring portable chargers and a charging phone case Always find the way to your tent Attach an AirTag to your tent to easily locate it within the festival grounds with the Find My app on iPhone, you'll never feel lost trying to find your way back to your tent in the dark, and after a long day of music and fun. iOS 17 lets you share AirTag with up to 5 people (in addition to yourself, for a total of six users per item – now that’s a tent-full), so everyone can see its location and find their way back after a long day in the field. Share the Experience Create a shared album on your iPhone to instantly share photos and memories with your friend group. Simply create an album, invite your friends to join, and everyone can contribute photos and videos to the shared album, ensuring everyone has access to the memories without the need for individual sharing. To set up a shared album you need to update your iPhone to the latest iOS – sign into iCloud with your Apple ID on your iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > [your name] > iCloud > Photos, then turn on Shared Albums. Stay connected with your friends Find people and share your location with the Find My app on iPhone to easily locate each other amidst the festival crowd. Keep track of your friends and ensure you're always part of the action. When you share your location in a Messages conversation, it updates in real time right in the conversation. You can share your location by tapping Current Location (above the keyboard) when somebody asks where you are. If both you and a friend are using an iPhone 15 model, you can use Precision Finding for Find My Friends to get precise directions and distance to their location once you’re near one another. See Use Precision Finding on iPhone 15 to meet up with a friend. Never lose your tickets Add your festival tickets to Wallet on your iPhone and Apple Watch for quick and easy access at the gate. Your passes in Wallet on iPhone will seamlessly sync to your Apple Watch, ensuring you always have your tickets handy. To add a pass to Wallet, open the app, email, notification or other communication that contains your boarding pass, ticket or other pass. When you add a boarding pass, ticket, or other pass to the Wallet app on your iPhone, it’s added automatically to the Wallet app on your paired Apple Watch.

author: Rio Yamat
title: Shiny monolith removed from mountains outside Las Vegas. How it got there still is a mystery
mainText: A mysterious monolith discovered in a remote mountain range near Las Vegas has been removed by authorities, sparking intrigue over how it appeared there. The 6-foot-4 prism, reminiscent of the one in '2001: A Space Odyssey,' was found near Gass Peak in the Desert National Wildlife Refuge. This occurrence echoes a global trend of similar monolith sightings since 2020 in locations like Utah, Romania, and downtown Las Vegas, all swiftly disappearing. The latest monolith in Las Vegas was deemed a public safety and environmental hazard due to its location on federal land designated for wildlife protection. Authorities are investigating its origin and have urged caution to prevent environmental damage. The monolith, constructed from reflective metal, was removed and is now under scrutiny by officials. The incident mirrors the controversial removal of a similar monolith in Utah, which led to landscape damage and public safety concerns. Both cases have raised questions about illegal installations on protected lands. The investigation into these monoliths continues as authorities work to address the environmental impact and maintain safety protocols. The bizarre appearance and removal of these structures remain unsolved phenomena that have captivated the public's curiosity and imagination.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: "No Consular Access Request": India On US Murder-For-Hire Plot Case
mainText: The government today said it has not received any consular access request from Nikhil Gupta, an Indian accused of being involved in a murder-for-hire plot against a Khalistani terrorist on American soil. "We are in touch with his family," it added. Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) Spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated, "We have so far not received any request for Consular access for Mr Gupta but his family has got in touch with us and we are in touch with the family members. We are looking at the matter as to what can be done on the request." India has designated Pannun a terrorist but dissociated itself from the plot. The lawyer of Mr Gupta mentioned that it is crucial not to jump to conclusions early in the case and that a vigorous defense will be pursued. The murder-for-hire case can lead to a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison, according to the US Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York. In a separate development, India voiced concern to the Canadian High Commission in Delhi regarding 'Citizen's Courts' organised by Khalistani activists in Canada. This protest by India followed a two-minute silence observed by the Canadian Parliament on the death anniversary of separatist Hardeep Singh Nijjar.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: India slams Canadian House's ‘silence’ tribute to Khalistani terrorist Nijjar
mainText: India on Friday slammed the Canadian parliament's ‘moment of silence’ for Khalistani Tiger Force terrorist Hardeep Singh Nijjar on June 18, exactly a year after he was gunned down in Surrey, British Columbia. “We oppose any move giving political space to extremism,” ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said at the weekly briefing. Canada's House of Commons had observed ‘moment of silence’ in the memory of Hardeep Singh Nijjar, whose killing has strained relations between India and Canada. Last September, Canadian prime minister Justin Trudeau claimed before the North American country's parliament about ‘credible allegations’ of a potential role of Indian agents in the killing of Nijjar. The Canadian intelligence has been trying to build a narrative to project Nijjar as an innocent and religious-minded head of Guru Nanak Gurudwara in Surrey, Canada. A dossier prepared by Indian intelligence agencies stated that Nijjar was became the head of the Sikh temple by threatening his own cousin Raghbir Singh Nijjar. However, Trudeau is yet to provide any concrete proof to substantiate his allegations. India has repeatedly asked Ottawa to crack down on pro-Khalistani extremists carrying out anti-India activities from its soil. However, Trudeau's government has turned a deaf ear to India's objections. On Thursday, India had lodged a strong protest with Canada over an event by pro-Khalistani elements burning the effigy of Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Vancouver. External affairs minister S Jaishankar last month had said that New Delhi gave Ottawa a list of 25 names that included Khalistani extremists and gangsters, for extradition, but there was no response from the Trudeau government. It is known that the Canadian prime minister runs a minority government with support of Khalistan-linked New Democratic Party run by India hater Jagmeet Singh. Foreign Secretary Vinay Kwatra last week said India's main issue with Canada continues to be the political space that Ottawa provides to anti-India elements which advocate extremism and violence.

author: Rapid Recap Team
title: 98 Indians Died Of Natural Causes During Hajj, Says Foreign Ministry
mainText: Ninety-eight Indians have died in Saudi Arabia during Hajj this year, the government said today. All deaths are due to "natural causes", the Foreign Ministry said. This year 1,75,000 Indians have visited Saudi for hajj till now, the government said. "We will do all we can for the Indians there," it said. Around 10 countries have reported 1,081 deaths during the pilgrimage, one of the five pillars of Islam which all Muslims with the means must complete at least once. The hajj, whose timing is determined by the lunar Islamic calendar, fell again this year during the oven-like Saudi summer.

title: Share Market Highlights 21 June 2024: Sensex and Nifty end winning streak, decline amid global market pressures
mainText: Aster DM Healthcare is in focus as Olympus Capital Asia Investment plans to sell 10.1% equity through a block deal. author: Kanav Khanduja
title: Vladimir Putin, Kim Jong Un drive each other in Russian Aurus limousine and exchange gifts — watch video | Mint
mainText: A recent video shows Russian President Vladimir Putin and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un driving a Russian-built Aurus Limousine. This attempt to show the connection between Russia and North Korea has gone viral on social media. Putin recently visited North Korea for the first time since 2000 to sign a treaty, that is crucial to both nations. The pact promises that both nations will provide immediate military support if either of them is attacked.The video shows Putin driving Kim Jong Un through a park in the Russian presidential vehicle, an armoured limousine, while both leaders have a seemingly pleasant conversation and are seen laughing.After exiting the car, they continued walking shoulder-to-shoulder on a footpath surrounded by greenery.Putin allegedly gifted Kim Jong Un the vehicle they can be seen driving. It has been reported that Putin had gifted Kim the same vehicle in February, meaning Kim now has two vehicles of the same kind. The car is the Aurus Senat with a retro style based on the ZIL Limousine of the Soviet era. Putin also showed Kim the vehicle when he visited Russia last September.Kim Jong Un is known to be an automobile enthusiast and has been seen in many luxury cars, even though the UN Security Council has banned the export of luxury goods to North Korea. His collection includes a Maybach Limousine, a Lexus sports car, a Rolls Royce Phantom, various Mercedes, and more.Kim did not allow Putin to go home empty-handed, either. He gifted Putin two Pungsan dogs, a hunting breed native to North Korea. A government broadcast on Thursday on Korean Central Television showed the two leaders having a chat with the pair of dogs tied in front of them. They also tended to and fed a horse, bonding over a shared passion for animals.

author: Jennifer Sinco Kelleher
title: Hawaii settles lawsuit from youths over climate change. Here's what to know about the historic deal
mainText: HONOLULU — About two years after 13 children and teens sued Hawaii over the threat posed by climate change, both sides reached a settlement that includes an ambitious requirement to decarbonize the state’s transportation system over the next 21 years. Navahine v. Hawaii Department of Transportation is the world’s first youth-led constitutional climate case addressing climate pollution from the transportation sector. One plaintiff, a 14-year-old Native Hawaiian, comes from a family that farmed taro for more than 10 generations, but climate change has impacted their crop yields and land. The settlement mandates zero greenhouse gas emissions across all transportation modes by 2045 and includes the expansion of electric vehicle charging networks. Hawaii is particularly vulnerable to climate disasters due to its isolated location in the Pacific. The agreement also places accountability on Hawaii through a judge, ensuring enforcement of the settlement. The state is not admitting liability but recognizing the importance of addressing climate issues. Similar climate-related legal battles are ongoing in Montana and Oregon, showcasing the growing youth activism on environmental concerns. The successful settlement in Hawaii reflects a collaborative effort between state officials, young plaintiffs, and legal representatives to combat climate change and protect future generations in the state.

author: Michael Williams
title: ‘Absolute nightmare’: cyberattack leaves thousands of car dealers in turmoil
mainText: If you’re in the market for a new vehicle, you might want to hit the brakes for now. A recent cyberattack has sent shockwaves through thousands of car dealerships across North America, disrupting their operations and crippling sales. The attack targeted CDK Global, a crucial provider of software services essential for car sales and dealership management. As a result, its systems have been offline for several days, impacting more than 15,000 auto dealerships in Canada and the United States. “The day-to-day is an absolute nightmare,” said Brian Matsumoto, a local car sales manager. “CDK is our main database tool, all of our information filters through it,” he added. Matsumoto explains that the system handles critical tasks such as finalizing deals, generating bills of sale, and processing necessary legal documents. “As a result, everything has to be handwritten,” he said. Matsumoto noted that the disruption is not only slowing down transactions but also deterring potential customers from making purchases. “What used to take ten to fifteen minutes, is now taking upwards of over an hour. Customers are getting a bit scared off, they’re used to digitized copies, it creates a huge insecurity with the customer.” CDK victim to multiple cyberattacks CDK Global initially fell victim to a cyberattack on Tuesday, according to cybersecurity news site Bleeping Computer. By Wednesday, a spokesperson from the company confirmed they were “actively investigating a cyber incident” and decided to shut down all systems as a precautionary measure. The situation then escalated further when another cyber incident occurred later on Wednesday evening. As of Friday morning, a recorded message on CDK’s customer hotline stated, “We do not have an estimated timeframe for resolution,” indicating that dealer systems could remain unavailable “for several days.” It is not currently known who is behind the attacks. However, on Friday, Bloomberg News reported that a group believed to be based in eastern Europe is claiming responsibility. The group is reportedly demanding millions of dollars in ransom to halt the ongoing hack. In 2022, Brookfield Business Partners acquired CDK Global, with the Toronto-based equity firm valuing the transaction at over $8 billion.

author: The Associated Press
title: Ex-CEO of Nevada-based health care company Ontrak convicted of $12.5 million insider trading scheme
mainText: LOS ANGELES (AP) — The former CEO and chairman of Ontrak, a publicly traded health care company based in Nevada, was found guilty Friday of a multimillion-dollar insider trading scheme. A federal jury in Los Angeles convicted Terren Scott Peizer, a resident of Puerto Rico and Santa Monica, California, of one count of securities fraud and two counts of insider trading. Authorities said Peizer violated some of those limits when he set up plans in 2021 to sell shares in order to avoid more than $12.5 million in losses, after he learned that Ontrak’s largest customer at the time was set to terminate its contract with the company based just outside of Las Vegas. After the news later became public, Ontrak’s stock price dropped by more than 44%, authorities said. One of Peizer’s lawyers, David Willingham, said in an emailed statement that they will appeal, and that testimony at trial showed Peizer didn’t act in bad faith because he relied on the advice of his management team when he set up the trading plans.

author: Jeremy Wilkinson
title: Kiwi mum Ellen Craig admits daughter’s manslaughter at Australian cult
mainText: A New Zealand mother, Ellen Craig, pleaded guilty to the manslaughter of her 2-year-old daughter, Tillie, at an Australian cult in 1987. Craig beat Tillie to death with a plastic pipe, and instead of seeking medical help, they waited for the cult leader, Alexander Wilon, to return. Wilon attempted to resurrect Tillie before burning her body in a metal drum and scattering the ashes in a river. The cult, known as the Ministry of God, was run by Wilon, who controlled his followers through physical and sexual abuse, strict rules, and isolation. Children, including Tillie, were subjected to physical discipline, and Wilon would personally beat them. Craig and another woman waited for Wilon after Tillie's death, following his orders to burn the body. Craig fled to New Zealand, changed her name, and worked with victims of domestic violence until she was arrested in 2021. Craig pleaded guilty to manslaughter, while Wilon was declared mentally unfit for trial. Additional charges against Wilon for assaulting teenagers and women were added. The case sheds light on the extreme control and abuse within cults like the Ministry of God, and the long journey to justice for Tillie and her family. Jeremy Wilkinson, a journalist covering court and justice matters, provides detailed insights into the disturbing events at the cult and the legal proceedings against Craig and Wilon.

author: Nicole Dorfman
title: Truck driver sentenced to 11 years in prison for crash that killed family of five on I-25
mainText: A Weld County judge sentenced a truck driver to more than a decade in prison Friday afternoon for causing a deadly crash that killed a family of five on Interstate 25 near Mead in 2022. Jesus Puebla, 28, was sentenced to 11 years in the Colorado Department of Correction Friday, according to a release from the Weld County District Attorney’s Office. A jury convicted Puebla in April on all counts, including five counts of vehicular homicide and vehicular assault, careless driving and reckless driving. Additionally, the jury also convicted Puebla of a commercial vehicle safety violation and also found him guilty of not having a commercial driver’s license, according to the release. Weld Deputy District Attorneys Yvette Guthrie and Erin Vargas Gutierrez prosecuted this case. “These families have had to deal with the trauma and this devastating loss every single day,” Guthrie said in a statement. “Absolutely nothing that this defendant did the day of this tragic crash was an accident. This wasn’t road rage; this was traffic terrorism. “Five amazing lives were taken on June 13 that changed everyone’s life that day,” the victims’ daughter said in the release. “My mom and dad were the best parents any child could wish for. I’ll never get another day with them. I wish there was an opportunity that heaven could have visiting hours because I miss them every day.” The fatal crash happened on June 13, 2022, on I-25 near Colo. 66 in Weld County. According to the release, Puebla was driving a box truck when he slammed into a vehicle, killing a family of five who was traveling back home to Wyoming. Puebla also crashed into another vehicle during the incident, severely injuring the driver.

author: Colin Mixson
title: Woman arrested for leaving kids in car without A/C in Bronx amid heatwave
mainText: A woman was arrested for leaving two kids alone in a car without air conditioning in Thursday’s sweltering heat, cops said. Haniya Agoro, 34, left a 10-year-old boy and a 7-year-old girl in a car double-parked outside a W. 183rd St. residential building near University Ave. around 10:22 a.m. A bystander flagged down paramedics, who found the kids had been alone in the car for 15 minutes with the windows cracked. The kids were taken to St. Barnabas Hospital for evaluation, cops said. Agoro, a Yonkers resident, was arrested on two counts of acting in a manner injurious to a child.

author: Emma Seiwell,Ellen Moynihan
title: Man bumped onto Brooklyn subway tracks, struck by R train lives to tell tale to Daily News
mainText: A 34-year-old man stared in the face of death after a hurrying straphanger knocked him into the path of an oncoming R train in Brooklyn, living to tell the tale to the Daily News from his hospital bed Friday. “I thought to myself, ‘So this is the day I’m gonna die?’’” said the victim, who was covered in cuts, scrapes and electrodes. Emmanuel Paul, 20, was charged with reckless endangerment and assault for sparking the bizarre chain of events at the Jay St.-MetroTech station in downtown Brooklyn. Paul was hurrying into the station around 11 a.m. Thursday when he jumped over a railing to a flight of stairs leading to the R train platform, police said. When Paul landed, he accidentally bumped into L.H., knocking him onto the tracks as a train entered the station. L.H., who is homeless and new to New York, was on his way back to his Sunset Park shelter after a jog, waiting on the platform when Paul collided with him. The victim said he was texting and listening to music on his headphones when the collision happened. As horrified straphangers helplessly watched, L.H., in a standing position, was pulled along the platform. It was Paul who pulled L.H. onto the platform after the train stopped and put a backpack under his head, apologizing profusely. L.H. immediately demanded to know why Paul had pulled such a risky move. As L.H. lay on the platform, people prayed over him. The victim was immobile as of Friday afternoon and hasn’t been able to shower or eat because medical staff is worried about his ability to swallow. He hopes to get a vendor’s license or open up his own business. “It means pay attention to those around you. If somebody needs help, help them. Be courteous. Help people out. Don’t stand that close to the platform. Stay away from the staircases,” he advised. L.H. said although Paul was careless and should be charged, he thinks a felony is too harsh unless he already has a history of committing them. Paul was awaiting arraignment in Brooklyn Criminal Court as of Friday evening.

author: Patrick Reilly
title: Dueling porch pirates fight to steal 'very expensive' package seconds after driver drops it off: video
mainText: Shocking security footage captured the moment two porch pirates raced each other to a Pennsylvania man’s front door and duked it out over a package just seconds after a FedEx driver had dropped it off. Kevin Lara, of Reading, posted a video on Facebook Tuesday showing the dueling thieves on his porch clamoring to nab some “very expensive” AT&T cell phones. In the clip, the FedEx driver can be seen walking up the driveway and gently placing the packing in front of Lara’s front door and snapping a photograph of the completed delivery. In the background, a white car suddenly pulls up, the video shows. While the driver is still in the driveway walking back to his van, two men — one in a black hoodie and the other in white shorts — suddenly jump out of their cars parked in front of the house at the same time and sprint to snatch the package. “Yo!” one of them yells at the other as they wrestle over the box like a loose fumble. The man in the hoodie grabs the package first and appears to pull out a knife and begin swinging it at the other, who backs away. The victorious thief takes his loot back to his car while the man in the white shorts picks up a flowerpot and yells at him on the front lawn. The man in the shorts then gets back in his car and the two drive away, the video shows. “Poor FedEx driver looks scared. Not really worried about the phones… but what if this guy would have hurt one of my family members…. Is this really what the world has come to?” Lara wrote in the post. The Post has reached out to the Reading Police Department for additional information. The wild theft recalls a similar incident earlier this month, also involving FedEx, where a masked crook in Columbus, Ohio made off with a package just seconds after the hapless driver placed it on a customer’s porch.

author: Dorian Geiger,Katherine Donlevy,Larry Celona
title: Man stabbed to death in NYC subway station during evening rush: NYPD
mainText: A man was fatally stabbed in a Manhattan subway station during the evening rush hour Friday, police said. The 40-year-old victim was attacked at the turnstiles of the 175th Street and Fort Washington Avenue station in Washington Heights just before 6 p.m., the NYPD said. He sustained several stab wounds to the torso. The victim was rushed to Harlem Hospital, where he was pronounced dead. No arrests have been made and the investigation remains ongoing.

author: Carson Swick
title: Pennsylvania House candidate opens ‘Battle Station’ in competitive district as GOP targets 3 million swing voters
mainText: ALLENTOWN, Pa. — With support from the National Republican Congressional Committee, Pennsylvania House candidate Ryan Mackenzie debuted his campaign’s “Battle Station” office Thursday evening — in a swing district whose Democratic incumbent can’t stop insulting her constituents. Mackenzie, a 12-year state representative from Lehigh County, told his enthusiastic audience of staffers and volunteers at the newly opened office in Allentown. Launched in January, the NRCC’s Battle Station initiative is designed to establish early contact with 3 million swing voters in competitive House districts. Mackenzie, 41, is taking aim at Democratic incumbent Susan Wild, who has represented Pennsylvania’s 7th Congressional District since 2018. Two county GOP chairmen, Lehigh’s Joe Vichot and Northampton’s Glenn Geissinger, spoke Thursday in support of Mackenzie — and dunking on Wild became a theme. Wild has been caught making disparaging comments about her constituents at least three times in recent years. Taking a more optimistic tone, Geissinger hunched his bet on a Mackenzie victory in notoriously purple Northampton County. In 2022, Wild won the county by fewer than 4,000 votes and the overall district by fewer than 6,000. NRCC spokesman Mike Marinella told The Post, "This new Battle Station will be critical in mobilizing voters to elect Ryan Mackenzie and send extreme Democrat Susan Wild packing."

author: Chris Nesi
title: Three Columbia deans placed on leave over disparaging text exchange during antisemitism panel
mainText: Three deans at Columbia University have been put on leave after being caught sending disparaging text messages, including a vomiting emoji, during a panel discussion on antisemitism. The exchange took place during a May 31 panel about Jewish life on campus, where speakers discussed the impact of rising antisemitism related to Israel's conflict with Hamas. The deans involved were Josef Sorett, Susan Chang-Kim, Matthew Patashnick, and Cristen Kromm. They made mocking and dismissive remarks throughout the panel, with Kromm using emojis to mock an op-ed by the school's campus rabbi and Patashnick accusing a panelist of exploiting the situation for fundraising. The messages were captured by an alumnus and later made public, causing an uproar. Sorett apologized for the harm caused by the messages but claimed they did not reflect the views of the individuals or the institution. The incident led to the deans being placed on leave. In response, Columbia University expressed its commitment to combating antisemitism and creating a safe and inclusive campus for all students. The university's Morningside Heights campus witnessed anti-Israel protests following the conflict with Hamas, including clashes with law enforcement and incidents of vandalism. The deans' behavior was widely condemned, and the university administration took swift action to address the situation.

author: Mara Siegler
title: Jewish Harvard student suing Ivy League school details antisemitism, unsafe environment on campus
mainText: Jewish Harvard student Shabbos Kestenbaum is suing Harvard along with other students over antisemitism, highlighting an unsafe environment on campus. He described incidents of intolerance towards Jewish students, including being spat on and a student being asked to leave class for being Israeli. Kestenbaum faced threats requiring private security, such as someone taunting him with a machete online. He expressed the fear and challenges Jewish students face in speaking out, mentioning the professional and social consequences. Kestenbaum, a progressive, feels abandoned by fellow liberals and condemned the rise of antisemitism on college campuses. He emphasized the urgent need to address bigotry and hatred towards Jewish students, invoking the Holocaust. Multiple schools, including UC Berkeley and Ohio State, are facing lawsuits for antisemitism. Harvard President Claudine Gay resigned following controversy over her testimony and accusations of plagiarism.

author: Sarah Montague
title: The debate: Would Labour’s plan to tax private school fees work?
mainText: Would Labour’s private school tax plan work? The Labour Party has pledged to add tax to private schools fees and use the funds to recruit teachers for state schools. The policy, proposed in Labour’s manifesto, has split opinion. Some argue it is a reasonable way to raise revenue and others think it’s an unfair charge that will fall on parents. The BBC’s Sarah Montague spoke with Sam Freedman, former adviser to the former Education Secretary Michael Gove, who is in favour of the proposed VAT charge, and Kristina Murkett, an English teacher at a private school, who is against. Their conversation was first broadcast on Monday 17 June on BBC Radio 4’s World At One.

author: Deutsche Welle
title: Apple delays release of new AI features in Europe
mainText: Apple said Friday it would delay the rollout of its recently announced AI features in Europe because of "regulatory uncertainties." An Apple spokesperson cited for the delay concerns over the European Union's Digital Markets Act (DMA), the bloc's landmark legislation aimed at curbing the power of big tech. "We do not believe we will be able to roll out these features to our EU users this year," the spokesperson said. Earlier this month, the company unveiled "Apple Intelligence," its suite of AI features for its coveted devices. The announcement came as an apparent attempt by Apple to reassure its users that it is not falling behind in the AI frenzy. It included a partnership with OpenAI to make ChatGPT available to iPhone users. Why is Apple delaying AI rollout in Europe? According to Apple, the AI capabilities were put on hold over concern "that the interoperability requirements of the DMA could force us to compromise the integrity of our products in ways that risk user privacy and data security." "We are committed to collaborating with the European Commission in an attempt to find a solution that would enable us to deliver these features to our EU customers without compromising their safety," the company added. Apple is also delaying the release of its iPhone Mirroring and SharePlay Screen Sharing enhancements in Europe. Apple Intelligence, which runs only on the company's in-house technology, will enable users to create their own emojis based on a description in everyday language, or to generate brief summaries of emails in the mailbox. What is the DMA? In an effort to establish fair competition in Europe, the EU's Digital Markets Act sets out a list of dos and don'ts for designated internet gatekeepers, including Apple. The DMA enables the European Commission, the EU's executive arm, to investigate, fine and impose structural remedies on non-compliant gatekeepers. Fines can reach up to 10 percent of global annual turnover, with repeat offenders facing fines of up to 20 percent. The EU's competition chief, Margrethe Vestager, warned on Tuesday that Apple was failing to comply with the DMA as the bloc conducts an investigation into Apple's business practices. dh/fb (AFP, Reuters)

author: Amy Bounds
title: ‘Future leaders’ enjoy BVSD’s Summer Leadership Academy pilot
mainText: A dozen Boulder Valley high school students participated in mock interviews as part of the Boulder Valley School District’s Summer Leadership Academy pilot. The academy includes workshops on leadership and job skills followed by internships in various departments and organizations. Stuart Lord, a leadership consultant, initiated the program to provide work-based learning opportunities for students. The program aims to help students explore careers, improve interview skills, and earn college credit. Students will receive stipends and the opportunity to participate in the state’s ASCENT program. The academy is designed to support students through high school and beyond. The program received over 100 applications for 12 spots, with a focus on students of color. The students shared their experiences and goals, highlighting their desire to gain work experience, improve skills, and explore different career paths. Participants appreciated the real work environment provided by the workshops and expressed enthusiasm about learning leadership styles and connecting with potential mentors. Overall, the program aims to prepare students for success in their future careers and provide valuable experiences in various industries.

author: Deutsche Welle
title: Milei EU trip: snubbed in Spain, low-key in Berlin
mainText: Argentine President Javier Milei arrived in Madrid on Friday to a rock star greeting from right-wing conservatives at an event organized by the Spanish far-right VOX party. Milei was snubbed by the Spanish government as well as the nation's royals. Speaking at the confab, Milei railed against the Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez and repeated claims that Sanchez's wife Begona Gomez is corrupt. The Spanish Foreign Ministry accused Milei of engaging in a "frontal attack on our democracy, on our institutions and Spain." Milei has rejected calls to apologize, preferring to continue his attacks. The second stop on Milei's EU tour will be Germany. There, the Argentine politician will accept an award from the Friedrich Hayek Society — named for the liberal Austrian-British economist Friedrich August von Hayek. Milei will wrap up his stay in Germany with a one-hour meeting with Chancellor Olaf Scholz. A spokesperson for the Argentine said that he requested a simple working meeting rather than one involving pomp. Plans originally entailed a military reception and a press conference, both of which were dropped as a courtesy to the South American. President Milei will conclude his trip to Europe with a stop in the Czech Republic.

author: Michelle Kapusta
title: Expert Reveals How Prince William Wants to ‘Honor’ Princess Diana When He’s King
mainText: Prince William is expected to honor Princess Diana when he becomes king by embodying both confidence and humility, according to body language and behavioral expert Darren Stanton. Stanton observed that William has transformed from a shy and introverted young royal to a confident and self-assured individual, much like his late mother. He noted William's growth in public speaking abilities, expressing genuine joy and pride in his humanitarian work. Stanton also predicted that William will follow Queen Elizabeth II's example in carrying out his royal duties with confidence and openness, gaining the trust and support of the nation. By continuing Diana's legacy of compassion and empathy, William aims to honor his mother in his future role as king.
